title: Chinese HSK 4
description: The fourth step in Mandarin Chinese, from HSK 3 to the new HSK 4 (HSK 3.0), the first of the intermediate levels. Grammar lessons cover 连…都, 即使…也, 尽管…但是, 不管…都, 既然…就, 不是…而是, 一方面…另一方面, 不仅…还, the extended 把 sentence, 叫 and 让 passives, A 不如 B, double negatives, rhetorical 难道…吗, written-style words such as 由, 将, 与 and 此, and numbers with 倍, 来, 左右 and percentages. Topics follow a final university year into first jobs: classes and graduation, the doctor, shopping and renting, job interviews and the office, journeys and hotels, family and feelings, the media, nature and the environment. The 1,000 new words (2,000 in all) are learned through typed review cards and the 441 new characters (1,096 in all) through notecards, words and tracing, with pinyin you can turn off and a switch to traditional characters. Readings grow to about 350 characters, and the last lessons practise the writing and speaking tasks and the exam format. Requires Chinese HSK 3.
author: Erudior

lessons.title: The last term begins: since, originally, never, each and any
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Welcome to HSK 4, the first intermediate level. You know about a thousand words and can join
clauses in a dozen ways. This course adds a thousand more words and a new kind of Chinese: the
**[[written register]]** ({书面语|shū miàn yǔ} in Chinese), the slightly formal style of notices, emails, news and
exam texts. You'll meet a few written words in every lesson, each beside the everyday word it
replaces, and you'll use them where they belong: in writing, not in a chat with a friend.

The story starts in spring 2029. {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) and {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming) are beginning the last term of
their degrees: she studies journalism ({新闻|xīn wén}{专业|zhuān yè}), he studies English ({英语|Yīng yǔ}{专业|zhuān yè}). {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) is in
her second year, and {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) works for a company and still comes to {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}'s evening class.

This lesson teaches:

- the first written words: {此|cǐ} (this), {此次|cǐ cì} (this time), {此外|cǐ wài} (besides), {入|rù} (to enter), and how
  they relate to {这|zhè}, {这|zhè}{次|cì}, {还|hái}{有|yǒu} and {进|jìn};
- the **[[demonstratives]]** {各|gè}, {各位|gè wèi}, {各种|gè zhǒng} and {各个|gè gè} (each, every, all kinds of) and {任何|rèn hé} (any);
- {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}…: since (we know that)…, then…;
- {本来|běn lái} (originally; by rights) and, in brief, {原来|yuán lái};
- {从来|cóng lái} with {不|bù} or {没|méi}: never, not once;
- university words: {本科|běn kē}, {学院|xué yuàn}, {专业|zhuān yè}, {课程|kè chéng}, {教授|jiào shòu}, {教师|jiào shī}, {师生|shī shēng}, {食堂|shí táng}, {操场|cāo chǎng}, {入学|rù xué}, and the verbs
  {适应|shì yìng} (to adapt) and {熟悉|shú xī} (to know well).

## Spoken and written Chinese

Every language has a formal written style. In English you write "commence" or "in addition" in a
notice and say "start" and "also" to a friend. Chinese does the same, but its written words often
come from classical Chinese, so they are short, single characters that look unfamiliar at first:
{此|cǐ} for {这|zhè}, {入|rù} for {进|jìn}, {与|yǔ} for {和|hé} (lesson 24). You'll see them on signs, in notices from a school or a
company, in the news and in the HSK reading paper. You don't need them to chat, and using them in
a chat sounds stiff, like saying "I shall commence my repast" at dinner.

| Written ({书面语|shū miàn yǔ}) | Spoken | Meaning | Where you see the written word |
|---|---|---|---|
| {此|cǐ} | {这|zhè} | this | {此次|cǐ cì}, {此外|cǐ wài}, {在此|zài cǐ} (here); signs |
| {此次|cǐ cì} | {这|zhè}{次|cì} | this time, this occasion | notices about an event or exam |
| {此外|cǐ wài} | {还|hái}{有|yǒu}, {另外|lìng wài} (lesson 04) | besides, in addition | the start of a new point in a text |
| {入|rù} | {进|jìn} | to enter | {入学|rù xué}, {加入|jiā rù}, {入口|rù kǒu} (an entrance, lesson 16) |
| {教师|jiào shī} | {老师|lǎo shī} | teacher | job titles, forms, news |
| {各位|gè wèi} | {大家|dà jiā} | everyone (addressed) | the start of a notice or a speech |

The reference sheet "Spoken and written Chinese" collects every written word of this level beside
its spoken partner; it grows lesson by lesson.

## {此|cǐ}, {此次|cǐ cì}, {此外|cǐ wài}: "this" in writing

{此|cǐ} is the written "this". On its own it lives in set phrases, while {这|zhè} does the everyday work:

{在此|zài cǐ}{祝|zhù}{大家|dà jiā}{新年|xīn nián}{快乐|kuài lè}！ — Here we wish you all a happy New Year! (the end of a formal letter;
{在此|zài cǐ}: here, at this point)

{此时|cǐ shí}，{学生|xué sheng}{们|men}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{教室|jiào shì}{里|lǐ}。 — At this moment, the students are all in the classroom. ({此时|cǐ shí}: at
this time, in a story or a report)

{此次|cǐ cì} is "this time" when the time is an occasion, such as an event, a trip or an exam:

{此次|cǐ cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}{三百|sān bǎi}{名|míng}{学生|xué sheng}{参加|cān jiā}。 — Three hundred students are taking part in this exam.
({名|míng}: the formal measure word for people)

In a chat you'd say {这|zhè}{次|cì}: {这|zhè}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{难|nán}{不|bu}{难|nán}？ (Was this exam hard?)

{此外|cǐ wài} (besides, in addition) starts a new point. It joins two sentences, so it comes at the start
of the second, followed by a comma:

{食堂|shí táng}{早上|zǎo shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{开门|kāi mén}。{此外|cǐ wài}，{学校|xué xiào}{东|dōng}{边|biān}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{咖啡|kā fēi}{馆|guǎn}。 — The canteen opens at half
past six in the morning. There is also a café on the east side of campus.

The second sentence often has {还|hái} or {也|yě} as well, as above. In speech, {还|hái}{有|yǒu} or {另外|lìng wài} (lesson 04) does
this job: {还|hái}{有|yǒu}，{别|bié}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{带|dài}{学生证|xué sheng zhèng}。 (And don't forget your student card. {学生证|xué sheng zhèng}: student card)

## {各|gè}, {各位|gè wèi}, {各种|gè zhǒng}, {各个|gè gè}: each and every

{各|gè} means "each, every" across a set: each one separately, but all of them. It's a
**[[demonstrative]]**, like {这|zhè} and {那|nà}, and it goes straight before a noun or a measure word. A {都|dōu} later
in the sentence is very common, because {各|gè} points at the whole set:

| Form | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {各|gè} + noun | some nouns of groups and places: {国|guó}, {班|bān}, {学院|xué yuàn}, {专业|zhuān yè} | {各|gè}{国|guó}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{来|lái}{了|le}。 Students from every country came. |
| {各位|gè wèi} | everyone (polite address, to a group) | {各位|gè wèi}{同学|tóng xué}，{大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！ Hello, everyone! |
| {各种|gè zhǒng} + noun | all kinds of, every sort of | {超市|chāo shì}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{各种|gè zhǒng}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。 The supermarket has all kinds of fruit. |
| {各个|gè gè} + noun | each and every one (of a set) | {各个|gè gè}{学院|xué yuàn}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{食堂|shí táng}。 Every college has its own canteen. |

- {各位|gè wèi} is how a speaker or a notice addresses a group: {各位|gè wèi}{老师|lǎo shī}, {各位|gè wèi}{同学|tóng xué}, or {各位|gè wèi} alone
  ("everyone"). It is polite and a little formal; with friends say {大家|dà jiā}.
- {各种|gè zhǒng} is followed by a noun and often by {都|dōu}: {他|tā}{各种|gè zhǒng}{运动|yùn dòng}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。 (He likes every kind of
  sport.) The set phrase {各种各样|gè zhǒng gè yàng} means "all sorts of": {各种各样|gè zhǒng gè yàng}{的|de}{书|shū} (all sorts of books).
- {各个|gè gè} stresses that no member of the set is left out. It sounds more formal than {每|měi}{个|gè}: {每|měi}{个|gè}
  {学生|xué sheng} (each student) is the everyday way to say it.
- {各|gè} can also stand before a verb, meaning "each": {我们|wǒ men}{各|gè}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yì}{本|běn}。 (We each bought one.)

## {任何|rèn hé}: any (at all)

{任何|rèn hé} (any) goes before a noun, usually with no measure word: {任何|rèn hé}{人|rén} (anyone), {任何|rèn hé}{事|shì} (anything),
{任何|rèn hé}{问题|wèn tí} (any question), {任何|rèn hé}{时候|shí hou} (any time), {任何|rèn hé}{地方|dì fang} (anywhere). It almost always comes with
{都|dōu} or {也|yě}, or after a negative:

{任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。 — Anyone can take part.

{有|yǒu}{任何|rèn hé}{问题|wèn tí}，{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{问|wèn}{我|wǒ}。 — If you have any questions at all, you can ask me.

{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{任何|rèn hé}{问题|wèn tí}。 — I don't have any questions at all.

{他|tā}{任何|rèn hé}{时候|shí hou}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn}。 — He's conscientious at all times.

When the {任何|rèn hé} phrase is the subject or comes before the verb, use {都|dōu} or {也|yě} after it ({任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}…).
When it's the object after a negative verb, no {都|dōu} is needed ({没有|méi yǒu}{任何|rèn hé}{问题|wèn tí}). {任何|rèn hé} is stronger
than {什么|shén me} in the same place: {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{什么|shén me}{问题|wèn tí} is "I haven't really got any questions", {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}
{任何|rèn hé}{问题|wèn tí} "I have no questions whatsoever".

## {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}…: since (we know that)…

{既然|jì rán} takes a fact that both speakers accept ("since…, now that…") and draws a conclusion from it,
usually a suggestion, a decision or a question. This is **[[inference]]**: not "because A happened, B
happened" ({因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ}) but "A is so, therefore let's do B". The second clause has {就|jiù} (or {那|nà}, {那么|nà me}, {还|hái}, {也|yě}):

{既然|jì rán}{你|nǐ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{决定|jué dìng}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{别|bié}{担心|dān xīn}{了|le}。 — Since you've made up your mind, stop worrying.

{既然|jì rán}{他|tā}{不|bù}{来|lái}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。 — Since he isn't coming, let's go.

{既然|jì rán}{是|shì}{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{学期|xué qī}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{认真|rèn zhēn}{学习|xué xí}{吧|ba}。 — Since it's our last term, let's study
hard.

{既然|jì rán}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}，{还|hái}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{干|gàn}{什么|shén me}？ — If you're not feeling well, why go to class? (a question:
"since that's so, why…?")

Where things go:

- {既然|jì rán} starts its clause or follows the subject: {既然|jì rán}{你|nǐ}{知道|zhī dào}{了|le}… or {你|nǐ}{既然|jì rán}{知道|zhī dào}{了|le}… Both are fine.
- {就|jiù} is an adverb, so it goes after the subject of the second clause: {既然|jì rán}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}
  {一起|yì qǐ}{吃|chī}{吧|ba}。
- The first clause is something already known, often something the other person has just said.
  That's the difference from {如果|rú guǒ} (if), which imagines: {如果|rú guǒ}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{一起|yì qǐ}{吃|chī} (if you come);
  {既然|jì rán}{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{了|le} (now that you're here).

| | The first clause is… | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ}… | a cause | {因为|yīn wèi}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{没|méi}{去|qù}。 Because it rained, we didn't go. |
| {如果|rú guǒ}…{就|jiù}… | a supposition | {如果|rú guǒ}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。 If it rains, we won't go. |
| {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}… | an accepted fact, for a conclusion | {既然|jì rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{别|bié}{去|qù}{了|le}。 Since it's raining, let's not go. |

## {本来|běn lái}: originally, at first; by rights

{本来|běn lái} has two uses.

**Originally, at first**, before something changed. The sentence (or the next one) usually tells
you what changed, often with {后来|hòu lái} (later) or {可是|kě shì} / {但是|dàn shì}:

{我|wǒ}{本来|běn lái}{想|xiǎng}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}，{后来|hòu lái}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{了|le}{机票|jī piào}。 — I'd meant to go by train, but then I got a plane
ticket.

{本来|běn lái}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{辣|là}{的|de}，{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{以后|yǐ hòu}{慢慢|màn màn}{习惯|xí guàn}{了|le}。 — I didn't like spicy food at first, but I
got used to it after coming to Beijing.

{本来|běn lái} can go before or after the subject ({本来|běn lái}{我|wǒ}… or {我|wǒ}{本来|běn lái}…), and it can describe a noun with {的|de}:
{本来|běn lái}{的|de}{计划|jì huà} (the original plan).

**By rights, it goes without saying**, usually as {本来|běn lái}{就|jiù}: what was true all along, so the speaker
isn't surprised or thinks something is obvious:

{他|tā}{本来|běn lái}{就|jiù}{很|hěn}{瘦|shòu}，{现在|xiàn zài}{更|gèng}{瘦|shòu}{了|le}。 — He was thin to begin with, and now he's even thinner.

{这|zhè}{本来|běn lái}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}，{你|nǐ}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}。 — This was your book anyway: take it.

You'll learn {原来|yuán lái} in lesson 20. It also means "originally" ({我|wǒ}{原来|yuán lái}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi} = {我|wǒ}{本来|běn lái}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi},
I used to live in Shanghai), but its main job is a discovery, "so that's it": {原来|yuán lái}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}！ (Oh,
it's you!) {本来|běn lái} never means "so it turns out", and {原来|yuán lái} never means "it goes without saying".

## {从来|cóng lái} + {不|bù} / {没|méi}: never

{从来|cóng lái} means "all along, at any time so far". With a negative it means "never":

- {从来|cóng lái}{不|bù} + verb: never, as a habit or a rule: {我|wǒ}{从来|cóng lái}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}。 (I never drink coffee.) {他|tā}
  {从来|cóng lái}{不|bù}{迟到|chí dào}。 (He's never late.)
- {从来|cóng lái}{没|méi} ({有|yǒu}) + verb + {过|guo}: never once, up to now: {我|wǒ}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 (I've never been to
  Shanghai.) {这样|zhè yàng}{的|de}{事|shì}，{我|wǒ}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{听说|tīng shuō}{过|guo}。 (I've never heard of such a thing.)

The difference is the same as between {不|bù} and {没|méi}: {不|bù} for habits and choices, {没|méi}…{过|guo} for experience.
{从来|cóng lái} is seldom used without a negative; when it is, {都|dōu} follows it: {他|tā}{从来|cóng lái}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn} (he has
always been conscientious). For a positive "always" in everyday speech, use {一直|yì zhí} or {总是|zǒng shì}.

## University words

- {本科|běn kē} is undergraduate study: {读|dú}{本科|běn kē} (to do a first degree), {本科|běn kē}{四年级|sì nián jí} (the fourth year), {本科生|běn kē shēng}
  (an undergraduate). {王芳|Wáng Fāng} and {李明|Lǐ Míng} are {本科|běn kē}{四年级|sì nián jí}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}.
- {学院|xué yuàn} is a college or school within a university, as in {外语学院|wài yǔ xué yuàn} (the school of foreign
  languages). It's also the name of some smaller institutions.
- {专业|zhuān yè} is your subject, your major: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{专业|zhuān yè}{的|de}？{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{新闻|xīn wén}{专业|zhuān yè}{的|de}。 (What's your major?
  Journalism.) As an adjective it means "professional": {他|tā}{做|zuò}{得|de}{很|hěn}{专业|zhuān yè}。
- {课程|kè chéng} is a course or the whole curriculum: {这|zhè}{学期|xué qī}{的|de}{课程|kè chéng} (this term's courses). A single class
  you take is {一|yì}{门|mén}{课|kè}.
- {教授|jiào shòu} is a professor, addressed with the surname: {罗|Luó}{教授|jiào shòu} (Professor Luo). {教师|jiào shī} is "teacher" in
  formal writing and on forms: {她|tā}{是|shì}{一|yì}{名|míng}{中学|zhōng xué}{教师|jiào shī}。 (She's a secondary-school teacher.) You
  never call someone {教师|jiào shī}: to a teacher, say {老师|lǎo shī}.
- {师生|shī shēng} (teachers and students) is a written word for a whole school: {全|quán}{校|xiào}{师生|shī shēng} (everyone in the
  school).
- {食堂|shí táng} is a canteen or dining hall; {操场|cāo chǎng} is the sports ground, the playing field.
- {入学|rù xué} is to start at a school or university: {九|jiǔ}{月|yuè}{入学|rù xué} (to start in September), {入学|rù xué}{考试|kǎo shì} (an
  entrance exam).
- {加入|jiā rù} is to join an organisation, a team or a group and become a member: {加入|jiā rù}{学生会|xué sheng huì} (to join the
  student union). You {参加|cān jiā} an event or an activity ({参加|cān jiā}{比赛|bǐ sài}, {参加|cān jiā}{考试|kǎo shì}).
- {适应|shì yìng} is to adapt, to get used to something new: {适应|shì yìng}{新|xīn}{环境|huán jìng} (a new environment), {还|hái}{不|bú}{太|tài}{适应|shì yìng}
  (not used to it yet). It takes an object directly.
- {熟悉|shú xī} is "familiar, knowing well" ({我|wǒ}{对|duì}{这儿|zhèr}{很|hěn}{熟悉|shú xī}, I know this place well) and also "to get to
  know": {先|xiān}{熟悉|shú xī}{一下|yí xià}{学校|xué xiào} (first get to know the university).

✎ marks the ten handwriting characters. Only {专|zhuān} has a different traditional form, {專|zhuān} ({寸|cùn} at the
bottom, 11 strokes); the other fourteen are the same in both scripts.

- **Sound parts.** {授|shòu} shòu has {受|shòu} shòu (to receive, HSK 3's {受|shòu}) on the right, with the same sound:
  a teacher's {授|shòu} "gives" what a student {受|shòu} "receives". {程|chéng} chéng has {呈|chéng} chéng, also still exact. {任|rèn}
  rèn has {壬|rén} rén (the same syllable in another tone), and {熟|shú} shú has {孰|shú} shú over the fire dots 灬. {堂|táng} táng has {尚|shàng} on top, the part you
  know from {常|cháng} cháng (HSK 3's {常常|cháng cháng}): the sound is close but no longer the same. {何|hé} hé is 亻 +
  {可|kě} kě, the {可|kě} of {河|hé} hé (river): there the sound has moved on.
- **{各|gè} as a sound part.** {各|gè} gè gives a rough sound to {客|kè} kè ({客人|kè rén}), and to {格|gé} gé in {合格|hé gé} and {严格|yán gé},
  next lesson's words, and {胳|gē} gē (the arm, lesson 06). It's 夂 over {口|kǒu}.
- **Families.** {禾|hé} (grain) is the radical of {科|kē} and {程|chéng}, as of {种|zhǒng} and {秋|qiū}. 扌 (hand) is the radical of {操|cāo} and {授|shòu}.
- **Look-alikes.** {入|rù} rù has the short left-falling stroke first and the long right-falling one
  second; {人|rén} rén has the long left-falling stroke and a shorter right one, and {八|bā} bā has two
  separate strokes. {此|cǐ} cǐ is the top of {些|xiē} xiē (HSK 1: {一些|yì xiē}): {些|xiē} is {此|cǐ} over {二|èr}. {既|jì} jì and {即|jí} jí
  ({即使|jí shǐ}, lesson 26) share the left side; {既|jì} has 旡 on the right, {即|jí} has 卩.
- **{食|shí} as a radical.** {食|shí} shí is a radical in its own right. On the left of a character it shrinks to
  饣, as in {饭|fàn}, {饿|è}, {馆|guǎn} and {饺|jiǎo}: food words.
- **A memory aid** for {熟悉|shú xī}: you know something well ({熟|shú}) when it's in your heart ({心|xīn}, the bottom of
  {悉|xī}).

### Stroke order

- **{入|rù}**: two strokes. The first is a short left-falling stroke; the second, the long
  right-falling stroke, starts on it near the top.
- **{专|zhuān}**: only four strokes: two horizontals, then one stroke that goes down, turns right and
  sweeps down-left, then the dot. Don't break the middle stroke in two.
- **{此|cǐ}**: {止|zhǐ} on the left (vertical, short horizontal, vertical, long rising stroke), then the
  right side: a left-falling stroke and a vertical bend hook.
- **{既|jì}**: the left side first (the frame, two short horizontals, a vertical with a rising tail,
  a dot), then 旡: a horizontal, a down-and-turn stroke, a left-falling stroke, and the long
  vertical bend hook last.
- **{熟|shú}**: the top-left part, then {丸|wán} on the top right, then the four fire dots 灬 at the bottom
  last (15 strokes).

## Pronunciation

- {此|cǐ} cǐ: *c* is like the *ts* in "cats", with a puff of air; the vowel is the buzzing *-i* of {字|zì} zì
  and {次|cì} cì. {此次|cǐ cì} cǐ cì is the same syllable twice, third tone then fourth.
- {各|gè} gè sounds exactly like the measure word {个|gè} gè; {各位|gè wèi} gè wèi and {各个|gè gè} gè gè are both 4+4.
- {熟|shú} is shú in the dictionary; in everyday Beijing speech you'll often hear shóu ({熟|shú}{了|le}: it's cooked).
  Both are correct; the course writes shú.
- {授|shòu} shòu and {受|shòu} shòu are homophones. {教授|jiào shòu} is jiào shòu with {教|jiào} in the fourth tone, as in {教室|jiào shì}: {教|jiāo} is
  jiāo only as the verb "to teach".
- {既然|jì rán} jì rán: *r* as in {然|rán}, close to the *s* in "pleasure".
- {入|rù} rù and {如|rú} rú ({如果|rú guǒ}) differ only in tone.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{既然|jì rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}~~: {既然|jì rán} pairs with {就|jiù} (or {那|nà}, {还|hái}), not {所以|suǒ yǐ}. Say {既然|jì rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，
  {我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。
- ~~{教师|jiào shī}，{您|nín}{好|hǎo}！~~: {教师|jiào shī} is a job title, never an address. Say {老师|lǎo shī}{好|hǎo}！
- {我|wǒ}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi} is heard, but for "never (in my life)" {从来|cóng lái}{没|méi} usually takes {过|guo} after the verb: {我|wǒ}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}
  {去|qù}{过|guo}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。 (Without {过|guo} it is heard mostly of a habit kept up so far: {他|tā}{从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{迟到|chí dào}, he has never once been late.)
- {任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā} sounds unfinished: {任何|rèn hé} before the verb takes {都|dōu} or {也|yě}: {任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。
- {各位|gè wèi}{同学|tóng xué}{们|men} is common in speech, but it says "all of you" twice: {各位|gè wèi} already does, so careful writing leaves out {们|men}. {各位|gè wèi}{同学|tóng xué} or {同学|tóng xué}{们|men}.
- {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{参加|cān jiā}{你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{小组|xiǎo zǔ} is heard, but to become a member, {加入|jiā rù} is the usual verb: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{加入|jiā rù}
  {你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}。 ({小组|xiǎo zǔ}: a group, lesson 04.) You {参加|cān jiā} an event.
- Using {此|cǐ} or {此外|cǐ wài} in a chat sounds stiff: in speech, {这|zhè} and {还|hái}{有|yǒu}. Keep them for writing.

## Key points

- Written Chinese ({书面语|shū miàn yǔ}) has its own words: {此|cǐ} = {这|zhè}, {此次|cǐ cì} = {这|zhè}{次|cì}, {此外|cǐ wài} = {还|hái}{有|yǒu} / {另外|lìng wài}, {入|rù} = {进|jìn},
  {教师|jiào shī} = {老师|lǎo shī}. Use them in notices, emails and essays.
- {各|gè} + noun or measure word ({各|gè}{国|guó}, {各位|gè wèi}, {各种|gè zhǒng}, {各个|gè gè}): each, every; often with {都|dōu}. {各位|gè wèi} addresses a
  group politely.
- {任何|rèn hé} + noun ({任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}, {任何|rèn hé}{问题|wèn tí}): any at all; with {都|dōu} / {也|yě} before the verb, or after a negative.
- {既然|jì rán} A ， (subject) {就|jiù} B: since A is so, B (a suggestion, decision or question); not with {所以|suǒ yǐ}.
- {本来|běn lái}: originally (something changed) and {本来|běn lái}{就|jiù}: by rights, all along. {原来|yuán lái} (lesson 20) adds "so
  it turns out".
- {从来|cóng lái}{不|bù} + verb: never (habit); {从来|cóng lái}{没|méi} + verb + {过|guo}: never once (experience).
- New characters (simplified): {={科|kē}、{操|cāo}、{此|cǐ}、{各|gè}、{授|shòu}、{程|chéng}、{入|rù}、{既|jì}、{食|shí}、{堂|táng}、{熟|shú}、{悉|xī}、{任|rèn}、{何|hé}、{专|zhuān}=}; only {专|zhuān} differs in traditional
  ({專|zhuān}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Classes, exams and marks: more 把, and doing it again
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

It's April, and mid-term exams are coming. {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) has a written and a spoken exam in
{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}'s class, and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang), in her last term, has her own work to finish. This lesson gives you
the words of classes and exams, and two kinds of grammar you need to talk about getting work done:

- more of the **{把|bǎ} sentence** (HSK 3 lesson 03): {把|bǎ} with {了|le} and {一下|yí xià} ({把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}, {把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{改|gǎi}{一下|yí xià}),
  with how many times ({把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}), and with adverbs before the verb ({把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{检查|jiǎn chá}{了|le}
  {一|yí}{遍|biàn});
- doing something again: {重新|chóng xīn} and {重|chóng} (again, from the start) beside {再|zài} and {又|yòu};
- {允许|yǔn xǔ} (to allow) and {严格|yán gé} (strict);
- exam words: {笔试|bǐ shì}, {口语|kǒu yǔ}, {听力|tīng lì}, {试题|shì tí}, {答案|dá àn}, {分数|fēn shù}, {合格|hé gé}, {考生|kǎo shēng}, {期中|qī zhōng}, {期末|qī mò}, {时间表|shí jiān biǎo};
- {预习|yù xí} and {自习|zì xí}, {错误|cuò wù} and {正确|zhèng què}, and {台|tái}, the measure word for machines ({一|yì}{台|tái}{打印机|dǎ yìn jī}).

## {把|bǎ} again: what the sentence needs

A {把|bǎ} sentence brings the object forward, before the verb, to say what you do **to** it and what
becomes of it. You know the basic shape from HSK 3:

subject + {把|bǎ} + object + verb + something more

{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{书|shū}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{吧|ba}。 — Put the book on the table.

{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{手机|shǒu jī}{忘|wàng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{了|le}。 — I've left my phone at home.

The rule that matters most: the verb can't stand alone at the end. Something has to follow it,
because a {把|bǎ} sentence tells you the result of the action. ~~{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{做|zuò}~~ is unfinished. HSK 3
used result complements ({做|zuò}{完|wán}, {洗|xǐ}{干净|gān jìng}) and places ({放|fàng}{在|zài}…). This lesson adds three more ways to
finish the sentence.

### {把|bǎ} + verb + {了|le}: get it done

A plain {了|le} after the verb says the action is done with, often with the feeling "and then it's
gone, it's over":

{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}。 — I've handed in my homework.

{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}{喝|hē}{了|le}{吧|ba}。 — Drink this glass of water up.

In requests and orders this {了|le} is the whole point: {把|bǎ}{药|yào}{吃|chī}{了|le}！ (Take your medicine!) {把|bǎ}{门|mén}{关|guān}{了|le}。
(Shut the door.) Without it the sentence breaks the rule above.

### {把|bǎ} + verb + {一下|yí xià}: do it quickly, have a go at it

{一下|yí xià} after the verb softens a request: "just…, would you…" It's the most common way to ask
someone to do something to a thing:

{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{改|gǎi}{一下|yí xià}。 — Could you correct the answer?

{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{时间表|shí jiān biǎo}{打印|dǎ yìn}{一下|yí xià}。 — I'll just print the timetable.

{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{读|dú}{一下|yí xià}，{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？ — Would you read this sentence, please?

### {把|bǎ} + verb + {了|le} + number of times

How many times you do something to the object goes after the verb, as a **[[verb measure word]]**
({遍|biàn}, {次|cì}, HSK 3 lesson 13):

{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}。 — I read the text through three times.

{老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{把|bǎ}{每|měi}{个|gè}{生词|shēng cí}{写|xiě}{十|shí}{遍|biàn}。 — The teacher had us write each new word ten times. ({生词|shēng cí}:
new words)

{遍|biàn} counts going through something from start to finish (a text, a film, a song); {次|cì} counts
occasions. With {把|bǎ}, {遍|biàn} is the usual one. A length of time can follow the verb in the same way, when
you spend that time working on something: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{想|xiǎng}{了|le}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}。 (I spent days thinking
this problem over.)

### Adverbs in a {把|bǎ} sentence

Words that describe the whole sentence go before {把|bǎ}: negatives, modal verbs and adverbs of time.

{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{带|dài}{来|lái}。 — I didn't bring my homework.

{你|nǐ}{应该|yīng gāi}{把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{写|xiě}{清楚|qīng chu}。 — You should write the answers clearly.

{他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{把|bǎ}{报告|bào gào}{交|jiāo}{了|le}。 — He has already handed in the report. ({报告|bào gào}: a report)

An adverb that says **how** the action is done (with {地|de}) can go either before {把|bǎ} or straight before
the verb; both are common:

{他|tā}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{检查|jiǎn chá}{了|le}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 = {他|tā}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{检查|jiǎn chá}{了|le}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 — He checked his homework
carefully, once through.

But {没|méi}, {不|bù}, {别|bié} and the modal verbs never go between the object and the verb: ~~{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{没|méi}{交|jiāo}~~ is
wrong; say {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{上去|shàng qù} (I didn't hand in my homework).

| What follows the verb | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| a result (HSK 3) | {把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{做|zuò}{完|wán}{了|le} | finished the homework |
| a place (HSK 3) | {把|bǎ}{书|shū}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng} | put the book on the table |
| {了|le} | {把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le} | handed the homework in |
| {一下|yí xià} | {把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{改|gǎi}{一下|yí xià} | correct the answer |
| number of times | {把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn} | read the text three times |
| an adverb before the verb | {把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{检查|jiǎn chá}{了|le}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} | checked the homework carefully |

## Again: {重新|chóng xīn}, {重|chóng}, {再|zài} and {又|yòu}

You know two words for "again": {再|zài} for a repetition still to come ({明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{来|lái}) and {又|yòu} for one that
has happened ({他|tā}{又|yòu}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}). HSK 4 adds a third idea: doing something **again from the start, in a
new way**, because the first attempt was wrong or has to be replaced.

- {重新|chóng xīn} (chóng xīn) + verb: again, anew, starting over: {这|zhè}{篇|piān}{作文|zuò wén}{写|xiě}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{重新|chóng xīn}{写|xiě}。 (This
  essay isn't good: I want to rewrite it. {作文|zuò wén}: an essay, lesson 29.) {我们|wǒ men}{重新|chóng xīn}{开始|kāi shǐ}{吧|ba}。 (Let's start again.)
- {重|chóng} + one-syllable verb: the short form, the same meaning: {重写|chóng xiě} (rewrite), {重做|chóng zuò} (redo),
  {重来|chóng lái} (start over). {这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{写|xiě}{错|cuò}{了|le}，{你|nǐ}{重写|chóng xiě}{一|yí}{个|gè}{吧|ba}。 (You've written this character wrong:
  write it again.) The character is the {重|zhòng} of {重要|zhòng yào}, but here it's read **chóng**: one character,
  two words.
- {再|zài} + verb: one more time, the same again: {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{再|zài}{说|shuō}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 (Please say it again.)

{再|zài} can join {重新|chóng xīn} when the redo is still to come: {你|nǐ}{再|zài}{重新|chóng xīn}{做|zuò}{一下|yí xià}。 (Do it over again.) The
difference between {再|zài} and {重新|chóng xīn} in practice:

| | Repeats… | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {再|zài} | the same thing, once more | {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听|tīng}{清楚|qīng chu}，{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{再|zài}{读|dú}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 I didn't catch that: read it again, please. |
| {重新|chóng xīn} / {重|chóng} | from the beginning, to replace the first try | {答案|dá àn}{错|cuò}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{重新|chóng xīn}{算|suàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{遍|biàn}。 The answer was wrong, so I worked it out again from scratch. ({算|suàn}: to calculate, lesson 15) |
| {又|yòu} | something that has already happened again | {他|tā}{昨天|zuó tiān}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}，{今天|jīn tiān}{又|yòu}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 He was late yesterday, and again today. |

## {允许|yǔn xǔ} and {严格|yán gé}

{允许|yǔn xǔ} (to allow, to permit) takes a person and then what they may do, like {让|ràng} (HSK 2) in a
**[[pivotal sentence]]**: the person is the object of {允许|yǔn xǔ} and the subject of the next verb.

{老师|lǎo shī}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}。 — The teacher doesn't allow us to use our phones in class.

{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{说话|shuō huà}。 — No talking during the exam. (no person: a general rule)

{允许|yǔn xǔ} is a little more formal than {让|ràng} and is the word for rules and permission. To ask, people say
{可以|kě yǐ}…{吗|ma}: {我|wǒ}{可以|kě yǐ}{用|yòng}{词典|cí diǎn}{吗|ma}？ (May I use a dictionary?)

{严格|yán gé} (strict) describes people and rules: {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}{对|duì}{学生|xué sheng}{很|hěn}{严格|yán gé}。 (Teacher Wang is strict with her
students.) It also works as an adverb before a verb: {严格|yán gé}{要求|yāo qiú} (to demand a lot of someone).

## Exam words

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {笔试|bǐ shì} | written exam | {笔试|bǐ shì}{一共|yí gòng}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 The written exam lasts two hours. |
| {口语|kǒu yǔ} | spoken language; oral exam | {他|tā}{的|de}{口语|kǒu yǔ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 His spoken Chinese is very good. |
| {听力|tīng lì} | listening (skill, exam part) | {听力|tīng lì}{部分|bù fen}{有|yǒu}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}{问题|wèn tí}。 The listening section has twenty questions. |
| {试题|shì tí} | exam question | {这|zhè}{次|cì}{的|de}{试题|shì tí}{不|bú}{太|tài}{难|nán}。 The questions this time weren't too hard. |
| {答案|dá àn} | answer (to a question) | {请|qǐng}{把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{写|xiě}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}。 Please write the answers here. |
| {答|dá} | to answer | {这|zhè}{道|dào}{题|tí}{我|wǒ}{答|dá}{对|duì}{了|le}。 I got this question right. |
| {分数|fēn shù} | mark, score | {他|tā}{的|de}{分数|fēn shù}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}。 His mark is very high. |
| {合格|hé gé} | up to standard, passing | {口语|kǒu yǔ}{和|hé}{笔试|bǐ shì}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{合格|hé gé}。 Both the oral and the written exam have to be passed. |
| {考生|kǎo shēng} | exam candidate | {每|měi}{位|wèi}{考生|kǎo shēng}{有|yǒu}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。 Each candidate has ten minutes. |
| {期中|qī zhōng} / {期末|qī mò} | mid-term / end of term | {期中|qī zhōng}{考试|kǎo shì}, {期末|qī mò}{考试|kǎo shì} |
| {时间表|shí jiān biǎo} | timetable, schedule | {考试|kǎo shì}{时间表|shí jiān biǎo} the exam timetable |

- {部分|bù fen} (part, section) is lesson 27's word; {道|dào} is the measure word for exam questions ({一|yí}{道|dào}{题|tí},
  lesson 08's {道|dào}).
- {期|qī} is a period or a term ({学期|xué qī}), and also a numbered issue: {第|dì}{一|yī}{期|qī} (the first issue, the first
  intake). {末|mò} is "end": {周末|zhōu mò} (the weekend), {期末|qī mò} (the end of term), {月|yuè}{末|mò} (the end of the month).
- {合格|hé gé} means "up to the standard", for people and products as well as exams ({合格|hé gé}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}, a
  qualified teacher). For simply passing an exam, people also say {及格|jí gé} (to get a pass mark).
- {答|dá} is the verb; {答案|dá àn} is the answer as a thing written down, often the answer key. {回答|huí dá} (HSK 3) is
  "to answer, a reply" to a question someone asks you.

## More class words

- {预习|yù xí} is preparing a lesson before class (looking ahead); {复习|fù xí} (HSK 3) is going over it afterwards.
  {自习|zì xí} is studying on your own in time set aside for it, at school or university: {星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}{下午|xià wǔ}{是|shì}
  {自习|zì xí} (Friday afternoon is a study period). Chinese schools have {晚自习|wǎn zì xí}, evening study.
- {课堂|kè táng} is the class as a place and an occasion: {课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng} (in class), {课堂|kè táng}{练习|liàn xí} (classwork). {教室|jiào shì} is the
  room.
- {功课|gōng kè} is schoolwork, homework, and also one's lessons in general: {他|tā}{的|de}{功课|gōng kè}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (he does well
  at school).
- {教学|jiào xué} is teaching as an activity or a profession ({教|jiào} is jiào here): {教学|jiào xué}{方法|fāng fǎ} (teaching methods).
- {点名|diǎn míng} is to call the register, to take attendance: {上课|shàng kè}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{老师|lǎo shī}{先|xiān}{点名|diǎn míng}。
- {交|jiāo} is to hand in ({交|jiāo}{作业|zuò yè}, {交|jiāo}{表|biǎo}: hand in a form, lesson 13) and also, as you know, to make friends ({交|jiāo}{朋友|péng you}).
- {改|gǎi} is to change or to correct: {老师|lǎo shī}{在|zài}{改|gǎi}{作业|zuò yè} (marking homework), {改|gǎi}{时间|shí jiān} (change the time),
  {改成|gǎi chéng} (change into).
- {基础|jī chǔ} is the base, the foundation: {他|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{基础|jī chǔ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 (He has a good grounding in Chinese.)
- {重点|zhòng diǎn} is the key point, the focus: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{重点|zhòng diǎn}。 Here {重|zhòng} is zhòng, as in {重要|zhòng yào}.
- {寒假|hán jià} is the winter holiday and {暑假|shǔ jià} the summer holiday: {寒|hán} is cold, {暑|shǔ} is summer heat.
- {打印|dǎ yìn} is to print and {复印|fù yìn} to photocopy; a printer is {一|yì}{台|tái}{打印机|dǎ yìn jī}.

## {台|tái} for machines

{台|tái} counts machines and appliances, especially ones that stand in one place: {一|yì}{台|tái}{打印机|dǎ yìn jī} (a
printer), {一|yì}{台|tái}{电脑|diàn nǎo} (a computer), {一|yì}{台|tái}{空调|kōng tiáo} (an air conditioner), {一|yì}{台|tái}{电视|diàn shì} (a television). {个|gè} is
heard too in speech, but {台|tái} is what you'll read and is never wrong.

The character {台|tái} is also in {台阶|tái jiē} (steps) and words for a platform or stage; in this course's
traditional script it stays {台|tái}.

## {错误|cuò wù} and {正确|zhèng què}

{错误|cuò wù} is "a mistake" (a noun) and "wrong" (an adjective, before a noun or in writing): {这|zhè}{篇|piān}{作文|zuò wén}
{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{错误|cuò wù}。 (This essay has a lot of mistakes.) {错误|cuò wù}{的|de}{答案|dá àn} (a wrong answer). In everyday
speech the adjective is {错|cuò}: {你|nǐ}{写|xiě}{错|cuò}{了|le}。

{正确|zhèng què} is "correct", the formal partner of {对|duì}: {正确|zhèng què}{的|de}{答案|dá àn} (the correct answer), {回答|huí dá}{正确|zhèng què} (answered
correctly). {你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{对|duì} (you're right) stays with {对|duì}: {正确|zhèng què} describes answers, methods and ideas, not
a person being right in a conversation.

### Stroke order

- **{印|yìn}**: the left part first, in three strokes (a short left-falling stroke, a vertical with a rising
  tail, a horizontal), then 卩: a horizontal that turns down into a hook, and the vertical last.
- **{严|yán}**: the long top horizontal, two short verticals, then a dot and a short left-falling
  stroke (not two dots), the horizontal, and the long left-falling stroke last.
- **{改|gǎi}**: {己|jǐ} in three strokes (a horizontal turning down, a horizontal, a vertical that bends and
  rises), then 攵 in four.
- **{允|yǔn}**: 厶 (a stroke that goes down and turns right, then a dot), then {儿|ér}: a left-falling stroke and
  a vertical bend hook.
- **{寒|hán}**: 宀, then two horizontals, two verticals and a third horizontal, the long left-falling and
  right-falling strokes, and the two dots at the bottom last.
- **{预|yù}**: {予|yǔ} first (a horizontal that turns down-left, a dot, a horizontal hook, a vertical hook),
  then {页|yè}.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{把|bǎ}{手机|shǒu jī}{关|guān}{了|le}。 — Please switch off your phones, everyone.
- {你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{名字|míng zi}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià}。 — Write your name, please.
- {考试|kǎo shì}{以前|yǐ qián}，{把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{再|zài}{读|dú}{两|liǎng}{遍|biàn}。 — Before the exam, read the texts through twice more.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Exams and homework
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{把|bǎ}{考试|kǎo shì}{时间表|shí jiān biǎo}{打印|dǎ yìn}{一下|yí xià}。
= I'd like to print out the exam timetable.
{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}{了|le}。
= I've read the text three times already.
{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{写|xiě}{错|cuò}{了|le}，{你|nǐ}{重写|chóng xiě}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
= You've written this character wrong: write it again.
{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{改|gǎi}{一下|yí xià}。
= Could you correct the answer?
{老师|lǎo shī}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}。
= The teacher doesn't allow us to use phones in class.
{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{仔细|zǐ xì}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。
= Be careful in the exam.
```

## Pronunciation

- The character 重 has two readings. {重新|chóng xīn}, {重写|chóng xiě}, {重做|chóng zuò}, {重来|chóng lái}: **chóng** (again). {重要|zhòng yào}, {重点|zhòng diǎn}: **zhòng** (heavy,
  important). The meaning decides.
- {答案|dá àn} dá àn: the *a* of {案|àn} starts a new syllable, so pinyin writes an apostrophe: dá'àn.
- {仔细|zǐ xì} zǐ xì: *z* then *x*; don't let them run together. {仔|zǐ} here is zǐ, third tone.
- {允许|yǔn xǔ} yǔn xǔ: two third tones, so in speech the first rises: yún xǔ. The pinyin keeps yǔn.
- {寒假|hán jià} and {暑假|shǔ jià}: {假|jià} is jià (holiday) here, as in {放假|fàng jià} and {请假|qǐng jià}. (It's jiǎ, "false", in lesson 09.)
- {口语|kǒu yǔ} kǒu yǔ is also 3+3: said kóu yǔ.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{做|zuò}~~: the verb in a {把|bǎ} sentence needs something after it: {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{做|zuò}{完|wán}{了|le} / {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}
  {作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{没|méi}{交|jiāo}~~: the negative goes before {把|bǎ}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{上去|shàng qù}.
- ~~{老师|lǎo shī}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{我们|wǒ men}~~: the person comes straight after {允许|yǔn xǔ}: {老师|lǎo shī}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{我们|wǒ men}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}.
- ~~{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{写|xiě}{错|cuò}{了|le}，{你|nǐ}{又|yòu}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià}~~: a redo still to come is {再|zài} or {重新|chóng xīn}, not {又|yòu}: {你|nǐ}{再|zài}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià} / {你|nǐ}
  {重新|chóng xīn}{写|xiě}{一下|yí xià}.
- {重新|chóng xīn} for a plain repeat sounds odd: {那个|nà ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}，{我|wǒ}{又|yòu}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} (I watched it again) is
  natural; {我|wǒ}{重新|chóng xīn}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} suggests the first viewing didn't count (you fell asleep).
- {一|yí}{个|gè}{打印机|dǎ yìn jī} is heard in speech, but {一|yì}{台|tái}{打印机|dǎ yìn jī} is the measure word to write.

## Key points

- {把|bǎ} + object + verb + {了|le} / {一下|yí xià} / a number of times: {把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}, {把|bǎ}{答案|dá àn}{改|gǎi}{一下|yí xià}, {把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}
  {三|sān}{遍|biàn}. Negatives and modal verbs go before {把|bǎ}; a {地|de} adverb can go before {把|bǎ} or before the verb.
- {重新|chóng xīn} / {重|chóng} + verb: again from the start ({重新|chóng xīn}{写|xiě}, {重写|chóng xiě}); {再|zài}: once more (to come); {又|yòu}: again (it
  happened).
- {允许|yǔn xǔ} + person + verb: to allow someone to do something. {严格|yán gé}: strict ({对|duì}{学生|xué sheng}{很|hěn}{严格|yán gé}).
- Exam words: {笔试|bǐ shì}, {口语|kǒu yǔ}, {听力|tīng lì}, {试题|shì tí}, {答案|dá àn}, {分数|fēn shù}, {合格|hé gé}, {考生|kǎo shēng}, {期中|qī zhōng}, {期末|qī mò}, {时间表|shí jiān biǎo}.
- {预习|yù xí} before class, {复习|fù xí} after it, {自习|zì xí} on your own; {错误|cuò wù} (a mistake, wrong) and {正确|zhèng què} (correct).
- {台|tái} counts machines: {一|yì}{台|tái}{打印机|dǎ yìn jī}, {一|yì}{台|tái}{电脑|diàn nǎo}.
- New characters (simplified): {={案|àn}、{印|yìn}、{功|gōng}、{寒|hán}、{改|gǎi}、{格|gé}、{误|wù}、{基|jī}、{础|chǔ}、{暑|shǔ}、{严|yán}、{台|tái}、{预|yù}、{允|yǔn}、{许|xǔ}、{确|què}、{仔|zǐ}、{细|xì}=}; seven differ in traditional.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Books, articles and words: even, so much as
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) is writing her graduation thesis and spends her days in the library looking up
material; {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming), an English major, has a translation to finish. This lesson is about
reading and writing: books and articles, writers and readers, words and grammar. Its grammar is the
Chinese way of saying "even":

- {连|lián}…{都|dōu} / {也|yě}: even ({连|lián}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}; {连|lián}{一|yí}{个|gè}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{写|xiě});
- {甚至|shèn zhì}: even, so much as, going one step further;
- {连|lián}…{都|dōu}…，{更|gèng}…: if even A…, then B all the more;
- the measure words {篇|piān} (articles, essays) and {首|shǒu} (songs, poems);
- {例如|lì rú}, {举例|jǔ lì} and {例子|lì zi} for examples, {叫作|jiào zuò} (to be called) and {其中|qí zhōng} (among them);
- reading words: {文章|wén zhāng}, {小说|xiǎo shuō}, {杂志|zá zhì}, {日记|rì jì}, {作者|zuò zhě}, {读者|dú zhě}, {作家|zuò jiā}, {作品|zuò pǐn}, {内容|nèi róng}, {资料|zī liào}, {知识|zhī shi}, {阅读|yuè dú}; and language
  words: {普通话|pǔ tōng huà}, {语法|yǔ fǎ}, {词语|cí yǔ}, {文字|wén zì}, {翻译|fān yì}, {自学|zì xué}.

All three "even" patterns make a **[[progressive complex sentence]]**: a sentence that goes one step
further than you'd expect.

## {连|lián}…{都|dōu} / {也|yě}: even

{连|lián} picks out the most unlikely member of a set, and {都|dōu} or {也|yě} says that even it is included. The
pattern is

(subject) + {连|lián} + the extreme thing + {都|dōu} / {也|yě} + verb

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{很|hěn}{简单|jiǎn dān}，{连|lián}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}。 — This question is easy: even a child knows it.

{他|tā}{太|tài}{忙|máng}{了|le}，{连|lián}{周末|zhōu mò}{也|yě}{要|yào}{工作|gōng zuò}。 — He's so busy he has to work even at weekends.

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{我|wǒ}{连|lián}{一|yí}{页|yè}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{看|kàn}。 — I haven't read a single page of this book.

What {连|lián} picks out can be:

- **the subject**: {连|lián}{老师|lǎo shī}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}。 (Even the teacher doesn't know this character.)
- **the object**, moved before the verb: {他|tā}{连|lián}{饭|fàn}{都|dōu}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{吃|chī}。 (He even forgot to eat.) The object
  must come before {都|dōu}; ~~{他|tā}{都|dōu}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{吃|chī}{连|lián}{饭|fàn}~~ is wrong.
- **{一|yī} + measure word + noun, with a negative**: "not a single…": {我|wǒ}{连|lián}{一|yì}{分|fēn}{钱|qián}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}。 (I
  haven't got a penny.) {他|tā}{连|lián}{一|yí}{个|gè}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{写|xiě}。 (He didn't write a single character.)
- **a verb, repeated after a negative**: {他|tā}{连|lián}{看|kàn}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{看|kàn}{就|jiù}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 (He left without so much as a
  look.) The verb comes once after {连|lián} and again after {都|dōu}{没|méi}.

{都|dōu} and {也|yě} are interchangeable here; {都|dōu} is a little more common in positive sentences, {也|yě} with
negatives. You can leave out {连|lián} in speech ({小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}, {一|yí}{页|yè}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{看|kàn}), but never {都|dōu} / {也|yě}.

## {甚至|shèn zhì}: even, so much as

{甚至|shèn zhì} points to the most extreme item at the end of a list or a description. It goes before that item:

{他|tā}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{努力|nǔ lì}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{学|xué}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{甚至|shèn zhì}{四|sì}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 — He studies Chinese very hard:
three hours a day, even four.

{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{五|wǔ}{月|yuè}{甚至|shèn zhì}{还|hái}{会|huì}{下|xià}{雪|xuě}。 — It's very cold here: it can even snow in May.

{甚至|shèn zhì} and {连|lián} often come together, {甚至|shèn zhì} first: {他|tā}{忙|máng}{得|de}{甚至|shèn zhì}{连|lián}{饭|fàn}{都|dōu}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{吃|chī}。 (He was so busy he even
forgot to eat.) The difference:

- {连|lián} needs {都|dōu} / {也|yě} after it and picks out one thing in its own clause.
- {甚至|shèn zhì} can stand alone as an adverb ({甚至|shèn zhì}{还|hái}{会|huì}{下|xià}{雪|xuě}) or start a clause like a conjunction (…，{甚至|shèn zhì}…),
  adding a further, surprising step to what came before.

## {连|lián}…{都|dōu}…，{更|gèng}…: if even A, then all the more B

The progression can go on to a second clause: if it's true even of the unlikely case, it's
certainly true of the ordinary one. The second clause takes {更|gèng} (all the more), often with {就|jiù} or
{了|le}:

{连|lián}{老师|lǎo shī}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{更|gèng}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{了|le}。 — Even the teacher doesn't know, so we certainly
don't.

{这|zhè}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}{连|lián}{中国|Zhōng guó}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{觉得|jué de}{难|nán}，{外国|wài guó}{人|rén}{就|jiù}{更|gèng}{看|kàn}{不|bu}{懂|dǒng}{了|le}。 — Even Chinese readers find
this article hard, so foreigners certainly can't follow it.

{连|lián}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{都|dōu}{会|huì}，{你|nǐ}{更|gèng}{应该|yīng gāi}{会|huì}。 — Even children can do it, so you certainly should.

{更加|gèng jiā} is a slightly more formal {更|gèng} before two-syllable words: {更加|gèng jiā}{努力|nǔ lì} (work even harder), {更加|gèng jiā}
{丰富|fēng fù} (even richer).

## {篇|piān} and {首|shǒu}: measure words for writing and songs

| Measure word | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {篇|piān} | a piece of writing: an article, an essay, a short story, a diary entry | {一|yì}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}, {两|liǎng}{篇|piān}{作文|zuò wén} ({作文|zuò wén}: an essay), {这|zhè}{篇|piān}{日记|rì jì} |
| {首|shǒu} | a song or a poem | {一|yì}{首|shǒu}{歌|gē}, {一|yì}{首|shǒu}{诗|shī} ({诗|shī}: a poem) |
| {本|běn} (HSK 1) | a bound book, a magazine | {一|yì}{本|běn}{小说|xiǎo shuō}, {一|yì}{本|běn}{杂志|zá zhì} |

A long novel as a book is {一|yì}{本|běn}{小说|xiǎo shuō}; {篇|piān} is for a story or text you read as a piece ({一|yì}{篇|piān}{短篇|duǎn piān}{小说|xiǎo shuō}, a
short story). {首|shǒu} is also "head, first" in {首都|shǒu dū} (capital city, lesson 18).

## Examples: {例如|lì rú}, {举例|jǔ lì}, {例子|lì zi}

- {例子|lì zi} is an example (the noun): {这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{好|hǎo}{例子|lì zi}。 (This is a good example.)
- {举例|jǔ lì} is "to give an example"; in speech people usually say it in full, {举|jǔ} + {个|gè} + {例子|lì zi}: {我|wǒ}{举|jǔ}{个|gè}{例子|lì zi}。 (Let me give an example.) {举|jǔ} is
  "to raise, to hold up".
- {例如|lì rú} introduces examples in a list, mostly in writing: {他|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{运动|yùn dòng}，{例如|lì rú}{游泳|yóu yǒng}、{跑步|pǎo bù}{和|hé}
  {打|dǎ}{篮球|lán qiú}。 (He likes many sports, for example swimming, running and basketball.) In speech {比如|bǐ rú}
  (HSK 3) is more common; the two mean the same.

## {叫作|jiào zuò} and {其中|qí zhōng}

{叫作|jiào zuò} is "to be called, to be known as": it names a thing or explains a term, and is a little more
formal than {叫|jiào}. {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{花|huā}{叫作|jiào zuò}{牡丹|mǔ dān}。 (This flower is called the peony.) {西红柿|xī hóng shì}{也|yě}{叫作|jiào zuò}{番茄|fān qié}。
(The tomato is also called {番茄|fān qié}; {西红柿|xī hóng shì}: a tomato, lesson 08.)

{其中|qí zhōng} means "among them, of which", pointing back to a group just mentioned:

{我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}{有|yǒu}{二十|èr shí}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}，{其中|qí zhōng}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}{是|shì}{留学生|liú xué shēng}。 — There are twenty students in our class, five of
them international students.

{他|tā}{写|xiě}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{小说|xiǎo shuō}，{其中|qí zhōng}{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{这|zhè}{一|yì}{本|běn}。 — He has written many novels; of them, I like
this one best.

## Words for reading and writing

- {文章|wén zhāng} (an article, an essay), {小说|xiǎo shuō} (a novel, fiction), {杂志|zá zhì} (a magazine), {日记|rì jì} (a diary: {写|xiě}{日记|rì jì}).
- {作者|zuò zhě} is the author of a particular work: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{的|de}{作者|zuò zhě}。{作家|zuò jiā} is a writer by profession: {她|tā}{是|shì}
  {一|yí}{位|wèi}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{作家|zuò jiā}。{作品|zuò pǐn} is a work (of literature or art): {他|tā}{的|de}{作品|zuò pǐn} (his works).
- {读者|dú zhě} is a reader of a book or a magazine; the {者|zhě} means "a person who…", as in {作者|zuò zhě}.
- {阅读|yuè dú} is to read, the formal word ({阅读|yuè dú}{能力|néng lì}, reading ability); {看|kàn}{书|shū} and {读|dú}{书|shū} are the everyday ones.
- {内容|nèi róng} is the content: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{的|de}{内容|nèi róng}{很|hěn}{丰富|fēng fù}。 (This book is rich in content.)
- {资料|zī liào} is material, information, documents for study or research: {查找|chá zhǎo}{资料|zī liào} (to look up material).
- {知识|zhī shi} is knowledge: {学|xué}{到|dào}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{知识|zhī shi}。
- {丰富|fēng fù} is rich, plentiful ({丰富|fēng fù}{的|de}{经验|jīng yàn}, rich experience; {内容|nèi róng}{丰富|fēng fù}) and also "to enrich".
- {提到|tí dào} is to mention: {他|tā}{在|zài}{信|xìn}{里|lǐ}{提到|tí dào}{了|le}{你|nǐ}。 (He mentioned you in his letter.)
- {回信|huí xìn} is to write back and also the reply letter itself: {我|wǒ}{还|hái}{没|méi}{给|gěi}{他|tā}{回信|huí xìn}。
- {顺序|shùn xù} is order, sequence ({按|àn}{顺序|shùn xù}, in order); {列|liè} is to list, and also a row or a column.
- {图|tú} is a picture, a chart, a diagram: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{图|tú}。
- {查找|chá zhǎo} is to search for, to look up (more formal than {找|zhǎo} and {查|chá}).

## Words for language

- {普通话|pǔ tōng huà} (Pǔtōnghuà, "the common speech") is standard Mandarin, the language this course teaches.
- {语法|yǔ fǎ} is grammar; {词语|cí yǔ} is words and expressions; {文字|wén zì} is writing, a script: {汉字|hàn zì}{是|shì}{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{文字|wén zì}。
- {翻译|fān yì} is to translate and also a translator: {把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}{翻译|fān yì}{成|chéng}{英文|Yīng wén} (translate this article into
  English); {她|tā}{是|shì}{一|yì}{名|míng}{翻译|fān yì} (she's a translator).
- {自学|zì xué} is to teach yourself: {他|tā}{是|shì}{自学|zì xué}{的|de}{英语|Yīng yǔ}。 (He taught himself English.)

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 翻 | to turn over; translate | fān | 羽 | 18 | {翻译|fān yì} |
| 译 (traditional 譯) | to translate | yì | 讠 | 7 | {翻译|fān yì} |
| 丰 (traditional 豐) | abundant | fēng | 丨 | 4 | {丰富|fēng fù} |
| 富 | rich | fù | 宀 | 12 | {丰富|fēng fù} |
| 例 ✎ | example | lì | 亻 | 8 | {例子|lì zi}, {例如|lì rú}, {举例|jǔ lì} |
| 举 ✎ (traditional 舉) | to raise, hold up | jǔ | 丶 | 9 | {举例|jǔ lì} |
| 列 | to list; a row | liè | 刂 | 6 | {列|liè} |
| 连 ✎ (traditional 連) | to link; even | lián | 辶 | 7 | {连|lián} |

- **Sound parts.** {例|lì} lì is 亻 + {列|liè} liè: a close sound. {翻|fān} fān has {番|fān} fān on the left (the same
  sound) and {羽|yǔ} (feathers) on the right: a memory aid, wings turning over. {篇|piān} piān is ⺮ (bamboo:
  early books were written on strips of bamboo) + {扁|biǎn} biǎn, a close sound. {通|tōng} tōng is 辶 + {甬|yǒng}; the same
  {甬|yǒng} is in {痛|tòng} tòng (pain, lesson 06) and {桶|tǒng} tǒng (a bucket, lesson 28). {富|fù} fù is 宀 over {畐|fú}, the part
  that gives {福|fú} fú ({幸福|xìng fú}, lesson 23) its sound. {序|xù} xù is {广|guǎng} over {予|yǔ}, the {予|yǔ} of {预|yù} yù (lesson 02):
  the sound has drifted.

  lesson 02. 讠 (speech): {译|yì}, after {误|wù} and {许|xǔ}.
- **Look-alikes.** {杂|zá} zá is {九|jiǔ} over {木|mù}; {条|tiáo} tiáo (HSK 2) is 夂 over {木|mù}. {志|zhì} zhì is {士|shì} over {心|xīn}; {忘|wàng} wàng
  ({忘记|wàng jì}) is {亡|wáng} over {心|xīn}. {内|nèi} nèi has {人|rén} inside 冂; {肉|ròu} ròu (meat) has two {人|rén}. {首|shǒu} shǒu is the right part of
  {道|dào} dào ({知道|zhī dào}): 辶 + {首|shǒu}. {至|zhì} zhì is the left part of {到|dào} dào (to arrive); both mean reaching a point.
  {丰|fēng} fēng has its vertical through all three horizontals and out at both ends; in {王|wáng} it stops at the
  top and bottom lines. {列|liè} liè and {例|lì} lì: {例|lì} adds 亻.
- **{译|yì} and {择|zé}.** The right side of {译|yì} is the right side of {择|zé} zé ({选择|xuǎn zé}, HSK 3): one simplified
  shape that stands for traditional {睪|yì} in both ({譯|yì}, {擇|zé}).

### Stroke order

- **{丰|fēng}**: the three horizontals first, then the long vertical through them, last.
- **{内|nèi}**: the left vertical, the horizontal-turn-hook, then {人|rén} inside (left-falling stroke, then
  the dot). Four strokes.
- **{至|zhì}**: the top horizontal, a stroke that goes down and turns right, a dot (厶), then {土|tǔ}: a
  horizontal, the vertical and the long bottom horizontal.
- **{连|lián}**, **{通|tōng}**: 辶 is written last: first {车|chē} (or {甬|yǒng}), then the dot, the turning stroke and the long
  flat sweep.
- **{甚|shèn}**: {甘|gān}'s horizontal and two verticals, two more horizontals inside, the long horizontal, then a
  left-falling stroke and a dot, and the last stroke, which goes down and turns right along the
  bottom.
- **{杂|zá}**: {九|jiǔ} (a left-falling stroke, then the horizontal that bends and hooks), then {木|mù} below: a
  horizontal, a vertical hook, a left-falling stroke and a dot.

"**How I came to love reading.** As a child I didn't like books at all. There wasn't a single
storybook at home, and my parents were busy at work every day and had no time to tell me stories.
The year I was ten, the old lady next door gave me a novel. 'This was my favourite book when I was
little,' she said. I only meant to leaf through a few pages, but once I started I couldn't stop.
That night I even forgot to eat, and read under the quilt till midnight. From then on I went to the
library by myself to borrow books. Novels, magazines, history books: I read everything. The books
were full of things, and I learned a great deal I could never have learned in class. I also started
keeping a diary, writing down everything I'd read and thought each day. Later I became a writer.
Now many readers write to me and ask how they can learn to write well. I usually write back and
tell them: if even someone like me, who didn't like books as a child, could come to love reading,
you certainly can. Read a lot first, then write a lot."

## Pronunciation

- {连|lián} lián and {脸|liǎn} liǎn (face) differ only in tone; {连|lián} is second tone.
- {篇|piān} piān has an aspirated *p*, with a puff of air; {遍|biàn} biàn (once through) has an unaspirated *b*.
  {一|yì}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng} yì piān, {读|dú}{一|yí}{遍|biàn} dú yí biàn.
- {甚至|shèn zhì} shèn zhì: *-en* then *zh-*; both fourth tones. Don't say shén (as in {什么|shén me}).
- {普通话|pǔ tōng huà} pǔ tōng huà: a dipping tone, then a high level one and a falling one.
- {知识|zhī shi} zhī shi: the second syllable is light. {作者|zuò zhě} zuò zhě and {读者|dú zhě} dú zhě keep a full third tone on
  {者|zhě}.
- {翻译|fān yì} fān yì: the *f* is like English *f*; {译|yì} is yì, like {一|yī} in its fourth-tone form.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{都|dōu}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{吃|chī}{连|lián}{饭|fàn}~~: the thing {连|lián} picks out comes before {都|dōu} and the verb: {他|tā}{连|lián}{饭|fàn}{都|dōu}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{吃|chī}.
- ~~{连|lián}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{知道|zhī dào}~~: {连|lián} needs {都|dōu} or {也|yě}: {连|lián}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{连|lián}{一|yí}{个|gè}{字|zì}{没|méi}{写|xiě}~~: here too, keep {都|dōu} / {也|yě}: {我|wǒ}{连|lián}{一|yí}{个|gè}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{写|xiě}.
- {一|yí}{个|gè}{文章|wén zhāng} is heard, but the measure word to write is {篇|piān}: {一|yì}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}. A song or a poem is {一|yì}{首|shǒu}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{读者|dú zhě}{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}~~: {读者|dú zhě} is "a reader" (a person); "to read" is {读|dú}, {看|kàn} or, formally, {阅读|yuè dú}.
- {例如|lì rú} at the start of a chat sounds formal: in speech {比如|bǐ rú} or {我|wǒ}{举|jǔ}{个|gè}{例子|lì zi}.

## Key points

- {连|lián} + the extreme case + {都|dōu} / {也|yě} + verb: even ({连|lián}{小孩儿|xiǎo háir}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}). With {一|yī} + M + noun and a negative:
  not a single ({连|lián}{一|yí}{页|yè}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{写|xiě}). With a repeated verb: {连|lián}{看|kàn}{都|dōu}{没|méi}{看|kàn}.
- {甚至|shèn zhì}: even, a further surprising step ({甚至|shèn zhì}{四|sì}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}; {甚至|shèn zhì}{连|lián}{饭|fàn}{都|dōu}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{吃|chī}).
- {连|lián} A {都|dōu}…，B {更|gèng}…: if even A, then B all the more. {更加|gèng jiā} is a formal {更|gèng}.
- {篇|piān} for articles and essays, {首|shǒu} for songs and poems, {本|běn} for books.
- {例子|lì zi} (an example), {举|jǔ}{个|gè}{例子|lì zi} (give an example), {例如|lì rú} (for example, in writing; {比如|bǐ rú} in speech).
- {作者|zuò zhě} (the author of a work), {作家|zuò jiā} (a writer by profession), {作品|zuò pǐn} (a work), {读者|dú zhě} (a reader).
- New characters (simplified): {={翻|fān}、{译|yì}、{丰|fēng}、{富|fù}、{例|lì}、{举|jǔ}、{列|liè}、{连|lián}、{内|nèi}、{篇|piān}、{普|pǔ}、{通|tōng}、{顺|shùn}、{序|xù}、{首|shǒu}、{甚|shèn}、{至|zhì}、{章|zhāng}、{杂|zá}、{志|zhì}=}; eight differ in
  traditional, and {志|zhì} becomes {誌|zhì} in {杂志|zá zhì}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Clubs, contests and prizes: not only… but also
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The university is holding a Chinese speech contest for its international students, and {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}
(Teacher Wang) wants her class to take part. {安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) is nervous; {大卫|Dà wèi} (David) has been asked to
lead a team. This lesson gives you the words of events, contests and prizes, and more ways to add
one point to another, the next step after lesson 03's {连|lián} and {甚至|shèn zhì}:

- {不仅|bù jǐn} and {不光|bù guāng}…{还|hái} / {而且|ér qiě} / {也|yě}: not only… but also;
- {并且|bìng qiě} (and also, moreover), {另外|lìng wài} and {此外|cǐ wài} (in addition), and {加上|jiā shàng} (on top of that);
- {举办|jǔ bàn} and {举行|jǔ xíng}: two verbs for holding an event;
- winning and losing: {赢|yíng}, {赢得|yíng dé}, {输|shū}, {打败|dǎ bài}, {获得|huò dé}, {获奖|huò jiǎng}, {奖|jiǎng}, {奖金|jiǎng jīn};
- {鼓励|gǔ lì} (to encourage), {表扬|biǎo yáng} (to praise), {庆祝|qìng zhù} (to celebrate), {邀请|yāo qǐng} (to invite);
- the measure words {场|chǎng} ({一|yì}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài}) and {项|xiàng} ({一|yí}{项|xiàng}{活动|huó dòng}).

## {不仅|bù jǐn} / {不光|bù guāng}…{还|hái} / {而且|ér qiě} / {也|yě}: not only… but also

You know {不但|bú dàn}…{而且|ér qiě} (HSK 3 lesson 26). {不仅|bù jǐn} and {不光|bù guāng} work the same way and mean the same: the second
clause adds a further point, usually a stronger one. {不仅|bù jǐn} suits both speech and writing; {不光|bù guāng}
(guāng: only) is everyday speech. The second clause takes {还|hái}, {而且|ér qiě} or {也|yě}, or two of them together
({而且|ér qiě}{还|hái}…):

{她|tā}{不仅|bù jǐn}{会|huì}{唱歌|chàng gē}，{还|hái}{会|huì}{跳舞|tiào wǔ}。 — She can not only sing but dance too.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{比赛|bǐ sài}{不光|bù guāng}{有|yǒu}{中国|Zhōng guó}{学生|xué sheng}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{留学生|liú xué shēng}。 — There aren't only Chinese students in this
contest: there are lots of international students too.

{他|tā}{不仅|bù jǐn}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{比赛|bǐ sài}，{而且|ér qiě}{还|hái}{获得|huò dé}{了|le}{第一名|dì yī míng}。 — He didn't just take part in the contest: he won
first place.

The subject follows the same rule as with {不但|bú dàn}:

| | Where the subject goes | Example |
|---|---|---|
| One subject for both clauses | first, before {不仅|bù jǐn} | {安娜|Ān nà}{不仅|bù jǐn}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{好|hǎo}，{还|hái}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{汉字|hàn zì}。 |
| Two different subjects | after {不仅|bù jǐn}, and the second clause often has {也|yě} | {不仅|bù jǐn}{学生|xué sheng}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{这个|zhè ge}{活动|huó dòng}，{老师|lǎo shī}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。 |

{不仅如此|bù jǐn rú cǐ} is a fixed phrase, "not only that", that starts the next sentence in writing: {不仅如此|bù jǐn rú cǐ}，
{学院|xué yuàn}{还|hái}{为|wèi}{获奖|huò jiǎng}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{了|le}{奖金|jiǎng jīn}。 (What's more, the college has prize money for the winners.)

## {并且|bìng qiě}: and also, moreover

{并且|bìng qiě} joins two verbs or two clauses that belong together, usually with the same subject, the
second adding to the first. It's a little formal, and common in writing and careful speech:

{他|tā}{报|bào}{了|le}{名|míng}，{并且|bìng qiě}{交|jiāo}{了|le}{钱|qián}。 — He signed up and also paid.

{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{认真|rèn zhēn}{准备|zhǔn bèi}，{并且|bìng qiě}{按时|àn shí}{参加|cān jiā}。 — Please prepare carefully, and be there on time. ({按时|àn shí}: on
time, lesson 07)

{并且|bìng qiě} can also be the second half of {不仅|bù jǐn}: {他|tā}{不仅|bù jǐn}{来|lái}{了|le}，{并且|bìng qiě}{带|dài}{来|lái}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{朋友|péng you}。 In speech, {而且|ér qiě}
or {还|hái} are more usual. {并且|bìng qiě} doesn't join two nouns: "teachers and students" is {老师|lǎo shī}{和|hé}{学生|xué sheng}, never
~~{老师|lǎo shī}{并且|bìng qiě}{学生|xué sheng}~~.

## {另外|lìng wài}, {此外|cǐ wài} and {加上|jiā shàng}: adding one more thing

- {另外|lìng wài} (lìng wài), "in addition, besides", starts a new point in speech and writing: {这|zhè}{门|mén}{课|kè}{有|yǒu}
  {笔试|bǐ shì}，{另外|lìng wài}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{口语|kǒu yǔ}{考试|kǎo shì}。 (The course has a written exam, and an oral too.) {此外|cǐ wài} (lesson 01)
  is the written partner.
- {另外|lìng wài} is also "another, other" before a number or a noun: {另外|lìng wài}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{队员|duì yuán} (the other two team
  members), {另外|lìng wài}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{事|shì} (another matter). {另|lìng} alone does the same in {另|lìng}{一|yí}{个|gè} (lesson 14).
- {加上|jiā shàng} (on top of that, plus) adds a further reason or circumstance, often with a result after it.
  {再|zài}{加上|jiā shàng} is common in speech:

{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{加上|jiā shàng}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{来|lái}{的|de}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}。 — It was cold, and with the rain on top, few people came.

{他|tā}{本来|běn lái}{就|jiù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}，{再|zài}{加上|jiā shàng}{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{鼓励|gǔ lì}，{就|jiù}{报名|bào míng}{参加|cān jiā}{了|le}{比赛|bǐ sài}。 — He liked Chinese anyway, and
with his teacher's encouragement on top, he signed up for the contest.

## Events: {活动|huó dòng}, {举办|jǔ bàn} and {举行|jǔ xíng}

{活动|huó dòng} is an activity or an event: {学校|xué xiào}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{活动|huó dòng} (the university has a lot going on), {参加|cān jiā}{活动|huó dòng} (take
part in an activity). The measure word is {项|xiàng} (an item, a part of a programme) or {个|gè} in speech: {一|yí}{项|xiàng}
{活动|huó dòng}.

{举办|jǔ bàn} and {举行|jǔ xíng} both mean "to hold" an event, from different angles:

| | Says | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {举办|jǔ bàn} | who organises, hosts or runs the event | {学校|xué xiào}{每|měi}{年|nián}{都|dōu}{举办|jǔ bàn}{一|yí}{次|cì}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{大赛|dà sài}。 The university holds a Chinese contest every year. |
| {举行|jǔ xíng} | that the event takes place (often where or when) | {比赛|bǐ sài}{在|zài}{大|dà}{礼堂|lǐ táng}{举行|jǔ xíng}。 The contest takes place in the main hall. |

So {举办|jǔ bàn} usually has the organiser as its subject, and {举行|jǔ xíng} often has the event as its subject or
comes with a time or place. Both can take the event as their object ({举办|jǔ bàn} / {举行|jǔ xíng}{了|le}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài}). {举行|jǔ xíng}
is the verb for ceremonies and meetings ({举行|jǔ xíng}{毕业|bì yè}{典礼|diǎn lǐ}, to hold a graduation ceremony). {举|jǔ} on its own
is "to raise, to hold up": {举手|jǔ shǒu} (raise your hand).

The rest of a contest:

- {报名|bào míng} is to sign up, to register: {报名|bào míng}{参加|cān jiā}{比赛|bǐ sài} (sign up for the contest), {报|bào}{了|le}{名|míng} (signed up).
- {参赛|cān sài} is to take part in a contest (written): {参赛|cān sài}{的|de}{人|rén} (the contestants), {参赛|cān sài}{人数|rén shù} (the number of
  contestants). {人数|rén shù} is the number of people.
- {大赛|dà sài} is a big competition, a contest; {比赛|bǐ sài} (HSK 2) is any match or contest.
- {组|zǔ} and {小组|xiǎo zǔ} are a group: {我们|wǒ men}{分|fēn}{成|chéng}{三|sān}{个|gè}{组|zǔ} (we split into three groups), {小组|xiǎo zǔ}{比赛|bǐ sài} (a group
  event). {组|zǔ} is also the verb "to form": {组|zǔ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{队|duì} (form a team).
- {队|duì} is a team ({球队|qiú duì}, a ball team, lesson 07) and also a queue ({排队|pái duì}, lesson 09). {队员|duì yuán} is a team member;
  {队长|duì zhǎng} is the team captain.
- {排|pái} is a row ({第|dì}{一|yī}{排|pái}, the front row) and the verb "to line up, to arrange".
- {进入|jìn rù} is to enter (a place or the next stage): {进入|jìn rù}{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài} (get into the final). {入|rù} is the
  written "enter" of lesson 01.

## Winning and losing

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {赢|yíng} | to win (a game; beat a team) | {我们|wǒ men}{赢|yíng}{了|le}！ We won! {我们|wǒ men}{赢|yíng}{了|le}{三|sān}{班|bān}。 We beat Class 3. |
| {赢得|yíng dé} | to win (praise, support, a prize) | {她|tā}{的|de}{演讲|yǎn jiǎng}{赢得|yíng dé}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{掌声|zhǎng shēng}。 Her speech won everyone's applause. |
| {输|shū} | to lose (a game) | {我们|wǒ men}{输|shū}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{分|fēn}。 We lost by two points. {输|shū}{给|gěi}{三|sān}{班|bān} lost to Class 3 |
| {打败|dǎ bài} | to defeat (someone) | {我们|wǒ men}{打败|dǎ bài}{了|le}{三|sān}{班|bān}。 We defeated Class 3. |
| {获得|huò dé} | to obtain, to win (formal) | {他|tā}{获得|huò dé}{了|le}{第一名|dì yī míng}。 He won first place. |
| {获奖|huò jiǎng} | to win a prize | {获奖|huò jiǎng}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué} the prizewinners |
| {奖|jiǎng} | a prize, an award | {一等奖|yī děng jiǎng} (first prize), {得|dé}{奖|jiǎng} (to win a prize) |
| {奖金|jiǎng jīn} | prize money; a bonus | {第一名|dì yī míng}{有|yǒu}{一千|yì qiān}{块|kuài}{奖金|jiǎng jīn}。 First place gets a thousand yuan. |

- {赢|yíng} takes the game ({赢|yíng}{了|le}{比赛|bǐ sài}) or, in speech, the opponent ({赢|yíng}{了|le}{三|sān}{班|bān}). {赢得|yíng dé} takes something you
  earn: {赢得|yíng dé}{支持|zhī chí} (win support), {赢得|yíng dé}{比赛|bǐ sài} (win the match, written).
- {输|shū} is "to lose" a game or a bet, never "to lose" a thing: losing your phone is {丢|diū} (HSK 3).
- {打败|dǎ bài} has the opponent as its object; with {被|bèi} it's "to be beaten": {我们|wǒ men}{被|bèi}{三|sān}{班|bān}{打败|dǎ bài}{了|le}。
- {获得|huò dé} is formal and goes with prizes, places, results and chances: {获得|huò dé}{奖学金|jiǎng xué jīn} (win a scholarship,
  lesson 05), {获得|huò dé}{机会|jī huì} (get a chance). In speech {得|dé} or {得到|dé dào}.
- {一等奖|yī děng jiǎng}, {二等奖|èr děng jiǎng}, {三等奖|sān děng jiǎng} are first, second and third prizes; {一|yī} here is yī (first).

## Encouraging, praising, celebrating, inviting

- {鼓励|gǔ lì} + person + verb: to encourage someone to do something: {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}{鼓励|gǔ lì}{安娜|Ān nà}{报名|bào míng}。 (Teacher Wang
  encouraged Anna to sign up.) As a noun: {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{鼓励|gǔ lì}。
- {表扬|biǎo yáng} is to praise, usually publicly, as a teacher or a boss does: {老师|lǎo shī}{在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng}{表扬|biǎo yáng}{了|le}{他|tā}。
- {庆祝|qìng zhù} is to celebrate: {庆祝|qìng zhù}{生日|shēng rì}, {庆祝|qìng zhù}{一下|yí xià} (celebrate a bit), {为|wèi}{她|tā}{获奖|huò jiǎng}{庆祝|qìng zhù} (celebrate her
  prize).
- {邀请|yāo qǐng} + person + verb: to invite someone, more formal than {请|qǐng}: {学院|xué yuàn}{邀请|yāo qǐng}{获奖|huò jiǎng}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{参加|cān jiā}{晚会|wǎn huì}。 As a
  noun: {谢谢|xiè xie}{您|nín}{的|de}{邀请|yāo qǐng}。
- {喊|hǎn} is to shout, to call out: {大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{喊|hǎn}“{加油|jiā yóu}！” (Everyone was shouting "come on!") {加油|jiā yóu} is the
  cheer (lesson 07).
- {棒|bàng} is "great, excellent" in speech: {你|nǐ}{真|zhēn}{棒|bàng}！ (You're brilliant!)

## {场|chǎng} and {项|xiàng}: measure words for events

- {场|chǎng} (chǎng) counts games, matches, shows and other events that take place: {一|yì}{场|chǎng}{比赛|bǐ sài} (a match), {一|yì}{场|chǎng}
  {电影|diàn yǐng} (a film showing), {一|yì}{场|chǎng}{考试|kǎo shì} (an exam sitting). {最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{场|chǎng} is the last round, the final.
- {项|xiàng} (xiàng) counts items in a list or a programme: {一|yí}{项|xiàng}{比赛|bǐ sài} (an event in a competition), {一|yí}{项|xiàng}{活动|huó dòng},
  {一|yí}{项|xiàng}{工作|gōng zuò} (a task). {大赛|dà sài}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{项|xiàng}{比赛|bǐ sài}。 (The contest has two events.)

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 资 ✎ (traditional 資) | capital; resources | zī | 贝 | 10 | {资料|zī liào} (lesson 03), {工资|gōng zī} (lesson 11) |
| 品 ✎ | goods; quality | pǐn | 口 | 9 | {作品|zuò pǐn} (lesson 03), {食品|shí pǐn} (food, lesson 08) |
| 阅 (traditional 閱) | to read; to review | yuè | 门 | 10 | {阅读|yuè dú} (lesson 03) |
| 扬 (traditional 揚) | to raise; to spread | yáng | 扌 | 6 | {表扬|biǎo yáng} |
| 棒 | stick; great | bàng | 木 | 12 | {棒|bàng} |
| 光 | light; only; bare | guāng | 儿 | 6 | {不光|bù guāng} |
| 并 ✎ (traditional 並) | and; side by side | bìng | 干 | 6 | {并且|bìng qiě} |
| 仅 (traditional 僅) | only | jǐn | 亻 | 4 | {不仅|bù jǐn} |
| 队 ✎ (traditional 隊) | team; queue | duì | 阝 | 4 | {队|duì}, {队员|duì yuán}, {队长|duì zhǎng} |
| 败 (traditional 敗) | to be defeated | bài | 贝 | 8 | {打败|dǎ bài} |

- **Sound parts.** {励|lì} lì is {厉|lì} lì ({厉害|lì hai}, lesson 06) + {力|lì}: the same sound. {扬|yáng} yáng has the same right
  side as {场|chǎng} chǎng and {汤|tāng} tāng (lesson 08): one sound family, now spread out. {资|zī} zī has {次|cì} cì on top:
  close in its consonant only. {喊|hǎn} hǎn is {口|kǒu} + {咸|xián} xián (salty, lesson 08), the part also in {感|gǎn} gǎn and
  {减|jiǎn} jiǎn (to reduce, lesson 15): the sound has drifted. {排|pái} pái is 扌 + {非|fēi} fēi: drifted too. {棒|bàng} bàng is {木|mù} + {奉|fèng}
  fèng: drifted.
- **Families.** {贝|bèi} (a shell, once money): {资|zī} and {败|bài}, and {赢|yíng} next lesson, as in {贵|guì} and {费|fèi} ({免费|miǎn fèi}, free, lesson 09).
  礻 (an altar): {祝|zhù}, as in {礼|lǐ} ({礼物|lǐ wù}), and {福|fú} (lesson 23). 扌: {扬|yáng} and {排|pái}.
- **Look-alikes.** {另|lìng} lìng is {口|kǒu} over {力|lì}, and {别|bié} bié ({别人|bié ren}) is {另|lìng} + 刂. {奖|jiǎng} jiǎng is 丬 and {夕|xī} over {大|dà};
  {将|jiāng} jiāng (lesson 05) has the same top left, with {寸|cùn} under {夕|xī} instead of {大|dà}. {并|bìng} bìng is 丷 over {开|kāi}.
  {队|duì} duì is 阝 + {人|rén}; {认|rèn} rèn ({认识|rèn shi}) is 讠 + {人|rén}. {仅|jǐn} jǐn is 亻 + {又|yòu}, as {汉|hàn} is 氵 + {又|yòu}. {品|pǐn} pǐn is three {口|kǒu}. {金|jīn}
  jīn is the metal radical; on the left it becomes 钅 ({钱|qián}, {银|yín}, {错|cuò}).
- **Memory aids.** {获|huò} has 艹, 犭 and {犬|quǎn} (two signs for a dog): hunting with dogs to catch
  something. {鼓|gǔ} is {壴|zhù}, a drum on a stand, with {支|zhī} beside it. {庆|qìng} is {广|guǎng} (a building) over {大|dà}: a big
  celebration indoors. {祝|zhù} is 礻 (an altar) with {兄|xiōng} beside it: someone saying a blessing. Treat these
  as aids to memory, not as the characters' history.

### Stroke order

- **{并|bìng}**: a dot and a short left-falling stroke on top (not two dots), two horizontals, then the
  left-falling stroke and the vertical.
- **{光|guāng}**: the short vertical, a dot on its left and a short left-falling stroke on its right (⺌),
  the horizontal, then {儿|ér}: a left-falling stroke and the vertical bend hook.
- **{队|duì}**: 阝 first, in two strokes (the winding hook stroke, then the vertical), then {人|rén}.
- **{金|jīn}**: {人|rén} on top (left-falling, then right-falling), then {王|wáng} with the two short strokes inside:
  horizontal, horizontal, vertical, a dot, a short left-falling stroke, and the bottom horizontal
  last.
- **{奖|jiǎng}**: 丬 (a dot, a rising stroke, a vertical), {夕|xī} (three strokes), then {大|dà}.
- **{另|lìng}**: {口|kǒu} first, then {力|lì}: the horizontal-turn-hook, then the left-falling stroke.
