> {梁|Liáng}{教练|jiào liàn}{说|shuō}，{健身|jiàn shēn}{要|yào}{注意|zhù yì}{下面|xià miàn}{几|jǐ}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}：{第|dì}{一|yī}，{不用|bú yòng}{天|tiān}{天|tiān}{去|qù}{健身房|jiàn shēn fáng}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}{次|cì}{就|jiù}{可以|kě yǐ}{了|le}。{第|dì}{二|èr}，{动作|dòng zuò}{比|bǐ}{时间|shí jiān}{更|gèng}{重要|zhòng yào}，{动作|dòng zuò}{不|bú}{对|duì}，{练|liàn}{得|de}{再|zài}{久|jiǔ}{也|yě}{没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng}，{还|hái}{容易|róng yì}{受伤|shòu shāng}。{第|dì}{三|sān}，{运动|yùn dòng}{以后|yǐ hòu}{要|yào}{让|ràng}{身体|shēn tǐ}{放松|fàng sōng}{一下|yí xià}，{比如|bǐ rú}{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{地|de}{散散步|sàn san bù}。{第|dì}{四|sì}，{要|yào}{按时|àn shí}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。{睡|shuì}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{力气|lì qi}，{也|yě}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{运动|yùn dòng}{了|le}。
>
> "{健身|jiàn shēn}{跟|gēn}{学|xué}{外语|wài yǔ}{一样|yí yàng}，"{梁|Liáng}{教练|jiào liàn}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}，"{最|zuì}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一|yì}{开始|kāi shǐ}{有|yǒu}{多|duō}{努力|nǔ lì}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}{养成|yǎng chéng}{习惯|xí guàn}。"

{梁|Liáng} Liáng is a surname, and {原因|yuán yīn} (reason) is lesson 17's word. {坚持|jiān chí} (to keep at it) is HSK 3; {练|liàn}{得|de}{再|zài}{久|jiǔ}{也|yě}{没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng} is "however long you train, it's no
use" ({再|zài} + adjective + {也|yě}: however…). {不|bú}{是|shì}…{而|ér}{是|shì} is lesson 05's: not… but.

1. Why, according to the coach, do many people give up?
2. How often does he say you need to go to the gym?
3. Why does he say movements matter more than time?
4. Why does he compare keeping fit to learning a foreign language?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. They're too eager to see results straight away ({太|tài}{想|xiǎng}{马上|mǎ shàng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{效果|xiào guǒ}{了|le}); it takes at least two or three months.
2. Three times a week is enough ({一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{三|sān}{次|cì}{就|jiù}{可以|kě yǐ}{了|le}); there's no need to go every day.
3. If the movements are wrong, training longer doesn't help, and you can get hurt ({练|liàn}{得|de}{再|zài}{久|jiǔ}{也|yě}{没|méi}{有用|yǒu yòng}，{还|hái}{容易|róng yì}{受伤|shòu shāng}).
4. Because both depend on forming a habit and keeping going, not on how hard you try at the start
   ({最|zuì}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一|yì}{开始|kāi shǐ}{有|yǒu}{多|duō}{努力|nǔ lì}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}{养成|yǎng chéng}{习惯|xí guàn}). That's the article's main point, in its title too: {最|zuì}{难|nán}{的|de}{是|shì}{坚持|jiān chí}.

"**Keeping fit: the hardest part is keeping at it.** Lots of people are very serious when they start
working out: they buy new clothes, go to the gym and even hire a trainer. But after a month or two,
they tend to stop going. Why?

Coach Liang at the gym says the main reason is that people are too eager to see results straight away. 'Your
weight doesn't come down in a week,' he says. 'You have to keep at it for at least two or three
months before you see results.'

Coach Liang says there are a few things to bear in mind. First, there's no need to go to the gym
every day: three times a week is fine. Second, movements matter more than time: if your movements
are wrong, however long you train it's no use, and it's easy to get hurt. Third, after exercise let
your body relax, for example with a slow walk. Fourth, go to bed at a regular time. If you sleep
badly, you have no strength the next day and don't feel like exercising.

'Keeping fit is like learning a foreign language,' says Coach Liang with a smile. 'What matters most
isn't how hard you try at the start, but whether you can make it a habit.'"
</details>

## Write it: a sentence about a picture

Write one sentence for each described picture, using the word given.

1. A man is asleep on the sofa with the television still on. Word: {睡|shuì}{着|zháo}
2. A crowd in a stadium waves flags and shouts as a footballer runs towards the goal. Word: {加油|jiā yóu}
3. A woman checks her watch, then swallows two pills with a glass of water: it's exactly eight o'clock.
   Word: {按时|àn shí}

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {他|tā}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{睡|shuì}{着|zháo}{了|le}。 — He fell asleep watching television.
- {球迷|qiú mí}{们|men}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{大|dà}{声|shēng}{喊|hǎn}："{加油|jiā yóu}！" — The fans are all shouting, "Come on!" ({喊|hǎn}, to shout, is lesson 04's.)
- {她|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{按时|àn shí}{吃|chī}{药|yào}。 — She takes her medicine at the same times every day.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Keeping fit
{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{至少|zhì shǎo}{健身|jiàn shēn}{三|sān}{次|cì}。
= I work out at least three times a week.
{周末|zhōu mò}{他|tā}{往往|wǎng wǎng}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}。
= At weekends he tends to go hiking.
{我|wǒ}{平常|píng cháng}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kā fēi}，{偶尔|ǒu ěr}{喝|hē}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}。
= I don't usually drink coffee; just a cup now and then.
{你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{老是|lǎo shi}{玩儿|wánr}{手机|shǒu jī}？
= Why are you always on your phone?
{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{一直|yì zhí}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{着|zháo}。
= I couldn't get to sleep at all last night.
{加油|jiā yóu}！{加油|jiā yóu}！
= Come on! Come on!
```

## Pronunciation

- {着|zháo} in {睡|shuì}{着|zháo} is zháo, second tone, a full syllable. The particle in {看|kàn}{着|zhe} is zhe, light. Mixing them
  changes the meaning: {睡|shuì}{着|zhe} shuì zhe would be "sleeping (and doing something else)", not "fallen asleep".
- {老是|lǎo shi} lǎoshi: the second syllable is light. {往往|wǎng wǎng} wǎngwǎng is two third tones: said wáng wǎng (third-tone
  sandhi), as is {偶尔|ǒu ěr} ǒu'ěr (said óu ěr).
- {教练|jiào liàn} jiàoliàn: {教|jiāo} is jiào here (as in {教室|jiào shì}), not jiāo (to teach).
- {散步|sàn bù} sànbù: {散|sàn} is sàn, fourth tone. {力气|lì qi} lìqi and {功夫|gōng fu} gōngfu have light second syllables.
- {乒乓球|pīng pāng qiú} pīngpāngqiú: two level tones, then a rising one: ping, pang, ball.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{以后|yǐ hòu}{往往|wǎng wǎng}{去|qù}{健身房|jiàn shēn fáng}~~: {往往|wǎng wǎng} describes a pattern you've seen, not a plan. Use {常常|cháng cháng}: {我|wǒ}{以后|yǐ hòu}{常常|cháng cháng}{去|qù}{健身房|jiàn shēn fáng}.
- ~~{请|qǐng}{往往|wǎng wǎng}{来|lái}{玩儿|wánr}~~: no requests with {往往|wǎng wǎng} either: {请|qǐng}{常常|cháng cháng}{来|lái}{玩儿|wánr}.
- {他|tā}{老是|lǎo shi}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng} sounds like a complaint. For a neutral habit, say {他|tā}{总是|zǒng shì}{七|qī}{点|diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{着|zháo}{了|le}~~: after {没|méi} drop the {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{没|méi}{睡|shuì}{着|zháo}. And {着|zháo} is read zháo.
- After a short night, {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{困|kùn} is the exact word (sleepy); {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi} is tiredness from effort.
- {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{运动|yùn dòng}，{尤其|yóu qí}{游泳|yóu yǒng} is heard, but before a noun {尤其|yóu qí}{是|shì} is the usual form: {尤其|yóu qí}{是|shì}{游泳|yóu yǒng}.

## Key points

- {往往|wǎng wǎng}: tends to (a pattern in a situation, from experience); no plans, no requests. {常常|cháng cháng} for those.
- {偶尔|ǒu ěr}: occasionally. {老是|lǎo shi}: always, as a complaint. {总是|zǒng shì}: always, neutral.
- {至少|zhì shǎo} + verb or number: at least. {尤其|yóu qí}({是|shì}) + noun, {尤其|yóu qí} + adjective: especially.
- {按时|àn shí}: at the set time. {好好|hǎo hǎo} + verb: properly ({好好|hǎo hǎo}{休息|xiū xi}).
- {睡|shuì}{着|zháo}: fall asleep; {没|méi}{睡|shuì}{着|zháo}; {睡|shuì}{不|bu}{着|zháo}: can't sleep. {找|zhǎo}{着|zháo} = {找|zhǎo}{到|dào}.
- {养成|yǎng chéng} + {习惯|xí guàn}: to get into a habit.
- Gym and sport: {健身|jiàn shēn}({房|fáng}), {教练|jiào liàn}, {动作|dòng zuò}, {力气|lì qi}, {体重|tǐ zhòng}, {汗|hàn}, {放松|fàng sōng}, {压力|yā lì}, {排球|pái qiú}, {乒乓球|pīng pāng qiú}, {球队|qiú duì}, {球迷|qiú mí}, {加油|jiā yóu}!
- New characters: {血|xuè} {痛|tòng} {镜|jìng} {按|àn} {汗|hàn} {松|sōng} {油|yóu} {困|kùn} {乒|pīng} {乓|pāng} {迷|mí} {散|sàn} {偶|ǒu} {尔|ěr} {效|xiào} {压|yā} {抬|tái} {躺|tǎng} {醒|xǐng} {晨|chén}; handwriting: {血|xuè} {痛|tòng} {油|yóu} {困|kùn} {压|yā} {晨|chén}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Cooking and tastes: 够…的, 一大碗 and borrowed measure words
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

After the doctor and the gym, the kitchen. This lesson gives you the words to describe how food
tastes and smells, what goes into a dish and how it's made, and the grammar that food talk
needs most: quantities.

- {够|gòu}…{的|de}: "really (quite enough)…": {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{够|gòu}{辣|là}{的|de}！ (This dish is plenty spicy!)
- number + *adjective* + measure word: {一|yí}{大|dà}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng} (a big bowl of soup), {一|yì}{小|xiǎo}{块|kuài}{巧克力|qiǎo kè lì} (a small piece of chocolate);
- **[[borrowed measure words]]**: a noun used to count, often meaning "a whole… full": {一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài} (a whole
  tableful of food), {一|yì}{脸|liǎn}{汗|hàn} (a face covered in sweat);
- the measure words {顿|dùn} (meals) and {道|dào} (dishes);
- weights: {两|liǎng} liǎng (50 g), {斤|jīn}, {公斤|gōng jīn} / {千克|qiān kè}, and {克|kè} (gram).

The reading is a recipe, a written text with its own style: short, numbered steps.

## {够|gòu}…{的|de}: really, quite

{够|gòu} gòu is "enough": {钱|qián}{够|gòu}{了|le} (there's enough money), {我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{够|gòu}{了|le} (I've had enough), {够|gòu}{不|bu}{够|gòu}？ (is it enough?).
Put an adjective between {够|gòu} and {的|de} and it becomes a comment: "it's really…, more than enough":

{这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{够|gòu}{辣|là}{的|de}！ — This dish is plenty spicy!

{今天|jīn tiān}{够|gòu}{冷|lěng}{的|de}，{多|duō}{穿|chuān}{点儿|diǎnr}{衣服|yī fu}{吧|ba}。 — It's pretty cold today: put on some more clothes.

{你们|nǐ men}{够|gòu}{忙|máng}{的|de}，{周末|zhōu mò}{还|hái}{要|yào}{上班|shàng bān}。 — You're really busy, working at weekends too.

It's spoken, and it usually carries a feeling: surprise, a complaint, or (with a smile) a compliment.
Keep the {的|de}: {够|gòu}{辣|là}{的|de}. Without it, {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{够|gòu}{辣|là} usually means "spicy enough". Another {够|gòu} pattern: {够|gòu} + person + verb + {的|de}, "enough
for someone to…": {这些|zhè xiē}{菜|cài}{够|gòu}{我们|wǒ men}{吃|chī}{的|de} (there's enough food here for us).

## A big bowl, a small piece: number + adjective + measure word

Two adjectives, {大|dà} and {小|xiǎo}, can go between a number and its measure word, nearly always with {一|yī}:

{一|yí}{大|dà}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng} — a big bowl of soup

{一|yì}{小|xiǎo}{块|kuài}{巧克力|qiǎo kè lì} — a small piece of chocolate

{一|yí}{大|dà}{杯|bēi}{果汁|guǒ zhī} — a large glass of juice

{一|yì}{小|xiǎo}{盒|hé}{饼干|bǐng gān} — a small box of biscuits ({盒|hé}, a box: lesson 28)

Other adjectives can't: not ~~{一|yì}{好|hǎo}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng}~~ or ~~{一|yì}{新|xīn}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}~~; they go before the noun with {的|de}
({一|yí}{件|jiàn}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}). {大|dà} and {小|xiǎo} here are about the container or the piece, not the food. One more word works the
same way, {满|mǎn} (full): {一|yì}{满|mǎn}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ} (a full glass of water), more often {满|mǎn}{满|mǎn}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{水|shuǐ}.

## Borrowed measure words: a whole… full

A **[[borrowed measure word]]** is an ordinary noun used to count. You've used the container ones for
years: {一|yì}{杯|bēi}{茶|chá}, {一|yì}{碗|wǎn}{饭|fàn}, {一|yì}{瓶|píng}{水|shuǐ} (a cup, a bowl, a bottle). The same works with places and parts of the
body, and then {一|yī} means "a whole…, all over":

| Phrase | Literally | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài} | a table of dishes | a whole tableful of food |
| {一|yì}{屋子|wū zi}{人|rén} | a room of people | a roomful of people |
| {一|yì}{脸|liǎn}{汗|hàn} | a face of sweat | a face covered in sweat |
| {一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn} | a body of sweat | sweating all over |
| {一|yì}{手|shǒu}{油|yóu} | a hand of oil | hands covered in grease |
| {一|yí}{地|dì}{水|shuǐ} | a floor of water | water all over the floor |

{桌子|zhuō zi} and {屋子|wū zi} often keep their {子|zi} here. The phrase is vivid, and usually comes after the verb ({做|zuò}{了|le}{一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài}, {出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}). Only {一|yī} is used in the
"whole… full" sense: {两|liǎng}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài} is "two tables of food", counting tables.

Compare {一些|yì xiē} (some): {一些|yì xiē}{菜|cài} is just "some dishes", {一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài} is "so many dishes the table is covered".

## Meals and dishes: {顿|dùn} and {道|dào}

- **{顿|dùn}** dùn counts meals: {一|yí}{顿|dùn}{饭|fàn} (a meal), {一|yì}{天|tiān}{三|sān}{顿|dùn}{饭|fàn} (three meals a day), {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{一|yí}{顿|dùn} (I'll treat you to a
  meal). It also counts a telling-off: {妈妈|mā ma}{说|shuō}{了|le}{他|tā}{一|yí}{顿|dùn} (his mum gave him a talking-to).
- **{道|dào}** dào counts dishes on a menu and questions on a paper: {四|sì}{道|dào}{菜|cài} (four dishes), {一|yí}{道|dào}{题|tí} (a
  question). {个|gè} is fine in speech ({四|sì}{个|gè}{菜|cài}), but {道|dào} is the usual word in a restaurant and on a menu.

The measure words of HSK 4, with these and the borrowed ones, are on the reference sheet.

## How much does it weigh? {两|liǎng}, {斤|jīn}, {公斤|gōng jīn}, {克|kè}

| Unit | Weight | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {两|liǎng} liǎng | 50 grams | {二两|èr liǎng}{饺子|jiǎo zi} (100 g of dumplings, about ten) |
| {斤|jīn} jīn (HSK 3) | 500 grams, ten {两|liǎng} | {一|yì}{斤|jīn}{苹果|píng guǒ} |
| {公斤|gōng jīn} / {千克|qiān kè} | a kilogram, two {斤|jīn} | {两|liǎng}{公斤|gōng jīn}{米|mǐ}, {两|liǎng}{千克|qiān kè}{米|mǐ} |
| {克|kè} kè (lesson 15) | a gram | {一百|yì bǎi}{克|kè}{盐|yán} |

- The weight {两|liǎng} is the same character as {两|liǎng} "two" (HSK 1), and also liǎng, but it's a measure word of its
  own. In noodle and dumpling shops you order by it: {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{二两|èr liǎng}{饺子|jiǎo zi}, {一两|yì liǎng}{米饭|mǐ fàn}. With this {两|liǎng}, "two" is usually
  {二|èr}: {二两|èr liǎng} (two liang), not ~~{两两|liǎng liǎng}~~.
- {斤|jīn} and {两|liǎng} are what you hear at a market. {公斤|gōng jīn} is the spoken word for a kilogram; {千克|qiān kè} is the same unit in
  writing (on packets, in recipes and in science).

## Tastes and smells

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {酸|suān} | sour | {这个|zhè ge}{苹果|píng guǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{酸|suān}。 This apple is a bit sour. |
| {甜|tián} (HSK 3) | sweet | {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{太|tài}{甜|tián}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}。 I don't like things too sweet. |
| {苦|kǔ} | bitter; hard (of life) | {这个|zhè ge}{药|yào}{真|zhēn}{苦|kǔ}。 This medicine is so bitter. |
| {辣|là} | hot, spicy | {四川|Sì chuān}{菜|cài}{很|hěn}{辣|là}。 Sichuan food is very spicy. |
| {咸|xián} | salty | {汤|tāng}{太|tài}{咸|xián}{了|le}。 The soup is too salty. |
| {香|xiāng} | fragrant; smells good, tastes good | {好|hǎo}{香|xiāng}{啊|a}！ That smells wonderful! |
| {鲜|xiān} | fresh; tasty (of soup, fish) | {这个|zhè ge}{鱼|yú}{汤|tāng}{很|hěn}{鲜|xiān}。 This fish soup is delicious. |
| {味道|wèi dao} / {味|wèi} | taste, flavour | {味道|wèi dao}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ How does it taste? |
| {闻|wén} | to smell | {你|nǐ}{闻闻|wén wen}，{香|xiāng}{不|bu}{香|xiāng}？ Smell this: doesn't it smell good? |
| {凉|liáng} | cool, cold (of food and drink) | {汤|tāng}{凉|liáng}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{热|rè}{一下|yí xià}。 The soup's gone cold: I'll heat it up. |
| {满|mǎn} | full | {杯子|bēi zi}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{水|shuǐ}{太|tài}{满|mǎn}{了|le}。 The glass is too full. |

- {酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là} (sour, sweet, bitter, hot) is a set phrase for all the flavours, and for all of life's ups and
  downs: {生活|shēng huó}{的|de}{酸甜苦辣|suān tián kǔ là}.

### The other characters

- {刀|dāo} dāo: a drawing of a knife (the {说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì} calls it a pictograph). It's also the radical of {切|qiē}, and (as 刂 on the right)
  of {到|dào}.
- {叶|yè} yè: in simplified characters, {口|kǒu} + {十|shí}. Traditional {葉|yè} is plant 艹 + {枼|yè}: a leaf. The simplified
  form took over an old character, read xié (as in {叶韵|xié yùn}, to rhyme), for {葉|yè}.
- {厨|chú} chú: under {厂|chǎng}, {豆|dòu} + {寸|cùn}. Traditional {廚|chú} has {广|guǎng} instead of {厂|chǎng}, and 15 strokes.
- {聚|jù} jù: {取|qǔ} (to take) on top. Its words are about people coming together: {聚餐|jù cān}, {聚会|jù huì}.
- {餐|cān} cān: food {食|shí} at the bottom, so it's a meal: {早餐|zǎo cān}, {午餐|wǔ cān}, {晚餐|wǎn cān} (breakfast, lunch, dinner: lesson 19).
- {辣|là} là: {辛|xīn} (pungent, as in {辛苦|xīn kǔ}) + {束|shù}. {酸|suān} suān: the wine jar {酉|yǒu} again (lesson 07: {醒|xǐng}).
- {克|kè} kè: {古|gǔ} over {儿|ér}. A sound in {巧克力|qiǎo kè lì} and the gram in {千克|qiān kè}; the old meaning, "to overcome", is in {克服|kè fú}
  (HSK 5).
- {巧|qiǎo} qiǎo: {工|gōng} (work) + {丂|kǎo}: skilful, and by chance ({真|zhēn}{巧|qiǎo}！, what a coincidence, lesson 20).

### Look-alikes

- {刀|dāo} and {力|lì} (strength): both are a horizontal-turn-hook and a left-falling stroke, in that order. In {刀|dāo}
  the left-falling stroke starts under the top and stays inside; in {力|lì} it starts above and crosses the
  top stroke.
- {倒|dào} dào and {到|dào} dào: the same sound; {倒|dào} adds 亻.
- {汁|zhī} (氵 + {十|shí}) and {汗|hàn} (氵 + {干|gān}, lesson 07).

### Stroke order

- **{尤|yóu}**: the horizontal, the left-falling stroke, the vertical-bend-hook, and the dot last, at the top
  right.
- **{餐|cān}**: the top left (5 strokes), then {又|yòu} at the top right, then {食|shí} underneath: 16 strokes.
- **{够|gòu}**: {句|jù} on the left first (5), then the two {夕|xī} on the right.
- **{巧|qiǎo}**: {工|gōng} (the horizontal, the vertical, the rising stroke), then {丂|kǎo} (a horizontal, then one long
  stroke that turns twice and hooks).

> {一|yī}、{把|bǎ}{西红柿|xī hóng shì}{洗|xǐ}{干净|gān jìng}，{用|yòng}{刀|dāo}{切|qiē}{成|chéng}{小|xiǎo}{块|kuài}。{把|bǎ}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{打|dǎ}{在|zài}{碗|wǎn}{里|lǐ}，{用|yòng}{筷子|kuài zi}{多|duō}{打|dǎ}{几|jǐ}{下|xià}。
>
> {二|èr}、{锅|guō}{里|lǐ}{倒|dào}{少量|shǎo liàng}{的|de}{油|yóu}。{油|yóu}{热|rè}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{放|fàng}{入|rù}{西红柿|xī hóng shì}，{炒|chǎo}{一两|yì liǎng}{分钟|fēn zhōng}，{炒|chǎo}{到|dào}{西红柿|xī hóng shì}{变|biàn}{软|ruǎn}。
>
> {三|sān}、{往|wǎng}{锅|guō}{里|lǐ}{倒|dào}{一|yí}{大|dà}{碗|wǎn}{水|shuǐ}。{水|shuǐ}{开|kāi}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{再|zài}{慢|màn}{慢|màn}{地|de}{倒|dào}{入|rù}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}，{一边|yì biān}{倒|dào}{一边|yì biān}{用|yòng}{勺子|sháo zi}{轻|qīng}{轻|qīng}{地|de}{推|tuī}{几|jǐ}{下|xià}。
>
> {四|sì}、{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{熟|shú}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{放|fàng}{少量|shǎo liàng}{的|de}{盐|yán}。{尝|cháng}{一|yi}{尝|cháng}，{不够|bú gòu}{咸|xián}{可以|kě yǐ}{再|zài}{加|jiā}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。
>
> {这个|zhè ge}{汤|tāng}{做法|zuò fǎ}{简单|jiǎn dān}，{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{做|zuò}{好|hǎo}。{味道|wèi dao}{又|yòu}{酸|suān}{又|yòu}{鲜|xiān}，{喜欢|xǐ huan}{酸|suān}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de}，{可以|kě yǐ}{多|duō}{放|fàng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{西红柿|xī hóng shì}。
>
> {注意|zhù yì}：{西红柿|xī hóng shì}{要|yào}{选|xuǎn}{红|hóng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de}，{味道|wèi dao}{更|gèng}{好|hǎo}。{倒|dào}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{不要|bú yào}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{倒|dào}{得|de}{太|tài}{快|kuài}{的话|de huà}，{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{变成|biàn chéng}{大|dà}{块|kuài}。{盐|yán}{要|yào}{最后|zuì hòu}{放|fàng}，{一|yí}{次|cì}{别|bié}{放|fàng}{太|tài}{多|duō}。

{家常|jiā cháng} is "home-style" (an HSK 6 word) and {家庭|jiā tíng} "a family, household" (lesson 21). {锅|guō} is a wok or pan, {切|qiē} to cut, {炒|chǎo} to stir-fry, {软|ruǎn} soft (all HSK 5 words). {左右|zuǒ yòu} (about) is lesson 15's,
and {推|tuī} (to push) lesson 10's: {用|yòng}{勺子|sháo zi}{轻|qīng}{轻|qīng}{地|de}{推|tuī}{几|jǐ}{下|xià}, "give it a few gentle stirs with a ladle".

1. How big a tomato do you need?
2. When do the eggs go in?
3. What should you do if the soup isn't salty enough at the end?
4. Which ingredient makes the soup sour?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. One tomato of about three liang ({三两|sān liǎng}{左右|zuǒ yòu}), that is, about 150 grams.
2. After the water has come to the boil ({水|shuǐ}{开|kāi}{了|le}{以后|yǐ hòu}): pour them in slowly.
3. Taste it and add a little more salt ({不够|bú gòu}{咸|xián}{可以|kě yǐ}{再|zài}{加|jiā}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}).
4. The tomato: if you like it more sour, you add another tomato ({喜欢|xǐ huan}{酸|suān}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{的|de}，{可以|kě yǐ}{多|duō}{放|fàng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{西红柿|xī hóng shì}). The
   text never says so in so many words: you work it out.

"**Tomato and egg soup** (for two). This is a home-style soup that lots of Chinese families make
often; adults and children all love it. You need: one tomato (about 150 g), two eggs, a big bowl of water,
a little salt and oil.

Method: 1. Wash the tomato and cut it into small pieces with a knife. Break the eggs into a bowl and
beat them well with chopsticks. 2. Pour a little oil into the wok. When the oil is hot, put in the
tomato and stir-fry it for a minute or two, until the tomato is soft. 3. Pour a big bowl of water into
the wok. When the water boils, slowly pour in the eggs, stirring gently with a ladle as you pour.
4. When the eggs are cooked, add a little salt. Taste it; if it isn't salty enough, add a bit more.

This soup is simple to make and ready in ten minutes. It tastes both sour and savoury; if you like it
sourer, add another tomato.

Note: choose redder tomatoes: they taste better. Don't pour the eggs in too fast: if you do, they turn
into big lumps. Add the salt last, and not too much at a time."
</details>

## Write it: a sentence about a picture

1. A family sits round a table covered with dishes, chopsticks raised. Word: {一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}
2. A child pulls a face after a spoonful of medicine. Word: {苦|kǔ}
3. A man pours tea from a pot into three cups. Word: {倒|dào}

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {妈妈|mā ma}{做|zuò}{了|le}{一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 — Mum has made a whole tableful of food, and everyone's happy.
- {这个|zhè ge}{药|yào}{太|tài}{苦|kǔ}{了|le}，{孩子|hái zi}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}。 — The medicine is too bitter: the child doesn't want to take it.
- {他|tā}{给|gěi}{客人|kè rén}{倒|dào}{了|le}{三|sān}{杯|bēi}{茶|chá}。 — He poured three cups of tea for his guests.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Food and tastes
{好|hǎo}{香|xiāng}{啊|a}！
= That smells wonderful!
{这个|zhè ge}{汤|tāng}{够|gòu}{咸|xián}{的|de}。
= This soup is pretty salty.
{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{一|yí}{大|dà}{碗|wǎn}{面|miàn}{条|tiáo}。
= I'd like a big bowl of noodles.
{妈妈|mā ma}{做|zuò}{了|le}{一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài}。
= Mum has made a whole tableful of food.
{我们|wǒ men}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{吃|chī}{三|sān}{顿|dùn}{饭|fàn}。
= We eat three meals a day.
{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{二两|èr liǎng}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。
= I'd like two liang of dumplings.
```

{面条|miàn tiáo} (noodles) isn't on the word list, but you've met it since HSK 1.

## Pronunciation

- {两|liǎng} liǎng is third tone in both senses ("two" and the weight). {二两|èr liǎng} is èr liǎng.
- {熟|shú} is shú in careful speech and dictionaries, shóu in much everyday speech. Write shú.
- {倒|dào} is dào for "to pour" ({倒|dào}{水|shuǐ}), dǎo for "to fall over".
- {馒头|mán tou} mántou, {葡萄|pú tao} pútao and {味道|wèi dao} wèidao have a light second syllable.
- {巧克力|qiǎo kè lì} qiǎokèlì: a third tone, then two fourth tones. {酸|suān} suān and {咸|xián} xián: watch the tones of the tastes,
  {酸|suān} 1, {甜|tián} 2, {苦|kǔ} 3, {辣|là} 4: a handy set, one of each tone, with {咸|xián} xián (2) and {香|xiāng} xiāng (1).

## Common mistakes

- {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{够|gòu}{辣|là} without {的|de} usually means "spicy enough"; for "really spicy" keep the {的|de}: {这个|zhè ge}{菜|cài}{够|gòu}{辣|là}{的|de}！
- ~~{一|yì}{好|hǎo}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng}~~: only {大|dà} and {小|xiǎo} go between the number and the measure word: {一|yí}{大|dà}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng}, but {一|yì}{碗|wǎn}{好|hǎo}{汤|tāng}.
- ~~{两两|liǎng liǎng}{饺子|jiǎo zi}~~: with the weight {两|liǎng}, say {二两|èr liǎng}{饺子|jiǎo zi}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{闻|wén}{很|hěn}{香|xiāng}~~ for "it smells good": {闻|wén} is the action. Say {闻|wén}{起来|qǐ lái}{很|hěn}{香|xiāng} or just {好|hǎo}{香|xiāng}！
- {食品|shí pǐn} for a meal: say {饭|fàn}; {食品|shí pǐn} is food as a product ({食品|shí pǐn}{店|diàn}).
- {一些|yì xiē}{菜|cài} is not wrong, but it doesn't say what {一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài} says (so many that the table is full).

## Key points

- {够|gòu} + adjective + {的|de}: really, quite (spoken, with feeling); {够|gòu} + person + verb + {的|de}: enough for someone to.
- Number (usually {一|yī}) + {大|dà} / {小|xiǎo} + measure word: {一|yí}{大|dà}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng}, {一|yì}{小|xiǎo}{块|kuài}{巧克力|qiǎo kè lì}.
- Borrowed measure words: {一|yì}{杯|bēi}, {一|yì}{碗|wǎn}; and "a whole… full": {一|yì}{桌子|zhuō zi}{菜|cài}, {一|yì}{屋子|wū zi}{人|rén}, {一|yì}{脸|liǎn}{汗|hàn}, {一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}.
- {顿|dùn} for meals ({一|yí}{顿|dùn}{饭|fàn}), {道|dào} for dishes and questions ({一|yí}{道|dào}{菜|cài}, {一|yí}{道|dào}{题|tí}).
- {两|liǎng} liǎng = 50 g ({二两|èr liǎng}{饺子|jiǎo zi}); {斤|jīn} = 500 g; {公斤|gōng jīn} / {千克|qiān kè} = 1 kg; {克|kè} = 1 g.
- Tastes: {酸|suān} {甜|tián} {苦|kǔ} {辣|là} {咸|xián} {香|xiāng} {鲜|xiān}; {味道|wèi dao}; {闻|wén} (to smell). Cooking: {烤|kǎo}, {倒|dào} dào, {生|shēng} / {熟|shú}, {少量|shǎo liàng}, {做法|zuò fǎ}.
- New characters: {尤|yóu} {饼|bǐng} {叶|yè} {厨|chú} {刀|dāo} {汁|zhī} {倒|dào} {够|gòu} {顿|dùn} {馒|mán} {聚|jù} {餐|cān} {烤|kǎo} {苦|kǔ} {辣|là} {葡|pú} {萄|táo} {巧|qiǎo} {克|kè} {酸|suān}; handwriting: {刀|dāo} {倒|dào} {够|gòu} {餐|cān} {克|kè}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Prices, shops and deliveries: 不如, 跟…相比 and 打八折
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 3 compared things with {比|bǐ}, {没有|méi yǒu}…{那么|nà me} and {跟|gēn}…{一样|yí yàng}. Shopping is where comparing matters most, so this
lesson adds the comparisons of HSK 4:

- **A {不如|bù rú} B**: A isn't as good as B ({这|zhè}{家|jiā}{的|de}{菜|cài}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{的|de}{好吃|hǎo chī});
- {跟|gēn}…{相比|xiāng bǐ}: compared with…;
- {一|yī} + measure word + {比|bǐ} + {一|yī} + measure word: {一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{贵|guì} (dearer by the day);
- **[[multiples]]** with {倍|bèi} (twice as expensive: {贵|guì}{一|yí}{倍|bèi}) and discounts ({打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}, 20 % off).

With them come the words for prices and paying, shops and members, deliveries, and clothes: {外套|wài tào},
{毛衣|máo yī}, {帽子|mào zi}, {袜子|wà zi}, {皮鞋|pí xié}, and the verbs for putting them on and taking them off.

## A {不如|bù rú} B: not as good as

{不如|bù rú} bùrú is "isn't as good as". On its own it's a verdict:

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{不如|bù rú}{他|tā}。 — My Chinese isn't as good as his.

{坐|zuò}{公交车|gōng jiāo chē}{不如|bù rú}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}。 — The bus isn't as good as the metro.

Add an adjective at the end to say in what way:

{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{的|de}{菜|cài}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{的|de}{好吃|hǎo chī}。 — The food here isn't as good as at that place.

{网上|wǎng shàng}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{不如|bù rú}{店|diàn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{质量|zhì liàng}{好|hǎo}。 — Clothes online aren't as good quality as in the shops.

The adjective is usually something good ({好|hǎo}, {好吃|hǎo chī}, {便宜|pián yi}, {方便|fāng biàn}, {漂亮|piào liang}): {不如|bù rú} says A falls short. "This one is
less expensive" is {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{没有|méi yǒu}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì} or {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}; {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì} is heard, but sounds odd to many speakers. And, as with {比|bǐ}, there's no {很|hěn}
or {非常|fēi cháng} before the adjective: not ~~{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}~~.

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| A {比|bǐ} B + adj. (HSK 3) | {那|nà}{家|jiā}{比|bǐ}{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{好吃|hǎo chī}。 | That place is better. |
| A {没有|méi yǒu} B ({那么|nà me}) + adj. (HSK 3) | {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{没有|méi yǒu}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{好吃|hǎo chī}。 | This place isn't as good as that one. |
| A {不如|bù rú} B (+ adj.) | {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{家|jiā}({好吃|hǎo chī})。 | This place isn't as good as that one. |

{没有|méi yǒu}…{那么|nà me} and {不如|bù rú} often mean the same. {不如|bù rú} sounds a little more like a judgement, and it can stand without
an adjective.

### {不如|bù rú} + a suggestion

Before a verb, {不如|bù rú} makes a suggestion: "you might as well…, it'd be better to…":

{外面|wài miàn}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{不如|bù rú}{打车|dǎ chē}{吧|ba}。 — It's raining: we might as well take a taxi.

The idea is the same: anything else is "not as good as" this.

## {跟|gēn}…{相比|xiāng bǐ}: compared with

{跟|gēn} B {相比|xiāng bǐ} sets up a comparison at the start of the sentence; the second half says what's different:

{跟|gēn}{去年|qù nián}{相比|xiāng bǐ}，{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{高|gāo}{了|le}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}。 — Compared with last year, prices are a good deal higher this year.

{跟|gēn}{大|dà}{商场|shāng chǎng}{相比|xiāng bǐ}，{小|xiǎo}{市场|shì chǎng}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{便宜|pián yi}{多|duō}{了|le}。 — Compared with a big shopping centre, things at a small market are much cheaper.

{和|hé} can replace {跟|gēn}, and in writing {与|yǔ} (lesson 24): {与|yǔ}{去年|qù nián}{相比|xiāng bǐ}. {相比|xiāng bǐ} is also a verb on its own:
{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{牌子|pái zi}{不|bù}{能|néng}{相比|xiāng bǐ} (these two brands aren't in the same league). {商场|shāng chǎng} is a shopping centre ({商店|shāng diàn} + {场|chǎng}).

## Better and better: {一|yī} + M + {比|bǐ} + {一|yī} + M

{一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān} (each day more than the last) describes a steady change. The measure word can be any one that
fits:

{天气|tiān qì}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 — It's getting colder by the day.

{东西|dōng xi}{一|yì}{年|nián}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{年|nián}{贵|guì}。 — Things get dearer every year.

{他|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{一|yí}{次|cì}{比|bǐ}{一|yí}{次|cì}{说|shuō}{得|de}{好|hǎo}。 — His Chinese gets better every time.

There's no {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè} here, though the meaning is close: {一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān} stresses the step-by-step change, {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}
(HSK 3) just the direction. Not ~~{一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~: no {很|hěn}.

## Twice as much: {倍|bèi}

{倍|bèi} bèi (lesson 15's word) counts **[[multiples]]**: "times as much". Two patterns:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{外套|wài tào}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{是|shì}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{的|de}{两|liǎng}{倍|bèi}。 — This jacket costs twice as much as that one. (A {是|shì} B {的|de} N {倍|bèi}: A is N times B.)

{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{比|bǐ}{去年|qù nián}{高|gāo}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi}。 — Prices this year are double last year's. (A {比|bǐ} B + adj. + {了|le} N {倍|bèi}: up by N times.)

Careful with the second: {高|gāo}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} (or, of a thing, {贵|guì}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi}) is "up by one times", that is, *twice* the price;
{高|gāo}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{倍|bèi} is three times. ({价格|jià gé} is {高|gāo} or {低|dī}; a thing is {贵|guì} or {便宜|pián yi}.) In speech people don't always count this way, so if the amount matters, say the figure
({从|cóng}{一百|yì bǎi}{块|kuài}{到|dào}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{块|kuài}).

## Discounts: {打折|dǎ zhé}

{打折|dǎ zhé} dǎzhé is "to give a discount". The number says how many tenths *you pay*:

| Sign | You pay | English |
|---|---|---|
| {打|dǎ}{九|jiǔ}{折|zhé} | 90 % | 10 % off |
| {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} | 80 % | 20 % off |
| {打|dǎ}{七五|qī wǔ}{折|zhé} | 75 % | 25 % off |
| {打|dǎ}{五|wǔ}{折|zhé} | 50 % | half price |

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{毛衣|máo yī}{打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}，{现在|xiàn zài}{八十|bā shí}{块|kuài}。 — This sweater is 20 % off: it's eighty yuan now.

So {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} is a smaller discount than {打|dǎ}{五|wǔ}{折|zhé}, not a bigger one: a common slip for English speakers. {打折|dǎ zhé}
is separable: {打|dǎ}{了|le}{八|bā}{折|zhé}, {打|dǎ}{不|bu}{打折|dǎ zhé}？ (is there a discount?). {降价|jiàng jià} is a price cut ({降|jiàng}, to fall); its opposite,
a rise, is {涨价|zhǎng jià} (an HSK 5 word).

## Prices and paying

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {价格|jià gé} | price | {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{店|diàn}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{比|bǐ}{市场|shì chǎng}{上|shàng}{高|gāo}。 Prices in this shop are higher than at the market. |
| {价钱|jià qian} | price (spoken) | {价钱|jià qian}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ How's the price? |
| {高价|gāo jià} / {低价|dī jià} | a high / low price | {他们|tā men}{低价|dī jià}{卖|mài}{旧|jiù}{货|huò}。 They sell second-hand things cheaply. |

### The {汤|tāng} family

In simplified characters {汤|tāng}, {场|chǎng} (place, lesson 04's measure word), {扬|yáng} ({表扬|biǎo yáng}, lesson 04) and {肠|cháng} (intestines)
share the right side 𠃓. In traditional characters they share {昜|yáng} (yáng): {湯|tāng}, {場|chǎng}, {揚|yáng}, {腸|cháng}.
{伤|shāng} (lesson 06) was in the family too, {傷|shāng}, before simplification gave it a different right side.

### Look-alikes

- {味|wèi} wèi has {未|wèi} wèi (not yet), whose top horizontal is *shorter* than the one below it; {末|mò} mò (end:
  {期末|qī mò}, lesson 02) has the *longer* horizontal on top.
- {戴|dài} dài (to wear) and {带|dài} dài (to bring): the same syllable, two different characters.
- {免|miǎn} miǎn and {兔|tù} tù (rabbit): {兔|tù} has one more stroke, a dot at the bottom right.
- {折|zhé} zhé (扌 + {斤|jīn}) and {析|xī} xī ({木|mù} + {斤|jīn}, in {分析|fēn xī}, HSK 5).

### Stroke order

- **{戴|dài}**: {土|tǔ} on top first, then {田|tián} and the strokes under it, then {戈|gē}'s long slanting hook, its
  left-falling stroke, and the dot last: 17 strokes.
- **{免|miǎn}**: the left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down to the left, then the box (a vertical, a horizontal-turn,
  a horizontal), then the left-falling stroke and the vertical-bend-hook.
- **{降|jiàng}**: 阝 on the left first (2 strokes), then the right side (6).
- **{牌|pái}**: {片|piàn} on the left (4 strokes: left-falling, vertical, horizontal, horizontal-turn), then
  {卑|bēi} (8).

```dialogue
王芳: {那|nà}{就|jiù}{买|mǎi}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}。{可以|kě yǐ}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{支付|zhī fù}{吗|ma}？
= Then I'll take it. Can I pay by phone?
店员: {可以|kě yǐ}，{现金|xiàn jīn}、{扫码|sǎo mǎ}{都|dōu}{行|xíng}。{我们|wǒ men}{还|hái}{可以|kě yǐ}{免费|miǎn fèi}{送|sòng}{货|huò}{上门|shàng mén}。
= Yes, cash or scanning a code, either's fine. We can also deliver to your door free of charge.
王芳: {不用|bú yòng}{了|le}，{谢谢|xiè xie}，{我|wǒ}{自己|zì jǐ}{拿|ná}{回去|huí qù}。
= No need, thanks, I'll carry it home myself.
```

- {一|yì}{年|nián}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{年|nián}{多|duō}: more every year ({一|yī} + M + {比|bǐ} + {一|yī} + M); {正式|zhèng shì} (formal, smart) is lesson 13's word.
- {打|dǎ}{完|wán}{折|zhé}: {打折|dǎ zhé} is separable, so {完|wán} goes between: "after the discount".
- {那|nà}{倒是|dào shi}: "that's true", conceding a point ({倒|dào} dào here is an adverb, "admittedly").
- {店|diàn}{员|yuán} is a shop assistant ({店|diàn} + {员|yuán}, as in {服务|fú wù}{员|yuán}).
- {七二|qī èr}{折|zhé}: 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so she pays 72 % of the 1,200 yuan: 864 yuan.

## Reading: a supermarket notice

A notice by the door of a supermarket: a written text, with the formal words {各位|gè wèi}, {此外|cǐ wài} (lesson 01)
and {购买|gòu mǎi}, {支付|zhī fù}.

> **{新城|Xīn chéng}{超市|chāo shì}{会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}**
>
> {各位|gè wèi}{顾客|gù kè}：
>
> {为了|wèi le}{感谢|gǎn xiè}{大家|dà jiā}，{从|cóng}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{每|měi}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{十八|shí bā}{号|hào}{是|shì}{新城|Xīn chéng}{超市|chāo shì}{的|de}"{会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}"。
>
> {一|yī}、{会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}{当天|dàng tiān}，{会员|huì yuán}{购买|gòu mǎi}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}、{牛奶|niú nǎi}、{面包|miàn bāo}，{一律|yí lǜ}{打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一些|yì xiē}{商品|shāng pǐn}{打|dǎ}{五|wǔ}{折|zhé}。
>
> {二|èr}、{会员|huì yuán}{购买|gòu mǎi}{一百|yì bǎi}{元|yuán}{以上|yǐ shàng}{的|de}{商品|shāng pǐn}，{可以|kě yǐ}{免费|miǎn fèi}{送|sòng}{货|huò}{上门|shàng mén}（{只|zhǐ}{送|sòng}{新城|Xīn chéng}{小区|xiǎo qū}）。{不|bú}{是|shì}{会员|huì yuán}{的|de}{顾客|gù kè}，{送|sòng}{货|huò}{每|měi}{次|cì}{收费|shōu fèi}{十|shí}{元|yuán}。
>
> {三|sān}、{成为|chéng wéi}{会员|huì yuán}{不|bù}{收费|shōu fèi}。{请|qǐng}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{扫码|sǎo mǎ}，{一|yì}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{可以|kě yǐ}{成为|chéng wéi}{会员|huì yuán}。
>
> {四|sì}、{可以|kě yǐ}{用|yòng}{现金|xiàn jīn}、{银行卡|yín háng kǎ}{或者|huò zhě}{手机|shǒu jī}{支付|zhī fù}。
>
> {五|wǔ}、{会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}{当天|dàng tiān}，{超市|chāo shì}{里|lǐ}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{商品|shāng pǐn}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{都|dōu}{比|bǐ}{平时|píng shí}{低|dī}，{跟|gēn}{网上|wǎng shàng}{相比|xiāng bǐ}{也|yě}{便宜|pián yi}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}。
>
> {六|liù}、{如果|rú guǒ}{您|nín}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{的|de}{商品|shāng pǐn}{质量|zhì liàng}{有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}，{七|qī}{天|tiān}{内|nèi}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{拿|ná}{来|lái}{换|huàn}。
>
> {七|qī}、{超市|chāo shì}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{开|kāi}{门|mén}，{晚上|wǎn shang}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{关|guān}{门|mén}，{会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}{也|yě}{一样|yí yàng}。
>
> {此外|cǐ wài}，{会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}{顾客|gù kè}{比较|bǐ jiào}{多|duō}，{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{耐心|nài xīn}{排队|pái duì}。{欢迎|huān yíng}{大家|dà jiā}{来|lái}{购物|gòu wù}，{谢谢|xiè xie}！
>
> {新城|Xīn chéng}{超市|chāo shì}

{感谢|gǎn xiè} (to thank) is lesson 14's word, {当天|dàng tiān} "that same day", {七|qī}{天|tiān}{内|nèi} "within seven days" ({内|nèi}: lesson 13's written word); {一律|yí lǜ} yílǜ "all, without exception", a written word; {小区|xiǎo qū} a housing compound
({新城|Xīn chéng} is the compound where Wang Fang and Anna live). {耐心|nài xīn} (patient, patiently) is lesson 22's word.

1. When is the member day?
2. What do members get if they spend over 100 yuan?
3. How do you become a member, and what does it cost?
4. Why does the notice ask people to be patient?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The eighteenth of every month, starting next month ({每|měi}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{十八|shí bā}{号|hào}).
2. Free delivery to their door, within the {新城|Xīn chéng} compound ({免费|miǎn fèi}{送|sòng}{货|huò}{上门|shàng mén}（{只|zhǐ}{送|sòng}{新城|Xīn chéng}{小区|xiǎo qū}）).
3. Scan the code at the door; it takes a minute and is free ({成为|chéng wéi}{会员|huì yuán}{不|bù}{收费|shōu fèi}).
4. Because the notice expects a lot of customers that day ({会员|huì yuán}{日|rì}{顾客|gù kè}{比较|bǐ jiào}{多|duō}): the discounts will bring
   people in, so there will be queues. The supermarket hopes the day will be busy.

"**Xincheng Supermarket Member Day.** Dear customers, to thank you all, from next month the 18th of
every month will be Xincheng Supermarket's 'Member Day'. 1. On Member Day, members buying fruit,
milk and bread get 20 % off without exception, and some other goods are half price. 2. Members who spend
over 100 yuan get free home delivery (to the Xincheng compound only). For customers who aren't
members, delivery is 10 yuan each time. 3. Membership is free. Scan the code at the door and you can
be a member in a minute. 4. You can pay in cash, by bank card or by phone. 5. On Member Day, many goods in the supermarket
are cheaper than usual, and a good deal cheaper than online. 6. If there's a problem with the quality
of anything you buy, you can bring it back and change it within seven days. 7. The supermarket opens at 8 a.m. and closes at
10 p.m. every day, Member Day included. In addition, there will be more customers than usual on
Member Day, so please queue patiently. Everyone is welcome: thank you! Xincheng
Supermarket"
</details>

## Write it: a sentence about a picture

1. A shop window with a big sign: 50 % OFF. Word: {打折|dǎ zhé}
2. Ten people stand in a line at a cash desk. Word: {排队|pái duì}
3. An old man in a hat and glasses reads a newspaper on a bench. Word: {戴|dài}

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{商店|shāng diàn}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu}{都|dōu}{打|dǎ}{五|wǔ}{折|zhé}。 — All the clothes in this shop are half price.
- {超市|chāo shì}{里|lǐ}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{排队|pái duì}。 — The supermarket is crowded, and everyone is queuing.
- {爷爷|yé ye}{戴|dài}{着|zhe}{帽子|mào zi}{和|hé}{眼镜|yǎn jìng}，{正在|zhèng zài}{看|kàn}{报纸|bào zhǐ}。 — Grandpa, in a hat and glasses, is reading the paper.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Shopping
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{外套|wài tào}{打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé}{吗|ma}？
= Is this jacket 20 % off?
{网上|wǎng shàng}{的|de}{东西|dōng xi}{不如|bù rú}{店|diàn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{质量|zhì liàng}{好|hǎo}。
= Things online aren't as good quality as in the shops.
{跟|gēn}{去年|qù nián}{相比|xiāng bǐ}，{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{价格|jià gé}{高|gāo}{了|le}{不|bù}{少|shǎo}。
= Compared with last year, prices are a good deal higher this year.
{东西|dōng xi}{一|yì}{年|nián}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{年|nián}{贵|guì}。
= Things get dearer every year.
{可以|kě yǐ}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{支付|zhī fù}{吗|ma}？
= Can I pay by phone?
{免费|miǎn fèi}{送|sòng}{货|huò}{上门|shàng mén}{吗|ma}？
= Is home delivery free?
```

## Pronunciation

- {价钱|jià qian} jiàqian has a light second syllable; {价格|jià gé} jiàgé doesn't.
- {打折|dǎ zhé} dǎzhé: {折|zhé} is zhé, second tone (not zhè, the {这|zhè} of "this").
- {戴|dài} dài (to wear) and {带|dài} dài (to bring) sound the same; {袜子|wà zi} wàzi and {帽子|mào zi} màozi have light {子|zi}.
- {逛|guàng} guàng is fourth tone; {降价|jiàng jià} jiàngjià is two fourth tones.
- {不如|bù rú} bùrú: {不|bù} stays bù before the rising {如|rú}.
- {假|jiǎ} is jiǎ for "fake" ({假|jiǎ}{货|huò}) and jià for "holiday" ({放假|fàng jià}).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}~~: no {很|hěn} in a comparison: {这|zhè}{家|jiā}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{家|jiā}{好吃|hǎo chī}.
- {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{不如|bù rú}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì} for "this one is cheaper" sounds odd: {不如|bù rú} usually takes a good quality. Say {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{比|bǐ}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi} or {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{没有|méi yǒu}{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}.
- {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} is 20 % off, not 80 %: you pay eight tenths.
- {贵|guì}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} is twice the price, not "one more yuan" or "the same".
- ~~{穿|chuān}{帽子|mào zi}~~, ~~{穿|chuān}{眼镜|yǎn jìng}~~: hats, glasses and watches take {戴|dài}: {戴|dài}{帽子|mào zi}, {戴|dài}{眼镜|yǎn jìng}.
- ~~{天气|tiān qì}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~: no {很|hěn}: {天气|tiān qì}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{冷|lěng}.
- {免费|miǎn fèi} is "free of charge" only. "Are you free?" is {你|nǐ}{有空|yǒu kòng}{吗|ma}？

## Key points

- A {不如|bù rú} B (+ good adjective): A isn't as good as B. {不如|bù rú} + verb: might as well.
- {跟|gēn} / {和|hé} / {与|yǔ} B {相比|xiāng bǐ}，…: compared with B.
- {一|yī} + M + {比|bǐ} + {一|yī} + M: {一|yì}{天|tiān}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{天|tiān}{冷|lěng}, {一|yì}{年|nián}{比|bǐ}{一|yì}{年|nián}{贵|guì} (step by step).
- A {是|shì} B {的|de} N {倍|bèi}; A {比|bǐ} B {贵|guì}{了|le}{一|yí}{倍|bèi} (= twice). {打|dǎ}{八|bā}{折|zhé} = pay 80 %.
- {价格|jià gé} / {价钱|jià qian}, {打折|dǎ zhé}, {降价|jiàng jià}, {免费|miǎn fèi} / {收费|shōu fèi}, {付|fù} / {支付|zhī fù}, {现金|xiàn jīn}, {扫码|sǎo mǎ}, {快递|kuài dì}, {上门|shàng mén}, {排队|pái duì}, {逛|guàng}, {购物|gòu wù} / {购买|gòu mǎi} (written).
- {穿|chuān} clothes and shoes, {戴|dài} hats, glasses and watches; {脱|tuō} to take off clothes.
- New characters: {汤|tāng} {味|wèi} {柿|shì} {盐|yán} {咸|xián} {低|dī} {价|jià} {折|zhé} {戴|dài} {付|fù} {购|gòu} {逛|guàng} {份|fèn} {货|huò} {递|dì} {帽|mào} {降|jiàng} {牌|pái} {免|miǎn} {费|fèi}; handwriting: {汤|tāng} {味|wèi} {低|dī} {份|fèn} {牌|pái}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Renting a flat: 不得不, 只好 and 差点儿
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 2 ends at home. Wang Fang and Anna still share the flat in the {新城|Xīn chéng} compound, and things go
wrong in flats: windows break, lights die, keys get lost. This lesson gives you the words for renting,
for the rooms and furniture, and for fixing, cleaning and tidying, and three grammar points for when
you have no choice or nearly come to grief:

- **[[double negation]]**: {不得不|bù dé bù} (have no choice but to), {不|bù}{能|néng}{不|bù} (can't not), {没有|méi yǒu}…{不|bù} (there's no one who
  doesn't…), {非|fēi}…{不|bù}{可|kě} (simply must);
- {只好|zhǐ hǎo} (have no choice but to, so…);
- {差点儿|chà diǎnr} (almost), and why {差点儿|chà diǎnr}{迟到|chí dào} and {差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi}{迟到|chí dào} mean the same thing.

## Two negatives make a strong positive

In a **[[double negation]]** two negative words cancel out, and the result is stronger than a plain
positive:

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {不得不|bù dé bù} + verb | have no choice but to | {钥匙|yào shi}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{不得不|bù dé bù}{找|zhǎo}{人|rén}{开|kāi}{门|mén}。 I'd lost my key, so I had no choice but to get someone to open the door. |
| {不|bù}{能|néng}{不|bù} + verb | can't not, must | {房东|fáng dōng}{的|de}{话|huà}，{我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{能|néng}{不|bù}{听|tīng}。 We can't ignore what the landlord says. |
| {没有|méi yǒu} + noun + {不|bù} + verb | there's no… that doesn't | {我们|wǒ men}{班|bān}{没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}。 There's no one in our class who doesn't like her. |
| {非|fēi} + verb + {不|bù}{可|kě} | simply must | {这个|zhè ge}{窗户|chuāng hu}{非|fēi}{修|xiū}{不|bù}{可|kě}{了|le}。 This window simply has to be fixed. |

- {不得不|bù dé bù} bùdébù is the most common. It says something outside you forces the action: {下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{不得不|bù dé bú}
  {坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}。 ({得|dé} is dé here, the {得|dé} of {得到|dé dào}.)
- {不|bù}{能|néng}{不|bù} is about duty or reason: you can't not do it.
- {没有|méi yǒu}…{不|bù} turns "everyone" into "no one fails to": {没有|méi yǒu}{人|rén}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào} (everyone knows), {没有|méi yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan} (every
  single person likes it).
- {非|fēi}…{不|bù}{可|kě} ({非|fēi} fēi, "not", as in {非常|fēi cháng}) is emphatic and spoken: {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{非|fēi}{去|qù}{不|bù}{可|kě} (I absolutely must go today).

Compare: {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{去|qù} (I'm going), {我|wǒ}{得|děi}{去|qù} (I have to go), {我|wǒ}{不得不|bù dé bú}{去|qù} (I have no choice but to go).

## {只好|zhǐ hǎo}: so I had no choice

{只好|zhǐ hǎo} zhǐhǎo (only + good: "the only thing to do") comes before the verb. It reports what you did
because there was nothing else for it, usually a little reluctantly:

{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{班|bān}{地铁|dì tiě}{走|zǒu}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{打车|dǎ chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。 — The last train had gone, so we had to take a taxi home.

{商店|shāng diàn}{关|guān}{门|mén}{了|le}，{他|tā}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{来|lái}。 — The shop was shut, so he'll have to come back tomorrow.

{只好|zhǐ hǎo} and {不得不|bù dé bù} are close. {只好|zhǐ hǎo} sounds resigned and goes with what actually happened; {不得不|bù dé bù} sounds forced
and can be about any time. The first half of a {只好|zhǐ hǎo} sentence usually gives the reason.

## {差点儿|chà diǎnr}: almost (but it didn't happen)

{差点儿|chà diǎnr} chàdiǎnr (also {差|chà}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}) is "almost, nearly": something came close to happening and didn't.

{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{迟到|chí dào}。 — I was nearly late today.

{我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{带|dài}{钥匙|yào shi}。 — I almost forgot my keys.

Now the puzzle. For something you *don't want*, adding {没|méi} changes nothing:

| Chinese | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 | I was nearly late (but wasn't). |
| {我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi}{迟到|chí dào}。 | I was nearly late (but wasn't). |

Why? With {差点儿|chà diǎnr}, the speaker is relieved: the bad thing was close, and it didn't happen. The {没|méi} in
the second sentence just underlines "it didn't happen"; it doesn't flip the meaning, because no one
says they "nearly weren't late" as if that were a disaster. Both are common.

For something you *do want*, {没|méi} does change the meaning:

| Chinese | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{了|le}。 | I almost got it (but didn't: a pity). |
| {我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}。 | I almost didn't get it (but I did: lucky). |

So: bad event, with or without {没|méi}, "it nearly happened". Good event, {差点儿|chà diǎnr} alone is "nearly, but no",
and {差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi} is "nearly missed it, but made it".

## Renting: {租|zū}, {出租|chū zū}, {房东|fáng dōng}, {房租|fáng zū}

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {租|zū} | to rent (as the tenant); to hire | {我们|wǒ men}{租|zū}{了|le}{一|yí}{套|tào}{房子|fáng zi}。 We've rented a flat. |
| {出租|chū zū} | to rent out, let | {这个|zhè ge}{房子|fáng zi}{出租|chū zū}。 This flat is to let. |
| {房东|fáng dōng} | landlord, landlady | {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{房东|fáng dōng}{是|shì}{唐|Táng}{阿姨|ā yí}。 Our landlady is Auntie Tang. |
| {房租|fáng zū} | rent | {房租|fáng zū}{每|měi}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{三千|sān qiān}{块|kuài}。 The rent is three thousand a month. |

- {租|zū} is both directions in English (rent from / rent out); in Chinese {租|zū} is the tenant's verb and {出租|chū zū} the
  owner's. {出租车|chū zū chē} (HSK 1) is a car for hire: a taxi.
- {一|yí}{套|tào}{房子|fáng zi} (a flat, a house): {套|tào} (lesson 10's character, an HSK 5 word) counts sets of rooms.

扌 (hand) is in five of today's characters, all things your hands do: {擦|cā} (wipe), {挂|guà} (hang), {拉|lā} (pull),

- {脱|tuō} tuō: flesh ⺼ + {兑|duì} duì. {兑|duì} is the sound part of {说|shuō} shuō and {阅|yuè} yuè ({阅读|yuè dú}, lesson 03) too: the
  vowels have drifted, but the family is easy to spot.
- {厕|cè} cè: under {厂|chǎng}, {则|zé} zé ({否则|fǒu zé}, lesson 11). {则|zé} gives cè in {侧|cè} (side) and {测|cè} (to measure).

- {底|dǐ} dǐ: {广|guǎng} + {氐|dī} dī, the sound part of {低|dī} (lesson 09).
- {破|pò} pò: stone {石|shí} + {皮|pí} pí (lesson 06): breaking stone.
- {敲|qiāo} qiāo: {高|gāo} gāo + {攴|pū} (a hand with a stick): knocking.
- {袜|wà} wà: clothing 衤 + {末|mò} mò. Traditional {襪|wà} has {蔑|miè} on the right.

### Two characters from the {说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì}

- {户|hù} hù: the {说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì} explains {户|hù} as one leaf of a door: "half a {门|mén}". So it's a door, then a household

- {弄|nòng} nòng: the {说文解字|Shuō wén jiě zì} has {玉|yù} (jade, written {王|wáng} here) held in two hands {廾|gǒng}: "to play with". Today it's
  the spoken "do, make".

- {底|dǐ} dǐ and {低|dī} dī (lesson 09): the same sound part {氐|dī}; {底|dǐ} has {广|guǎng} (a building: the base), {低|dī} has 亻.

- {推|tuī} tuī and {准|zhǔn} zhǔn (lesson 17): 扌 + {隹|zhuī} against 冫 + {隹|zhuī}.

- **{乱|luàn}**: {舌|shé} first (6 strokes), then the vertical-bend-hook last.
- **{套|tào}**: {大|dà} on top (3), then {镸|cháng} underneath: a horizontal, the vertical, three horizontals, then the
  turning stroke and the dot.
- **{弄|nòng}**: {王|wáng} first (horizontal, horizontal, vertical, horizontal), then the three strokes of {廾|gǒng} (a
  horizontal, a left-falling stroke, a vertical).
- **{支|zhī}**: {十|shí} (2 strokes), then {又|yòu} (the horizontal-left-falling stroke, the right-falling stroke).
- **{厅|tīng}**: {厂|chǎng}, then {丁|dīng} (a horizontal, then the vertical hook).

## Reading: a flat to let

A notice on the board of the compound's entrance, in the brief written style of such ads. {一|yí}{室|shì}{一|yì}{厅|tīng}
(one bedroom, one living room) is how flats are described; {平方米|píng fāng mǐ} is a square metre (an HSK 6 word).

> **{房屋|fáng wū}{出租|chū zū}**
>
> {新城|Xīn chéng}{小区|xiǎo qū}{五|wǔ}{号|hào}{楼|lóu}{二|èr}{层|céng}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{套|tào}{房子|fáng zi}{出租|chū zū}，{一|yí}{室|shì}{一|yì}{厅|tīng}，{四十|sì shí}{平方米|píng fāng mǐ}。
>
> {房间|fáng jiān}{和|hé}{客厅|kè tīng}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{亮|liàng}，{家具|jiā jù}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}：{床|chuáng}、{桌子|zhuō zi}、{椅子|yǐ zi}、{沙发|shā fā}，{客厅|kè tīng}{里|lǐ}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{台|tái}{电视|diàn shì}。{厨房|chú fáng}{和|hé}{厕所|cè suǒ}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{干净|gān jìng}，{楼|lóu}{下|xià}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{院子|yuàn zi}。
>
> {周围|zhōu wéi}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}：{小区|xiǎo qū}{门口|mén kǒu}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{超市|chāo shì}，{走路|zǒu lù}{五|wǔ}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{地铁|dì tiě}{站|zhàn}，{附近|fù jìn}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{医院|yī yuàn}{和|hé}{银行|yín háng}。
>
> {房子|fáng zi}{在|zài}{二|èr}{层|céng}，{没有|méi yǒu}{电梯|diàn tī}，{但是|dàn shì}{上下|shàng xià}{楼|lóu}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}。{客厅|kè tīng}{的|de}{窗户|chuāng hu}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{对面|duì miàn}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{公园|gōng yuán}，{环境|huán jìng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。{房东|fáng dōng}{不|bú}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{这里|zhè lǐ}，{房子|fáng zi}{有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}{可以|kě yǐ}{给|gěi}{他|tā}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}，{他|tā}{会|huì}{马上|mǎ shàng}{找|zhǎo}{人|rén}{来|lái}{修理|xiū lǐ}。{至少|zhì shǎo}{租|zū}{一|yì}{年|nián}。
>
> {厨房|chú fáng}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{冰箱|bīng xiāng}{和|hé}{洗衣机|xǐ yī jī}，{都|dōu}{是|shì}{去年|qù nián}{新|xīn}{买|mǎi}{的|de}。
>
> {房租|fáng zū}{每|měi}{月|yuè}{三千|sān qiān}{元|yuán}，{水|shuǐ}{电|diàn}{费|fèi}{自己|zì jǐ}{付|fù}。
>
> {要求|yāo qiú}：{爱|ài}{干净|gān jìng}；{不|bù}{能|néng}{养|yǎng}{猫|māo}、{狗|gǒu}；{晚上|wǎn shang}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{以后|yǐ hòu}{请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào}{大|dà}{声|shēng}{放|fàng}{音乐|yīn yuè}。
>
> {有|yǒu}{兴趣|xìng qù}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}，{请|qǐng}{给|gěi}{房东|fáng dōng}{钱|qián}{先生|xiān sheng}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}：123 4567 8910（{晚上|wǎn shang}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{以后|yǐ hòu}{不|bù}{接|jiē}{电话|diàn huà}）。

{房屋|fáng wū} is the written word for a house or flat; {水|shuǐ}{电|diàn}{费|fèi} water and electricity bills ({费|fèi}, a fee, lesson 15); {大|dà}{声|shēng}
loudly; {接|jiē}{电话|diàn huà} to answer the phone. {钱|qián} Qián is a surname here.

1. What's in the flat?
2. What do you pay on top of the rent?
3. Name two of the landlord's conditions.
4. What kind of person do you think {钱|qián}{先生|xiān sheng} hopes to find?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. A bed, a table, chairs and a sofa, and a television in the living room ({家具|jiā jù}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}……); a clean kitchen and
   toilet, and a small yard downstairs.
2. The water and electricity bills ({水|shuǐ}{电|diàn}{费|fèi}{自己|zì jǐ}{付|fù}).
3. Any two of: keep it clean ({爱|ài}{干净|gān jìng}); no cats or dogs ({不|bù}{能|néng}{养|yǎng}{猫|māo}、{狗|gǒu}); no loud music after ten at night.
4. A quiet, tidy person without pets: someone like a student or a young worker who comes home and
   goes to bed at a regular hour. His own rule of no calls after nine, and his no-music-after-ten rule,
   suggest he likes a quiet life too. (Other answers are fine if the notice supports them.)

"**Flat to let.** A flat to let in Building 5 of the Xincheng compound, second floor: one bedroom, one
living room, forty square metres. The bedroom and living room are both bright, and it's fully
furnished: a bed, a table, chairs and a sofa, and a television in the living room. The kitchen and
toilet are very clean, and there's a small yard downstairs. Very convenient: there's a supermarket
right at the compound gate, it's a five-minute walk to the metro station, and there's a hospital and a bank
nearby. The flat is on the second floor; there's no lift, but the stairs are easy. The living-room
window is big and looks onto a small park opposite: a lovely setting. The landlord doesn't live
here; if there's a problem with the flat, ring him and he'll get someone to fix it straight away.
Minimum let one year. There's a fridge and a washing machine in the kitchen, both bought new last
year. Rent 3,000 yuan a month; water and electricity paid by the tenant. Requirements: tidy; no
cats or dogs; no loud music after 10 p.m. If you're interested, please ring the landlord, Mr Qian:
123 4567 8910 (no calls after 9 p.m.)."
</details>

## Write it: a sentence about a picture

1. A young woman runs for a bus; the doors are closing just as she jumps on. Word: {差点儿|chà diǎnr}
2. Rain is pouring down; a man without an umbrella stands in a shop doorway, waiting. Word: {只好|zhǐ hǎo}
3. A boy's bedroom with clothes, books and shoes all over the floor. Word: {乱|luàn}

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {她|tā}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi}{赶上|gǎn shàng}{公共汽车|gōng gòng qì chē}。 — She nearly missed the bus. ({赶上|gǎn shàng}, to catch, is lesson 17's word; {差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi}{赶上|gǎn shàng}
  is a good event that nearly didn't happen.)
- {雨|yǔ}{太|tài}{大|dà}{了|le}，{他|tā}{没|méi}{带|dài}{伞|sǎn}，{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{在|zài}{商店|shāng diàn}{门口|mén kǒu}{等|děng}{着|zhe}。 — It was pouring and he had no umbrella, so he had to wait in the
  shop doorway.
- {他|tā}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{太|tài}{乱|luàn}{了|le}，{得|děi}{好好|hǎo hǎo}{收拾|shōu shi}{一下|yí xià}。 — His room is a mess: it needs a proper tidy.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At home
{钥匙|yào shi}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{不得不|bù dé bù}{找|zhǎo}{人|rén}{开|kāi}{门|mén}。
= I'd lost my key, so I had no choice but to get someone to open the door.
{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{班|bān}{地铁|dì tiě}{走|zǒu}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{打车|dǎ chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。
= The last train had gone, so we had to take a taxi home.
{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{迟到|chí dào}。
= I was nearly late today.
{房间|fáng jiān}{太|tài}{乱|luàn}{了|le}，{快|kuài}{收拾|shōu shi}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
= The room's a mess: let's tidy it.
{厕所|cè suǒ}{的|de}{灯|dēng}{不|bú}{亮|liàng}{了|le}。
= The light in the toilet isn't working.
{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{敲|qiāo}{门|mén}。
= Someone's knocking at the door.
```

## Pronunciation

- {差点儿|chà diǎnr} chàdiǎnr: {差|chà} is chà here (as in {差不多|chà bu duō}), and {点儿|diǎnr} is one syllable, diǎnr.
- {不得不|bù dé bù} bùdébù: {得|dé} is dé here (don't say děi), so the first {不|bù} stays bù; the last {不|bù} changes like any other: {不得不|bù dé bú}{去|qù}, but {不得不|bù dé bù}{走|zǒu}.
- {窗户|chuāng hu} chuānghu, {钥匙|yào shi} yàoshi, {收拾|shōu shi} shōushi: light second syllables.
- {空|kōng} kōng (empty) and {空|kòng} (free time): one character, two tones.
- {理发|lǐ fà} lǐfà: the second syllable is fà (hair, as in {头发|tóu fa}), not fā (to send).
- {弄|nòng} nòng: the -ong is the same as in {农|nóng} and {龙|lóng}; it isn't nèng (heard in some dialects).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{不得不|bù dé bú}{不|bú}{去|qù}~~: one {不得不|bù dé bù} is enough: {我|wǒ}{不得不|bù dé bú}{去|qù} (I had to go) or {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù} (I can't go).
- ~~{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{我们|wǒ men}{打车|dǎ chē}~~: {只好|zhǐ hǎo} is an adverb, after the subject: {我们|wǒ men}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{打车|dǎ chē}.
- {我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi}{迟到|chí dào} for "I was nearly late" is right, and so is {我|wǒ}{差点儿|chà diǎnr}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}. Don't "correct" one to the other.
- {窗户|chuāng hu}{坏|huài}{了|le} for broken glass is heard, but {窗户|chuāng hu}{破|pò}{了|le} is the exact word; {坏|huài} is for things that stop working.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{租|zū}{出|chū}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{房子|fáng zi}~~: the owner's verb is {出租|chū zū}: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{房子|fáng zi}{出租|chū zū} or {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{房子|fáng zi}{租|zū}{出去|chū qù}{了|le}.
- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{家具|jiā jù}~~: furniture counts with {件|jiàn}: {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{家具|jiā jù}.

## Key points

- Double negation is a strong positive: {不得不|bù dé bù} (have no choice but to), {不|bù}{能|néng}{不|bù} (must), {没有|méi yǒu}…{不|bù} (everyone),
  {非|fēi}…{不|bù}{可|kě} (simply must).
- {只好|zhǐ hǎo} + verb: so (I) had no choice but to; resigned, after a reason.
- {差点儿|chà diǎnr} (+ {没|méi}) + an unwanted event: it nearly happened (both forms). With a wanted event, {差点儿|chà diǎnr} = nearly,
  but no; {差点儿|chà diǎnr}{没|méi} = nearly missed, but made it.
- {租|zū} (to rent), {出租|chū zū} (to let), {房东|fáng dōng}, {房租|fáng zū}; rooms: {客厅|kè tīng}, {厕所|cè suǒ}, {院子|yuàn zi}, {窗户|chuāng hu}; {家具|jiā jù}, {镜子|jìng zi}, {钥匙|yào shi}, {对面|duì miàn}, {周围|zhōu wéi}, {底下|dǐ xia}.
- {修|xiū} / {修理|xiū lǐ}, {擦|cā}, {收拾|shōu shi}, {整理|zhěng lǐ}, {挂|guà}, {推|tuī} / {拉|lā}, {敲|qiāo}, {弄|nòng}; {破|pò} (cracked, torn) vs {坏|huài} (not working); {乱|luàn}, {亮|liàng}, {响|xiǎng}, {空|kōng} kōng.
- New characters: {袜|wà} {套|tào} {脱|tuō} {质|zhì} {支|zhī} {厕|cè} {窗|chuāng} {户|hù} {擦|cā} {底|dǐ} {挂|guà} {具|jù} {厅|tīng} {拉|lā} {乱|luàn} {弄|nòng} {破|pò} {敲|qiāo} {拾|shí} {推|tuī}; handwriting: {套|tào} {支|zhī} {挂|guà} {拉|lā} {弄|nòng} {推|tuī}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Tai chi and martial arts: 太极拳, 少林 and 武术
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In HSK 1 (lesson 25h1) you watched people doing tai chi in a park: {打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán}. Lesson 07 gave you the
words for working out, and {功夫|gōng fu} (kung fu). This lesson goes further into China's martial arts: where
tai chi comes from and why it has several styles, the Shaolin Temple, and {武术|wǔ shù} as a modern
competitive sport. The facts come from UNESCO, China's intangible-heritage website and the sports
federations (see the end); the Chinese is our own.

Three words to start:

- {武术|wǔ shù} wǔshù (an HSK 5 word): the martial arts as a whole, and the modern sport. {武|wǔ} is "martial, military"
  and {术|shù} "skill, art" ({技术|jì shù}, lesson 27).
- {功夫|gōng fu} gōngfu (lesson 07): the everyday word, and the one that went into English as "kung fu". In Chinese it
  also means skill and effort in anything: {他|tā}{的|de}{汉字|hàn zì}{写|xiě}{得|de}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{功夫|gōng fu} (his characters show real skill).
- {太极拳|tài jí quán} tàijíquán: tai chi. {太|tài}{极|jí} is the "supreme ultimate" of Chinese philosophy (the turning circle of
  yin and yang), and {拳|quán} quán is "fist", a style of boxing.

## {太极拳|tài jí quán}: slow, and three hundred years old

According to UNESCO, which added Taijiquan to its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural
Heritage of Humanity in 2020, tai chi began in the mid-seventeenth century in {温县|Wēn Xiàn} (Wenxian County), in
{河南|Hé nán} (Henan Province), and is practised all over China by people of all ages. China's own heritage
website names the place more exactly: {陈家沟|Chén jiā gōu} (Chenjiagou), a village in {温县|Wēn Xiàn}, where {陈王廷|Chén Wáng tíng} (Chen Wangting)
created what is now called Chen-style tai chi at the end of the Ming dynasty and the start of the Qing.

From that one village, tai chi spread and divided into *styles* ({流派|liú pài} liúpài), each named after the
family or the master who passed it on. China's heritage website lists six that have spread at home
and abroad:

| Style | Pinyin | Named after |
|---|---|---|
| {陈|Chén}{式|shì} | Chén shì | the {陈|Chén} family of {陈家沟|Chén jiā gōu} |
| {杨|Yáng}{式|shì} | Yáng shì | {杨|Yáng}, a master |
| {武|Wǔ}{式|shì} | Wǔ shì | {武|Wǔ}, a master |
| {吴|Wú}{式|shì} | Wú shì | {吴|Wú}, a master |
| {孙|Sūn}{式|shì} | Sūn shì | {孙|Sūn}, a master |
| {和|Hé}{式|shì} | Hé shì | {和|Hé}, a master |

{式|shì} (as in {方式|fāng shì}, lesson 25, and {正式|zhèng shì}, lesson 13) is "style, form". Two of the styles are both "Wu" in
English: {武|Wǔ}{式|shì} Wǔ (third tone, "martial") and {吴|Wú}{式|shì} Wú (second tone, a surname). The tones keep them apart.

Tai chi is slow: the whole body moves in soft, circular movements ({动作|dòng zuò}) while the mind stays calm and
the breathing even. UNESCO describes it as working "in concert with breath regulation and the
cultivation of a righteous and neutral mind". Many people practise it for exercise, often early in the
morning in parks, in groups behind a leader.

## {少林|Shào lín}: the temple and its kung fu

The other famous name is {少林寺|Shào lín sì} (Shàolín Sì), the Shaolin Temple, a Buddhist temple on {嵩山|Sōng shān} (Mount Song),
near {登封|Dēng fēng} (Dengfeng) in {河南|Hé nán}, the same province as {陈家沟|Chén jiā gōu}. China's heritage website says it was founded in
495, under the Northern Wei ({北魏|Běi Wèi}), and that {少林|Shào lín}{功夫|gōng fu} (Shaolin kung fu) grew up inside its Buddhist life:
at first to protect the temple, then, over more than 1,500 years, into a whole system of fist forms,
weapon forms and exercises. Hundreds of routines have been practised there over the centuries, and 255 are still passed on today.

{寺|sì} sì is a Buddhist temple: {少林寺|Shào lín sì}. You'll often hear {少林|Shào lín} alone for the temple and its kung fu, as in
{少林|Shào lín}{功夫|gōng fu}.

## {武术|wǔ shù}: the modern sport

As a sport, {武术|wǔ shù} is organised by the International Wushu Federation, founded in Beijing in 1990,
during the 11th Asian Games ({亚运会|Yà yùn huì}). Wushu has been on the Asian Games programme since those same
Games. Competitions have two parts:

| Event | Pinyin | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| {套路|tào lù} | tàolù | routines (forms): set sequences, with or without weapons, judged on movement and skill |
| {散打|sǎn dǎ} | sǎndǎ | sparring: two fighters, in weight classes |

{套路|tào lù} has {套|tào} (a set, lesson 10's character) and {路|lù} (a road, a way): a set path of movements. Tai chi is one of
the {套路|tào lù} events, beside the fast long-fist ({长拳|cháng quán}) and southern-fist ({南拳|nán quán}) styles.

## Words for watching and doing

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán} | to do tai chi ({打|dǎ}, as for ball games) |
| {练|liàn}{功夫|gōng fu} / {练|liàn}{武术|wǔ shù} | to practise kung fu / martial arts |
| {动作|dòng zuò} (lesson 07) | a movement |
| {慢|màn} / {快|kuài} | slow / fast |
| {放松|fàng sōng} (lesson 07) | to relax |
| {教练|jiào liàn} (lesson 07) | a coach |
| {比赛|bǐ sài} (HSK 3) | a competition, a match |

## Reading: tai chi in the park

{安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) has started doing tai chi in the park near the {新城|Xīn chéng} compound on Saturday mornings. She writes
about it for her Chinese class.

> **{在|zài}{公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{学|xué}{太极拳|tài jí quán}**
>
> {我们|wǒ men}{小区|xiǎo qū}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{公园|gōng yuán}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早晨|zǎo chén}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{在|zài}{那儿|nàr}{锻炼|duàn liàn}。{上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}，{我|wǒ}{开始|kāi shǐ}{跟|gēn}{齐|Qí}{大爷|dà ye}{学|xué}{太极拳|tài jí quán}。{齐|Qí}{大爷|dà ye}{七十|qī shí}{多|duō}{岁|suì}{了|le}，{打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán}{已经|yǐ jīng}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{四十|sì shí}{年|nián}。
>
> {第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{上课|shàng kè}，{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{太极拳|tài jí quán}{很|hěn}{容易|róng yì}，{因为|yīn wèi}{动作|dòng zuò}{那么|nà me}{慢|màn}。{可是|kě shì}{只|zhǐ}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{十|shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{出|chū}{了|le}{一|yì}{身|shēn}{汗|hàn}。{齐|Qí}{大爷|dà ye}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}："{慢|màn}{不|bù}{等于|děng yú}{容易|róng yì}。{动作|dòng zuò}{越|yuè}{慢|màn}，{越|yuè}{要|yào}{用心|yòng xīn}。"
>
