{齐|Qí}{大爷|dà ye} is "Grandpa Qi", a polite name for an old man ({大爷|dà ye} dàye, in Beijing). {等于|děng yú} is "to equal"; {用心|yòng xīn} "to put
your mind to it"; {村子|cūn zi} a village ({村|cūn}, lesson 26); {忘掉|wàng diào} "to forget, put out of mind" ({掉|diào}, lesson 20). {联合国教科文组织|Lián hé guó Jiào kē wén Zǔ zhī} is UNESCO; {列入|liè rù} "to enter (on a list)", {人类|rén lèi} "humanity",
{非|fēi}{物质|wù zhì}{文化|wén huà}{遗产|yí chǎn} "intangible cultural heritage", {名录|míng lù} "a list": all words for reading, not for learning now.

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"**Learning tai chi in the park.** There's a park next to our compound, and every morning lots of
people exercise there. Last month I started learning tai chi with Grandpa Qi. He's over seventy, and
he's been doing tai chi for forty years.

At my first class I thought tai chi would be easy, because the movements are so slow. But after only
ten minutes I was sweating all over. Grandpa Qi laughed and said, 'Slow doesn't mean easy. The slower
the movement, the more you have to concentrate.'

Grandpa Qi told me that tai chi began in a small village in Henan, more than three hundred years
ago. Later it divided into different styles, such as Chen, Yang and Wu, and each style's movements are
a little different. He himself does Yang style. In 2020 UNESCO put tai chi on its list of the
'Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity'.

Grandpa Qi also said that not everyone who does tai chi is old. Lots of young people come to learn
after work now: some to keep fit, some to relax and forget the pressure of work.

My friend Wang Fang says she learned a little tai chi at secondary school, but didn't keep it up.
She says she'll come with me next month.

Now I go to the park every Saturday. My movements still aren't good enough, but after tai chi I feel
much lighter, in body and in mind. Grandpa Qi says learning tai chi is like learning Chinese: you
can't rush it, you have to practise every day."
</details>

## Key points

- {武术|wǔ shù} (the martial arts; the sport), {功夫|gōng fu} (kung fu; skill), {太极拳|tài jí quán} (tai chi: {打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán}).
- Tai chi began in the mid-17th century in {温县|Wēn Xiàn}, {河南|Hé nán} (UNESCO; China's heritage site names {陈家沟|Chén jiā gōu} and
  {陈王廷|Chén Wáng tíng}); UNESCO's Representative List since 2020. Styles named after families or masters: {陈|Chén} {杨|Yáng} {武|Wǔ} {吴|Wú} {孙|Sūn} {和|Hé}.
- {少林寺|Shào lín sì}: a Buddhist temple on {嵩山|Sōng shān} in {河南|Hé nán}, founded in 495; {少林|Shào lín}{功夫|gōng fu} grew up there.
- Modern wushu: the International Wushu Federation (Beijing, 1990), at the Asian Games since 1990;
  {套路|tào lù} (routines) and {散打|sǎn dǎ} (sparring).
- {武|Wǔ}{式|shì} Wǔ and {吴|Wú}{式|shì} Wú: two styles that only the tones tell apart.

lessons.title: Zhang Heng's earthquake detector: 张衡 and the 地动仪
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 3 (lesson 05h2) met the four great inventions: paper, printing, the compass and gunpowder. This
lesson is about one man of the Eastern Han dynasty, {张衡|Zhāng Héng} Zhāng Héng, and the instrument he is best known
for: a bronze vessel that, the old history says, could tell that an earthquake had happened far away,
and in which direction. Nobody knows exactly how it worked, and that's part of the story: you'll read
what the source says, how modern scientists have tried to rebuild it, and what is still guesswork.

Words you'll need (mostly HSK 5 and 6, for reading only): {地震|dì zhèn} dìzhèn (earthquake), {仪器|yí qì} yíqì (instrument),
{铜|tóng} tóng (bronze, copper), {龙|lóng} lóng (dragon), {天文|tiān wén} tiānwén (astronomy), {发明|fā míng} fāmíng (to invent; an invention),
{模型|mó xíng} móxíng (a model), {古代|gǔ dài} gǔdài (ancient times), {记录|jì lù} jìlù (a record).

## Who was {张衡|Zhāng Héng}?

{张衡|Zhāng Héng} lived from 78 to 139, under the Eastern Han ({东汉|Dōng Hàn}, 25–220). He came from {南阳|Nán yáng} (Nanyang), in what is
now {河南|Hé nán} (Henan) Province. He was an official at court (for years in charge of astronomy and the calendar), an astronomer, a
mathematician and a writer: his 《{二京赋|Èr jīng fù}》 (*Rhapsody on the Two Capitals*) is counted among the great long
poems of the Han. His astronomy book, 《{灵宪|Líng xiàn}》
(*Língxiàn*), describes the universe, the sun, the moon and the stars.

He is remembered above all for two instruments: a water-driven armillary sphere for showing the
movement of the stars, and the earthquake detector, the {地动仪|dì dòng yí} (dìdòngyí: "earth-movement instrument").

## The {地动仪|dì dòng yí}: what the old history says

The source is the 《{后汉书|Hòu Hàn shū}》 (*Hòu Hàn shū*, the *Book of the Later Han*), a history by {范晔|Fàn Yè} (Fàn Yè), who wrote it in the fifth century and died in 445: some three
centuries after {张衡|Zhāng Héng}'s time. Its life of {张衡|Zhāng Héng} opens the account like this:

> {阳嘉|Yáng jiā}{元年|yuán nián}，{复|fù}{造|zào}{候风地动仪|hòu fēng dì dòng yí}。
>
> In the first year of Yangjia (132), he also made the {候风地动仪|hòu fēng dì dòng yí}, the "wind-watching earth-movement
> instrument".

{阳嘉|Yáng jiā} is the name of a reign period; its first year ({元年|yuán nián}) was 132. In {复造|fù zào} the first character is "also, further", and {造|zào} is "to
make". The account then describes the instrument, which we put in modern words:

- It was cast in bronze ({铜|tóng}), round, shaped like a large wine vessel, and eight {尺|chǐ} (an old unit of
  length) across.
- Around the outside were eight dragons ({龙|lóng}), facing eight directions, each holding a bronze ball in
  its mouth. Below each dragon sat a toad with its mouth open.
- Inside was a mechanism. When the earth moved, one dragon's mouth opened, its ball dropped into the
  toad below, and the direction of that dragon showed where the earthquake was.

Then comes the story that made it famous. Once a ball dropped, but nobody in the capital, {洛阳|Luò yáng} (Luòyáng),
had felt anything, and the scholars there doubted the instrument. A few days later a messenger
arrived: {果|guǒ}{地震|dì zhèn}{陇西|Lǒng xī}, "there had indeed been an earthquake in {陇西|Lǒng xī}" (Lǒngxī, far to the west, in today's
Gansu). After that, the history says, everyone believed in it.

Which earthquake was it? The history doesn't give the year. It's usually taken to be the earthquake
of 138 that other records name; some modern researchers argue for one in 134. Dates for the {地动仪|dì dòng yí} story
are best given as "in the 130s".

## How did it work? Reconstructions

The instrument itself is long lost, and the 《{后汉书|Hòu Hàn shū}》 says little about its inside: only that there was a
central pillar, {都柱|dū zhù} (dūzhù), with eight channels around it. Everything else is reconstruction.

- **1951**: the scholar {王振铎|Wáng Zhèn duó} (Wáng Zhènduó) built a model with an upright pole in the middle: when
  the ground shook, the pole would fall towards one dragon and push out its ball. For decades this
  model was the picture of the {地动仪|dì dòng yí} in Chinese textbooks, often without saying it was a modern
  reconstruction. Critics point out that an upright pole falls over at the smallest vibration, so it
  couldn't work as a detector.
- **The 2000s**: a team of seismologists and museum researchers led by {冯锐|Féng Ruì} (Féng Ruì) built a new model
  with a hanging pendulum inside, which responds to the side-to-side shaking of an earthquake wave. It
  passed laboratory tests with simulated earthquakes and is shown at the China Science and Technology
  Museum, but there is no report of it detecting a real earthquake far away.

Scholars still disagree. Some doubt that any Han-dynasty instrument could have done what the story
says; others think it could, with the right design. What the original looked like inside, as a Chinese
science newspaper put it, is still a mystery. So the honest summary is: the 《{后汉书|Hòu Hàn shū}》
describes the instrument and one success, and modern models are attempts to make that description
work.

## Watching the sky: the armillary sphere

{张衡|Zhāng Héng} also built a water-driven armillary sphere ({浑天仪|hún tiān yí} húntiānyí): a bronze globe marked with the stars, the
ecliptic and the celestial equator, turned evenly by gears powered by the steady flow of a water clock,
so that it showed the stars rising and setting. It's described as the earliest well-recorded instrument
in the world that showed the movement of the heavens automatically.

It illustrated the {浑天说|hún tiān shuō} (the "enveloping-sky theory"), an older idea that {张衡|Zhāng Héng} developed: the sky is like
an eggshell, and the earth sits inside it like the yolk.

## His name today

In February 2018 China launched a satellite to study the earth's electromagnetic field, in part for
earthquake research. Its name is {张衡一号|Zhāng Héng yī hào}, "Zhang Heng No. 1".

## Reading: {张衡|Zhāng Héng} and the earthquake detector

> **{张衡|Zhāng Héng}{和|hé}{地动仪|dì dòng yí}**
>
> {张衡|Zhāng Héng}{是|shì}{东汉|Dōng Hàn}{的|de}{科学家|kē xué jiā}，{也|yě}{是|shì}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{很|hěn}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{作家|zuò jiā}。{他|tā}{对|duì}{天文|tiān wén}{特别|tè bié}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}，{做|zuò}{过|guo}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{种|zhǒng}{仪器|yí qì}。
>
> {公元|gōng yuán}132{年|nián}，{张衡|Zhāng Héng}{做|zuò}{成|chéng}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}"{地动仪|dì dòng yí}"。《{后汉书|Hòu Hàn shū}》{上|shàng}{说|shuō}，{地动仪|dì dòng yí}{是|shì}{用|yòng}{铜|tóng}{做|zuò}{的|de}，{样子|yàng zi}{像|xiàng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{酒器|jiǔ qì}。{外面|wài miàn}{有|yǒu}{八|bā}{条|tiáo}{龙|lóng}，{对|duì}{着|zhe}{八|bā}{个|gè}{方向|fāng xiàng}，{每|měi}{条|tiáo}{龙|lóng}{的|de}{嘴|zuǐ}{里|lǐ}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{铜|tóng}{球|qiú}。{下面|xià miàn}{有|yǒu}{八|bā}{只|zhī}{蛤蟆|há ma}，{都|dōu}{张|zhāng}{着|zhe}{嘴|zuǐ}。{哪个|nǎ ge}{方向|fāng xiàng}{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{地震|dì zhèn}，{那个|nà ge}{方向|fāng xiàng}{的|de}{龙|lóng}{嘴|zuǐ}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{球|qiú}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{掉|diào}{下来|xià lái}，{落|luò}{到|dào}{蛤蟆|há ma}{的|de}{嘴|zuǐ}{里|lǐ}。
>
> {有|yǒu}{一|yí}{次|cì}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{球|qiú}{掉|diào}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}，{可是|kě shì}{首都|shǒu dū}{洛阳|Luò yáng}{的|de}{人|rén}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{感觉|gǎn jué}{到|dào}{地震|dì zhèn}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{相信|xiāng xìn}。{过|guò}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}，{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{从|cóng}{很|hěn}{远|yuǎn}{的|de}{陇西|Lǒng xī}{来|lái}，{说|shuō}{那里|nà lǐ}{真|zhēn}{的|de}{发生|fā shēng}{了|le}{地震|dì zhèn}。{从此|cóng cǐ}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{相信|xiāng xìn}{了|le}{地动仪|dì dòng yí}。
>
> {可惜|kě xī}{的|de}{是|shì}，{张衡|Zhāng Héng}{的|de}{地动仪|dì dòng yí}{早|zǎo}{就|jiù}{没有|méi yǒu}{了|le}，《{后汉书|Hòu Hàn shū}》{里|lǐ}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}{写|xiě}{清楚|qīng chu}{它|tā}{里面|lǐ miàn}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{样子|yàng zi}{的|de}。{今天|jīn tiān}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{地动仪|dì dòng yí}，{都|dōu}{是|shì}{现代|xiàn dài}{科学家|kē xué jiā}{根据|gēn jù}{这些|zhè xiē}{记录|jì lù}{做|zuò}{的|de}{模型|mó xíng}。{它们|tā men}{跟|gēn}{原来|yuán lái}{的|de}{一样|yí yàng}{不|bu}{一样|yí yàng}，{谁|shéi}{也|yě}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}。
>
> {除了|chú le}{地动仪|dì dòng yí}，{张衡|Zhāng Héng}{还|hái}{做|zuò}{过|guo}{一|yí}{个|gè}{用|yòng}{水|shuǐ}{带动|dài dòng}{的|de}{浑天仪|hún tiān yí}，{人|rén}{们|men}{可以|kě yǐ}{从|cóng}{它|tā}{上面|shàng miàn}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{星星|xīng xing}{在|zài}{天上|tiān shàng}{是|shì}{怎么|zěn me}{运动|yùn dòng}{的|de}。2018{年|nián}，{中国|Zhōng guó}{发射|fā shè}{了|le}{一|yì}{颗|kē}{研究|yán jiū}{地球|dì qiú}{的|de}{卫星|wèi xīng}，{它|tā}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}{就|jiù}{叫|jiào}"{张衡一号|Zhāng Héng yī hào}"。

{酒器|jiǔ qì} is a wine vessel; {蛤蟆|há ma} háma a toad ({蟾蜍|chán chú} chánchú is the more formal word); {张|zhāng}{着|zhe}{嘴|zuǐ} "with mouths open"
({张|zhāng}, to open: HSK 3 has it as a measure word). {博物馆|bó wù guǎn} is a museum, {根据|gēn jù} "on the basis of" (HSK 3). {公元|gōng yuán} is "CE" and {现代|xiàn dài} "modern"; {带动|dài dòng} is "to drive (a machine)", {发射|fā shè} "to launch", {颗|kē} the measure word
for satellites (and stars), {卫星|wèi xīng} a satellite, {研究|yán jiū} (to study) lesson 27's word and {地球|dì qiú} (the earth) lesson 26's. Later HSK 4 words appear here too: {首都|shǒu dū} (capital, lesson 18), {掉|diào} (to fall),
{从此|cóng cǐ} (from then on) and {原来|yuán lái} (original, all lesson 20), {样子|yàng zi} (appearance, lesson 22), {可惜|kě xī} (a pity, lesson 23)
and {落|luò} (to land, lesson 26).

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

"**Zhang Heng and the earthquake detector.** Zhang Heng was a scientist of the Eastern Han, and also a
famous writer. He was especially interested in astronomy, and made several kinds of instrument.

In 132 CE Zhang Heng completed a 'didongyi', an earthquake detector. According to the *Book of the
Later Han*, it was made of bronze and looked like a very large wine vessel. Around the outside were
eight dragons facing eight directions, each with a bronze ball in its mouth. Below sat eight toads,
all with their mouths open. If an earthquake happened in any direction, the ball would fall from the
mouth of the dragon facing that way and land in a toad's mouth.

Once, a ball fell, but nobody in the capital, Luoyang, had felt any earthquake, and many people didn't
believe it. A few days later someone came from far-off Longxi and said there really had been an
earthquake there. From then on, everyone believed in the instrument.

Sadly, Zhang Heng's detector disappeared long ago, and the *Book of the Later Han* doesn't explain
clearly what was inside it. The detectors in museums today are all models made by modern scientists
from these records. Whether they're the same as the original, nobody knows.

Besides the earthquake detector, Zhang Heng also made a water-driven armillary sphere, on which people
could see how the stars move across the sky. In 2018 China launched a satellite to study the earth,
and it's called 'Zhang Heng No. 1'."
</details>

## Key points

- {张衡|Zhāng Héng} (78–139), Eastern Han, from {南阳|Nán yáng}: official, astronomer, mathematician, writer; author of 《{灵宪|Líng xiàn}》.
- The {候风地动仪|hòu fēng dì dòng yí} ({地动仪|dì dòng yí}), 132 ({阳嘉|Yáng jiā}{元年|yuán nián}): bronze, eight dragons, eight toads; a ball dropped towards the
  direction of the earthquake. The 《{后汉书|Hòu Hàn shū}》 tells of an earthquake in {陇西|Lǒng xī} that it detected (usually dated
  138; some say 134).
- The original is lost. Modern models ({王振铎|Wáng Zhèn duó} 1951, upright pole; {冯锐|Féng Ruì}'s team in the 2000s, hanging
  pendulum) are reconstructions, and how it really worked is still debated.
- A water-driven armillary sphere ({浑天仪|hún tiān yí}) showed the stars turning; the {浑天说|hún tiān shuō} pictured the sky as an egg
  around the earth.
- {张衡一号|Zhāng Héng yī hào}: a satellite launched in 2018, named after him.

lessons.title: A part-time job: advertisements, 要是 and 否则
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 3 follows {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) from graduation into her first work. She studied journalism
({新闻|xīn wén}{专业|zhuān yè}), and this summer a news website is looking for interns. This lesson is the level-4
task of **reading a job advertisement and asking about it**, and of writing a short one yourself.

You'll learn:

- the words of a job advertisement: {招聘|zhāo pìn} (to recruit), {应聘|yìng pìn} (to apply), {条件|tiáo jiàn} (conditions), {年龄|nián líng} (age),
  {性别|xìng bié} (sex), {男性|nán xìng} and {女性|nǚ xìng} (male, female: formal), {工资|gōng zī} (pay), {负责|fù zé} and {负责人|fù zé rén} (to be in charge, the
  person in charge), {符合|fú hé} (to meet requirements);
- {要是|yào shi}…{就|jiù}, the spoken "if", beside {如果|rú guǒ} (HSK 3);
- {否则|fǒu zé}, "otherwise": do this, or else something bad follows;
- {好|hǎo} before a verb, "so that…": {早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{去|qù}，{好|hǎo}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{票|piào} (go early so you can get tickets);
- words for work and jobs: {打工|dǎ gōng}, {干活儿|gàn huór}, {工人|gōng rén}, {工厂|gōng chǎng} and {厂|chǎng}, {师傅|shī fu}, {职业|zhí yè}, {责任|zé rèn}, {辛苦|xīn kǔ}, {专门|zhuān mén}, {普通|pǔ tōng}, {无法|wú fǎ}, and
  in passing {律师|lǜ shī}, {经济|jīng jì} and {生意|shēng yi}.

Two words you'll meet glossed: {编辑|biān jí} (an editor; to edit) and {实习|shí xí} (to work as an intern; {实习生|shí xí shēng}, an
intern). They're HSK 5 words, but you can't talk about Wang Fang's summer without them.

## Reading a job advertisement

A job advertisement is a {招聘|zhāo pìn}{广告|guǎng gào} (a recruitment advertisement): {广告|guǎng gào} is any advertisement, and {招聘|zhāo pìn} is
what the employer does, "to invite applications, to recruit". The person who answers it {应聘|yìng pìn} (applies
for the job). The two words share {聘|pìn} (to engage, to hire), a character you'll learn in lesson 12.

{我们|wǒ men}{公司|gōng sī}{在|zài}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{一|yì}{名|míng}{司机|sī jī}。 — Our company is looking for a driver. ({名|míng}: the measure word for people in
formal writing, as in {两|liǎng}{名|míng}{学生|xué sheng}.)

{她|tā}{去|qù}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{应聘|yìng pìn}，{想|xiǎng}{当|dāng}{编辑|biān jí}。 — She applied to a website: she'd like to be an editor. ({当|dāng}: to work
as.)

Most advertisements have the same parts, often as short headings:

| Heading | Meaning | What follows |
|---|---|---|
| {工作|gōng zuò}{内容|nèi róng} | what the work is | {负责|fù zé}{写|xiě}{新闻|xīn wén} (in charge of writing news items) |
| {条件|tiáo jiàn} / {要求|yāo qiú} | conditions, requirements | age, studies, skills |
| {工资|gōng zī} | pay | {每|měi}{天|tiān}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{元|yuán}, {每|měi}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{五千|wǔ qiān}{元|yuán} |
| {时间|shí jiān} | hours, dates | {周末|zhōu mò}, {七|qī}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{到|dào}{八|bā}{月|yuè}{三十一|sān shí yī}{日|rì} |
| {负责人|fù zé rén} / {联系|lián xì}{人|rén} | the person in charge; the contact person ({联系|lián xì}: lesson 13) | a name and a phone number |

{条件|tiáo jiàn} is the condition you must meet, and {符合|fú hé} is "to meet, to match" it: {你|nǐ}{符合|fú hé}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{条件|tiáo jiàn} (you meet our
requirements). {符合|fú hé} takes words like {条件|tiáo jiàn}, {要求|yāo qiú} and {规定|guī dìng} (rules, lesson 13), never a person.

{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{的|de}{条件|tiáo jiàn}{不|bú}{太|tài}{高|gāo}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{符合|fú hé}。 — The requirements for this job aren't very high: plenty of
students meet them.

Forms and advertisements ask for {年龄|nián líng} (age) and {性别|xìng bié} (sex). {年龄|nián líng} is the formal word; in speech you ask
{多|duō}{大|dà} or {几|jǐ}{岁|suì} (HSK 1). {性别|xìng bié} is answered {男|nán} or {女|nǚ}. The formal words for "male" and "female" are {男性|nán xìng} and
{女性|nǚ xìng}: you meet them in forms, statistics and news. In conversation people say {男|nán}{的|de} and {女|nǚ}{的|de}, or {男人|nán rén} and
{女人|nǚ rén}.

{这个|zhè ge}{职业|zhí yè}{的|de}{女性|nǚ xìng}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}。 — There are more and more women in this profession.

{性别|xìng bié}、{年龄|nián líng}{都|dōu}{没有|méi yǒu}{要求|yāo qiú}，{只要|zhǐ yào}{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{写|xiě}{东西|dōng xi}{就|jiù}{行|xíng}。 — No requirements on sex or age: as long as you like
writing, that's fine.

The pay is {工资|gōng zī} (wages; a salary): {工资|gōng zī}{很|hěn}{高|gāo}, {这个|zhè ge}{月|yuè}{的|de}{工资|gōng zī}{还|hái}{没|méi}{发|fā}. The person in charge is the {负责人|fù zé rén}, from
{负责|fù zé}, "to be responsible for, to be in charge of". {负责|fù zé} takes the job as its object:

{小李|Xiǎo Lǐ}{负责|fù zé}{写|xiě}{广告|guǎng gào}，{我|wǒ}{负责|fù zé}{找|zhǎo}{图片|tú piàn}。 — Xiao Li is in charge of writing the advert and I'll find the
pictures.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{的|de}{负责人|fù zé rén}{是|shì}{郑|Zhèng}{老师|lǎo shī}。 — The person in charge of this round of hiring is Ms Zheng.

(In Chinese newsrooms, schools and publishers, colleagues often address an editor or a senior
colleague as {老师|lǎo shī}, as Wang Fang does with {郑华|Zhèng Huá} below.)

The noun behind {负责|fù zé} is {责任|zé rèn} (responsibility): {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{责任|zé rèn} (it's my responsibility), and an
advertisement may ask for someone {有|yǒu}{责任心|zé rèn xīn} (with a sense of responsibility: {责任|zé rèn} + {心|xīn}).

A few notes:

- {打工|dǎ gōng} is work you do for someone else for a time, often while studying: {在|zài}{咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn}{打工|dǎ gōng}, {暑假|shǔ jià}{打工|dǎ gōng}. It isn't
  a career. {工作|gōng zuò} covers any work, and a permanent job.
- {干活儿|gàn huór} is spoken and down to earth: {干活儿|gàn huór} is what you do with your hands, at home, on a farm or in a
  factory. {干|gàn} here is gàn (to do: HSK 3's {干|gàn}{什么|shén me}). With the traditional script on, this {干|gàn} is written as in {+{干活儿|gàn huór}+}.
- {师傅|shī fu} is a respectful word for anyone with a trade: drivers, cooks, repairers. Calling the taxi
  driver or the person who comes to fix the window {师傅|shī fu} is normal and polite.
- {辛苦|xīn kǔ} is also something you say to thank someone for their effort: {你|nǐ}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}{了|le}！ (Thank you for all your
  hard work!) Say it to a colleague after a long day, or to a delivery driver.
- {专门|zhuān mén} before a verb is "specially, for this one purpose": {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{是|shì}{专门|zhuān mén}{为|wèi}{孩子|hái zi}{写|xiě}{的|de} (this book was written
  specially for children). Before a noun it's "specialised": {专门|zhuān mén}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò} (specialist work).
- {无法|wú fǎ} is the written partner of {没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ} / {不|bù}{能|néng}: {无法|wú fǎ} + a two-syllable verb, usually: {无法|wú fǎ}{回答|huí dá},
  {无法|wú fǎ}{解决|jiě jué} (no way to solve it). In speech, {没|méi}{办法|bàn fǎ} or {没法儿|méi fǎr} is more natural.

Two words in passing: {生意|shēng yi} is business, trade ({做|zuò}{生意|shēng yi}, to do business; {生意|shēng yi}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, business is good), and
{经济|jīng jì} is the economy ({这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}{这里|zhè lǐ}{的|de}{经济|jīng jì}{发展|fā zhǎn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}, the economy here has grown fast these last few years;
{发展|fā zhǎn}: to develop). You'll read them in the news more than you'll say them.

## {要是|yào shi}…{就|jiù}: if (spoken)

{要是|yào shi} means the same as {如果|rú guǒ} (HSK 3) and works the same way: {要是|yào shi} opens the condition, and {就|jiù} goes after
the subject of the second clause. {要是|yào shi} is more spoken; {如果|rú guǒ} suits both speech and writing.

{要是|yào shi}{你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}{吧|ba}。 — If you're free tomorrow, let's go and see a film.

{要是|yào shi}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{就|jiù}{别|bié}{骑|qí}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{了|le}。 — If it rains, don't cycle.

{你|nǐ}{要是|yào shi}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{就|jiù}{告诉|gào su}{他|tā}。 — If you don't want to go, tell him.

As with {如果|rú guǒ}, {要是|yào shi} can stand at the start or after the subject ({你|nǐ}{要是|yào shi}…), and {的话|de huà} can close the clause:
{要是|yào shi}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{舒服|shū fu}{的话|de huà}，{就|jiù}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{吧|ba} (if you're not feeling well, go home and rest).

Note the reading: {要是|yào shi} yào shi, with a light second syllable. It sounds the same as {钥匙|yào shi} (keys, lesson
10): {要是|yào shi}{你|nǐ}{找不到|zhǎo bu dào}{钥匙|yào shi}… (if you can't find your keys…).

## {否则|fǒu zé}: otherwise

{否则|fǒu zé} starts a second clause that says what will happen **if the first doesn't**. The first clause is
usually advice, a rule or something necessary, and the {否则|fǒu zé} clause is the bad result:

{你|nǐ}{得|děi}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{走|zǒu}，{否则|fǒu zé}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào}。 — You'd better leave early, otherwise you'll be late.

{请|qǐng}{写|xiě}{清楚|qīng chu}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ}，{否则|fǒu zé}{我们|wǒ men}{无法|wú fǎ}{通知|tōng zhī}{你|nǐ}。 — Please write your phone number clearly, or we'll have no
way of letting you know. ({通知|tōng zhī}: to notify, lesson 13.)

{出门|chū mén}{要|yào}{带|dài}{上|shàng}{钥匙|yào shi}，{否则|fǒu zé}{就|jiù}{进不了|jìn bu liǎo}{门|mén}。 — Take your keys when you go out, or you won't be able to get in.

So {否则|fǒu zé} = "if not, then…": {你|nǐ}{得|děi}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{走|zǒu}，{否则|fǒu zé}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào} says the same as {如果|rú guǒ}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{走|zǒu}，{你|nǐ}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào}. This
**[[otherwise clause]]** is a condition turned round: instead of "if not A, then B", you say "A, otherwise
B". {否则|fǒu zé} often has {就|jiù} or {会|huì} after it, or {的话|de huà}: {否则|fǒu zé}{的话|de huà} (otherwise).

- {否则|fǒu zé} is a little formal: it's at home in notices, advertisements and careful speech. In everyday
  talk people often say {不然|bù rán} or {要不|yào bù} (both: otherwise, or else): {快|kuài}{点儿|diǎnr}，{不然|bù rán}{来不及|lái bu jí}{了|le} (hurry up, or we
  won't make it: {来不及|lái bu jí}, not have time enough, lesson 17). You'll learn them later; recognise them for now.
- {否则|fǒu zé} joins two clauses. It doesn't start a conversation or answer a question on its own.

## {好|hǎo} + verb: so that

A second clause with {好|hǎo} before its verb says **what the first action makes possible**: "so that
(someone) can…". {好|hǎo} here is not "good": it's an adverb meaning "so as to be able to".

{我们|wǒ men}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{去|qù}，{好|hǎo}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{票|piào}。 — Let's go early so we can get tickets.

{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ}{写|xiě}{下来|xià lái}，{我|wǒ}{好|hǎo}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。 — Write your number down so I can ring you.

{多|duō}{带|dài}{点儿|diǎnr}{钱|qián}，{好|hǎo}{在|zài}{路上|lù shang}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{吃|chī}。 — Take a bit more money so you can buy something to eat on the way.

The {好|hǎo} clause comes second. When it has its own subject, the subject goes before {好|hǎo} ({我|wǒ}{好|hǎo}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}),
as with {就|jiù}. {好|hǎo} is still read hǎo, third tone. Compare {为了|wèi le} (HSK 3), which states a goal and usually
comes first: {为了|wèi le}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{票|piào}，{我们|wǒ men}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{去|qù}. The {好|hǎo} sentence is more spoken and puts the action first.

### Families and look-alikes

- **贝 (shell) for money and value.** Shells were once used as money, and 贝 is in many characters
  about money, buying and owing: 负 (to bear; to owe), 责 (duty; to blame), and ones you
  know: 贵 (expensive), 费 (fee: lesson 15), 货 (goods: lesson 09), 购
  (to buy: lesson 09), 赚 (to earn: lesson 15). In traditional the part is 貝: 負, 責, 貴.
- **生 gives the sound -ing.** 性 xìng is 忄 (the heart) + 生 shēng; you know the same sound part
  in 姓 xìng (surname), 星 xīng (star) and 生 itself. Your nature, {性|xìng}, is what you're born with in
  your heart: that's a memory aid, not a history.
- **令 gives the sound.** 龄 líng is 齿 (teeth) + 令 lìng, which you know in 零 líng (zero) and,
  a little further off, 冷 lěng (cold). A memory aid: you can tell an animal's age by its teeth.
- **尃 in 傅 and 博.** 傅 fu ({师傅|shī fu}) and 博 bó ({博士|bó shì}, lesson 05) share their right half; in 傅 it
  still gives the sound fu, in 博 it no longer matches.
- **厂 and 广.** 广 is 厂 with a dot on top. 广 keeps only the outer frame of traditional 廣;
  厂 is the frame of traditional 廠 (written with 广) without its dot.
- **否 = 不 + 口**: "not" in the mouth, "no". A memory aid that happens to match how it's built.
- **职 and 识.** 职 zhí ({职业|zhí yè}) and 识 shí ({认识|rèn shi}, HSK 1) have the same right half, 只. In
  traditional both have 戠 there: 職 and 識.
- **无 and 無.** Simplified 无 has four strokes; traditional 無 has twelve. Don't confuse 无
  with 天, 元 and 夫: 无's last stroke turns up to the right (a vertical-bend-hook).
- **则 and 责** are both zé. 则 has 刂 (a knife) and means "rule; then" ({否则|fǒu zé}, otherwise);
  责 has 贝 and means "duty" ({负责|fù zé}, {责任|zé rèn}). (Traditional 則 has 貝 on the left too.)

### Stroke order

- **厂**: the horizontal, then the long left-falling stroke: 2 strokes. **广**: the dot first,
  then the same two: 3.
- **无**: two horizontals, the left-falling stroke, then the vertical-bend-hook.
- **修**: 亻, then the short vertical in the middle (stroke 3), then 夂 (left-falling,
  horizontal-left-falling, right-falling), and 彡 last.
- **性**: 忄 first, as in every heart radical: the left dot, the right dot, then the vertical.
- **负**: the left-falling stroke and the bent stroke on top, then 贝: the vertical, the
  horizontal-turn, the left-falling stroke and the dot.

<details>
<summary>A model story</summary>

{暑假|shǔ jià}{到|dào}{了|le}，{小程|Xiǎo Chéng}{想|xiǎng}{找|zhǎo}{个|gè}{地方|dì fang}{打工|dǎ gōng}。{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{广告|guǎng gào}。{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{天|tiān}，{他|tā}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{一|yì}{家|jiā}{咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn}{在|zài}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{学生|xué sheng}，{条件|tiáo jiàn}{他|tā}{都|dōu}{符合|fú hé}。{他|tā}{马上|mǎ shàng}{给|gěi}{咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}，{负责人|fù zé rén}{让|ràng}{他|tā}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{去|qù}{看看|kàn kan}，{他|tā}{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{时间|shí jiān}{和|hé}{地址|dì zhǐ}{写|xiě}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}，{好|hǎo}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{找|zhǎo}{得|de}{到|dào}{地方|dì fang}。{现在|xiàn zài}{他|tā}{每|měi}{个|gè}{周末|zhōu mò}{在|zài}{咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn}{干活儿|gàn huór}，{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}，{但是|dàn shì}{他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}。

— The summer holidays came, and Xiao Cheng wanted to find a part-time job. Every day he looked at job
adverts on his phone. One day he saw that a café was looking for students, and he met all the
requirements. He rang the café at once; the person in charge told him to come and have a look the next
day, so he wrote down the time and the address so that he could find the place the next day. Now he works at the café every
weekend: it's hard work, but he finds it really interesting. ({地址|dì zhǐ}: address, lesson 19.)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Asking about a job
{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{了|le}{你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{广告|guǎng gào}。
= I saw your job advertisement online.
{请问|qǐng wèn}，{我|wǒ}{符合|fú hé}{你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{条件|tiáo jiàn}{吗|ma}？
= Excuse me, do I meet your requirements?
{这|zhè}{次|cì}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{的|de}{负责人|fù zé rén}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}？
= Who's in charge of this round of hiring?
{要是|yào shi}{你们|nǐ men}{需要|xū yào}，{周末|zhōu mò}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{可以|kě yǐ}{来|lái}。
= If you need me, I can come at weekends too.
{请|qǐng}{写|xiě}{清楚|qīng chu}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{电话|diàn huà}{号码|hào mǎ}，{否则|fǒu zé}{我们|wǒ men}{无法|wú fǎ}{通知|tōng zhī}{你|nǐ}。
= Please write your phone number clearly, or we'll have no way to let you know.
{我们|wǒ men}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{去|qù}，{好|hǎo}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{票|piào}。
= Let's go early so we can get tickets.
{你|nǐ}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}{了|le}！
= Thanks for all your hard work!
```

## Pronunciation

- {要是|yào shi} yào shi and {钥匙|yào shi} yào shi (keys) sound the same: fourth tone, then a light syllable. Context
  tells them apart.
- {师傅|shī fu} shī fu: the second syllable is light. {师父|shī fu} (a master who teaches a craft or martial art) is said
  the same way.
- {律师|lǜ shī} lǜ shī: lǜ has ü, so lips rounded as for *u*, tongue as for *i*. {女性|nǚ xìng} nǚ xìng has it too.
- {否则|fǒu zé} fǒu zé: z is like *ds* in "cards". {责任|zé rèn} zé rèn has the same zé.
- {职业|zhí yè} zhí yè: a rising, then a falling tone; zh is retroflex (tongue tip curled back).
- {干活儿|gàn huór} gàn huór: the erhua joins huó into one syllable, huór.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{要是|yào shi}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}，{就|jiù}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}~~: as with {如果|rú guǒ}, {就|jiù} goes after the subject of the second clause: {要是|yào shi}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{去|qù}.
- ~~{否则|fǒu zé}{你|nǐ}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào}，{你|nǐ}{得|děi}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{走|zǒu}~~: the {否则|fǒu zé} clause comes second: {你|nǐ}{得|děi}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{走|zǒu}，{否则|fǒu zé}{会|huì}{迟到|chí dào}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{符合|fú hé}{你|nǐ}~~: {符合|fú hé} takes a condition or requirement, not a person: {我|wǒ}{符合|fú hé}{你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{条件|tiáo jiàn}.
- {他|tā}{在|zài}{工厂|gōng chǎng}{工作|gōng zuò} and {他|tā}{在|zài}{工厂|gōng chǎng}{打工|dǎ gōng} are both fine, but they say different things: {打工|dǎ gōng} is temporary or
  part-time, often for students. Don't call a long career {打工|dǎ gōng}.
- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{去|qù}，{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{票|piào}{好|hǎo}~~: {好|hǎo} goes before the verb of the second clause: {我们|wǒ men}{早点儿|zǎo diǎnr}{去|qù}，{好|hǎo}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{票|piào}.
- {我|wǒ}{男性|nán xìng} isn't a sentence: on a form, {性别|xìng bié}：{男|nán}; in speech, {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{男|nán}{的|de}.

## Key points

- Job advertisements: {招聘|zhāo pìn} (recruit) and {应聘|yìng pìn} (apply), {条件|tiáo jiàn} and {符合|fú hé}, {年龄|nián líng}, {性别|xìng bié}, {男性|nán xìng} / {女性|nǚ xìng} (formal),
  {工资|gōng zī}, {负责|fù zé} / {负责人|fù zé rén}, {责任|zé rèn}.
- {要是|yào shi}…{就|jiù}: spoken "if", used like {如果|rú guǒ}; {要是|yào shi} yào shi sounds like {钥匙|yào shi}.
- A, {否则|fǒu zé} B: do A, otherwise B happens. Formal-leaning; {不然|bù rán} and {要不|yào bù} in speech.
- A, (subject) {好|hǎo} + verb: so that someone can. {好|hǎo} comes second; {为了|wèi le} states a goal first.
- Work words: {打工|dǎ gōng} (part-time), {干活儿|gàn huór} (spoken), {工人|gōng rén}, {工厂|gōng chǎng} / {厂|chǎng}, {师傅|shī fu} (also a polite address), {职业|zhí yè},
  {律师|lǜ shī}, {辛苦|xīn kǔ} ({你|nǐ}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}{了|le}!), {专门|zhuān mén}, {普通|pǔ tōng}, {无法|wú fǎ} (written).
- New characters: {修|xiū} {钥|yào} {匙|chí} {围|wéi} {整|zhěng} {厂|chǎng} {负|fù} {责|zé} {广|guǎng} {符|fú} {否|fǒu} {则|zé} {济|jì} {律|lǜ} {性|xìng} {龄|líng} {傅|fù} {无|wú} {辛|xīn} {职|zhí}; ✎ {厂|chǎng} {广|guǎng} {否|fǒu} {济|jì} {性|xìng} {无|wú}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: The job interview: pivotal sentences and 作为
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) has an interview ({面试|miàn shì}) at the news website on Monday. Over the weekend {李明|Lǐ Míng} (Li Ming)
helps her practise. This lesson gives you the words to talk about yourself at an interview, your
strong and weak points, your experience and abilities, and the grammar to describe people: what
you like about someone, what job they've been given, how something made you feel.

You'll learn:

- **[[pivotal sentences]]** beyond HSK 3's {让|ràng} / {叫|jiào} / {请|qǐng} + person + verb: liking someone for something
  ({我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}), naming and appointing ({大家|dà jiā}{选|xuǎn}{他|tā}{当|dāng}{班长|bān zhǎng}), causing a feeling ({这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng});
- {作为|zuò wéi}, "as, in the role of": {作为|zuò wéi}{学生|xué sheng}…;
- 为 read **wéi**, "to be, to act as", in {成为|chéng wéi}, {作为|zuò wéi} and {分为|fēn wéi} (written words);
- interview words: {经验|jīng yàn}, {能力|néng lì}, {优点|yōu diǎn} and {缺点|quē diǎn}, {表现|biǎo xiàn}, {自信|zì xìn} and {信心|xìn xīn}, {积极|jī jí}, {优秀|yōu xiù}, {适合|shì hé}, {证明|zhèng míng}, {保证|bǎo zhèng}, {达到|dá dào},
  {取得|qǔ dé}, {积累|jī lěi}, {加强|jiā qiáng}, {减轻|jiǎn qīng}, {竞争|jìng zhēng}, {面对|miàn duì}, {重视|zhòng shì}, {缺|quē} and {缺少|quē shǎo}, {能够|néng gòu}, {基本|jī běn} and {基本上|jī běn shang}, {流利|liú lì}, {困难|kùn nan}, {强|qiáng}.

## Pivotal sentences

In {老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{写|xiě}{文章|wén zhāng} (the teacher had us write an essay), {我们|wǒ men} does two jobs: it is the **[[object]]** of
{让|ràng} and the **[[subject]]** of {写|xiě}. A noun that is both at once is the "pivot" of the sentence, and a
sentence built round one is a **[[pivotal sentence]]**. You met the commonest kind in HSK 3, with {让|ràng}, {叫|jiào}
and {请|qǐng} (making or asking someone do something). HSK 4 adds three more families.

| Kind | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| asking, making (HSK 3) | {让|ràng} / {叫|jiào} / {请|qǐng} + person + verb | {老师|lǎo shī}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{写|xiě}{文章|wén zhāng}。 |
| liking, disliking, praising | {喜欢|xǐ huan} / {表扬|biǎo yáng} / {讨厌|tǎo yàn} + person + what they're like or do | {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}。 |
| naming, appointing | {选|xuǎn} / {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} + person + {当|dāng} / {做|zuò} / {负责|fù zé} … | {大家|dà jiā}{选|xuǎn}{他|tā}{当|dāng}{班长|bān zhǎng}。 |
| causing a feeling | {让|ràng} / {叫|jiào} + person + feeling | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 |

### Liking someone for something

The first verb is a feeling or a judgement; the second part says **why**: what the person is like,
or what they did.

{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}。 — I like her because she's conscientious. (literally: I like her doing things
carefully.)

{老师|lǎo shī}{表扬|biǎo yáng}{他|tā}{作业|zuò yè}{写|xiě}{得|de}{好|hǎo}。 — The teacher praised him for writing his homework well.

{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{他|tā}{总是|zǒng shì}{迟到|chí dào}。 — I don't like the way he's always late.

English often says "like someone **for**…" or "like the way…"; Chinese simply puts the reason after
the person. ({表扬|biǎo yáng} is lesson 04's "to praise". {讨厌|tǎo yàn}, to dislike, is lesson 23's.)

### Naming and appointing

The first verb chooses or names someone; the second says the role. The role verb is often {当|dāng} (to
work as, to be), {做|zuò} or {负责|fù zé}:

{大家|dà jiā}{选|xuǎn}{他|tā}{当|dāng}{班长|bān zhǎng}。 — Everyone chose him as class monitor. ({班长|bān zhǎng}: the student in charge of a class.)

{公司|gōng sī}{让|ràng}{她|tā}{负责|fù zé}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{招聘|zhāo pìn}。 — The company has put her in charge of this round of hiring.

{同学|tóng xué}{们|men}{都|dōu}{叫|jiào}{他|tā}"{小|xiǎo}{老师|lǎo shī}"。 — The other students all call him "little teacher".

### Causing a feeling

With {让|ràng} (spoken) or {叫|jiào}, the second part is a feeling or a state:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 — This made me very happy.

{他|tā}{的话|de huà}{让|ràng}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{放心|fàng xīn}{了|le}。 — What he said put everyone's mind at rest.

{面试|miàn shì}{以前|yǐ qián}，{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{让|ràng}{她|tā}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}。 — Before the interview, everything made her nervous. ({紧张|jǐn zhāng}: nervous, lesson
23.)

The thing that causes the feeling comes first, the person who feels it after {让|ràng}. Lesson 23 adds {使|shǐ},
the written partner of {让|ràng} in this pattern.

In every family, the pivot can't be dropped or moved: ~~{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}{她|tā}~~ is not Chinese. And a
negative usually goes before the first verb: {他|tā}{的|de}{回答|huí dá}{没|méi}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{满意|mǎn yì} (his answer didn't satisfy me).

## {作为|zuò wéi}: as, in the role of

{作为|zuò wéi} + a role says in what capacity someone speaks or acts. It usually starts the sentence:

{作为|zuò wéi}{学生|xué sheng}，{我们|wǒ men}{应该|yīng gāi}{认真|rèn zhēn}{学习|xué xí}。 — As students, we should study hard.

{作为|zuò wéi}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{招聘|zhāo pìn}{的|de}{负责人|fù zé rén}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{跟|gēn}{大家|dà jiā}{说|shuō}{几|jǐ}{句|jù}{话|huà}。 — As the person in charge of this round of hiring, I'd like
to say a few words.

{作为|zuò wéi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新人|xīn rén}，{你|nǐ}{得|děi}{多|duō}{问|wèn}、{多|duō}{学|xué}。 — As a newcomer, you should ask a lot and learn a lot. ({新人|xīn rén}: a newcomer;
{得|děi}: must.)

{作为|zuò wéi} is a little formal, but you'll hear it in speech whenever someone states their role. It also
works as a verb, "to take as, to treat as": {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{实习|shí xí}{作为|zuò wéi}{一|yí}{次|cì}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{机会|jī huì} (he's treating this
internship as a chance to learn; {机会|jī huì}: a chance).

## {为|wéi}: to be, to act as

You know 为 as **wèi**, "for" ({为了|wèi le}, {为什么|wèi shén me}, {我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{高兴|gāo xìng}: HSK 2 and 3). In written words 为 is also
**wéi**, "to be, to become, to act as", and that's the {为|wéi} of {成为|chéng wéi} (to become, lesson 05) and {作为|zuò wéi}:

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {为了|wèi le} | wèi le | in order to |
| {为什么|wèi shén me} | wèi shén me | why |
| {成为|chéng wéi} | chéng wéi | to become |
| {作为|zuò wéi} | zuò wéi | as; to take as |
| {分为|fēn wéi} | fēn wéi | to divide into (lesson 27) |

{她|tā}{成为|chéng wéi}{了|le}{一|yì}{名|míng}{优秀|yōu xiù}{的|de}{律师|lǜ shī}。 — She became an excellent lawyer.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{面试|miàn shì}{分为|fēn wéi}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{部分|bù fen}。 — The interview is in two parts. ({部分|bù fen}: a part, lesson 27.)

A rule of thumb: 为 joined to the verb before it ({成为|chéng wéi}, {作为|zuò wéi}, {分为|fēn wéi}) is wéi, "to be"; 为 before a person or
a purpose ({为|wèi}{你|nǐ}, {为了|wèi le}) is wèi, "for".

## Talking about yourself: the interview words

**Experience and ability**

- {经验|jīng yàn} is experience as **knowledge gained**: {有|yǒu}{经验|jīng yàn} (experienced), {经验|jīng yàn}{很|hěn}{多|duō}, {积累|jī lěi}{经验|jīng yàn} (to build up
  experience). ({经历|jīng lì}, lesson 20, is experience as **something you went through**.)
- {能力|néng lì} is ability: {能力|néng lì}{很|hěn}{强|qiáng} (very capable), {学习|xué xí}{能力|néng lì} (the ability to learn).
- {强|qiáng} is strong: {能力|néng lì}{强|qiáng}, {她|tā}{的|de}{英语|Yīng yǔ}{能力|néng lì}{很|hěn}{强|qiáng}. {加强|jiā qiáng} is to strengthen: {加强|jiā qiáng}{练习|liàn xí} (practise more).
- {积累|jī lěi} is to build up, accumulate: {积累|jī lěi}{经验|jīng yàn}, {积累|jī lěi}{知识|zhī shi}.
- {能够|néng gòu} is "to be able to", a little more formal than {能|néng}: {我|wǒ}{能够|néng gòu}{保证|bǎo zhèng}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{来|lái}{上班|shàng bān} (I can guarantee to
  come to work every day).

**Strong and weak points**

- {优点|yōu diǎn} (merit, strong point) and {缺点|quē diǎn} (shortcoming): {他|tā}{的|de}{优点|yōu diǎn}{是|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}，{缺点|quē diǎn}{是|shì}{太|tài}{着急|zháo jí}.
- {优秀|yōu xiù} is excellent, outstanding: {优秀|yōu xiù}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}, {她|tā}{的|de}{成绩|chéng jì}{很|hěn}{优秀|yōu xiù}.
- {积极|jī jí} is active, keen, positive: {他|tā}{上课|shàng kè}{很|hěn}{积极|jī jí} (he takes an active part in class), {积极|jī jí}{参加|cān jiā}{活动|huó dòng}.
- {自信|zì xìn} is confident, self-confident: {她|tā}{很|hěn}{自信|zì xìn}. {信心|xìn xīn} is confidence **in** something: {对|duì}…{有|yǒu}{信心|xìn xīn} (to be
  confident about…), {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{信心|xìn xīn}{通过|tōng guò}{面试|miàn shì} (I'm confident I'll pass the interview).
- {流利|liú lì} is fluent: {她|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{流利|liú lì}.

**Lacking, meeting and proving**

- {缺|quē} is to lack, be short of: {缺|quē}{钱|qián}, {缺|quē}{人|rén} (short-staffed). {缺少|quē shǎo} means the same with a longer object, and
  sounds a little more formal: {缺少|quē shǎo}{经验|jīng yàn} (to lack experience).
- {达到|dá dào} is to reach a level or a goal: {达到|dá dào}{要求|yāo qiú} (to meet the requirements), {达到|dá dào}{目标|mù biāo} (to reach a target).
- {取得|qǔ dé} is to achieve, gain: {取得|qǔ dé}{好|hǎo}{成绩|chéng jì} (to get good results), {取得|qǔ dé}{成功|chéng gōng} (to succeed).
- {证明|zhèng míng} is to prove; as a noun, a certificate: {用|yòng}{事实|shì shí}{证明|zhèng míng} (to prove with facts; {事实|shì shí}: a fact), {工作|gōng zuò}{证明|zhèng míng} (a
  letter confirming your employment).
- {保证|bǎo zhèng} is to guarantee, promise: {我|wǒ}{保证|bǎo zhèng}{明天|míng tiān}{以前|yǐ qián}{做|zuò}{完|wán} (I promise I'll finish it by tomorrow).
- {表现|biǎo xiàn} is to show, perform, and a performance: {她|tā}{面试|miàn shì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{表现|biǎo xiàn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (she did very well at the
  interview), {他|tā}{的|de}{表现|biǎo xiàn}{让|ràng}{大家|dà jiā}{很|hěn}{满意|mǎn yì}.

**Pressure and competition**

- {竞争|jìng zhēng} is to compete; competition: {竞争|jìng zhēng}{很|hěn}{大|dà} (the competition is tough), {跟|gēn}{别人|bié ren}{竞争|jìng zhēng}.
- {面对|miàn duì} is to face: {面对|miàn duì}{困难|kùn nan} (to face difficulties), {面对|miàn duì}{压力|yā lì} (to face pressure; {压力|yā lì}, lesson 07).
- {困难|kùn nan} is difficult (adjective) and a difficulty (noun): {他|tā}{家|jiā}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}{很|hěn}{困难|kùn nan} (his family is badly off) / {遇到|yù dào}{困难|kùn nan} (to run into
  difficulties). Note the reading kùn nan, with a light second syllable.
- {减轻|jiǎn qīng} is to lighten, ease: {减轻|jiǎn qīng}{压力|yā lì} (to ease the pressure).
- {重视|zhòng shì} is to value, take seriously: {公司|gōng sī}{很|hěn}{重视|zhòng shì}{新人|xīn rén}{的|de}{培养|péi yǎng} (the company takes training newcomers seriously;
  {培养|péi yǎng}: to train, bring on).

**{适合|shì hé} or {合适|hé shì}?**

Both mean "suitable", but they work differently. {适合|shì hé} is a **verb** and takes an object; {合适|hé shì} (HSK 3)
is an **adjective** and doesn't:

{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{适合|shì hé}{你|nǐ}。 — This job suits you.

{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{对|duì}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì}。 — This job is right for you.

So ~~{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì}{你|nǐ}~~ is wrong: with an object, use {适合|shì hé}.

**{基本|jī běn} and {基本上|jī běn shang}**

{基本|jī běn} is basic: {基本|jī běn}{的|de}{要求|yāo qiú} (the basic requirements). {基本上|jī běn shang} is an adverb, "basically, on the whole":
{我|wǒ}{基本上|jī běn shang}{能|néng}{看|kàn}{懂|dǒng}{英文|Yīng wén}{新闻|xīn wén} (I can basically understand English news). Note {基本上|jī běn shang} jī běn shang, light on the
last syllable.

### Sound parts and families

- **正 → 证 整.** 证 zhèng is 讠 (speech) + 正 zhèng; lesson 11's 整 zhěng has 正 at the
  bottom. (Traditional 證 is 言 + 登: the sound part is different, and the character has 19
  strokes.)
- **召 → 招 绍 照.** 招 zhāo is 扌 (hand) + 召 zhào; 召 is also in 绍 shào ({介绍|jiè shào}) and,
  with 日 beside it and four dots below, in 照 zhào ({照片|zhào piàn}). A memory aid for 招: beckoning with your hand.
- **夬 → 快 块 决 缺.** 缺 quē is 缶 (an earthenware jar) + 夬, the right half you know
  from 快 kuài, 块 kuài and 决 jué ({决定|jué dìng}). The sound has drifted, but the shape is a good clue.
- **佥 → 检 脸 险 验 签.** 验 yàn is 马 (horse) + 佥: the same right half as 检 jiǎn
  ({检查|jiǎn chá}), 脸 liǎn (face) and, later, 险 ({危险|wēi xiǎn}, lesson 28) and 签 ({签证|qiān zhèng}, lesson 17). In traditional the
  part is 僉: 驗, 檢, 臉, 險, 簽.
- **尤 → 优.** 优 yōu is 亻 + 尤 yóu ({尤其|yóu qí}, lesson 07).
- **禾 (grain)** is on the left of 积 and 利 and on top of 秀. Traditional 積 is 禾 + 責:
  lesson 11's 责!

### Look-alikes and traps

- **取 and 最.** 最 zuì (most) has 取 at the bottom. A memory aid for 取 itself: a hand (又) taking
  hold of an ear (耳).
- **减 has two dots of ice (冫), not three of water.** Traditional 減 has the water radical 氵.
  That makes 减 a classic slip in either direction.
- **争 and 净.** 净 ({干净|gān jìng}) is 冫 + 争; 静 ({安静|ān jìng}) has 争 on the right too.
- **竞 and 竟.** 竞 jìng ({竞争|jìng zhēng}) is 立 over 兄; 竟 jìng ({竟然|jìng rán}, lesson 20) is 立 over 日 and
  儿. Traditional 競 doubles the whole character: two 竞 side by side.
- **强**: 弓 on the left, then 口 and 虫 on the right. Traditional 強 has 厶 where simplified
  has 口.

### Stroke order

- **达** and every character with 辶: the inside first (大), the walking radical last.
- **争**: the left-falling stroke and the bent stroke on top, then the horizontal-turn, two
  horizontals, and the vertical hook through them last.
- **减**: 冫 first (a dot and a rising stroke), then the frame of 咸: the horizontal, the
  left-falling stroke, the inside, the slanting hook, and the left-falling stroke and the dot last.
- **秀**: 禾, then 乃 (a long bent stroke written in one go, and the left-falling stroke last).

4. New graduates with little experience ({作为|zuò wéi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{刚|gāng}{毕业|bì yè}{的|de}{学生|xué sheng}…); the writer wants them to feel
   that this isn't a problem: with good preparation they can do well, so they shouldn't be too
   nervous ({经验|jīng yàn}{少|shǎo}{没关系|méi guān xi}…{只要|zhǐ yào}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{得|de}{好|hǎo}，{你|nǐ}{就|jiù}{能|néng}…).

"**What matters most at an interview?** Many students are very nervous at their first interview
and don't know what to say. In fact, what interviewers care about most isn't whether your answers
sound nice but whether you can prove your ability. First, prepare examples. Just saying 'I'm keen'
or 'I'm very capable' is no use; it's best to talk about something you've done, such as an event
you were in charge of and what it achieved. Second, don't be afraid to talk about weaknesses.
Everyone has weak points; if you say you have none, the interviewer will only believe you less.
You can give one real weakness and then say how you're correcting it. Third, be confident, but
not arrogant. It doesn't matter if you don't have much experience: you can tell them that you're
willing to learn and confident that through hard work you can meet the job's requirements.
Finally, before the interview ends, you can also ask one or two questions about the job. That
makes the other side feel you take the job seriously. As a new graduate, of course you won't have
much experience. But as long as you prepare well, you'll be able to show your best side at the
interview."
</details>

## Write it

**A sentence about a picture.** The picture: a young man in a suit sits up straight across a table
from two interviewers, smiling as he answers. Write one sentence with {自信|zì xìn}.

**Your strong and weak points.** Write three sentences about yourself for an interview: one
strong point, one weak point and what you're doing about it, and one sentence with {作为|zuò wéi}.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {他|tā}{回答|huí dá}{问题|wèn tí}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{很|hěn}{自信|zì xìn}。 — He's very confident as he answers the questions. (Or:
  {他|tā}{笑|xiào}{着|zhe}{回答|huí dá}{面试官|miàn shì guān}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}，{看起来|kàn qǐ lai}{很|hěn}{自信|zì xìn}。 {看起来|kàn qǐ lai}: to look, seem.)
- {我|wǒ}{的|de}{优点|yōu diǎn}{是|shì}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}，{同事|tóng shì}{们|men}{常常|cháng cháng}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{检查|jiǎn chá}{文章|wén zhāng}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{缺点|quē diǎn}{是|shì}{说话|shuō huà}{太|tài}{快|kuài}，{现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学|xué}{着|zhe}{说|shuō}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。{作为|zuò wéi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新人|xīn rén}，{我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{多|duō}{学习|xué xí}。
  — My strong point is that I'm careful: colleagues often ask me to check their articles. My weak
  point is that I talk too fast; I'm learning to speak more slowly now. As a newcomer, I'm happy to
  learn as much as I can.
</details>

## Speaking: answering questions

In the last part of the speaking test, as reported, you hear two questions and answer each for
about a minute. Try these two aloud, then compare with the models.

1. {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{自己|zì jǐ}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{优点|yōu diǎn}{和|hé}{缺点|quē diǎn}？
2. {你|nǐ}{以后|yǐ hòu}{想|xiǎng}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}{职业|zhí yè}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{优点|yōu diǎn}{是|shì}{积极|jī jí}，{也|yě}{很|hěn}{重视|zhòng shì}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{意见|yì jiàn}。{上|shàng}{大学|dà xué}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{同学|tóng xué}{们|men}{选|xuǎn}{我|wǒ}{负责|fù zé}{班|bān}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{活动|huó dòng}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{做|zuò}{得|de}{不错|bú cuò}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{缺点|quē diǎn}{是|shì}{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{太|tài}{着急|zháo jí}，{想|xiǎng}{一下子|yí xià zi}{把|bǎ}{事情|shì qing}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{完|wán}，{结果|jié guǒ}{反而|fǎn ér}{做|zuò}{得|de}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}。{现在|xiàn zài}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学|xué}{着|zhe}{先|xiān}{做|zuò}{计划|jì huà}，{再|zài}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{地|de}{做|zuò}。
   — I think my strong points are that I'm keen and I value other people's views. At university my
   classmates chose me to organise class events, and everyone said I did a good job. My weakness
   is that I'm sometimes too impatient and want to get everything done at once, and then I do it
   worse. Now I'm learning to make a plan first and do things one at a time. ({意见|yì jiàn}: opinion, lesson
   14; {结果|jié guǒ}: as a result, lesson 17.)
2. {我|wǒ}{以后|yǐ hòu}{想|xiǎng}{当|dāng}{律师|lǜ shī}。{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{职业|zhí yè}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yì si}，{也|yě}{能|néng}{帮助|bāng zhù}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。{当然|dāng rán}，{当|dāng}{律师|lǜ shī}{很|hěn}{辛苦|xīn kǔ}，{竞争|jìng zhēng}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{可是|kě shì}{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{信心|xìn xīn}。{作为|zuò wéi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{学生|xué sheng}，{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{要|yào}{多|duō}{积累|jī lěi}{知识|zhī shi}，{也|yě}{要|yào}{加强|jiā qiáng}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{英语|Yīng yǔ}，{因为|yīn wèi}{以后|yǐ hòu}{可能|kě néng}{会|huì}{有|yǒu}{外国|wài guó}{客户|kè hù}。
   — I'd like to be a lawyer. I think it's an interesting profession, and you can help a lot of
   people. Of course, being a lawyer is hard work and the competition is tough, but I'm confident.
   As a student, I need to build up my knowledge now and strengthen my English, because there may
   be foreign clients later on. ({客户|kè hù}: a client.)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At the interview
{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{先|xiān}{介绍|jiè shào}{一下|yí xià}{自己|zì jǐ}。
= First, please tell us about yourself.
{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{报纸|bào zhǐ}{做|zuò}{过|guo}{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{编辑|biān jí}，{积累|jī lěi}{了|le}{一些|yì xiē}{经验|jīng yàn}。
= I was an editor on the student paper for two years, so I've built up some experience.
{我|wǒ}{的|de}{优点|yōu diǎn}{是|shì}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}，{缺点|quē diǎn}{是|shì}{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{太|tài}{着急|zháo jí}。
= My strong point is that I'm conscientious; my weak point is that I'm sometimes too impatient.
{作为|zuò wéi}{一|yí}{个|gè}{新人|xīn rén}，{我|wǒ}{愿意|yuàn yì}{多|duō}{学习|xué xí}。
= As a newcomer, I'm happy to learn as much as I can.
{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{信心|xìn xīn}{达到|dá dào}{你们|nǐ men}{的|de}{要求|yāo qiú}。
= I'm confident I can meet your requirements.
{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{适合|shì hé}{你|nǐ}。
= This job suits you.
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
= This made me very happy.
```

## Pronunciation

- 为 in {成为|chéng wéi}, {作为|zuò wéi}, {分为|fēn wéi} is **wéi** (rising); in {为了|wèi le} and {为什么|wèi shén me} it's **wèi** (falling).
- {困难|kùn nan} kùn nan and {基本上|jī běn shang} jī běn shang end light. {竞争|jìng zhēng} jìng zhēng: jìng with *-ing*, zhēng with *-eng*.
- {经验|jīng yàn} jīng yàn: yàn rhymes with "yen". Don't confuse it with {经历|jīng lì} jīng lì (lesson 20).
- {积极|jī jí} jī jí: j + i, first then second tone. {积累|jī lěi} jī lěi: lěi, not lèi ({累|lèi}, tired, is lèi).
- {优秀|yōu xiù} yōu xiù and {自信|zì xìn} zì xìn: in xiù and xìn the x is between *s* and *sh*, tongue flat.
- {缺|quē} quē, {却|què} què (lesson 14) and {确|què} què ({正确|zhèng què}, lesson 02): q + üe, written ue. Watch the tones.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì}{你|nǐ}~~: with an object, use the verb {适合|shì hé}: {这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{很|hěn}{适合|shì hé}{你|nǐ}. ({合适|hé shì} has no object:
  {这个|zhè ge}{工作|gōng zuò}{对|duì}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{合适|hé shì}.)
- ~~{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}{她|tā}~~: in a pivotal sentence the person comes straight after the first verb:
  {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}.
- ~~{作为|zuò wéi}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}~~: {作为|zuò wéi} isn't a time expression. "When I was a student" is {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou} or
  {上学|shàng xué}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}; {作为|zuò wéi}{学生|xué sheng} is "as a student" (in that role).
- {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{自信|zì xìn} and {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{自信|zì xìn} are both fine. For confidence about one particular thing, {信心|xìn xīn} is the usual
  word: {我|wǒ}{对|duì}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{面试|miàn shì}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{信心|xìn xīn} (I'm confident about this interview).
- {我|wǒ}{缺少|quē shǎo}{钱|qián} is heard, but {缺|quē} is more natural with a one-syllable object: {我|wǒ}{缺|quē}{钱|qián}. {缺少|quē shǎo} suits
  longer ones: {缺少|quē shǎo}{经验|jīng yàn}, {缺少|quē shǎo}{时间|shí jiān}.
- {成为|chéng wéi} is chéng wéi, not chéng wèi.

## Key points

- Pivotal sentences: verb 1 + person + verb 2, the person being object of the first and subject of
  the second. Liking: {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{她|tā}{做|zuò}{事|shì}{认真|rèn zhēn}. Appointing: {大家|dà jiā}{选|xuǎn}{他|tā}{当|dāng}{班长|bān zhǎng}, {公司|gōng sī}{让|ràng}{她|tā}{负责|fù zé}…. Causing: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}.
- {作为|zuò wéi} + role (as…): {作为|zuò wéi}{学生|xué sheng}，…. It isn't "when".
- {为|wéi} in {成为|chéng wéi}, {作为|zuò wéi}, {分为|fēn wéi}; {为|wèi} in {为了|wèi le}, {为什么|wèi shén me}.
- {适合|shì hé} (verb, + object) vs {合适|hé shì} (adjective). {自信|zì xìn} (self-confident) vs {信心|xìn xīn} (confidence in something).
  {缺|quē} + one syllable, {缺少|quē shǎo} + two.
- Interview words: {经验|jīng yàn}, {能力|néng lì}, {优点|yōu diǎn} / {缺点|quē diǎn}, {优秀|yōu xiù}, {积极|jī jí}, {表现|biǎo xiàn}, {证明|zhèng míng}, {保证|bǎo zhèng}, {达到|dá dào}, {取得|qǔ dé}, {积累|jī lěi}, {加强|jiā qiáng}, {减轻|jiǎn qīng},
  {竞争|jìng zhēng}, {面对|miàn duì}, {重视|zhòng shì}, {能够|néng gòu}, {基本|jī běn} / {基本上|jī běn shang}, {流利|liú lì}, {困难|kùn nan}, {强|qiáng}.
- New characters: {聘|pìn} {招|zhāo} {保|bǎo} {证|zhèng} {达|dá} {验|yàn} {积|jī} {强|qiáng} {减|jiǎn} {竞|jìng} {争|zhēng} {流|liú} {利|lì} {缺|quē} {取|qǔ} {优|yōu} {秀|xiù}; ✎ {保|bǎo} {达|dá} {验|yàn} {强|qiáng} {流|liú} {利|lì} {取|qǔ}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: In the office: 由, 按照 and 将 in notices
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) got the internship. This lesson is her first week at the news website: the
department, the tasks, the rules, the forms. Offices run on written notices, so this is also a
lesson in **reading the written register** of work: the words that turn up in notices, emails and
forms, beside the spoken words you'd use for the same thing.

You'll learn:

- {由|yóu}, the written way to say **who does something** ({这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{由|yóu}{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{负责|fù zé}), and {由|yóu} "from";
- {按|àn} and {按照|àn zhào}, "according to" (a rule, a plan, the instructions);
- {将|jiāng} as the written form of {把|bǎ} ({请|qǐng}{将|jiāng}{表格|biǎo gé}{交|jiāo}{到|dào}{办公室|bàn gōng shì});
- notices and forms: {通知|tōng zhī}, {规定|guī dìng}, {说明|shuō míng} and {说明书|shuō míng shū}, {填写|tián xiě}, {表格|biǎo gé} and {表|biǎo}, {材料|cái liào}, {文件|wén jiàn}, {详细|xiáng xì}, {正式|zhèng shì}, {暂时|zàn shí}, {现有|xiàn yǒu},
  {内|nèi}, {便于|biàn yú};
- office life: {部门|bù mén}, {单位|dān wèi}, {人员|rén yuán}, {任务|rèn wu}, {安排|ān pái}, {管理|guǎn lǐ} and {管|guǎn}, {办公|bàn gōng}, {办理|bàn lǐ}, {办事|bàn shì}, {加班|jiā bān}, {出差|chū chāi}, {联系|lián xì}, {进行|jìn xíng}, {使用|shǐ yòng},
  {同时|tóng shí}, {定|dìng}, {查看|chá kàn}, {提出|tí chū}, {指出|zhǐ chū}.

## {由|yóu}: who does it

In notices and plans, {由|yóu} + a person (or a department) + a verb says **whose job** something is. The
thing to be done usually comes first, as the topic:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{由|yóu}{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{负责|fù zé}。 — Xiao Wang is responsible for this.

{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{会|huì}{由|yóu}{郑|Zhèng}{老师|lǎo shī}{主持|zhǔ chí}。 — Today's meeting will be chaired by Ms Zheng. ({主持|zhǔ chí}: to chair, host.)

{新|xīn}{同事|tóng shì}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}{由|yóu}{各|gè}{部门|bù mén}{安排|ān pái}。 — New colleagues' work is arranged by each department.

You could say each of these without {由|yóu} ({这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{负责|fù zé}), and in speech people often do. {由|yóu} makes it
formal and puts the doer in focus. {由|yóu} is the **[[agent marker]]** of written Chinese: it marks the
agent, the one who acts.

Don't use {被|bèi} (HSK 3) for this. {被|bèi} marks something done **to** the subject, often something unwelcome
({我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}). {由|yóu} marks whose task or decision it is, and the subject is the task itself:

| | Says | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {被|bèi} | something happened to the subject | {他|tā}{的|de}{文章|wén zhāng}{被|bèi}{老师|lǎo shī}{改|gǎi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 His article was heavily corrected by the teacher. |
| {由|yóu} | someone is in charge of the subject | {这|zhè}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}{由|yóu}{他|tā}{来|lái}{写|xiě}。 This article is for him to write. |

~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{被|bèi}{小王|Xiǎo Wáng}{负责|fù zé}~~ is wrong: nothing is happening to the matter; Xiao Wang is in charge of it.

{由|yóu} also means **from**, the written partner of {从|cóng}: {由|yóu}{北京|Běi jīng}{出发|chū fā} (setting off from Beijing), and on signs
{由此|yóu cǐ}{进入|jìn rù} (enter here: {此|cǐ}, this place, lesson 01). Lesson 17 adds {由于|yóu yú} (because, written).

## {按|àn} and {按照|àn zhào}: according to

{按照|àn zhào} + a rule, plan or set of instructions says what you follow:

{按照|àn zhào}{规定|guī dìng}，{新人|xīn rén}{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{不|bù}{能|néng}{自己|zì jǐ}{发|fā}{新闻|xīn wén}。 — Under the rules, newcomers can't publish news on their own in
their first month.

{请|qǐng}{按照|àn zhào}{说明书|shuō míng shū}{使用|shǐ yòng}。 — Please use (it) according to the instructions.

{我们|wǒ men}{按照|àn zhào}{计划|jì huà}，{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{开始|kāi shǐ}{招聘|zhāo pìn}。 — According to plan, we start recruiting next month.

{按|àn} means the same and is shorter; it's common before a one-syllable word and in set phrases: {按时|àn shí} (on
time, lesson 07), {按|àn}{月|yuè} (monthly), {按|àn}{天|tiān}{算|suàn} (counted by the day: {算|suàn}, lesson 15). {按|àn} is also a verb, **to press**: {按|àn}{电梯|diàn tī} (to
press the lift button), {按|àn}{这里|zhè lǐ} (press here).

How is {按照|àn zhào} different from {根据|gēn jù} (HSK 3)? {按照|àn zhào} is "following" a rule or instruction; {根据|gēn jù} is "on the basis
of" facts, information or a source: {根据|gēn jù}{天气|tiān qì}{预报|yù bào}，{明天|míng tiān}{有|yǒu}{雨|yǔ} (according to the forecast, it'll rain
tomorrow). You'd say {按照|àn zhào}{规定|guī dìng} and {根据|gēn jù}{调查|diào chá} (according to a survey; {调查|diào chá}, lesson 25), and either with {计划|jì huà}.

## {将|jiāng}: the written {把|bǎ}

You met {将|jiāng} in lesson 05 as the written "will" ({我们|wǒ men}{将|jiāng}{在|zài}{明天|míng tiān}{出发|chū fā}). In notices it is also the written
form of **{把|bǎ}**, with exactly the same word order:

{请|qǐng}{将|jiāng}{表格|biǎo gé}{交|jiāo}{到|dào}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}。 = {请|qǐng}{把|bǎ}{表格|biǎo gé}{交|jiāo}{到|dào}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}。 — Please hand the form in at the office.

{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{将|jiāng}{手机|shǒu jī}{关|guān}{上|shàng}。 = {请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{把|bǎ}{手机|shǒu jī}{关|guān}{上|shàng}。 — Would everyone please switch off their phones.

{我们|wǒ men}{将|jiāng}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}{改|gǎi}{为|wéi}{下|xià}{星期|xīng qī}{五|wǔ}。 — We have moved the event to next Friday. ({改|gǎi}{为|wéi}: to change to; 为
is wéi, lesson 12.)

As with {把|bǎ}, the verb needs something after it: a result ({关|guān}{上|shàng}, {填写|tián xiě}{完整|wán zhěng}), a place ({交|jiāo}{到|dào}{办公室|bàn gōng shì}) or {为|wéi}. In
conversation, always use {把|bǎ}: {将|jiāng} sounds like a notice.

## Notices, forms and the written register

A notice ({通知|tōng zhī}) has its own way of saying things. Here are the commonest written words beside the
ones you'd use in speech:

| Written | Spoken | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {将|jiāng} | {把|bǎ} | (marks the object) |

- {表格|biǎo gé} is a form or a table; {表|biǎo} alone is the same in compounds and speech: {填|tián}{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{表|biǎo} (fill in a form). ({表|biǎo}

  is a document or a computer file.

  {三|sān}{天|tiān}{以内|yǐ nèi} (lesson 15), {办公室|bàn gōng shì}{里|lǐ}.

### Sound parts

- **才 → 材.** 材 cái is 木 (wood) + 才 cái ({刚才|gāng cái}).
- **官 → 管 馆.** 管 guǎn is ⺮ (bamboo; 管 is also a tube or pipe) + 官 guān; you know 官 from 馆 guǎn
  ({饭馆|fàn guǎn}, {咖啡馆|kā fēi guǎn}), with 饣 (food).
- **羊 → 详 洋 样.** 详 xiáng is 讠 (speech) + 羊 yáng; 羊 gives -ang in 样 yàng ({怎么样|zěn me yàng})
  and 洋 yáng ({海洋|hǎi yáng}, lesson 26).
- **式 → 试.** 试 shì ({考试|kǎo shì}) is 讠 + 式 shì. Learn 式 and you have most of 试.
- **由 → 油 邮.** 由 yóu gives its whole sound to 油 yóu ({加油|jiā yóu}, lesson 07) and 邮 yóu ({邮件|yóu jiàn}).
- **咅 → 部 倍.** 部 bù and 倍 bèi (lesson 15) share their left part; the sound has drifted.

### Families and look-alikes

- **阝 on the right or the left.** On the right, 阝 is a town or a region: 部, 都, 那, 邮. On
  the left it is a hill or a wall: 院, 阿, 除, 际. Same shape, two different sources (in
  dictionaries: 邑 and 阜).
- **田, 由, 甲, 申.** 由 is 田 with the vertical sticking out at the top; 甲 (first) has it
  sticking out at the bottom, and 申 ({申请|shēn qǐng}, lesson 05) at both ends. Write 由 as: the vertical, the
  horizontal-turn, the horizontal, the middle vertical, and the bottom horizontal last.
- **规**: 夫 + 见. In traditional 規 the right part is 見, as in 見 ({见|jiàn}).
- **联**: 耳 + 关 ({关心|guān xīn}). Traditional 聯 keeps 耳 but has a quite different right side, 17
  strokes.
- **指**: 扌 (the hand) + 旨. Fingers are the hand's: a meaning clue.
- **暂** is 斩 over 日 (the sun). A memory aid: 日 for time, as in 时, 早 and 晚.

### Stroke order

- **式**: the long horizontal first, then 工 (its short top horizontal, the vertical, and a rising
  stroke at the bottom: stroke 4 rises, it isn't a horizontal), the slanting hook, and the dot at the
  top right last. The same order is in 试.
- **管**: ⺮ (the bamboo top, six strokes) first, then 官: the dot, the left dot, the bent
  stroke, then the frame of the two boxes.
- **使**: 亻, then the horizontal, 口, and the long left-falling and right-falling strokes last.
