lessons.title: The first emperor's standards
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module has been about work, money and numbers: wages, forms, rules, units. Its first honors
lesson goes back to the man who, more than two thousand years ago, made much of China count,
weigh, write and pay in the same way: the first emperor of the Qin dynasty. You'll read what the
standards were, what became of them and how his tomb was found in 1974, in English and then in a
Chinese text written for this course. This is history as it's known from the sources, with no
judgement of the ruler.

New words in this lesson are glossed where they appear; none of them joins your vocabulary
reviews.

## Seven states become one

Before 221 BCE, the land we now call China was divided among several rival states. Historians call
the centuries before unification the Warring States period ({战国|Zhàn guó}). The states had their own
rulers, their own coins and their own ways of writing many characters.

In 221 BCE the state of Qin ({秦国|Qín guó}), in the north-west, conquered the last of its rivals. Its king
took a new title, {皇帝|huáng dì} (emperor), and called himself the first: {始|shǐ}{皇帝|huáng dì}. History knows him as {秦始皇|Qín Shǐ huáng}
(Qín Shǐ huáng, the First Emperor of Qin; born about 259 BCE, died 210 BCE). The dynasty he founded,
the {秦朝|Qín cháo}, was short: it fell a few years after his death (the last Qin ruler surrendered in 206 BCE,
and many books date the dynasty 221–207 BCE).

## One script, one measure, one coin

The first emperor ordered standards across the whole empire. The main ones, as the historical
sources and today's historians describe them:

| What | Before | After unification |
|---|---|---|
| writing ({文字|wén zì}) | many characters written differently in different states | the Qin forms, the small seal script ({小篆|xiǎo zhuàn}), became the standard; other forms were dropped |
| weights and measures ({长度|cháng dù}, {重量|zhòng liàng}) | each state had its own units | one set of units for length, volume and weight |
| money ({钱|qián}) | many kinds of coins: some shaped like knives or spades | one bronze coin, round with a square hole, inscribed {半两|bàn liǎng} ("half a liang"); gold was used for large sums |
| carts | wheels set different distances apart | one width between the wheels, so carts could use the same ruts on the roads |
| roads ({道路|dào lù}) | local roads | a network of roads across the empire |

A set phrase sums the reforms up: {书|shū}{同|tóng}{文|wén}，{车|chē}{同|tóng}{轨|guǐ}, "the same script for writing, the same gauge for
carts".

Some of this lasted far longer than the dynasty. The round coin with a square hole became the
usual shape of Chinese coins for about two thousand years. The script went on changing (lesson
05h2 follows it from seal script to the characters of today), but the idea of one written
standard for the whole country stayed.

You can see the link with this module: {标准|biāo zhǔn} (standard), {统一|tǒng yī} (to unify, make the same) and {规定|guī dìng} (a
rule) are words a notice would use today, and the first emperor's standards were exactly that: rules
for how much a {两|liǎng} weighed and how characters were written.

## The terracotta army

In March 1974 farmers digging a well near {西安|Xī'ān} (Xi'an), in the north-west, found pieces of pottery
figures. Archaeologists ({考古人员|kǎo gǔ rén yuán}) then uncovered pits full of life-sized soldiers and horses made of
fired clay, buried about 1.5 km east of the first emperor's tomb mound. They are called {兵马俑|bīng mǎ yǒng}
(bīng mǎ yǒng: soldiers, horses and figures) and, in English, the terracotta army.

- Estimates put the figures in the three main pits at more than 8,000 soldiers, with horses and
  chariots; many of them are still in the ground.
- The figures were once painted in bright colours, most of which faded quickly after they were dug
  up.
- The army was buried with the emperor around 210–209 BCE; work on his tomb had begun decades
  before.
- In 1987 the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor ({秦始皇陵|Qín Shǐ huáng líng}) was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage
  List ({世界|shì jiè}{文化|wén huà}{遗产|yí chǎn}, World Cultural Heritage).

## Reading: the first emperor's standards

A short text for learners. {统一|tǒng yī} is to unify, {皇帝|huáng dì} an emperor, {公元前|gōng yuán qián} "BCE", {长度|cháng dù} and {重量|zhòng liàng} length and
weight, {称|chēng} chēng to weigh, {铜钱|tóng qián} a bronze coin, {圆|yuán} round, {方孔|fāng kǒng} a square hole, {轮子|lún zi} a wheel, {距离|jù lí} a distance (lesson 16), {影响|yǐng xiǎng} to
influence (HSK 3), {农民|nóng mín} a farmer, {挖|wā}{井|jǐng} to dig a well, {陶|táo} pottery, {估计|gū jì} to estimate (lesson 25), {样子|yàng zi} a shape, a look (lesson 22), {各地|gè dì} everywhere and {参观|cān guān}
to visit (lesson 18), and {列入|liè rù} to be put on a list.

> **{秦始皇|Qín Shǐ huáng}{的|de}"{标准|biāo zhǔn}"**
>
> {两千二百|liǎng qiān èr bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{以前|yǐ qián}，{中国|Zhōng guó}{还|hái}{分为|fēn wéi}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}。{每|měi}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{文字|wén zì}{和|hé}{钱|qián}，{长度|cháng dù}、{重量|zhòng liàng}{的|de}{标准|biāo zhǔn}{也|yě}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。{公元前|gōng yuán qián}221{年|nián}，{秦国|Qín guó}{统一|tǒng yī}{了|le}{这些|zhè xiē}{国家|guó jiā}，{秦国|Qín guó}{的|de}{王|wáng}{成为|chéng wéi}{了|le}{中国|Zhōng guó}{的|de}{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{皇帝|huáng dì}，{后来|hòu lái}{的|de}{人|rén}{叫|jiào}{他|tā}"{秦始皇|Qín Shǐ huáng}"。
>
> {统一|tǒng yī}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{秦始皇|Qín Shǐ huáng}{做|zuò}{了|le}{许多|xǔ duō}{事情|shì qing}，{其中|qí zhōng}{很|hěn}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}，{就|jiù}{是|shì}{统一|tǒng yī}{标准|biāo zhǔn}。{第|dì}{一|yī}，{全|quán}{国|guó}{使用|shǐ yòng}{同一|tóng yī}{种|zhǒng}{文字|wén zì}，{这|zhè}{就|jiù}{是|shì}"{小篆|xiǎo zhuàn}"。{这样|zhè yàng}，{各个|gè gè}{地方|dì fang}{的|de}{人|rén}{写|xiě}{的|de}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{一样|yí yàng}，{便于|biàn yú}{交流|jiāo liú}。{第|dì}{二|èr}，{全|quán}{国|guó}{按照|àn zhào}{同一|tóng yī}{个|gè}{标准|biāo zhǔn}{来|lái}{量|liáng}{长度|cháng dù}、{称|chēng}{重量|zhòng liàng}。{第|dì}{三|sān}，{全|quán}{国|guó}{只|zhǐ}{用|yòng}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{铜钱|tóng qián}。{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{铜钱|tóng qián}{是|shì}{圆|yuán}{的|de}，{中间|zhōng jiān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{方孔|fāng kǒng}，{上面|shàng miàn}{写着|xiě zhe}"{半两|bàn liǎng}"{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{字|zì}。{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{圆形|yuán xíng}{方孔|fāng kǒng}{的|de}{样子|yàng zi}，{后来|hòu lái}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}{用|yòng}{了|le}{两千|liǎng qiān}{多|duō}{年|nián}。{第|dì}{四|sì}，{车|chē}{的|de}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{轮子|lún zi}{之间|zhī jiān}{的|de}{距离|jù lí}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{了|le}{统一|tǒng yī}{的|de}{规定|guī dìng}，{这样|zhè yàng}，{车|chē}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{在|zài}{全|quán}{国|guó}{的|de}{道路|dào lù}{上|shàng}{走|zǒu}。
>
> {秦朝|Qín cháo}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}{不|bù}{长|cháng}，{仅仅|jǐn jǐn}{十|shí}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}。{然而|rán ér}，{它|tā}{定|dìng}{下|xià}{的|de}{许多|xǔ duō}{标准|biāo zhǔn}，{却|què}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}{了|le}{后来|hòu lái}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}。
>
> {一九七四|yī jiǔ qī sì}{年|nián}，{西安|Xī'ān}{附近|fù jìn}{的|de}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{农民|nóng mín}{在|zài}{挖|wā}{井|jǐng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{发现|fā xiàn}{了|le}{一些|yì xiē}{陶|táo}{做|zuò}{的|de}{人|rén}。{后来|hòu lái}，{考古人员|kǎo gǔ rén yuán}{在|zài}{这里|zhè lǐ}{找|zhǎo}{到|dào}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{和|hé}{真人|zhēn rén}{差不多|chà bu duō}{大|dà}{的|de}{兵马俑|bīng mǎ yǒng}，{他们|tā men}{估计|gū jì}{一共|yí gòng}{有|yǒu}{八千|bā qiān}{多|duō}{个|gè}。{一九八七|yī jiǔ bā qī}{年|nián}，{秦始皇陵|Qín Shǐ huáng líng}{被|bèi}{列入|liè rù}{了|le}{世界|shì jiè}{文化|wén huà}{遗产|yí chǎn}。{今天|jīn tiān}，{每|měi}{年|nián}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{从|cóng}{世界|shì jiè}{各地|gè dì}{来|lái}{这里|zhè lǐ}{参观|cān guān}。

1. What did the different states have before 221 BCE?
2. Name the four standards the text describes.
3. What does the text say about the shape of the coin?
4. Why do you think the writer uses {然而|rán ér} and {却|què} in the sentence about the dynasty?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Their own writing and money, and different standards of length and weight
   ({每|měi}{个|gè}{国家|guó jiā}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{自己|zì jǐ}{的|de}{文字|wén zì}{和|hé}{钱|qián}，{长度|cháng dù}、{重量|zhòng liàng}{的|de}{标准|biāo zhǔn}{也|yě}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}).
2. One script ({小篆|xiǎo zhuàn}); one standard for measuring length and weight; one bronze coin; one fixed distance
   between cart wheels.
3. It was round with a square hole and the characters {半两|bàn liǎng}, and this shape was used in China for
   over two thousand years afterwards.
4. To contrast the dynasty's short life ({仅仅|jǐn jǐn}{十|shí}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}) with the long life of its standards: {然而|rán ér} starts the
   contrast and {却|què} after the subject ({它|tā}{定|dìng}{下|xià}{的|de}{许多|xǔ duō}{标准|biāo zhǔn}) stresses it.

"**The First Emperor's 'standards'.** More than 2,200 years ago, China was still divided into
several states. Each had its own writing and money, and their standards of length and weight were
different too. In 221 BCE the state of Qin unified these states, and the king of Qin became China's
first emperor; later people called him 'Qin Shi Huang'. After unification, the First Emperor did
many things, and one of the most important was to unify the standards. First, the whole country
used one script: the 'small seal'. In this way people everywhere wrote characters the same way,
which made communication easier. Second, the whole country measured length and weight by the same
standard. Third, the whole country used only one kind of bronze coin. It was round, with a square hole in
the middle, and the two characters 'ban liang' written on it. This round coin with a square hole
was used in China for more than two thousand years. Fourth, the distance between a cart's two
wheels was fixed by a single rule, so that carts could travel on roads all over the country. The
Qin dynasty didn't last long, only some fifteen years. However, many of the standards it set
influenced the long period that followed. In 1974, some farmers near Xi'an were digging a well
when they found some figures made of pottery. Later, archaeologists found many life-sized
terracotta warriors and horses here; they estimate there are over 8,000 in all. In 1987, the First
Emperor's mausoleum was put on the World Heritage list. Today, many people come from all over the
world to visit every year."
</details>

## Key points

- 221 BCE: the state of {秦|Qín} unified the rival states; its king became the first {皇帝|huáng dì}, {秦始皇|Qín Shǐ huáng} (died 210 BCE).
  The {秦朝|Qín cháo} was short (to 207/206 BCE).
- Standards ({标准|biāo zhǔn}): one script ({小篆|xiǎo zhuàn}, small seal), one system of weights and measures, one bronze coin (round,
  square hole, {半两|bàn liǎng}), one width between cart wheels, and roads across the empire. {书|shū}{同|tóng}{文|wén}，{车|chē}{同|tóng}{轨|guǐ}.
- The terracotta army ({兵马俑|bīng mǎ yǒng}): found by farmers digging a well near {西安|Xī'ān} in 1974; an estimated 8,000+
  figures; the mausoleum on the World Heritage List since 1987.
- Words met in the reading: {统一|tǒng yī}, {皇帝|huáng dì}, {公元前|gōng yuán qián}, {长度|cháng dù}, {重量|zhòng liàng}, {圆|yuán}, {农民|nóng mín}, {挖|wā}, {陶|táo}, {考古|kǎo gǔ}, {列入|liè rù}.

lessons.title: The Grand Canal
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The second honors lesson of the money module is about a waterway that kept an empire's economy
moving for more than a thousand years: the Grand Canal ({大运河|Dà Yùn hé}), which links Beijing in the north with
Hangzhou in the south. You'll read how it was built in stages, what it carried and which cities
grew along it, first in English and then in a Chinese text written for this course. Figures are
rounded, and where the sources give different dates, both are mentioned.

New words are glossed where they appear; none of them joins your vocabulary reviews.

## A river made by people

China's great rivers, the Yellow River ({黄河|Huáng hé}) and the Yangtze ({长江|Cháng jiāng}), flow from west to east. For a
government in the north that needed rice and other grain from the rich south, that was a problem:
there was no waterway from south to north. The Grand Canal is the answer people dug.

- **Length**: the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal ({京杭大运河|Jīng Háng Dà Yùn hé}) is about 1,800 km long, and it's often
  described as the longest waterway ever built by people. Not all of it is a dug channel: in places it
  runs through rivers and lakes.
- **Where**: from Beijing in the north to Hangzhou ({杭州|Háng zhōu}) in {浙江|Zhè jiāng} (Zhejiang) province in the south,
  crossing the Yellow River and the Yangtze on the way.

## Built in stages

The canal wasn't built at once.

1. **Early canals.** Sections were dug from the 5th century BCE onwards, by different states, for
   their own needs.
2. **The Sui dynasty ({隋朝|Suí cháo}).** In the early 600s CE, the emperor Yangdi of Sui ordered the sections to be
   linked into one system. The great works began in 605 and took only a few years (sources give
   604–609 or 605–610). The route then ran from Hangzhou north to Yangzhou ({扬州|Yáng zhōu}), west to the capital
   region around Luoyang ({洛阳|Luò yáng}), and north again towards today's Beijing. Huge numbers of workers were
   forced to build it, and many died.
3. **The Yuan dynasty ({元朝|Yuán cháo}).** In the 13th century the capital moved to today's Beijing, then called
   Dadu. To bring grain there more directly, new sections were cut across Shandong in the 1280s (one,
   the Huitong Canal, was finished in 1289). The canal no longer went round by Luoyang: it ran almost
   straight from south to north, several hundred kilometres shorter. This is essentially the route of
   today's Beijing–Hangzhou canal.

## What it carried

For centuries the canal's main job was carrying tax grain from the south to the capital and the
armies of the north: a state transport system known as {漕运|cáo yùn} (cáo yùn, grain shipment). Boats also
carried salt and other goods, officials, merchants and travellers. Cities along it grew rich on the
trade: Hangzhou, Suzhou ({苏州|Sū zhōu}) and Yangzhou in the south, Huai'an and Jining further north, and
Tianjin near the northern end. (In 1855 a great flood changed the course of the Yellow River and cut the canal in Shandong; ships at sea and, later, railways took over much of its trade.)

Today barges still carry goods on long stretches, above all in the south, and boat trips show
visitors the old towns along its banks. In 2014 the Grand Canal was inscribed on UNESCO's World
Heritage List ({世界|shì jiè}{文化|wén huà}{遗产|yí chǎn}), as a series of canal sections and related sites (locks, bridges, wharves and others) spread over eight present-day provinces.

## Reading: the Grand Canal

A short text for learners. {运河|yùn hé} is a canal ({运|yùn}, to transport, + {河|hé}, a river), {人工|rén gōng} man-made, {挖|wā} to dig,
{工程|gōng chéng} engineering works, {隋朝|Suí cháo} and {元朝|Yuán cháo} the Sui and Yuan dynasties, {粮食|liáng shi} grain, {运|yùn} to carry, {河道|hé dào} a
channel, {绕|rào} to go round, {路程|lù chéng} the distance travelled, {来往|lái wǎng} coming and going, {列入|liè rù} to be put on a list and
{河段|hé duàn} a stretch (of a river or canal). {公元|gōng yuán} is "CE" and {下令|xià lìng} "to give an order".

> **{大运河|Dà Yùn hé}**
>
> {中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{河|hé}，{它|tā}{不|bù}{全|quán}{是|shì}{自然|zì rán}{的|de}{河|hé}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{河段|hé duàn}{是|shì}{人|rén}{挖|wā}{出来|chū lái}{的|de}，{这|zhè}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{大运河|Dà Yùn hé}。{大运河|Dà Yùn hé}{北|běi}{边|biān}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{开始|kāi shǐ}，{南|nán}{边|biān}{到|dào}{浙江|Zhè jiāng}{的|de}{杭州|Háng zhōu}，{长|cháng}{约|yuē}{一千八百|yì qiān bā bǎi}{公里|gōng lǐ}，{是|shì}{世界|shì jiè}{上|shàng}{最|zuì}{长|cháng}{的|de}{人工|rén gōng}{河|hé}。
>
> {大运河|Dà Yùn hé}{不|bú}{是|shì}{一|yí}{次|cì}{建成|jiàn chéng}{的|de}。{两千|liǎng qiān}{多|duō}{年|nián}{以前|yǐ qián}，{就|jiù}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{开始|kāi shǐ}{在|zài}{不同|bù tóng}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}{挖|wā}{河|hé}。{到|dào}{了|le}{隋朝|Suí cháo}，{皇帝|huáng dì}{下令|xià lìng}{把|bǎ}{这些|zhè xiē}{河道|hé dào}{连|lián}{起来|qǐ lái}。{公元|gōng yuán}{六|liù}〇{五|wǔ}{年|nián}{前后|qián hòu}，{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{工程|gōng chéng}{开始|kāi shǐ}{了|le}，{仅仅|jǐn jǐn}{用|yòng}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}，{南方|nán fāng}{和|hé}{北方|běi fāng}{就|jiù}{被|bèi}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{运河|yùn hé}{连|lián}{在|zài}{了|le}{一起|yì qǐ}。
>
> {元朝|Yuán cháo}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{首都|shǒu dū}{在|zài}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{北京|Běi jīng}。{为了|wèi le}{更|gèng}{快|kuài}{地|de}{把|bǎ}{南方|nán fāng}{的|de}{粮食|liáng shi}{运|yùn}{到|dào}{北京|Běi jīng}，{人们|rén men}{又|yòu}{挖|wā}{了|le}{新|xīn}{的|de}{河道|hé dào}。{运河|yùn hé}{不|bú}{再|zài}{绕|rào}{到|dào}{西|xī}{边|biān}{的|de}{洛阳|Luò yáng}，{而|ér}{是|shì}{从|cóng}{南|nán}{到|dào}{北|běi}{几乎|jī hū}{一直|yì zhí}{往|wǎng}{前|qián}，{路程|lù chéng}{短|duǎn}{了|le}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{百|bǎi}{公里|gōng lǐ}。{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{京杭大运河|Jīng Háng Dà Yùn hé}，{基本上|jī běn shang}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}。
>
> {一千|yì qiān}{多|duō}{年|nián}{来|lái}，{运河|yùn hé}{上|shàng}{的|de}{船|chuán}{运|yùn}{过|guo}{粮食|liáng shi}、{盐|yán}{和|hé}{铁|tiě}，{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{也|yě}{运送|yùn sòng}{军队|jūn duì}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{各种各样|gè zhǒng gè yàng}{的|de}{货物|huò wù}{和|hé}{来来往往|lái lái wǎng wǎng}{的|de}{人|rén}。{那|nà}{时候|shí hou}，{运河|yùn hé}{是|shì}{连接|lián jiē}{南方|nán fāng}{和|hé}{北方|běi fāng}{最|zuì}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{路|lù}。{运河|yùn hé}{边|biān}{上|shàng}{出现|chū xiàn}{了|le}{许多|xǔ duō}{城市|chéng shì}，{像|xiàng}{扬州|Yáng zhōu}、{苏州|Sū zhōu}、{杭州|Háng zhōu}，{生意|shēng yi}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{得|de}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。
>
> {二|èr}〇{一四|yī sì}{年|nián}，{大运河|Dà Yùn hé}{被|bèi}{列入|liè rù}{了|le}{世界|shì jiè}{文化|wén huà}{遗产|yí chǎn}。{今天|jīn tiān}，{一些|yì xiē}{河段|hé duàn}{上|shàng}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{船|chuán}{在|zài}{运|yùn}{货|huò}，{有的|yǒu de}{河段|hé duàn}{还|hái}{给|gěi}{农田|nóng tián}{送|sòng}{水|shuǐ}，{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{坐|zuò}{船|chuán}{游玩|yóu wán}，{看|kàn}{两岸|liǎng àn}{的|de}{风景|fēng jǐng}。

({铁|tiě}: iron; {运送|yùn sòng}: to transport; {军队|jūn duì}: troops; {连接|lián jiē}: to link; {农田|nóng tián}: farmland; {约|yuē}: about, written; {公里|gōng lǐ}: a kilometre, lesson 16; {自然|zì rán}: natural, lesson 27; {首都|shǒu dū}: a capital and {游玩|yóu wán},
{风景|fēng jǐng}: lesson 18; {出现|chū xiàn}: to appear, lesson 20; {几乎|jī hū}: almost, HSK 3; {各种各样|gè zhǒng gè yàng}: all kinds of; {来来往往|lái lái wǎng wǎng}: coming
and going; {两岸|liǎng àn}: both banks.)

1. Why isn't the canal simply a "natural" river?
2. What did the Sui emperor do, and roughly when?
3. Why was a new route dug under the Yuan, and what did it change?
4. Why does the writer mention the cities of Yangzhou, Suzhou and Hangzhou?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. Not all of it is a natural river: many stretches were dug by people ({它|tā}{不|bù}{全|quán}{是|shì}{自然|zì rán}{的|de}{河|hé}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{河段|hé duàn}{是|shì}{人|rén}{挖|wā}{出来|chū lái}{的|de}). The text still calls it the longest man-made river in the world.
2. He ordered the existing channels to be joined up; the great works began around 605 and took only a
   few years ({公元|gōng yuán}{六|liù}〇{五|wǔ}{年|nián}{前后|qián hòu}…{仅仅|jǐn jǐn}{用|yòng}{了|le}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}).
3. The capital was in today's Beijing, and grain from the south had to reach it faster; the new route
   went almost straight north instead of round by Luoyang, several hundred kilometres shorter.
4. To show what the canal brought: cities grew up along it and did a great deal of business
   ({生意|shēng yi}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{得|de}{很|hěn}{大|dà}). The writer moves from what the canal carried to what it made possible.

"**The Grand Canal.** China has a very long river that isn't all natural: many stretches of it were dug by
people. This is the Grand Canal. In the north it starts at Beijing, in the south it reaches Hangzhou in Zhejiang;
it is about 1,800 km long, the longest man-made river in the world. The Grand Canal wasn't built
all at once. More than two thousand years ago, people began digging channels in different places.
In the Sui dynasty, the emperor ordered these channels to be joined up. Around 605 CE huge works
began, and in only a few years the south and the north were joined by a single canal. In the Yuan
dynasty, the capital was in today's Beijing. To get grain from the south to Beijing faster, people
dug new channels. The canal no longer went round by Luoyang in the west, but ran almost straight
from south to north, several hundred kilometres shorter. Today's Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal
follows basically this route. For more than a thousand years, boats on the canal carried grain, salt and iron, and sometimes troops, as well as all kinds of goods and people coming and going. In those days the canal was the most important route linking south and north. Many cities grew up beside the canal, such
as Yangzhou, Suzhou and Hangzhou, and they did a great deal of business. In 2014 the Grand Canal
was put on the World Heritage list. Today some stretches still have boats carrying goods, some carry water to farmland, and many people take boat trips to see the scenery on both banks."
</details>

## Key points

- The Grand Canal ({大运河|Dà Yùn hé}, {京杭大运河|Jīng Háng Dà Yùn hé}) links Beijing and Hangzhou: about 1,800 km, often called the
  longest waterway built by people.
- Built in stages: early canals from the 5th century BCE; joined into one system under the Sui (works
  from about 605 CE); a direct south–north route under the Yuan (1280s).
- It carried tax grain north ({漕运|cáo yùn}), and salt, goods and people; cities such as Yangzhou, Suzhou and
  Hangzhou grew along it.
- UNESCO World Heritage List: 2014. Parts are still used by barges and boat trips.
- Words met in the reading: {运河|yùn hé}, {人工|rén gōng}, {挖|wā}, {工程|gōng chéng}, {粮食|liáng shi}, {运|yùn}, {河道|hé dào}, {路程|lù chéng}, {河段|hé duàn}.

lessons.title: Traffic and getting around
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 4 is about journeys: getting around the city (this lesson), planes and trains (17), sights
(18), hotels and meals on the road (19) and telling the story of a trip afterwards (20). You can
already ask the way, take a taxi and say how far somewhere is with {离|lí} (HSK 2 and 3). This lesson
adds the words of public transport, roads and parking, and four patterns that you'll meet in signs,
notices and news about traffic:

- {随着|suí zhe} (along with, as): one change going with another;
- {当|dāng}…{的|de}{时候|shí hou} / {当|dāng}…{时|shí} (when, at the moment when);
- written {自|zì} and {自|zì}…{起|qǐ} (from, starting from): the {从|cóng} of notices;
- {超过|chāo guò} (to exceed; to overtake).

At the end you can follow a route with a change of line, understand road signs, and read a
transport notice written in formal style.

## {随着|suí zhe}: along with, as

{随着|suí zhe} + a noun phrase says what something changes **along with**. The phrase usually names a change
(more cars, colder weather, a city growing), and the main clause names a second change that follows
from it:

{随着|suí zhe}{车|chē}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}，{堵车|dǔ chē}{也|yě}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{严重|yán zhòng}{了|le}。 — As there are more and more cars, the traffic jams are getting worse.

{随着|suí zhe}{天气|tiān qì}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}，{骑|qí}{电动车|diàn dòng chē}{上班|shàng bān}{的|de}{人|rén}{少|shǎo}{了|le}。 — As the weather gets colder, fewer people ride e-bikes to work.

{随着|suí zhe}{地铁|dì tiě}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{方便|fāng biàn}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{不|bù}{开车|kāi chē}{了|le}。 — With the metro getting more and more convenient, a lot of people have stopped driving.

Three things to notice:

- {随着|suí zhe} comes first, before the subject of the main clause: {随着|suí zhe}…，{堵车|dǔ chē}…, not ×{堵车|dǔ chē}{随着|suí zhe}….
- The main clause usually has a word of change: {越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}, {变|biàn}, {了|le}, {多|duō}{了|le} / {少|shǎo}{了|le}, {也|yě}. Without one,
  the sentence feels unfinished.
- {随着|suí zhe} sounds a little formal: it's common in news, notices and essays, and you'll hear it in
  careful speech. In a chat, people often just say {车|chē}{多|duō}{了|le}，{堵车|dǔ chē}{也|yě}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{严重|yán zhòng}{了|le}.

The {着|zhe} in {随着|suí zhe} is zhe, light, the same as in {看|kàn}{着|zhe} or {等|děng}{着|zhe}. {随|suí} alone means "to follow".

## {当|dāng}…{的|de}{时候|shí hou} and {当|dāng}…{时|shí}: when

You know …{的|de}{时候|shí hou} (HSK 2): {我|wǒ}{到|dào}{家|jiā}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{他|tā}{已经|yǐ jīng}{睡|shuì}{了|le}. Putting {当|dāng} dāng in front marks the moment more
clearly, "at the time when, just as":

{当|dāng}{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{车|chē}{已经|yǐ jīng}{开|kāi}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — When I got to the bus stop, the bus had already gone.

{当|dāng}{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{前方|qián fāng}{的|de}{十字路口|shí zì lù kǒu}{时|shí}，{向|xiàng}{右|yòu}{转|zhuǎn}。 — When you see the crossroads ahead, turn right.

{当|dāng}{车速|chē sù}{超过|chāo guò}{每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí}{一百|yì bǎi}{公里|gōng lǐ}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{要|yào}{特别|tè bié}{注意|zhù yì}{安全|ān quán}。 — When you're doing over a hundred kilometres an hour, take special care.

- {当|dāng} is optional in speech: {我|wǒ}{到|dào}{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}… says the same. With {当|dāng}, the sentence sounds more careful or
  written.
- {当|dāng}…{时|shí} ({时|shí} for {的|de}{时候|shí hou}) is the written short form: notices and instructions use it.
- {当|dāng} opens the clause; the subject comes after it: {当|dāng}{我|wǒ}{到|dào}…, not ×{我|wǒ}{当|dāng}{到|dào}…

## {自|zì} and {自|zì}…{起|qǐ}: from (written)

{自|zì} zì is the written word for {从|cóng} (from): it marks where or when something starts. You know it from
{来自|lái zì} (to come from, HSK 3). On signs, timetables and notices you'll see {自|zì}…{起|qǐ}, "starting from":

{自|zì}{十|shí}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{起|qǐ}，{地铁|dì tiě}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{开|kāi}{门|mén}。 — From 1 October, the metro opens at five every morning.

{自|zì}{下|xià}{周|zhōu}{一|yī}{起|qǐ}，{这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{公路|gōng lù}{上|shàng}{不|bù}{能|néng}{停车|tíng chē}。 — From next Monday, there's no parking on this road.

In speech the same idea is {从|cóng}…{开始|kāi shǐ} or {从|cóng}…{起|qǐ}:

| Written | Spoken | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {自|zì}{十|shí}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{起|qǐ} | {从|cóng}{十|shí}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{开始|kāi shǐ} | from 1 October on |
| {本|běn}{次|cì}{列车|liè chē}{自|zì}{北京|Běi jīng}{开出|kāi chū} | {这|zhè}{趟|tàng}{车|chē}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{开|kāi} | this train departs from Beijing |
| {自此|zì cǐ} (lesson 20: {从此|cóng cǐ}) | {从|cóng}{这个|zhè ge}{时候|shí hou}{开始|kāi shǐ} | from then on |

({列车|liè chē}: a train, the word of station announcements; {开出|kāi chū}: to depart.)

Don't use {自|zì} in conversation: {我|wǒ}{自|zì}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái} sounds like a radio announcement. Say {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}.

## {超过|chāo guò}: to exceed, to overtake

{超过|chāo guò} is "to go beyond": a number, a limit, or another car.

{市区|shì qū}{道路|dào lù}{上|shàng}，{车速|chē sù}{不|bù}{能|néng}{超过|chāo guò}{每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí}{六十|liù shí}{公里|gōng lǐ}。 — On city roads, your speed mustn't go over sixty kilometres an hour. ({市区|shì qū}: the city, the built-up area: lesson 18.)

{这|zhè}{趟|tàng}{大巴|dà bā}{的|de}{乘客|chéng kè}{已经|yǐ jīng}{超过|chāo guò}{五十|wǔ shí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{了|le}。 — This coach already has more than fifty passengers.

{前面|qián miàn}{的|de}{车|chē}{太|tài}{慢|màn}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{超过|chāo guò}{它|tā}。 — The car in front is too slow: I want to overtake it.

With a number, {超过|chāo guò} is the same as {以上|yǐ shàng} or {多|duō} in meaning ("more than"), but it's a verb: {超过|chāo guò}{五十|wǔ shí}{个|gè}{人|rén}.
Speeds are {每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí} + number + {公里|gōng lǐ}: {每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí}{六十|liù shí}{公里|gōng lǐ} (60 km an hour). In speech the {每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí} is often dropped
when it's clear: {他|tā}{开|kāi}{到|dào}{了|le}{一百二|yì bǎi èr}.

## Getting around: the words

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {交通|jiāo tōng} / {公共|gōng gòng}{交通|jiāo tōng} | traffic, transport / public transport | {北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{公共|gōng gòng}{交通|jiāo tōng}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}。 |
| {公共|gōng gòng} | public | {公共|gōng gòng}{汽车|qì chē} (a bus, written), {公共|gōng gòng}{厕所|cè suǒ} (a public toilet) |
| {乘坐|chéng zuò} / {乘|chéng} | to travel by (written) | {请|qǐng}{乘坐|chéng zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{前往|qián wǎng}。 Please go by metro. |
| {乘客|chéng kè} | passenger | {各位|gè wèi}{乘客|chéng kè}，… Dear passengers, … |
| {换乘|huàn chéng} | to change (lines, trains) | {在|zài}{这|zhè}{一|yí}{站|zhàn}{换乘|huàn chéng}{十号线|shí hào xiàn}。 |
| {出行|chū xíng} | to go out, travel (about town) | {节日|jié rì}{出行|chū xíng}{的|de}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 |
| {大巴|dà bā} | a coach, a big bus | {坐|zuò}{大巴|dà bā}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng} |
| {动车|dòng chē} | a high-speed train (the D trains) | {坐|zuò}{动车|dòng chē}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。 |
| {电动车|diàn dòng chē} | an e-bike, an electric scooter | {骑|qí}{电动车|diàn dòng chē} |
| {公路|gōng lù} / {高速|gāo sù} | a road, a highway / the expressway ({高速|gāo sù}{公路|gōng lù}) | {走|zǒu}{高速|gāo sù}{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 |
| {道路|dào lù} / {街道|jiē dào} | roads (written) / streets; a neighbourhood | {道路|dào lù}{两|liǎng}{边|biān}, {这|zhè}{条|tiáo}{街道|jiē dào} |
| {十字路口|shí zì lù kǒu} | a crossroads | {在|zài}{十字路口|shí zì lù kǒu}{向|xiàng}{左|zuǒ}{转|zhuǎn} |
| {前方|qián fāng} | ahead (written) | {前方|qián fāng}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{米|mǐ} |
| {入口|rù kǒu} / {出口|chū kǒu} | entrance / exit; {出口|chū kǒu} is also "to export" | {地铁|dì tiě}B{出口|chū kǒu} |
| {停|tíng} / {停车|tíng chē} | to stop; to park | {停|tíng}{一下|yí xià}{车|chē}, {在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{停车|tíng chē}？ |
| {停车场|tíng chē chǎng} / {车位|chē wèi} | a car park / a parking space | {停车场|tíng chē chǎng}{没有|méi yǒu}{车位|chē wèi}{了|le}。 |
| {加油站|jiā yóu zhàn} | a petrol station | {前面|qián miàn}{有|yǒu}{个|gè}{加油站|jiā yóu zhàn}。 |
| {交警|jiāo jǐng} | a traffic police officer (short for {交通|jiāo tōng}{警察|jǐng chá}; {警察|jǐng chá}, the police, is lesson 19's word) | {交警|jiāo jǐng}{让|ràng}{我们|wǒ men}{停车|tíng chē}。 |
| {堵车|dǔ chē} | to be in a traffic jam; a jam | {路上|lù shang}{堵车|dǔ chē}{了|le}。 |
| {速度|sù dù} / {车速|chē sù} | speed / the speed of a vehicle | {速度|sù dù}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}, {车速|chē sù}{太|tài}{快|kuài} |
| {快速|kuài sù} / {加快|jiā kuài} | fast (written) / to speed up | {快速|kuài sù}{公交|gōng jiāo}, {加快|jiā kuài}{速度|sù dù} |
| {距离|jù lí} | distance; to be (some way) from | {距离|jù lí}{太|tài}{远|yuǎn}{了|le}, {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{距离|jù lí}{公司|gōng sī}{五|wǔ}{公里|gōng lǐ}。 |
| {公里|gōng lǐ} | a kilometre | {四十|sì shí}{公里|gōng lǐ} |
| {路过|lù guò} | to pass by | {我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{上班|shàng bān}{都|dōu}{路过|lù guò}{这个|zhè ge}{公园|gōng yuán}。 |
| {转|zhuǎn} | to turn | {向|xiàng}{左|zuǒ}{转|zhuǎn}, {往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{转|zhuǎn} |
| {趟|tàng} | (a trip: there and back; a scheduled run) | {去|qù}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}{超市|chāo shì}, {下|xià}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}{车|chē} |

  write: {请|qǐng}{乘坐|chéng zuò}{地铁|dì tiě} (please take the metro), {乘|chéng}{车|chē} (to ride, in a sign). A person who rides is a
  {乘客|chéng kè}.

## Signs

Signs are short, written-style texts. Here are some you'll see in a Chinese city:

> {入口|rù kǒu} · {出口|chū kǒu} · {停车场|tíng chē chǎng} → · {前方|qián fāng}500{米|mǐ} {加油站|jiā yóu zhàn} · {地铁|dì tiě}{换乘|huàn chéng} · {此处|cǐ chù}{不|bù}{能|néng}{停车|tíng chē} · {车速|chē sù}{不|bù}{能|néng}{超过|chāo guò}60{公里|gōng lǐ}

{此处|cǐ chù} is "here" in writing ({此|cǐ} + {处|chù}, a place). Signs and notices also love {请|qǐng} + verb: {请|qǐng}{慢行|màn xíng} (please
drive slowly), {请|qǐng}{乘坐|chéng zuò}…, {请|qǐng}{从|cóng}B{出口|chū kǒu}{出站|chū zhàn} (please leave the station by exit B; {出站|chū zhàn}: to exit a station).
On the metro you'll hear {前方|qián fāng}{到站|dào zhàn}… (the next station is…): {前方|qián fāng} here means "coming up".

  turning stroke, the long sweep). {走|zǒu} is the other way round: in {趟|tàng}, all of {走|zǒu} comes first, its long
  sweep included, and {尚|shàng} sits on it afterwards (as in {起|qǐ} and {超|chāo}). {乘|chéng}: the short left-falling stroke and
  the long horizontal, then the two verticals of the middle, then the rest, with the long
  left-falling and right-falling strokes last. {度|dù}: {广|guǎng} first, then 廿 inside it, then {又|yòu}. {转|zhuǎn}: {车|chē} on the
  left (its last stroke rises, as {车|chē} does at the side), then {专|zhuān}.

(Traditional {+{随|suí}+}: 14 strokes; traditional {+{转|zhuǎn}+}: 車 + 專, 18 strokes.)

```trace
速乘巴堵警距
```

```trace
度停趟随转
```

**Write it** (✎ handwriting characters): {巴|bā} {度|dù} {停|tíng} {随|suí} {转|zhuǎn}. Write each three times from memory, on paper
or on the pad, then the words {大巴|dà bā}, {速度|sù dù}, {停车|tíng chē}, {随着|suí zhe} and {转|zhuǎn}.
=}

## Write it

1. **A sentence about a picture.** The picture: a long line of cars on an expressway; a driver is
   looking at his watch. Write one sentence with {堵车|dǔ chē}.
2. **A short text (80–120 characters).** How do you get to work or school? Say how far it is ({距离|jù lí}…{公里|gōng lǐ}),
   what you take ({换乘|huàn chéng}?), how long it takes, and what happens when the traffic is bad ({当|dāng}…{的|de}{时候|shí hou}).

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {高速|gāo sù}{公路|gōng lù}{上|shàng}{堵车|dǔ chē}{了|le}，{司机|sī jī}{一直|yì zhí}{看|kàn}{手表|shǒu biǎo}，{他|tā}{怕|pà}{迟到|chí dào}。 — There's a jam on the expressway; the driver keeps looking at his watch: he's afraid of being late.
2. {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{距离|jù lí}{公司|gōng sī}{十二|shí èr}{公里|gōng lǐ}。{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{乘坐|chéng zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{上班|shàng bān}，{要|yào}{换乘|huàn chéng}{一|yí}{次|cì}，{路上|lù shang}{大概|dà gài}{要|yào}{四十|sì shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}。{有|yǒu}{时候|shí hou}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{骑|qí}{电动车|diàn dòng chē}，{速度|sù dù}{不|bú}{快|kuài}，{可是|kě shì}{不|bú}{会|huì}{堵车|dǔ chē}。{当|dāng}{地铁|dì tiě}{上|shàng}{人|rén}{特别|tè bié}{多|duō}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{出门|chū mén}。{随着|suí zhe}{天气|tiān qì}{变|biàn}{冷|lěng}，{我|wǒ}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{骑|qí}{车|chē}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{冬天|dōng tiān}{我|wǒ}{一般|yì bān}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}。 — My home is twelve kilometres from the office. I take the metro to work every day, with one change; it takes about forty minutes. Sometimes I ride an e-bike: it isn't fast, but I don't get stuck in traffic. When the metro is really crowded, I leave home a bit earlier. As the weather gets colder I feel less and less like cycling, so in winter I usually take the metro. (about 110 characters)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Getting around
{请问|qǐng wèn}，{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}{要|yào}{换乘|huàn chéng}{吗|ma}？
= Excuse me, do I have to change to get to the airport?
{大巴|dà bā}{二十|èr shí}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}。
= There's a coach every twenty minutes.
{在|zài}{前面|qián miàn}{的|de}{十字路口|shí zì lù kǒu}{向|xiàng}{左|zuǒ}{转|zhuǎn}。
= Turn left at the crossroads ahead.
{学校|xué xiào}{距离|jù lí}{市区|shì qū}{四十|sì shí}{公里|gōng lǐ}。
= The school is forty kilometres from the city centre.
{车速|chē sù}{不|bù}{能|néng}{超过|chāo guò}{每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí}{六十|liù shí}{公里|gōng lǐ}。
= The speed mustn't go over sixty kilometres an hour.
{当|dāng}{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{车|chē}{已经|yǐ jīng}{开|kāi}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。
= When I got to the stop, the bus had already left.
```

## Pronunciation

- {乘|chéng} chéng (to ride) and {城|chéng} chéng (a city, lesson 18) are said the same; {乘客|chéng kè} chéng kè, {换乘|huàn chéng} huàn chéng.
- {距离|jù lí} jù lí: *ju* is written with u but said with ü (after j, q, x and y, ü is written u); *li* is a
  plain *i*.
- {堵车|dǔ chē} dǔ chē (3+1) and {停车|tíng chē} tíng chē (2+1): keep the tone of the first syllable clear, because {停|tíng} and {堵|dǔ}
  are the words that change.
- {趟|tàng} tàng (fourth tone) and {躺|tǎng} tǎng (to lie down, lesson 07, third tone): same syllable.
- {速度|sù dù} sù dù: two falling tones. {公里|gōng lǐ} gōng lǐ: {里|lǐ} keeps its third tone here.
- {随着|suí zhe} suí zhe: the {着|zhe} is light.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{堵车|dǔ chē}{随着|suí zhe}{车|chē}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}~~: {随着|suí zhe} opens the sentence: {随着|suí zhe}{车|chē}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{多|duō}，{堵车|dǔ chē}{也|yě}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{严重|yán zhòng}{了|le}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{当|dāng}{到|dào}{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}~~: {当|dāng} comes before the subject: {当|dāng}{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{车站|chē zhàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}….
- {我|wǒ}{自|zì}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái} in conversation isn't wrong grammar, but it sounds like an announcement: say
  {我|wǒ}{从|cóng}{北京|Běi jīng}{来|lái}. Keep {自|zì} and {自|zì}…{起|qǐ} for notices.
- {去|qù}{一|yí}{趟|tàng} and {去|qù}{一|yí}{次|cì}: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{了|le}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}{银行|yín háng} is a trip (there and back, often an errand); {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{过|guo}{三|sān}{次|cì}{上海|Shàng hǎi} counts
  occasions. {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{了|le}{三|sān}{趟|tàng}{上海|Shàng hǎi} is heard, but for visits to a city {次|cì} is the usual word.
- {坐|zuò} / {乘坐|chéng zuò}: {我|wǒ}{乘坐|chéng zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{上班|shàng bān} is correct, but stiff in a chat. Say {我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{上班|shàng bān} and keep {乘坐|chéng zuò} for
  notices and announcements.
- {车速|chē sù}{超过|chāo guò}{六十|liù shí} on a sign is fine, but in a sentence give the unit when it isn't clear: {超过|chāo guò}{每|měi}{小时|xiǎo shí}{六十|liù shí}{公里|gōng lǐ}.

## Key points

- {随着|suí zhe} + a change, main clause + another change ({越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}, {了|le}, {也|yě}): along with, as.
- ({当|dāng})…{的|de}{时候|shí hou} / {当|dāng}…{时|shí}: when; {当|dāng} before the subject; …{时|shí} is written.
- {自|zì} / {自|zì}…{起|qǐ}: from, starting from (written) = {从|cóng} / {从|cóng}…{开始|kāi shǐ} (spoken).
- {超过|chāo guò} + number or + a car: more than; to overtake.
- Register pairs: {乘坐|chéng zuò} / {坐|zuò}, {距离|jù lí} / {离|lí}, {前方|qián fāng} / {前面|qián miàn}, {不便|bú biàn} / {不|bù}{方便|fāng biàn}, {此处|cǐ chù} / {这儿|zhèr}.
- {趟|tàng} counts trips ({去|qù}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}) and scheduled runs ({下|xià}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}{车|chē}); {次|cì} counts occasions.
- New characters: {速|sù} {乘|chéng} {巴|bā} {堵|dǔ} {警|jǐng} {距|jù} {度|dù} {停|tíng} {趟|tàng} {随|suí} {转|zhuǎn} (✎: {巴|bā} {度|dù} {停|tíng} {随|suí} {转|zhuǎn}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Planes, trains and delays
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Last lesson got you round the city; this one gets you on a plane or a train, and deals with what
goes wrong on the way: delays, cancellations, a missed connection. The grammar is the language of
causes and results, and of hurrying:

- written {由于|yóu yú}…{因此|yīn cǐ} (because of… therefore), beside spoken {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ};
- {结果|jié guǒ} (as a result, and it turned out…);
- {来得及|lái de jí} / {来不及|lái bu jí} (there's still time / there's no time);
- {赶紧|gǎn jǐn} / {赶快|gǎn kuài} (hurry up and…), and the verb {赶|gǎn} (to rush to catch);
- written {再次|zài cì} (once again);
- {准时|zhǔn shí}, {准确|zhǔn què} and {准|zhǔn}: on time, exact, accurate.

At the end you can follow an airport delay notice, explain why you're late, and retell a short
travel story aloud, the first of the speaking-test tasks in this module.

## {由于|yóu yú}…{因此|yīn cǐ}: written cause and result

You've said "because… so" with {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ} since HSK 2. Notices, news and formal emails prefer **{由于|yóu yú}**
for the cause and **{因此|yīn cǐ}** for the result:

{由于|yóu yú}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn}，{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{起飞|qǐ fēi}。 — Owing to the weather, the flight's departure is delayed.

{由于|yóu yú}{雨|yǔ}{下|xià}{得|de}{太|tài}{大|dà}，{因此|yīn cǐ}{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{比赛|bǐ sài}{取消|qǔ xiāo}{了|le}。 — Because the rain is so heavy, today's match has been cancelled.

{由于|yóu yú}{路上|lù shang}{堵车|dǔ chē}，{我们|wǒ men}{没有|méi yǒu}{赶上|gǎn shàng}{飞机|fēi jī}，{因此|yīn cǐ}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{改|gǎi}{坐|zuò}{动车|dòng chē}。 — Because of a jam on the way, we didn't catch the plane, so we had to take the train instead.

How they combine:

| Cause | Result | Where |
|---|---|---|
| {因为|yīn wèi}… | {所以|suǒ yǐ}… | everywhere, above all speech |
| {由于|yóu yú}… | {所以|suǒ yǐ}… / {因此|yīn cǐ}… | writing, formal speech |
| (…。) | {因此|yīn cǐ}… | writing: {因此|yīn cǐ} can open a new sentence |

- {由于|yóu yú} can take a whole clause ({由于|yóu yú}{路上|lù shang}{堵车|dǔ chē}) or just a noun phrase ({由于|yóu yú}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn}, {由于|yóu yú}{大雨|dà yǔ}). With a
  noun, it's a preposition: "owing to".
- {因此|yīn cǐ} can open a new sentence after a full stop: {最近|zuì jìn}{机场|jī chǎng}{的|de}{安检|ān jiǎn}{很|hěn}{严格|yán gé}。{因此|yīn cǐ}，{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{提前|tí qián}{到|dào}{机场|jī chǎng}。 {所以|suǒ yǐ} can
  too, but {因此|yīn cǐ} sounds more like writing.
- {因为|yīn wèi}…{因此|yīn cǐ} is heard, but careful writers avoid it: pair {因为|yīn wèi} with {所以|suǒ yǐ}, and {由于|yóu yú} with {因此|yīn cǐ} or {所以|suǒ yǐ}.

The word {原因|yuán yīn} (a reason, a cause) goes with them: {由于|yóu yú}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn} (owing to the weather, literally "because
of weather reasons"), {航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{的|de}{原因|yuán yīn}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}？

## {结果|jié guǒ}: as a result

{结果|jié guǒ} is a noun, "result": {考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{结果|jié guǒ} (the exam results). At the start of a clause it means "and as a
result, and what happened was…", often something nobody wanted:

{他|tā}{早上|zǎo shang}{起|qǐ}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{结果|jié guǒ}{没|méi}{赶上|gǎn shàng}{飞机|fēi jī}。 — He got up late, and as a result he missed the plane.

{我们|wǒ men}{想|xiǎng}{走|zǒu}{近路|jìn lù}，{结果|jié guǒ}{走|zǒu}{错|cuò}{了|le}，{比|bǐ}{平时|píng shí}{还|hái}{晚|wǎn}{到|dào}{了|le}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 — We tried to take a short cut, and ended up going the wrong way: we arrived half an hour later than usual.

{结果|jié guǒ} belongs to stories: it reports what happened. For a reason or an explanation, use {因此|yīn cǐ} or {所以|suǒ yǐ}. ({走|zǒu}{近路|jìn lù}:
to take a short cut.)

## {来得及|lái de jí} and {来不及|lái bu jí}: is there still time?

{来得及|lái de jí} is "there's (still) enough time"; {来不及|lái bu jí} is "there isn't enough time, it's too late". They're
potential complements of {来|lái} (HSK 3's pattern, as in {听|tīng}{得|de}{懂|dǒng} / {听不懂|tīng bu dǒng}), and they can take a verb:

{现在|xiàn zài}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}{还|hái}{来得及|lái de jí}{吗|ma}？ — Is there still time to get to the airport?

{来得及|lái de jí}，{飞机|fēi jī}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{起飞|qǐ fēi}。 — Yes, there's time: the plane doesn't leave till ten.

{来不及|lái bu jí}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{打车|dǎ chē}{吧|ba}！ — There's no time: let's take a taxi!

{我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{来不及|lái bu jí}{吃|chī}{早饭|zǎo fàn}，{在|zài}{路上|lù shang}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{面包|miàn bāo}。 — I didn't have time for breakfast this morning, so I bought a bun on the way.

The {得|de} is light (de) and so is the {不|bù} (bu): lái de jí, lái bu jí. There's no ×{来|lái}{得|de}{不|bù}{及|jí}.

## {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}, {赶快|gǎn kuài} and {赶|gǎn}: hurry

{赶|gǎn} gǎn is "to rush to get somewhere in time", and it takes the thing you're rushing for:

{赶|gǎn}{飞机|fēi jī} (to rush for a plane), {赶|gǎn}{火车|huǒ chē}, {赶|gǎn}{时间|shí jiān} (to be in a hurry). {赶上|gǎn shàng} is "to catch, to make it in time
for": {我们|wǒ men}{赶上|gǎn shàng}{了|le}{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}{车|chē} (we caught the last bus); {没|méi}{赶上|gǎn shàng} (missed it).

{赶紧|gǎn jǐn} and {赶快|gǎn kuài} are adverbs: "quickly, at once, hurry up and…". Both work in requests:

{快|kuài}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{了|le}，{赶快|gǎn kuài}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}！ / {快|kuài}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{了|le}，{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{走|zǒu}{吧|ba}！ — It's nearly nine: hurry, let's go!

In a story, {赶紧|gǎn jǐn} is the more usual one:

{听|tīng}{到|dào}{广播|guǎng bō}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{他|tā}{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{拿|ná}{起|qǐ}{背包|bēi bāo}{去|qù}{了|le}{登机口|dēng jī kǒu}。 — When he heard the announcement, he grabbed his backpack and hurried to the gate.

({广播|guǎng bō}: an announcement, a broadcast: lesson 24's word. {登机口|dēng jī kǒu}: the departure gate.)

Don't confuse {赶快|gǎn kuài} with {快|kuài}: {快|kuài} + verb + {了|le} is "about to" ({快|kuài}{起飞|qǐ fēi}{了|le}, it's about to take off), while {赶快|gǎn kuài} + verb
is "hurry and…".

## {再次|zài cì}: once again (written)

{再次|zài cì} is the written word for "again": it can look back like {又|yòu} or forward like {再|zài}.

{航班|háng bān}{再次|zài cì}{推迟|tuī chí}。 — The flight has been delayed again.

{再次|zài cì}{感谢|gǎn xiè}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{支持|zhī chí}！ — Thank you all once again for your support!

In speech you'd say {航班|háng bān}{又|yòu}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le} or {谢谢|xiè xie}{大家|dà jiā}. {再次|zài cì} is for notices, speeches and emails.

## {准时|zhǔn shí}, {准确|zhǔn què} and {准|zhǔn}

All three come from {准|zhǔn} zhǔn, "accurate, exact":

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {准时|zhǔn shí} | on time, punctual | {飞机|fēi jī}{准时|zhǔn shí}{起飞|qǐ fēi}{了|le}。 {请|qǐng}{准时|zhǔn shí}{到|dào}。 |
| {准确|zhǔn què} | accurate, exact (information, numbers, words) | {准确|zhǔn què}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}, {他|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{发音|fā yīn}{很|hěn}{准确|zhǔn què}。 |
| {准|zhǔn} | accurate (spoken; of a clock, a guess, a forecast) | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手表|shǒu biǎo}{不|bù}{准|zhǔn}, {你|nǐ}{猜|cāi}{得|de}{真|zhēn}{准|zhǔn}！ |

{准时|zhǔn shí} is for people and timetables; {准确|zhǔn què} for facts and language; {准|zhǔn} alone is mostly spoken, often with
{不|bù}: {天气预报|tiān qì yù bào}{不|bú}{太|tài}{准|zhǔn} (the forecast isn't very reliable; {天气预报|tiān qì yù bào}: the weather forecast). ({猜|cāi}, to guess, is
lesson 20's word.)

## Flying and taking the train

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {航班|háng bān} | a flight | {这个|zhè ge}{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。 |
| {登机|dēng jī} | to board (a plane) | {九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}{开始|kāi shǐ}{登机|dēng jī}。 |
| {安检|ān jiǎn} | the security check | {过|guò}{安检|ān jiǎn} (to go through security), {安检|ān jiǎn}{很|hěn}{严格|yán gé}。 |
| {起飞|qǐ fēi} / {降落|jiàng luò} | to take off / to land | {飞机|fēi jī}{降落|jiàng luò}{了|le}。 |
| {推迟|tuī chí} / {提前|tí qián} | to postpone, delay / to bring forward, do in advance | {推迟|tuī chí}{半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, {提前|tí qián}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{到|dào} |
| {取消|qǔ xiāo} | to cancel | {航班|háng bān}{取消|qǔ xiāo}{了|le}。 |
| {错过|cuò guò} | to miss (a flight, a chance) | {错过|cuò guò}{了|le}{飞机|fēi jī} |
| {转机|zhuǎn jī} | to change planes | {在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{转机|zhuǎn jī} |
| {暂停|zàn tíng} | to stop for a while, suspend | {这|zhè}{趟|tàng}{车|chē}{暂停|zàn tíng}{一|yì}{天|tiān}。 |
| {座位|zuò wèi} | a seat | {靠窗|kào chuāng}{的|de}{座位|zuò wèi} (a window seat) |

with the questions in mind: what's happened, until when, and what should passengers do?

> **{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{通知|tōng zhī}**
>

## Speaking: retell it

In the speaking test, as reported from the sample papers, you hear a short passage twice and retell
it in your own words (about forty seconds each, for two passages). Practise with this one: listen,
then retell it without looking. You needn't use every word: keep the order of events and the key
words ({推迟|tuī chí}, {来不及|lái bu jí}, {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}, {结果|jié guǒ}).

```speak
# Retell: the last flight
{上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{成都|Chéng dū}{出差|chū chāi}，{回|huí}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{那|nà}{天|tiān}，{由于|yóu yú}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn}，{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。{我|wǒ}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{要|yào}{开会|kāi huì}，{开始|kāi shǐ}{我|wǒ}{以为|yǐ wéi}{来不及|lái bu jí}{了|le}，{心里|xīn li}{很|hěn}{着急|zháo jí}。{我|wǒ}{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{给|gěi}{经理|jīng lǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}，{经理|jīng lǐ}{说|shuō}{会议|huì yì}{可以|kě yǐ}{推迟|tuī chí}{到|dào}{下午|xià wǔ}。{结果|jié guǒ}，{飞机|fēi jī}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十一|shí yī}{点|diǎn}{才|cái}{起飞|qǐ fēi}，{两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{多|duō}{才|cái}{降落|jiàng luò}。{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{我|wǒ}{准时|zhǔn shí}{到|dào}{了|le}{公司|gōng sī}，{会|huì}{也|yě}{开|kāi}{得|de}{很|hěn}{顺利|shùn lì}。
= Last month I went to Chengdu on business. On the day I flew back to Beijing, the flight was delayed three hours because of the weather. I had a meeting at nine the next morning, and at first I thought I wouldn't make it: I was really worried. I quickly rang my manager, who said the meeting could be moved to the afternoon. In the end the plane only took off at eleven at night and landed after two. The next day I was at the office on time, and the meeting went smoothly.
```

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

{说话人|shuō huà rén}{去|qù}{成都|Chéng dū}{出差|chū chāi}，{回|huí}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。{他|tā}{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{上午|shàng wǔ}{要|yào}{开会|kāi huì}，{怕|pà}{来不及|lái bu jí}，{就|jiù}{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{给|gěi}{经理|jīng lǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}，{经理|jīng lǐ}{把|bǎ}{会议|huì yì}{推迟|tuī chí}{到|dào}{了|le}{下午|xià wǔ}。{结果|jié guǒ}{飞机|fēi jī}{两|liǎng}{点|diǎn}{多|duō}{才|cái}{到|dào}{北京|Běi jīng}，{第|dì}{二|èr}{天|tiān}{他|tā}{还是|hái shi}{准时|zhǔn shí}{到|dào}{了|le}{公司|gōng sī}，{会|huì}{开|kāi}{得|de}{很|hěn}{顺利|shùn lì}。

The speaker went to Chengdu on business, and the flight back was delayed three hours. There was a
meeting the next morning; afraid of not making it, the speaker rang the manager, who moved the
meeting to the afternoon. In the end the plane only landed after two, but the speaker was at the office on
time the next day, and the meeting went well. ({会议|huì yì}: a meeting, written; {说话人|shuō huà rén}: the speaker. The passage
doesn't say whether the speaker is a man or a woman: {他|tā} here is a choice; {她|tā} would be as good.)
</details>

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 背 ✎ | to carry on the back; the back | bēi, bèi | ⺼ | 9 | {背|bēi}, {背包|bēi bāo} |
| 籍 | register; records | jí | ⺮ | 20 | {国籍|guó jí} |
| 航 | to sail, fly | háng | 舟 | 10 | {航班|háng bān} |
| 登 | to climb, board | dēng | 癶 | 12 | {登机|dēng jī} |
| 赶 (traditional {+赶+}) | to hurry, catch | gǎn | {走|zǒu} | 10 | {赶|gǎn}, {赶上|gǎn shàng}, {赶紧|gǎn jǐn}, {赶快|gǎn kuài} |
| 紧 (traditional {+紧+}) | tight; urgent | jǐn | 糸 | 10 | {赶紧|gǎn jǐn} ({紧张|jǐn zhāng}: lesson 23) |
| 落 | to fall, land | luò | 艹 | 12 | {降落|jiàng luò} |
| 售 | to sell | shòu | {口|kǒu} | 11 | {售票员|shòu piào yuán} |
| 签 (traditional {+签+}) | to sign | qiān | ⺮ | 13 | {签证|qiān zhèng} |
| 消 | to vanish; to remove | xiāo | 氵 | 10 | {取消|qǔ xiāo} |
| 秒 | a second | miǎo | 禾 | 9 | {秒|miǎo} |
| 座 ✎ | a seat | zuò | {广|guǎng} | 10 | {座位|zuò wèi} ({座|zuò}: lesson 18) |

Three differ in traditional: {赶|gǎn} is {+{赶|gǎn}+} (14 strokes: 走 with 旱, not {干|gān}), {紧|jǐn} is {+{紧|jǐn}+} (14 strokes), and
{签|qiān} is {+签+} (19 strokes).

- **Phonetic series.** 肖 xiāo gives the sound of {消|xiāo} xiāo (氵 + 肖), and, less closely, of {销|xiāo} and {宵|xiāo}
  (later). {少|shǎo} shǎo is inside {秒|miǎo} miǎo (禾 + {少|shǎo}): the sound no longer matches. 亢 kàng gives the sound of
  {航|háng} háng (舟 + 亢) only loosely. {坐|zuò} zuò inside {座|zuò} zuò matches exactly: {广|guǎng} (a building) + {坐|zuò} (to sit),
  a seat.
- **Semantic families.** 舟 (a boat) on the left of {航|háng}, as in {船|chuán} (a ship): sailing came before flying.
  ⺮ (bamboo) on top of {签|qiān} and {籍|jí}: labels and records were once written on bamboo strips (that's
  history; read the character as a memory aid). 艹 on {落|luò}: the first meaning is said to be leaves
  falling (a memory aid).
- **Look-alikes.** {座|zuò} and {坐|zuò}: {坐|zuò} is the verb (to sit), {座|zuò} the seat ({座位|zuò wèi}) and a measure word ({一|yí}{座|zuò}{山|shān},
  lesson 18). {售|shòu} and {集|jí} share 隹 on top ({口|kǒu} below in {售|shòu}, {木|mù} in {集|jí}). {紧|jǐn} and {坚|jiān} (firm, later) share their top: two short
  verticals and {又|yòu}; {紧|jǐn} has 糸 below, {坚|jiān} has 土.
- **Stroke order.** {赶|gǎn}: {走|zǒu} is written in full first (its long sweep too), then {干|gān} sits on it. {登|dēng}: 癶 first
  (5 strokes), then {豆|dòu}. {背|bēi}: {北|běi} on top (left side first: vertical, horizontal, rising stroke; then the
  right: left-falling, then the vertical-bend-hook), then {月|yuè}. {秒|miǎo}: 禾 (5), then {少|shǎo} (4).

(Traditional {+{赶|gǎn}+}: 走 + 旱; traditional {+签+}: ⺮ over 僉.)

```trace
背籍航登赶紧
```

```trace trad=落售簽消秒座
落售签消秒座
```

**Write it** (✎ handwriting characters): {背|bēi} and {座|zuò}. Write each three times from memory, then the words
{背包|bēi bāo} and {座位|zuò wèi}.
=}

## Write it

1. **A sentence about a picture.** The picture: a woman is running through an airport with a
   suitcase; the clock above the gate says 9:58, and a sign says "10:00 {停止|tíng zhǐ}{登机|dēng jī}" (boarding closes at
   ten). Write one sentence with {来得及|lái de jí} or {来不及|lái bu jí}.
2. **A short text (80–120 characters).** Write about a journey that didn't go to plan: what went
   wrong ({由于|yóu yú}…), what you did ({赶紧|gǎn jǐn}…), and how it ended ({结果|jié guǒ}…).

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {还|hái}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{就|jiù}{停止|tíng zhǐ}{登机|dēng jī}{了|le}，{她|tā}{跑|pǎo}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}，{希望|xī wàng}{还|hái}{来得及|lái de jí}。 — Boarding closes in two minutes: she's running fast, hoping she'll still make it. ({停止|tíng zhǐ}: to stop, written: lesson 28.)
2. {去年|qù nián}{寒假|hán jià}{我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{回|huí}{老家|lǎo jiā}。{由于|yóu yú}{下|xià}{大雪|dà xuě}，{火车|huǒ chē}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{才|cái}{开|kāi}。{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{站|zhàn}{换乘|huàn chéng}{别的|bié de}{车|chē}，{可是|kě shì}{到站|dào zhàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{已经|yǐ jīng}{来不及|lái bu jí}{了|le}，{那|nà}{趟|tàng}{车|chē}{刚|gāng}{开|kāi}{走|zǒu}。{我|wǒ}{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{去|qù}{问|wèn}{售票员|shòu piào yuán}，{她|tā}{说|shuō}{晚上|wǎn shang}{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{趟|tàng}。{结果|jié guǒ}{我|wǒ}{十二|shí èr}{点|diǎn}{多|duō}{才|cái}{到|dào}{家|jiā}，{不过|bú guò}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{人|rén}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{等|děng}{我|wǒ}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{温暖|wēn nuǎn}。 — Last winter holiday I took the train home. Because of heavy snow, the train left two hours late. I was due to change trains in Beijing, but by the time we got in it was too late: my train had just left. I hurried to ask the ticket seller, and she said there was another one in the evening. In the end I didn't get home till after twelve, but my family had waited up for me, and it felt very warm. ({老家|lǎo jiā}: your family's home town, lesson 21; {温暖|wēn nuǎn}: warm, glossed.) (about 115 characters)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# At the airport
{由于|yóu yú}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn}，{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。
= The flight has been delayed because of the weather.
{现在|xiàn zài}{去|qù}{机场|jī chǎng}{还|hái}{来得及|lái de jí}{吗|ma}？
= Is there still time to get to the airport?
{来不及|lái bu jí}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{赶紧|gǎn jǐn}{打车|dǎ chē}{吧|ba}！
= There's no time: let's get a taxi, quick!
{请问|qǐng wèn}，{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{开始|kāi shǐ}{登机|dēng jī}？
= Excuse me, what time does boarding start?
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{要|yào}{一|yí}{个|gè}{靠窗|kào chuāng}{的|de}{座位|zuò wèi}。
= I'd like a window seat.
{他|tā}{起|qǐ}{晚|wǎn}{了|le}，{结果|jié guǒ}{没|méi}{赶上|gǎn shàng}{飞机|fēi jī}。
= He got up late, and missed the plane.
```

## Pronunciation

- {赶|gǎn} gǎn and {敢|gǎn} gǎn (to dare, lesson 20) are the same syllable; {干|gàn} gàn (to do) has the fourth tone.
- {来得及|lái de jí} lái de jí / {来不及|lái bu jí} lái bu jí: the middle syllable is light in both.
- {背|bēi} bēi (to carry: {背包|bēi bāo} bēi bāo) and {背|bèi} bèi (the back; to learn by heart): only the tone tells them
  apart.
- {准时|zhǔn shí} zhǔn shí, {准确|zhǔn què} zhǔn què: *zh* with the tongue curled back; {确|què} què has *q* + ü (written ue).
- {航班|háng bān} háng bān: rising, then level. {降落|jiàng luò} jiàng luò: two falling tones.
- {秒|miǎo} miǎo, third tone: {三十|sān shí}{秒|miǎo} sān shí miǎo.

## Common mistakes

- {因为|yīn wèi}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn}，{因此|yīn cǐ}{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le} is heard, but careful writers pair {因为|yīn wèi} with {所以|suǒ yǐ} and {由于|yóu yú} with {因此|yīn cǐ}: {由于|yóu yú}{北京|Běi jīng}{有|yǒu}{大雨|dà yǔ}，{因此|yīn cǐ}….
  After a short {由于|yóu yú} phrase (a noun, not a clause), writers usually leave {因此|yīn cǐ} out: {由于|yóu yú}{天气|tiān qì}{原因|yuán yīn}，{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}.
- ~~{来|lái}{得|de}{不|bù}{及|jí}~~: the forms are {来得及|lái de jí} and {来不及|lái bu jí}, nothing in between.
- {结果|jié guǒ} for a reason: ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{结果|jié guǒ}{我|wǒ}{早|zǎo}{睡|shuì}{了|le}~~ reads as if going to bed early was an unlucky outcome. For a
  choice you made, say {所以|suǒ yǐ}: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{早|zǎo}{睡|shuì}{了|le}.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{错过|cuò guò}{你|nǐ}~~ for "I miss you": {错过|cuò guò} is missing a plane or a chance; missing a person is {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{你|nǐ}.
- ~~{航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}{到|dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}~~: the new time goes straight after the verb: {航班|háng bān}{推迟|tuī chí}{到|dào}{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{了|le}, or the amount: {推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}.
- {准时|zhǔn shí} for people and timetables, {准确|zhǔn què} for facts: ~~{他|tā}{的|de}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{很|hěn}{准时|zhǔn shí}~~ → {他|tā}{的|de}{发音|fā yīn}{很|hěn}{准确|zhǔn què}.

## Key points

- {由于|yóu yú}…({因此|yīn cǐ} / {所以|suǒ yǐ}): cause and result in writing; {由于|yóu yú} + noun = owing to.
- {结果|jié guǒ}: and as a result… (a reported outcome, often unwanted).
- {来得及|lái de jí} / {来不及|lái bu jí} (+ verb): there's still time / it's too late.
- {赶|gǎn} + plane / train; {赶上|gǎn shàng} (to catch); {赶紧|gǎn jǐn} / {赶快|gǎn kuài} + verb (hurry and…).
- {再次|zài cì}: again (written). {推迟|tuī chí} later, {提前|tí qián} earlier, + the time.
- {准时|zhǔn shí} (on time), {准确|zhǔn què} (exact), {准|zhǔn} (spoken: accurate).
- New characters: {背|bēi} {籍|jí} {航|háng} {登|dēng} {赶|gǎn} {紧|jǐn} {落|luò} {售|shòu} {签|qiān} {消|xiāo} {秒|miǎo} {座|zuò} (✎: {背|bēi} {座|zuò}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Scenery and sights
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

You can already say a place is beautiful ({漂亮|piào liang}, HSK 1) or very beautiful ({太|tài}{漂亮|piào liang}{了|le}, {漂亮|piào liang}{极了|jí le}). This lesson
gives you the words of sightseeing (scenery, sights, provinces, bridges, guides) and two ways of
saying more:

- exclamations with **{多么|duō me}** and the strong adverb **{十分|shí fēn}**;
- **{既|jì}…{又|yòu} / {既|jì}…{也|yě}**: both… and (a more careful {又|yòu}…{又|yòu}).

There's also the measure word **{座|zuò}** for mountains, bridges, buildings and cities, and the
difference between {参观|cān guān}, {游玩|yóu wán}, {旅行|lǚ xíng} and {度假|dù jià}. At the end you can read a guidebook entry and talk
about a weekend trip.

## {多么|duō me}: how…! what a…!

{多么|duō me} + adjective makes an exclamation, usually closed by {啊|a} (after a vowel it often sounds like ya):

{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{风景|fēng jǐng}{多么|duō me}{美|měi}{啊|a}！ — How beautiful the scenery is here!

{多么|duō me}{美丽|měi lì}{的|de}{景色|jǐng sè}{啊|a}！ — What a beautiful view!

You know the short spoken form {多|duō} + adjective + {啊|a} ({多|duō}{好|hǎo}{啊|a}!). {多么|duō me} is the same, a little more
emphatic, and common in writing, songs and speeches. It also works inside a statement, to say how
much:

{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{我|wǒ}{多么|duō me}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{承德|Chéng dé}。 — You don't know how much I want to go to Chengde.

Don't confuse it with {多|duō} in questions: {承德|Chéng dé}{多|duō}{远|yuǎn}？ (how far is Chengde?) asks for an amount; {承德|Chéng dé}{多么|duō me}{远|yuǎn}{啊|a}！ (how
far Chengde is!) exclaims.

## {十分|shí fēn}: very (and more)

{十分|shí fēn} (literally "ten parts out of ten") is a strong "very", about as strong as {非常|fēi cháng} and a little more formal:

{山庄|shān zhuāng}{里|lǐ}{十分|shí fēn}{安静|ān jìng}。 — It's very quiet in the resort.

{这个|zhè ge}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{十分|shí fēn}{值得|zhí de}{去|qù}。 — This sight is very much worth a visit.

{我们|wǒ men}{十分|shí fēn}{感谢|gǎn xiè}{导游|dǎo yóu}{的|de}{帮助|bāng zhù}。 — We're very grateful for the guide's help.

- {十分|shí fēn} goes before adjectives and verbs of feeling or attitude: {十分|shí fēn}{高兴|gāo xìng}, {十分|shí fēn}{满意|mǎn yì}, {十分|shí fēn}{重视|zhòng shì}.
- It can come before {不|bù}: {十分|shí fēn}{不|bù}{方便|fāng biàn} (very inconvenient). Its opposite, {不|bù}{十分|shí fēn} (not very), is written
  style; speech says {不|bú}{太|tài}.
- Don't use it with a degree complement or {极了|jí le}: ~~{十分|shí fēn}{好|hǎo}{极了|jí le}~~. One intensifier is enough.

## {既|jì}…{又|yòu} and {既|jì}…{也|yě}: both… and

{既|jì} jì…{又|yòu}… joins two qualities of the same thing, like {又|yòu}…{又|yòu} (HSK 3), but sounds more careful and
puts a little more weight on the second:

{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{既|jì}{安静|ān jìng}{又|yòu}{漂亮|piào liang}。 — This place is both quiet and pretty.

{承德|Chéng dé}{的|de}{秋天|qiū tiān}{既|jì}{不|bú}{太|tài}{热|rè}，{也|yě}{不|bú}{太|tài}{冷|lěng}。 — Autumn in Chengde is neither too hot nor too cold.

{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{去|qù}{承德|Chéng dé}{既|jì}{快|kuài}{又|yòu}{方便|fāng biàn}。 — Taking the high-speed train to Chengde is quick and convenient.

{既|jì}…{也|yě} is more usual when the two parts are verb phrases or longer:

{山庄|shān zhuāng}{里|lǐ}{既|jì}{可以|kě yǐ}{爬|pá}{山|shān}，{也|yě}{可以|kě yǐ}{看|kàn}{湖|hú}。 — In the resort you can climb hills and also look at the lakes.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{旅行|lǚ xíng}，{我们|wǒ men}{既|jì}{参观|cān guān}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{景点|jǐng diǎn}，{也|yě}{吃|chī}{到|dào}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{美食|měi shí}。 — On this trip we visited lots of sights and ate lots of good food too.

Rules:

- One subject, before {既|jì}: {这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{既|jì}…{又|yòu}…. ~~{既|jì}{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{安静|ān jìng}…~~ is wrong.
- The two halves should match in kind (two adjectives, or two verb phrases).
- {既|jì} here is not {既然|jì rán} (lesson 01: since, now that), even though they share a character.

## {座|zuò}: mountains, bridges, buildings, cities

{座|zuò} is the measure word for large, fixed things:

{一|yí}{座|zuò}{山|shān}, {一|yí}{座|zuò}{桥|qiáo}, {两|liǎng}{座|zuò}{楼|lóu} (two buildings), {一|yí}{座|zuò}{城市|chéng shì}, {这|zhè}{座|zuò}{寺庙|sì miào} (this temple).

A building is also counted with {栋|dòng} dòng ({一|yí}{栋|dòng}{楼|lóu}), or just {个|gè} in casual speech, but {座|zuò} is the word for
mountains and bridges. {座|zuò} is also a seat ({座位|zuò wèi}, lesson 17): the character shows {={广|guǎng}=} (a building) over
{坐|zuò} (to sit).

"**Chengde.** Chengde is in the northeast of Hebei province, a little over 200 km from the capital,
Beijing: about an hour by high-speed train. It isn't a big city, but it's very much worth a visit.
Chengde's most famous sight is the Mountain Resort. From 1703 to 1792 the Qing emperors spent nearly
ninety years building great grounds here. Beijing is hot in summer, but Chengde is cool, so the
emperors often came to stay for several months. The resort has hills and lakes, and many bridges
and old buildings too. The scenic area is huge: you couldn't see it all in a day's walking. In 1994
the Mountain Resort and the temples around it became a World Heritage site together. Besides the
resort, there are many beautiful views around Chengde. In autumn the leaves on the hills turn red,
and the scenery is gorgeous, drawing visitors from all over the world. Tips: the city of Chengde isn't big, and it's easy to get to all the
sights by taxi. From Beijing you can go in the morning and come back in the evening, but it's best
to stay a night. On public holidays the scenic area is very crowded, so it's best to buy tickets online in advance. Visiting the resort
takes about a day; you can hire a guide and hear stories about it, which makes it more fun. And
when you travel to Chengde, don't forget to try the local snacks."

| 景 | a view, scenery | jǐng | {日|rì} | 12 | {风景|fēng jǐng}, {景点|jǐng diǎn}, {景区|jǐng qū}, {景色|jǐng sè}, {美景|měi jǐng} |
| 导 ✎ (traditional {+导+}) | to guide, lead | dǎo | 寸 | 6 | {导游|dǎo yóu} |
| 江 ✎ | a (big) river | jiāng | 氵 | 6 | {江|jiāng} |
| 郊 | the outskirts | jiāo | 阝 | 8 | {郊区|jiāo qū} |
| 桥 (traditional {+桥+}) | a bridge | qiáo | {木|mù} | 10 | {桥|qiáo} |
| 省 ✎ | a province; to save | shěng | {目|mù} | 9 | {省|shěng} |
| 纪 (traditional {+纪+}) | a record; an age | jì | 纟 | 6 | {世纪|shì jì} |
| 丽 (traditional {+丽+}) | beautiful | lì | 丶 | 7 | {美丽|měi lì} |
| 亚 ✎ (traditional {+亚+}) | Asia; second | yà | {一|yī} | 6 | {亚洲|Yà zhōu} |
| 洲 | a continent | zhōu | 氵 | 9 | {亚洲|Yà zhōu} |
| 吸 | to breathe in, draw | xī | {口|kǒu} | 6 | {吸引|xī yǐn} |
| 引 | to lead, draw | yǐn | 弓 | 4 | {吸引|xī yǐn} |
| 著 | to write; marked | zhù | 艹 | 11 | {著名|zhù míng} |

Six of these differ in traditional, with many more strokes: {+{观|guān}+} (25: 雚 + 見), {+{导|dǎo}+} (15: {道|dào} + 寸),
{+{桥|qiáo}+} (16), {+{纪|jì}+} (9: 糸 on the left), {+{丽|lì}+} (19: 丽 over 鹿) and {+{亚|yà}+} (8).

- **Phonetic series.** {交|jiāo} jiāo gives the sound of {郊|jiāo} jiāo ({交|jiāo} + 阝) exactly, and you know it in {校|xiào} xiào
  and {饺|jiǎo} jiǎo too. {工|gōng} gōng gives the sound of {江|jiāng} jiāng only loosely (as in {红|hóng} hóng, {空|kōng} kōng). {州|zhōu} zhōu
  in {洲|zhōu} zhōu matches exactly: 氵 + {州|zhōu} (a region), a continent. {京|jīng} jīng is inside {景|jǐng} jǐng ({日|rì} + {京|jīng}): a
  close sound. {己|jǐ} jǐ gives the sound of {纪|jì} jì (纟 + {己|jǐ}) and {记|jì} jì (讠 + {己|jǐ}): mind the look-alike {已|yǐ}
  yǐ.
- **Semantic families.** 氵 (water) in {江|jiāng} and {洲|zhōu}, as in {河|hé} and {海|hǎi}. 纟 (silk, thread) in {纪|jì}, as in {红|hóng}, {级|jí}, {结|jié}. {口|kǒu} in {吸|xī} (to breathe in) and {吃|chī}, {喝|hē}. {目|mù} (an eye) is
  under {少|shǎo} in {省|shěng}: the "save" meaning of {省|shěng} ({省|shěng}{钱|qián}, to save money) is everyday speech.
- **Look-alikes.** {纪|jì} / {记|jì}: 纟 or 讠 with {己|jǐ}. {观|guān} / {现|xiàn} / {见|jiàn}: {观|guān} is {又|yòu} + {见|jiàn}, {现|xiàn} is {王|wáng} + {见|jiàn}. {引|yǐn} is 弓 + a vertical. {著|zhù} / {着|zhe}: {著|zhù} has 艹 and {者|zhě}, {着|zhe} has a {羊|yáng}-like top and {目|mù}; in traditional script {着|zhe} is
  written {+{著|zhù}+} (lesson 16's {随着|suí zhe} → {+{随着|suí zhe}+}).
- **Stroke order.** {江|jiāng}: the three water strokes first, then {工|gōng}. {导|dǎo}: 巳 on top (the turning stroke, the
  short horizontal, the vertical-bend-hook), then 寸. {亚|yà}: the top horizontal, the two inner verticals,
  then the dot and the short left-falling stroke, and the long bottom horizontal last. {省|shěng}: {少|shǎo} first
  (vertical, then the left-falling stroke, the dot, the long left-falling stroke), then {目|mù}. {丽|lì}: the long
  horizontal first, then each half (a vertical, a turning hook, a dot), left then right.

```trace
观景导江郊桥省
```

```trace
纪丽亚洲吸引著
```

**Write it** (✎ handwriting characters): {观|guān} {导|dǎo} {江|jiāng} {省|shěng} {亚|yà}. Write each three times from memory, then the
words {参观|cān guān}, {导游|dǎo yóu}, {长江|Cháng Jiāng} (the Yangtze: {长|cháng} is cháng here), {省|shěng} and {亚洲|Yà zhōu}.
=}

## Write it

1. **A sentence about a picture.** The picture: a stone bridge over a lake, mountains behind, two
   people taking a photo. Write one sentence with {既|jì}…{又|yòu} or {多么|duō me}.
2. **A short text (80–120 characters).** Write about a place you've visited: where it is, what's
   there ({既|jì}…{又|yòu}…), what you did ({参观|cān guān}, {拍照|pāi zhào}), and whether it's worth visiting ({值得|zhí de}).

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {这儿|zhèr}{既|jì}{有|yǒu}{湖|hú}{又|yòu}{有|yǒu}{山|shān}，{风景|fēng jǐng}{多么|duō me}{美|měi}{啊|a}！ — There's a lake and there are mountains: what scenery!
2. {去年|qù nián}{夏天|xià tiān}，{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{朋友|péng you}{去|qù}{杭州|Háng zhōu}{旅行|lǚ xíng}。{杭州|Háng zhōu}{在|zài}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{的|de}{西南|xī nán}{边|biān}，{坐|zuò}{高铁|gāo tiě}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}{就|jiù}{到|dào}{了|le}。{那儿|nàr}{最|zuì}{著名|zhù míng}{的|de}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{是|shì}{西湖|Xī hú}，{湖|hú}{边|biān}{既|jì}{有|yǒu}{山|shān}，{又|yòu}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{座|zuò}{桥|qiáo}。{我们|wǒ men}{参观|cān guān}{了|le}{一些|yì xiē}{老|lǎo}{房子|fáng zi}，{拍|pāi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{照片|zhào piàn}，{还|hái}{吃|chī}{了|le}{当地|dāng dì}{的|de}{小吃|xiǎo chī}。{杭州|Háng zhōu}{的|de}{景色|jǐng sè}{十分|shí fēn}{美丽|měi lì}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{非常|fēi cháng}{值得|zhí de}{一|yí}{去|qù}。 — Last summer I went to Hangzhou with a friend. Hangzhou is southwest of Shanghai, an hour away by high-speed train. Its most famous sight is the West Lake, with hills by the water and many bridges. We visited some old buildings, took lots of photos and tried the local snacks. The scenery in Hangzhou is very beautiful: I think it's well worth a visit. (about 105 characters)
</details>

## Speaking: questions to answer

The speaking test, as reported, ends with two questions to answer, each with a minute or two to
think first. Try these aloud, then compare with the models.

1. {你|nǐ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{地方|dì fang}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？
2. {旅行|lǚ xíng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{跟|gēn}{导游|dǎo yóu}{一起|yì qǐ}{参观|cān guān}，{还是|hái shi}{自己|zì jǐ}{游玩|yóu wán}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{是|shì}{一|yí}{座|zuò}{山|shān}，{离|lí}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{不|bù}{远|yuǎn}。{那儿|nàr}{的|de}{风景|fēng jǐng}{既|jì}{美|měi}{又|yòu}{安静|ān jìng}，{春天|chūn tiān}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{花|huā}，{秋天|qiū tiān}{的|de}{树叶|shù yè}{是|shì}{红|hóng}{的|de}。{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{次|cì}{去|qù}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{拍|pāi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{照片|zhào piàn}。{爬|pá}{到|dào}{山|shān}{上|shàng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{可以|kě yǐ}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{整个|zhěng gè}{城市|chéng shì}，{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{特别|tè bié}{放松|fàng sōng}。 — My favourite place is a mountain not far from home. The scenery there is beautiful and quiet; there are lots of flowers in spring, and in autumn the leaves are red. I take lots of photos every time. When you get to the top, you can see the whole city, and I feel really relaxed.
2. {我|wǒ}{比较|bǐ jiào}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{自己|zì jǐ}{游玩|yóu wán}。{跟|gēn}{导游|dǎo yóu}{一起|yì qǐ}{参观|cān guān}，{虽然|suī rán}{能|néng}{知道|zhī dào}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{历史|lì shǐ}{和|hé}{故事|gù shi}，{可是|kě shì}{时间|shí jiān}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{安排|ān pái}{好|hǎo}{的|de}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{在|zài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}{多|duō}{待|dāi}{一会儿|yí huìr}。{自己|zì jǐ}{游玩|yóu wán}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}，{累|lèi}{了|le}{就|jiù}{休息|xiū xi}。{不过|bú guò}，{参观|cān guān}{博物馆|bó wù guǎn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{有|yǒu}{导游|dǎo yóu}{会|huì}{更|gèng}{有趣|yǒu qù}。 — I'd rather go round on my own. With a guide you learn a lot of history and stories, but the timing is all fixed, and you can't stay longer where you like it. On your own you go wherever you want, and rest when you're tired. In a museum, though, a guide makes it more interesting. ({待|dāi} dāi, to stay: next lesson's word; {博物馆|bó wù guǎn}: a museum.)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Sightseeing
{这儿|zhèr}{的|de}{风景|fēng jǐng}{多么|duō me}{美|měi}{啊|a}！
= How beautiful the scenery is here!
{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{既|jì}{安静|ān jìng}{又|yòu}{漂亮|piào liang}。
= This place is both quiet and pretty.
{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{这|zhè}{座|zuò}{桥|qiáo}{上|shàng}{拍|pāi}{张|zhāng}{照|zhào}{吧|ba}。
= Let's take a photo on this bridge.
{这个|zhè ge}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{十分|shí fēn}{值得|zhí de}{去|qù}。
= This sight is very much worth a visit.
{节假日|jié jià rì}{游客|yóu kè}{太|tài}{多|duō}{了|le}。
= There are far too many tourists on public holidays.
{这|zhè}{趟|tàng}{旅行|lǚ xíng}{真|zhēn}{值得|zhí de}！
= This trip was really worth it!
```

## Pronunciation

- {景|jǐng} jǐng (a view) and {警|jǐng} jǐng (police, lesson 16): same syllable; {京|jīng} jīng (capital) is first tone.
- {参观|cān guān} cān guān: two level tones; keep them high.
- {导游|dǎo yóu} dǎo yóu: 3+2. {旅行|lǚ xíng} lǚ xíng: ü after l is written with its dots.
- {省|shěng} shěng: *sheng* has a back nasal (-ng); compare {身|shēn} shēn (-n).
- {世纪|shì jì} shì jì: two falling tones; {著名|zhù míng} zhù míng: 4+2.
- {江|jiāng} jiāng, {桥|qiáo} qiáo: *j* and *q* before *i*, said with the tongue tip down behind the lower teeth.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{参观|cān guān}{了|le}{朋友|péng you}~~: you {参观|cān guān} places, not people: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{看|kàn}{了|le}{朋友|péng you} / {去|qù}{朋友|péng you}{家|jiā}{了|le}.
- ~~{既|jì}{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{安静|ān jìng}{又|yòu}{漂亮|piào liang}~~: the subject goes before {既|jì}: {这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{既|jì}{安静|ān jìng}{又|yòu}{漂亮|piào liang}.
- ~~{十分|shí fēn}{好|hǎo}{极了|jí le}~~: one intensifier: {十分|shí fēn}{好|hǎo} or {好|hǎo}{极了|jí le} ({十分|shí fēn}{好|hǎo} is heard; {非常|fēi cháng}{好|hǎo} is more usual).
- {一|yí}{个|gè}{桥|qiáo} is heard in casual speech, but the measure word for a bridge or a mountain is {座|zuò}: {一|yí}{座|zuò}{桥|qiáo}, {一|yí}{座|zuò}{山|shān}.
- ~~{值得|zhí de}~~ + noun: ~~{这个|zhè ge}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{值得|zhí de}{时间|shí jiān}~~ → {这个|zhè ge}{景点|jǐng diǎn}{值得|zhí de}{去|qù} / {值得|zhí de}{花|huā}{时间|shí jiān}{去|qù} ({花|huā}: to spend).
- {二十一|èr shí yī}{世纪|shì jì} for "the 21st century": the number comes before {世纪|shì jì}, with no {第|dì}.

## Key points

- {多么|duō me} + adjective + {啊|a}！: how…!; also "how much" in statements ({不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{我|wǒ}{多么|duō me}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}).
- {十分|shí fēn}: very (strong, a little formal); not with {极了|jí le}.
- (subject) {既|jì} A {又|yòu} B (adjectives) / {既|jì} A，{也|yě} B (verb phrases): both… and.
- {座|zuò}: mountains, bridges, buildings, cities.
- {参观|cān guān} (places, to look and learn), {游玩|yóu wán} (enjoy yourself), {旅行|lǚ xíng} (travel), {度假|dù jià} (a holiday).
- {值得|zhí de} + verb: worth doing. {著名|zhù míng} (written) / {有名|yǒu míng} (spoken).
- New characters: {观|guān} {景|jǐng} {导|dǎo} {江|jiāng} {郊|jiāo} {桥|qiáo} {省|shěng} {纪|jì} {丽|lì} {亚|yà} {洲|zhōu} {吸|xī} {引|yǐn} {著|zhù} (✎: {观|guān} {导|dǎo} {江|jiāng} {省|shěng} {亚|yà}).

lessons.title: Hotels and eating on the road
topics: Passive with 叫 and 让
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Anna and Wang Fang's weekend in Chengde goes on: they check in at a small hotel, go out to eat, and
something goes missing. Along the way this lesson teaches:

- the **[[spoken passive]]** with {叫|jiào} and {让|ràng} ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{钱包|qián bāo}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}: "my wallet's been taken by someone"),
  beside the {被|bèi} sentence you learned in HSK 3;
- **{顺便|shùn biàn}** (while you're at it, on the way);
- **{待|dāi}** dāi (to stay, spoken);
- the words of hotels and restaurants, with the written words you'll see on notices ({旅客|lǚ kè}, {入住|rù zhù}, {提供|tí gōng},
  {早餐|zǎo cān}, {外出|wài chū}).

The reference sheet for this lesson ({把|bǎ} and {被|bèi} at HSK 4) puts the {把|bǎ} patterns of lesson 02 and the
passives side by side.

## The passive with {叫|jiào} and {让|ràng}

You know the {被|bèi} sentence (HSK 3): the thing affected comes first, {被|bèi} introduces the doer, and the
verb has something after it (a result, a direction, {了|le}):

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{钱包|qián bāo}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — My wallet's been taken (by someone).

In everyday speech, especially in the north, **{叫|jiào}** jiào and **{让|ràng}** ràng do the same job as {被|bèi}:

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{钱包|qián bāo}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — My wallet's been taken.

{我|wǒ}{的|de}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{让|ràng}{朋友|péng you}{骑|qí}{走|zǒu}{了|le}。 — My bike's been taken by a friend (a friend rode off on it).

{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{叫|jiào}{弟弟|dì di}{吃|chī}{了|le}。 — The cake on the table got eaten by my little brother.

| | {被|bèi} | {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} |
|---|---|---|
| Register | speech and writing | speech only, casual |
| The doer | may be left out: {钱包|qián bāo}{被|bèi}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le} | must be named ({人|rén} if you don't know who): {钱包|qián bāo}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le} |
| After the verb | a result, a direction or {了|le} | the same |
| Negative | {没|méi} before {被|bèi}: {钱包|qián bāo}{没|méi}{被|bèi}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu} | {没|méi} before {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng}: {钱包|qián bāo}{没|méi}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu} |
| Typical events | mostly unwelcome ones | the same |

Three rules to remember:

- **Name the doer.** ~~{我|wǒ}{的|de}{钱包|qián bāo}{叫|jiào}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}~~ is wrong; say {叫|jiào}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le} or {被|bèi}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}.
- **Not in writing.** Notices, news and the readings of this course write {被|bèi}: {贵重物品|guì zhòng wù pǐn}{被|bèi}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}，{旅馆|lǚ guǎn}{不|bú}{负责|fù zé}
  (if valuables are taken, the hotel isn't responsible).
- **{让|ràng} is also "to let, to make"** (the pivotal sentences of lesson 12). When the first noun is a
  thing, the passive meaning is clear: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{蛋糕|dàn gāo}{让|ràng}{弟弟|dì di}{吃|chī}{了|le} (a cake can't let anyone do anything). When
  it's a person, context decides: {他|tā}{让|ràng}{老师|lǎo shī}{批评|pī píng}{了|le}{一|yí}{顿|dùn} is passive (he got told off by the teacher), but
  {他|tā}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{去|qù} is "he made / let me go".

{叫|jiào} here is not {叫|jiào} "to be called" ({我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安娜|Ān nà}) or "to call" ({叫|jiào}{一|yí}{辆|liàng}{出租车|chū zū chē}). Its passive use always has a
doer and a verb with something after it (a result, a direction or {了|le}).

## {顺便|shùn biàn}: while you're at it

{顺便|shùn biàn} is doing something extra because you're already doing something else, "on the way, at the
same time, while you're about it":

{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{的话|de huà}，{顺便|shùn biàn}{帮|bāng}{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{瓶|píng}{水|shuǐ}。 — If you're going to the supermarket, could you get me a bottle of water while you're there?

{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{出差|chū chāi}，{顺便|shùn biàn}{看看|kàn kan}{老|lǎo}{朋友|péng you}。 — I'm going to Beijing on business, and I'll see some old friends while I'm at it.

{顺便|shùn biàn}{问|wèn}{一下|yí xià}，{附近|fù jìn}{有|yǒu}{银行|yín háng}{吗|ma}？ — By the way, is there a bank nearby?

- {顺便|shùn biàn} goes before the verb (or before {帮|bāng} + person + verb).
- {顺便|shùn biàn}{问|wèn}{一下|yí xià} and {顺便|shùn biàn}{说|shuō}{一下|yí xià} are set phrases: "by the way…" when you add a question or a remark.
- Don't confuse it with {随便|suí biàn} (as you like, casual: lesson 22's word): {顺便|shùn biàn} is "on the way", {随便|suí biàn} is
  "whatever".

## {待|dāi}: to stay (spoken)

{待|dāi} dāi is "to stay (somewhere for a time)", the everyday word, especially in the north:

{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{承德|Chéng dé}{待|dāi}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}。 — We're staying in Chengde for two days.

{周末|zhōu mò}{你|nǐ}{别|bié}{总|zǒng}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{待|dāi}{着|zhe}，{出去|chū qù}{走走|zǒu zou}{吧|ba}。 — Don't stay at home all weekend: get out a bit.

- The time comes after the verb: {待|dāi}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}, {待|dāi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}. The place comes before it with {在|zài}: {在|zài}{家|jiā}{待|dāi}{着|zhe}.
- {住|zhù} (to stay, to live) is for where you sleep: {住|zhù}{旅馆|lǚ guǎn}, {住|zhù}{在|zài}{朋友|péng you}{家|jiā}. {待|dāi} is for where you spend time:
  {在|zài}{咖啡|kā fēi}{馆|guǎn}{待|dāi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{下午|xià wǔ} (spent the whole afternoon in a café).
- The same character read dài is "to treat" ({对待|duì dài}, HSK 5). In this course's words it's dāi.

  state-run; {酒店|jiǔ diàn} a hotel, often a bigger or newer one (it isn't a bar). Most people say {酒店|jiǔ diàn} for a
  hotel today.

  vehicle.

  (to fix a time). People mix them up in writing; this course writes {订|dìng} for bookings.

- **{早餐|zǎo cān} and {早饭|zǎo fàn}.** Both are breakfast. {早饭|zǎo fàn}, {午饭|wǔ fàn}, {晚饭|wǎn fàn} (HSK 1–2) are what you say at home; {早餐|zǎo cān}, {午餐|wǔ cān},
  {晚餐|wǎn cān} are the words of hotels, menus and notices, and of polite speech: {酒店|jiǔ diàn}{提供|tí gōng}{早餐|zǎo cān}.
- **{结账|jié zhàng}.** "Pay the bill" is {结账|jié zhàng} everywhere; {买单|mǎi dān} (mǎi dān) is also very common in restaurants. Call
  it out: {服务|fú wù}{员|yuán}，{结账|jié zhàng}！ (or {买单|mǎi dān}！). Many places today let you pay by scanning a code at the table
  ({扫码|sǎo mǎ}, lesson 09).
- **{干杯|gān bēi}** is literally "dry the glass". At a meal, the host often toasts: {为|wèi}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{健康|jiàn kāng}{干杯|gān bēi}！ (To everyone's
  health!) {为|wèi} here is wèi (for). You needn't empty your glass every time: saying {我|wǒ}{随意|suí yì} (I'll drink as I
  like) is polite.

## Dialogue 1: checking in

{安娜|Ān nà} (Anna) and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (Wang Fang) check in at a small hotel in Chengde. {前台|qián tái} is the front desk (and
the person there).

```dialogue
# At the front desk
```

- {两位|liǎng wèi}: you two (polite: {位|wèi} is the polite measure word for people). {出示|chū shì}: to show (written, official).
- {标准间|biāo zhǔn jiān}: a standard twin room (two beds). A single is {单人间|dān rén jiān}.

- {往|wǎng}{右|yòu}{走|zǒu}: turn right, go right. {带|dài}{好|hǎo}: take (and keep) with you.

```dialogue
# A missing wallet
```

- {哎呀|āi yā} āi yā: oh no! (surprise, dismay). {找找|zhǎo zhao}: look a bit (a repeated verb, light second syllable).
- {是|shì}{不|bu}{是|shì}{叫|jiào}{人|rén}{拿|ná}{走|zǒu}{了|le}？: "could someone have taken it?": {是|shì}{不|bu}{是|shì} + a guess. Next lesson's {难道|nán dào}…{吗|ma} is a stronger
