Some of these are more mixed than they look:

- {骄傲|jiāo ào} is "arrogant" when you describe someone ({他|tā}{很|hěn}{骄傲|jiāo ào}), but "proud" in {为|wèi}…{感到|gǎn dào}{骄傲|jiāo ào}: {我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{感到|gǎn dào}{骄傲|jiāo ào}！ (I'm
  proud of you!) and {是|shì}…{的|de}{骄傲|jiāo ào} (…is the pride of…).
- {随便|suí biàn} is "careless, too casual" about behaviour, and "as you like, any" in an offer or an answer: {你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{什么|shén me}？
  ——{随便|suí biàn}。 (What do you want to eat? — Anything.) Many people find a bare {随便|suí biàn} a lazy answer.
- {笨|bèn} is "stupid", but people mostly say it of themselves ({我|wǒ}{真|zhēn}{笨|bèn}！) or of clumsy hands ({笨手笨脚|bèn shǒu bèn jiǎo}, all thumbs).
  Calling someone else {笨|bèn} is rude.
- {懒|lǎn} also gives {懒得|lǎn de} + verb, "can't be bothered to": {我|wǒ}{懒得|lǎn de}{做饭|zuò fàn}，{叫|jiào}{外卖|wài mài}{吧|ba}。 (I can't be bothered to cook;
  let's order a takeaway. {外卖|wài mài}: takeaway.)

### Jokes and intentions: {开玩笑|kāi wán xiào}, {笑话|xiào hua}, {好笑|hǎo xiào}, {故意|gù yì}

- {开玩笑|kāi wán xiào} is "to joke, to kid": {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{开玩笑|kāi wán xiào}{呢|ne}！ (I'm only joking!) {开|kāi}{什么|shén me}{玩笑|wán xiào}！ (You must be joking!) The person
  you joke with takes {跟|gēn}.
- {笑话|xiào hua} is "a joke" ({讲|jiǎng}{笑话|xiào hua}, to tell jokes) and also "to laugh at someone": {别|bié}{笑话|xiào hua}{我|wǒ}！ (Don't laugh at me!)
- {好笑|hǎo xiào} is "funny, laughable": {这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{太|tài}{好笑|hǎo xiào}{了|le}。 {有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{好笑|hǎo xiào}{的|de}？ (What's so funny?) It's built like {好吃|hǎo chī} and
  {好看|hǎo kàn}: {好|hǎo} + verb, "good to…".
- {故意|gù yì} is "on purpose": {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{故意|gù yì}{的|de}。 (Sorry, I didn't mean to.)
- {尊重|zūn zhòng} is "to respect": {我们|wǒ men}{要|yào}{尊重|zūn zhòng}{别人|bié ren}{的|de}{想法|xiǎng fǎ}。 (We should respect other people's ideas. {想法|xiǎng fǎ}: an idea, lesson 25.)

## Four-character patterns

Chinese loves phrases of four characters. Many are fixed idioms with a story behind them ({成语|chéng yǔ}, HSK 5),
but some are built from frames that you can fill with words you know. A **[[four-character pattern]]**
is such a frame: two fixed characters and two slots, here A and B. A and B are usually two related
one-character words (two verbs, two nouns), and the phrase works like one adjective or adverb.

### {有|yǒu}A{有|yǒu}B: having both

{有|yǒu}A{有|yǒu}B says that both things are there, in good measure. It's warm and positive:

| Phrase | Literally | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {有说有笑|yǒu shuō yǒu xiào} | have talking, have laughing | chatting and laughing |
| {有山有水|yǒu shān yǒu shuǐ} | have hills, have water | scenic, with hills and rivers |
| {有吃有喝|yǒu chī yǒu hē} | have food, have drink | plenty to eat and drink |

{办公室|bàn gōng shì}{里|lǐ}{大家|dà jiā}{有说有笑|yǒu shuō yǒu xiào}{的|de}。 — Everyone in the office is chatting and laughing.

{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{有山有水|yǒu shān yǒu shuǐ}，{非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}。 — This place has hills and water: it's beautiful.

A {的|de} often follows when the phrase describes a state ({有说有笑|yǒu shuō yǒu xiào}{的|de}). Before a verb it takes {地|de}:
{他们|tā men}{有说有笑|yǒu shuō yǒu xiào}{地|de}{走|zǒu}{进来|jìn lái}。 (They came in chatting and laughing.)

### {无|wú}A{无|wú}B: having neither

{无|wú} (a word of this lesson) is the written {没有|méi yǒu}: "to have no, without". {无|wú}A{无|wú}B says that neither is there:

| Phrase | Literally | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {无忧无虑|wú yōu wú lǜ} | no worries, no cares | carefree ({忧|yōu}: worry; {虑|lǜ} as in {考虑|kǎo lǜ}) |
| {无声无息|wú shēng wú xī} | no sound, no breath | silently, without a trace ({息|xī} as in {消息|xiāo xi}, news: lesson 24) |

{小时候|xiǎo shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{过|guò}{得|de}{无忧无虑|wú yōu wú lǜ}。 — As a child, I lived without a care in the world.

{无声无息|wú shēng wú xī} often has a sad or uneasy feel: {他|tā}{无声无息|wú shēng wú xī}{地|de}{走|zǒu}{了|le} (he left without a word to anyone).

{无|wú} appears in other written words you know or will meet: {无法|wú fǎ} (unable to, lesson 11), {无聊|wú liáo} (bored,
boring, lesson 23), {无论|wú lùn} (no matter, lesson 25). On its own, in notices: {无|wú}{人|rén} (nobody), {今天|jīn tiān}{无|wú}{课|kè} (no
classes today). In speech, say {没有|méi yǒu}.

### {一|yī}A{一|yī}B: every single…, wholly

{一|yī}A{一|yī}B puts {一|yī} before each of two related words. It means "every single", or "wholly, entirely":

| Phrase | Literally | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {一心一意|yì xīn yí yì} | one heart, one mind | wholeheartedly, with complete devotion |
| {一言一行|yì yán yì xíng} | one word, one deed | every word and deed, everything someone says and does |

{他|tā}{一心一意|yì xīn yí yì}{地|de}{学习|xué xí}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。 — He studies Chinese wholeheartedly.

{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{一言一行|yì yán yì xíng}，{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{看在眼里|kàn zài yǎn lǐ}。 — Pupils notice everything a teacher says and does. ({看在眼里|kàn zài yǎn lǐ}: to take note of)

Watch the tones: {一|yī} changes before each syllable in the normal way: yì xīn yí yì (yì before a first
tone, yí before a fourth), yì yán yì xíng.

### Using them

These phrases are safe in speech and writing. Don't build new ones freely: {有说有笑|yǒu shuō yǒu xiào} is a set phrase, but a
home-made {有|yǒu}{吃|chī}{有|yǒu}{睡|shuì} is not one. Learn each phrase as a whole, and recognise the frame when you meet a new one.

## X {是|shì} X，Y {是|shì} Y: keeping things apart

The **[[fixed format]]** X {是|shì} X，Y {是|shì} Y repeats two nouns around {是|shì}. It says that the two are different things
and must not be mixed up:

{工作|gōng zuò}{是|shì}{工作|gōng zuò}，{朋友|péng you}{是|shì}{朋友|péng you}。 — Work is work and friends are friends. (Being friends doesn't change what the work needs.)

{一|yī}{是|shì}{一|yī}，{二|èr}{是|shì}{二|èr}。 — One is one and two is two. (Let's be exact; let's not mix things up.)

{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}，{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{想法|xiǎng fǎ}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。 — You're you and I'm me: we see it differently.

A fixed format is a frame of fixed words with slots, like the four-character patterns but at the
level of a sentence. The reference sheet *Fixed formats* lists all the level-4 ones.

## The suffix {性|xìng}: -ness

{性|xìng} (nature, quality) after an adjective or a verb makes a noun for that quality, like English "-ness"
or "-ity". The **[[suffix 性]]** is common in written Chinese:

| Word | Made of | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {积极性|jī jí xìng} | {积极|jī jí} (active, keen: lesson 12) + {性|xìng} | enthusiasm, motivation |
| {重要性|zhòng yào xìng} | {重要|zhòng yào} (important) + {性|xìng} | importance |
| {可能性|kě néng xìng} | {可能|kě néng} (possible) + {性|xìng} | possibility |

{老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{表扬|biǎo yáng}{能|néng}{提高|tí gāo}{学生|xué sheng}{的|de}{积极性|jī jí xìng}。 — Teachers' praise can raise pupils' motivation.

{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{知道|zhī dào}{学|xué}{外语|wài yǔ}{的|de}{重要性|zhòng yào xìng}。 — We all know how important it is to learn a foreign language.

{性|xìng} is also the first character of {性格|xìng gé} (personality) and of {性别|xìng bié} (sex, gender, lesson 11), {男性|nán xìng} and {女性|nǚ xìng}.

- {本|běn} běn (root) is the sound part of {笨|bèn} bèn: ⺮ (bamboo) + {本|běn}.

said the plan had three problems, and she explained each one very clearly. The meeting room went

## Pronunciation

- Light second syllables: {脾气|pí qi} pí qi, {态度|tài du} tài du, {活泼|huó po} huó po, {客气|kè qi} kè qi, {样子|yàng zi} yàng zi, {笑话|xiào hua} xiào hua.
- {骄傲|jiāo ào} jiāo ào: two syllables, the second starting with a vowel, so pinyin writes jiāo'ào inside the word.
  Don't run them together into one long *jiaoao*.
- {诚实|chéng shí} chéng shí: *ch*, then *sh*, both with the tongue curled back. {冷静|lěng jìng} lěng jìng: *eng*, then *ing*.
- {幽默|yōu mò} yōu mò sounds a little like English "humour", which it comes from.
- {一心一意|yì xīn yí yì} yì xīn yí yì and {一言一行|yì yán yì xíng} yì yán yì xíng: each {一|yī} changes by the next syllable's tone.
- {懒|lǎn} lǎn (lazy) and {蓝|lán} lán (blue): the same syllable, third tone against second.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{骄傲|jiāo ào}{你|nǐ}~~ for "I'm proud of you": say {我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{感到|gǎn dào}{骄傲|jiāo ào} or {我|wǒ}{为|wèi}{你|nǐ}{骄傲|jiāo ào}.
- {他|tā}{很|hěn}{耐心|nài xīn} and {他|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn} are both right; ~~{他|tā}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{耐心|nài xīn}~~ is not: {很|hěn} goes before {有|yǒu} ({很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn}).
- {开玩笑|kāi wán xiào} takes the person with {跟|gēn}: {我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{开玩笑|kāi wán xiào}{呢|ne}; ~~{我|wǒ}{开玩笑|kāi wán xiào}{你|nǐ}~~ is wrong.
- Home-made four-character phrases ({有|yǒu}{吃|chī}{有|yǒu}{睡|shuì}) aren't set phrases: use the ones you've learned.
- {随便|suí biàn} alone as an answer is fine between friends, but it can sound as if you don't care; with a host, say
  {什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ} (anything's fine) or name something.

## Key points

- Character words: {性格|xìng gé} (personality), {脾气|pí qi} (temper), {态度|tài du} (attitude), {特点|tè diǎn} (feature), {样子|yàng zi} (look).
- Good: {诚实|chéng shí}, {勇敢|yǒng gǎn}, {幽默|yōu mò}, {活泼|huó po}, {耐心|nài xīn}, {细心|xì xīn}, {冷静|lěng jìng}, {友好|yǒu hǎo}, {有|yǒu}{礼貌|lǐ mào}, {客气|kè qi}, {帅|shuài}. Less good: {笨|bèn}, {懒|lǎn}, {粗心|cū xīn}, {骄傲|jiāo ào} (also
  "proud of": {为|wèi}…{感到|gǎn dào}{骄傲|jiāo ào}), {害羞|hài xiū}, {随便|suí biàn}.
- {开玩笑|kāi wán xiào} ({跟|gēn}…{开玩笑|kāi wán xiào}), {笑话|xiào hua} (a joke; to laugh at), {好笑|hǎo xiào} (funny), {故意|gù yì} (on purpose), {尊重|zūn zhòng} (to respect).
- Four-character patterns: {有|yǒu}A{有|yǒu}B ({有说有笑|yǒu shuō yǒu xiào}, {有山有水|yǒu shān yǒu shuǐ}), {无|wú}A{无|wú}B ({无忧无虑|wú yōu wú lǜ}, {无声无息|wú shēng wú xī}), {一|yī}A{一|yī}B ({一心一意|yì xīn yí yì}, {一言一行|yì yán yì xíng}):
  learn each phrase whole.
- X {是|shì} X，Y {是|shì} Y keeps two things apart: {工作|gōng zuò}{是|shì}{工作|gōng zuò}，{朋友|péng you}{是|shì}{朋友|péng you}.
- {性|xìng} makes "-ness" nouns: {积极性|jī jí xìng}, {重要性|zhòng yào xìng}, {可能性|kě néng xìng}. {无|wú} is the written {没有|méi yǒu}.
- New characters: {笨|bèn} {诚|chéng} {粗|cū} {羞|xiū} {貌|mào} {泼|pō} {骄|jiāo} {傲|ào} {懒|lǎn} {脾|pí} {耐|nài} {帅|shuài} {态|tài} {尊|zūn} {勇|yǒng} {幽|yōu} {默|mò}; ✎ {态|tài}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Feelings: 使, 受不了, 再也不, 怎么都不, 还 X 呢
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 3 gave you the basic feelings: {高兴|gāo xìng}, {难过|nán guò}, {生气|shēng qì}, {担心|dān xīn}, {害怕|hài pà}, and {让|ràng} + person + feeling
({这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}). This lesson goes deeper. You'll tell apart the many kinds of excitement, sadness and annoyance
that English often lumps together ({激动|jī dòng}, {兴奋|xīng fèn} and {感动|gǎn dòng}; {伤心|shāng xīn} and {失望|shī wàng}; {烦|fán}, {讨厌|tǎo yàn} and {无聊|wú liáo}), and you'll learn
the grammar people use when feelings run high:

- **[[causative 使]]**, the written partner of {让|ràng}: {这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}{使|shǐ}{大家|dà jiā}{很|hěn}{激动|jī dòng} ({消息|xiāo xi}: news, lesson 24);
- {受不了|shòu bu liǎo} (can't stand it) and its partner {受得了|shòu de liǎo};
- three **[[fixed formats]]**: {再也|zài yě}{不|bù} / {再也|zài yě}{没|méi} (never again), {怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu}{不|bù} / {怎么|zěn me}{也|yě}{没|méi} (just won't, however hard you
  try) and {还|hái} X {呢|ne} (some X you are!);
- the **[[suffix 感]]**, "a sense of…": {安全感|ān quán gǎn}, {幸福感|xìng fú gǎn};
- the interjections {啊|ā} ā (oh!) and {嗯|èn} èn (mm, yes).

The dialogue is a goodbye: Li Ming ({李明|Lǐ Míng}) flies to Britain tomorrow to start his master's.

## Words for feelings

### Excited, moved, thrilled: {激动|jī dòng}, {兴奋|xīng fèn}, {感动|gǎn dòng}, {感人|gǎn rén}

| Word | The feeling | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {激动|jī dòng} | strong emotion that stirs you up: excitement, being deeply moved | {听|tīng}{到|dào}{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}，{她|tā}{激动|jī dòng}{得|de}{哭|kū}{了|le}。 (When she heard the news she was so moved she cried. {消息|xiāo xi}: news, lesson 24) |
| {兴奋|xīng fèn} | thrilled, full of energy, too excited to sit still | {明天|míng tiān}{去|qù}{旅行|lǚ xíng}，{孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{兴奋|xīng fèn}{得|de}{睡不着|shuì bu zháo}。 (The children are too excited to sleep.) |
| {感动|gǎn dòng} | moved, touched (by kindness, by a story) | {他|tā}{的话|de huà}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}。 (What he said really touched me.) |
| {感人|gǎn rén} | moving, touching (describes the thing) | {这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{很|hěn}{感人|gǎn rén}。 (It's a moving story.) |

{兴奋|xīng fèn} is pure energy and usually joy. {激动|jī dòng} is stronger and can come from joy, gratitude or even anger
({别|bié}{激动|jī dòng}！calm down!). {感动|gǎn dòng} is how you feel; {感人|gǎn rén} is what the story is: {一|yí}{个|gè}{感人|gǎn rén}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}.

### Sad, disappointed, regretful: {伤心|shāng xīn}, {失望|shī wàng}, {后悔|hòu huǐ}, {可惜|kě xī}

- {伤心|shāng xīn} (heartbroken, deeply sad), stronger than {难过|nán guò} (HSK 3): {她|tā}{的|de}{猫|māo}{丢|diū}{了|le}，{她|tā}{伤心|shāng xīn}{了|le}{好|hǎo}{几|jǐ}{天|tiān}。 (She was
  heartbroken for days when her cat went missing.)
- {失望|shī wàng} (disappointed): {我|wǒ}{对|duì}{这|zhè}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{的|de}{成绩|chéng jì}{很|hěn}{失望|shī wàng}。 {别|bié}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{失望|shī wàng}！ (Don't let me down!)
- {后悔|hòu huǐ} (to regret) takes a verb or a clause: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{后悔|hòu huǐ}{没|méi}{早|zǎo}{点儿|diǎnr}{学|xué}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。 (I really regret not learning Chinese
  sooner.)
- {可惜|kě xī} (it's a pity, what a shame) is about bad luck, not your own fault: {太|tài}{可惜|kě xī}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{差|chà}{一|yì}{分|fēn}{就|jiù}{赢|yíng}{了|le}。 (What a
  shame: we lost by just one point.)

{后悔|hòu huǐ} looks back at what you did; {可惜|kě xī} at what happened. {失去|shī qù} (to lose something you had, often abstract)
goes with them: {失去|shī qù}{机会|jī huì} (to lose a chance), {失去|shī qù}{信心|xìn xīn} (to lose confidence). For a lost object, use {丢|diū}.

### Annoyed, bored, envious, smug: {烦|fán}, {烦恼|fán nǎo}, {讨厌|tǎo yàn}, {无聊|wú liáo}, {羡慕|xiàn mù}, {得意|dé yì}

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {烦|fán} | annoyed, fed up; annoying | {别|bié}{烦|fán}{我|wǒ}！ (Leave me alone!) {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{真|zhēn}{烦人|fán rén}。 (This is so annoying.) |
| {烦恼|fán nǎo} | worried, troubled; worries | {年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{有|yǒu}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{的|de}{烦恼|fán nǎo}。 (Young people have their own worries.) |
| {讨厌|tǎo yàn} | to dislike, hate; annoying | {我|wǒ}{讨厌|tǎo yàn}{下雨|xià yǔ}{天|tiān}。 (I hate rainy days.) |
| {无聊|wú liáo} | bored; boring | {这个|zhè ge}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}{太|tài}{无聊|wú liáo}{了|le}。 (This TV series is so boring. {电视剧|diàn shì jù}: lesson 24) |
| {羡慕|xiàn mù} | to envy, admire | {我|wǒ}{真|zhēn}{羡慕|xiàn mù}{你|nǐ}{能|néng}{去|qù}{英国|Yīng guó}{留学|liú xué}。 (I really envy you studying in Britain.) |
| {得意|dé yì} | pleased with yourself, smug | {他|tā}{考|kǎo}{了|le}{第|dì}{一|yī}，{很|hěn}{得意|dé yì}。 (He came top and was very pleased with himself.) |

{讨厌|tǎo yàn} is strong, but among friends it's also a teasing "you're awful!" ({讨厌|tǎo yàn}！{你|nǐ}{又|yòu}{开|kāi}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{玩笑|wán xiào}！). {羡慕|xiàn mù} is a
friendly envy, closer to admiration. {无聊|wú liáo} describes both the person ({我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{无聊|wú liáo}, I'm bored) and the thing
({电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{无聊|wú liáo}, the film is boring).

### Happy and pleasant: {幸福|xìng fú}, {愉快|yú kuài}

{幸福|xìng fú} is a deep, lasting happiness, well-being: {祝|zhù}{你们|nǐ men}{幸福|xìng fú}！ (said to a couple), {幸福|xìng fú}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó} (a happy life).
{愉快|yú kuài} is pleasant, cheerful, about a time or an experience: {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{周末|zhōu mò}{愉快|yú kuài}！ (Have a nice weekend!)
{我们|wǒ men}{合作|hé zuò}{得|de}{很|hěn}{愉快|yú kuài} (we worked together very pleasantly; {合作|hé zuò}, to work together). For a happy moment, {高兴|gāo xìng}, {开心|kāi xīn} and {快乐|kuài lè}
(HSK 1–3) are still the words.

### Love and the heart: {感情|gǎn qíng}, {感受|gǎn shòu}, {爱情|ài qíng}, {爱心|ài xīn}, {心|xīn}, {心情|xīn qíng}, {内心|nèi xīn}, {气|qì}

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {感情|gǎn qíng} | feelings; the bond between people | {他们|tā men}{俩|liǎ}{感情|gǎn qíng}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 (They're very close.) |
| {感受|gǎn shòu} | what you feel or experience; to feel | {说说|shuō shuo}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{感受|gǎn shòu}。 (Tell us how you feel about it.) |
| {爱情|ài qíng} | romantic love | {一|yí}{个|gè}{关于|guān yú}{爱情|ài qíng}{的|de}{电影|diàn yǐng} (a film about love) |
| {爱心|ài xīn} | kindness, a caring heart | {她|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{爱心|ài xīn}，{常常|cháng cháng}{帮助|bāng zhù}{别人|bié ren}。 |
| {心|xīn} | heart | {我|wǒ}{的|de}{心|xīn}{跳|tiào}{得|de}{很|hěn}{快|kuài}。 (My heart is racing.) |
| {心情|xīn qíng} | mood | {今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{心情|xīn qíng}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 |
| {内心|nèi xīn} | your inner self, deep down | {他|tā}{的|de}{内心|nèi xīn}{很|hěn}{孤单|gū dān}。 (Deep down he's lonely. {孤单|gū dān}: lonely) |
| {气|qì} | anger; breath, air | {气|qì}{死|sǐ}{我|wǒ}{了|le}！ (I'm furious! {死|sǐ}{了|le} after a feeling: lesson 06) |

{感情|gǎn qíng}, {感受|gǎn shòu} and {感觉|gǎn jué} (lesson 06) all start with {感|gǎn} (to feel). {感觉|gǎn jué} is a sensation or an impression
({我|wǒ}{感觉|gǎn jué}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng}; {我|wǒ}{感觉|gǎn jué}{他|tā}{不|bú}{太|tài}{高兴|gāo xìng}); {感受|gǎn shòu} is what an experience is like for you, often asked for ({你|nǐ}{的|de}{感受|gǎn shòu}); {感情|gǎn qíng} is the
feeling between people. {气|qì} you know from {生气|shēng qì} (to be angry); on its own, {气|qì} is anger ({他|tā}{还|hái}{在|zài}{气头上|qì tóu shang}, he's still
angry: {气头上|qì tóu shang}, in the heat of anger) or breath and air ({天气|tiān qì}, {空气|kōng qì}: air, lesson 28).

### Dates and hugs: {约|yuē}, {约会|yuē huì}, {浪漫|làng màn}, {鲜花|xiān huā}, {抱|bào}, {永远|yǒng yuǎn}

- {约|yuē} (to arrange to meet, to ask someone out): {我|wǒ}{约|yuē}{了|le}{朋友|péng you}{明天|míng tiān}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}。 (I've arranged to go hiking with a
  friend tomorrow.)
- {约会|yuē huì} (a date; to go on a date; any appointment to meet): {今天|jīn tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{个|gè}{约会|yuē huì}。
- {浪漫|làng màn} (romantic): {他|tā}{很|hěn}{浪漫|làng màn}，{常常|cháng cháng}{给|gěi}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}{送|sòng}{鲜花|xiān huā}。 ({鲜花|xiān huā}, fresh flowers)
- {抱|bào} (to hug; to hold in your arms): {妈妈|mā ma}{抱|bào}{着|zhe}{孩子|hái zi}。 {来|lái}，{抱|bào}{一下|yí xià}！ (Come here, give me a hug!)
- {永远|yǒng yuǎn} (forever, always): {我|wǒ}{永远|yǒng yuǎn}{不|bú}{会|huì}{忘记|wàng jì}{那|nà}{一|yì}{天|tiān}。 (I'll never forget that day.)

## {使|shǐ} + person + feeling: the written causative

You know {让|ràng} + person + feeling (HSK 3): {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}. Writing uses {使|shǐ} shǐ in the same place. The
**[[causative 使]]** makes the sentence a cause and its effect: X {使|shǐ} Y + feeling or change.

{这个|zhè ge}{好|hǎo}{消息|xiāo xi}{使|shǐ}{大家|dà jiā}{非常|fēi cháng}{激动|jī dòng}。 — The good news made everyone very excited.

{他|tā}{的话|de huà}{使|shǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}。 — What he said moved me deeply.

{经常|jīng cháng}{锻炼|duàn liàn}{可以|kě yǐ}{使|shǐ}{人|rén}{心情|xīn qíng}{愉快|yú kuài}。 — Regular exercise can put you in a good mood.

| | Spoken | Written |
|---|---|---|
| causing a feeling | {让|ràng} | {使|shǐ} |
| example | {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}。 | {这|zhè}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}{使|shǐ}{我|wǒ}{深受|shēn shòu}{感动|gǎn dòng}。 ({部|bù}: the measure word for films, lesson 24; {深受|shēn shòu}: deeply) |

Two limits keep {使|shǐ} apart from {让|ràng}:

- {使|shǐ} is only "to cause, to make". It can't mean "to let, allow" ({让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{看看|kàn kan}, let me see) or "to ask someone
  to" ({妈妈|mā ma}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{菜|cài}): those are {让|ràng} only.
- {使|shǐ} is for written texts: articles, reports, essays, formal speeches. In conversation {使|shǐ} sounds stiff;
  use {让|ràng}.

## {受不了|shòu bu liǎo} and {受得了|shòu de liǎo}: can't stand, can stand

{受不了|shòu bu liǎo} shòu bu liǎo is a potential complement made from {受|shòu} (to bear) + {不了|bu liǎo} (not able to manage): "can't
bear it, can't stand it". It follows a feeling or a situation, or stands alone:

{天气|tiān qì}{太|tài}{热|rè}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo}{了|le}！ — It's too hot: I can't stand it any more!

{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{迟到|chí dào}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo}{他|tā}。 — He's late every day: nobody can stand him.

After an adjective it says the feeling has gone past what you can bear: {热|rè}{得|de}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo} (unbearably hot),
{累|lèi}{得|de}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo} (exhausted). The positive form, {受得了|shòu de liǎo} shòu de liǎo, is mostly used in questions and doubts:
{你|nǐ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{受得了|shòu de liǎo}{吗|ma}？ (Can you cope on your own?) Both are light in the middle: {不|bu} bu and {得|de} de, with {了|liǎo} read liǎo.

## Fixed formats for strong feelings

A fixed format is a frame of fixed words with a slot (lesson 22's X {是|shì} X，Y {是|shì} Y is one). These three
are among the commonest in speech.

### {再也|zài yě}{不|bù} / {再也|zài yě}{没|méi}: never again

{再也|zài yě} + {不|bù} + verb is "never again, not any more" from now on. {再也|zài yě} + {没|méi} + verb is "never again" since
then, about the past:

{那|nà}{家|jiā}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{的|de}{菜|cài}{太|tài}{难吃|nán chī}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{再也|zài yě}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。 — The food at that restaurant was awful: I'm never going back.

{他|tā}{去|qù}{了|le}{国外|guó wài}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{再也|zài yě}{没|méi}{回来|huí lái}。 — After he went abroad, he never came back.

{不|bù} for a decision about the future, {没|méi} for what didn't happen again. {再也|zài yě}{不|bù} often ends in {了|le} ({再也|zài yě}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}).

### {怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu} / {怎么|zěn me}{也|yě} + {不|bù} / {没|méi}: however hard you try

{怎么|zěn me} + {都|dōu} or {也|yě} + a negative says that something just won't happen, whatever you do. It often goes
with a potential complement ({睡不着|shuì bu zháo}, {记不住|jì bu zhù}):

{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu}{睡不着|shuì bu zháo}。 — I just couldn't get to sleep last night.

{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{我|wǒ}{怎么|zěn me}{也|yě}{记不住|jì bu zhù}。 — However hard I try, I can't remember this character.

{我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{他|tā}{打|dǎ}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{次|cì}{电话|diàn huà}，{他|tā}{怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{接|jiē}。 — I rang him again and again, but he wouldn't answer.

The pattern is the same as the question words without a question of HSK 3 ({谁|shéi}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}, nobody knows;
{哪儿|nǎr}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}, I don't want to go anywhere): {怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu}{不|bù} is "in no way at all".

### {还|hái} X {呢|ne}: and you call yourself X!

{还|hái} + noun or verb + {呢|ne} says that someone falls short of what they claim to be, or that they're the last
person who should talk. The tone is teasing or reproachful:

{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{大学生|dà xué shēng}{呢|ne}，{这个|zhè ge}{字|zì}{都|dōu}{不|bú}{认识|rèn shi}？ — And you call yourself a university student? You don't even know this character?

{还|hái}{说|shuō}{呢|ne}！{你|nǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{也|yě}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。 — Look who's talking! You were late yesterday too.

{还|hái}{说|shuō}{呢|ne} alone is very common: "don't even mention it!" or "you're one to talk!" Context decides which.

## The suffix {感|gǎn} and the interjections {啊|ā}, {嗯|èn}

### {感|gǎn}: a sense of…

{感|gǎn} after a noun or an adjective makes "a sense of…, a feeling of…". The **[[suffix 感]]** is very
productive in modern Chinese:

| Word | Made of | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {安全感|ān quán gǎn} | {安全|ān quán} (safe) + {感|gǎn} | a sense of security |
| {幸福感|xìng fú gǎn} | {幸福|xìng fú} (happy) + {感|gǎn} | a sense of happiness, well-being |
| {责任感|zé rèn gǎn} | {责任|zé rèn} (responsibility, lesson 11) + {感|gǎn} | a sense of responsibility |

{他|tā}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{责任感|zé rèn gǎn}。 — He has a strong sense of responsibility.

{父母|fù mǔ}{常常|cháng cháng}{陪|péi}{孩子|hái zi}，{孩子|hái zi}{就|jiù}{会|huì}{有|yǒu}{安全感|ān quán gǎn}。 — When parents spend time with their children, the children feel secure.

### {啊|ā} ā and {嗯|èn} èn

{啊|ā} ā (first tone) is a cry of surprise or admiration at the start of a sentence: {啊|ā}，{下|xià}{雪|xuě}{了|le}！ (Oh, it's
snowing!) {啊|ā}，{这么|zhè me}{多|duō}{鲜花|xiān huā}！ (Oh, so many flowers!) It's the same character as the particle a at the end of a
sentence ({好|hǎo}{啊|a}, HSK 2), but here it comes first and has its own tone. In speech, {啊|ā} at the start can also
rise (á? — "what?") or fall (à — "oh, I see"); this lesson teaches the surprised ā.

{嗯|èn} èn is "mm, uh-huh, yes": a quiet agreement or a sign that you're listening. {你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{来|lái}{吗|ma}？——{嗯|èn}。 (Are you
coming tomorrow? — Mm.) Dictionaries list several readings for it (ǹg is common in speech, and the HSK
syllabus writes ǹg); this course writes èn.

### The heart radical: 忄 and {心|xīn}

Four of today's characters have 忄 (the heart, written at the side): {悔|huǐ}, {恼|nǎo}, {惜|xī} and {愉|yú}. You already know
many: {情|qíng}, {快|kuài}, {慢|màn}, {忙|máng}, {怕|pà}, {怪|guài}, {惯|guàn}, {懂|dǒng}. When {心|xīn} sits at the bottom it keeps its full shape: {感|gǎn}, {想|xiǎng}, {意|yì}, {态|tài} (lesson 22),
and {慕|mù} has a third form, ⺗, at the bottom. Feelings and thoughts are very often written with the heart.

### Sound families

- {每|měi} měi gives the sound, now drifted, of {悔|huǐ} huǐ (忄 + {每|měi}) and {海|hǎi} hǎi (氵 + {每|měi}).
- {昔|xī} xī (formerly) is the right half of {惜|xī} xī (忄 + {昔|xī}), with the same sound, and of {借|jiè} jiè (to borrow, HSK 3),
  where it has drifted.
- {俞|yú} yú is the right half of {愉|yú} yú (忄 + {俞|yú}), and of {输|shū} shū (to lose a game, lesson 04), where it has drifted.
- {良|liáng} liáng is in {浪|làng} làng (氵 + {良|liáng}) and in lesson 21's {娘|niáng} niáng.
- {曼|màn} màn gives the sound of {漫|màn} màn (氵 + {曼|màn}), {慢|màn} màn (slow, HSK 2) and {馒|mán} mán ({馒头|mán tou}, lesson 08).
- {莫|mò} mò is the top of {慕|mù} mù ({莫|mò} + ⺗); the same {莫|mò} is in {摸|mō} mō (to touch) and {墓|mù} mù (a tomb).
- {畐|fú} is the sound part of {福|fú} fú (礻 + {畐|fú}) and of {富|fù} fù (rich, lesson 03: 宀 + {畐|fú}).
- {恩|ēn} ēn (kindness: {因|yīn} + {心|xīn}) is the right part of {嗯|èn} èn ({口|kǒu} + {恩|ēn}): the mouth radical marks a sound you make.

### Look-alikes

- {幸|xìng} xìng (fortunate) and {辛|xīn} xīn (hard, lesson 11's {辛苦|xīn kǔ}): {幸|xìng} starts with {土|tǔ} on top, then a dot and a short
  left-falling stroke, then {干|gàn}; {辛|xīn} starts with {立|lì} (a dot at the very top) and ends in {十|shí}. A dot at the
  top means {辛|xīn}.
- {羡|xiàn} has {次|cì} at the bottom in simplified (two dots and 欠). In traditional 羨 it has three dots, 㳄: 13
  strokes against 12.
- {永|yǒng} and {水|shuǐ}: {永|yǒng} has a dot on top, and its middle stroke turns first ({横折钩|héng zhé gōu}) where
  {水|shuǐ} has a plain vertical hook ({竖钩|shù gōu}). Calligraphy teachers
  traditionally use {永|yǒng} to practise the basic strokes: the "eight principles of {永|yǒng}" ({永字八法|yǒng zì bā fǎ}) find eight
  kinds of brush stroke in its five.

### The others

- {厌|yàn}: {厂|chǎng} (a cliff) over {犬|quǎn} (dog). Traditional 厭 has {猒|yàn} under {厂|chǎng}: 14 strokes.
- {奋|fèn}: {大|dà} (big) over 田 (field). Traditional 奮 has {隹|zhuī} (a bird) between them: {大|dà} + {隹|zhuī} + 田, 16 strokes.
- {恼|nǎo}: 忄 + a lid {亠|tóu} over {凶|xiōng} (a cross inside an open box). Traditional 惱 is 忄 + 𡿺 (12 strokes).

### Stroke order

- **{永|yǒng}**: dot ({点|diǎn}), horizontal-turn-hook ({横折钩|héng zhé gōu}), then the short horizontal-left-falling stroke on the left
  ({横撇|héng piě}), and last the left-falling ({撇|piě}) and right-falling ({捺|nà}) strokes on the right.
- **忄** in {悔|huǐ}, {恼|nǎo}, {惜|xī}, {愉|yú}: the left dot, the right dot, then the vertical.
- **{嗯|èn}**: {口|kǒu} first, then {因|yīn}, then {心|xīn} at the bottom.

## Dialogue: the night before he leaves

Li Ming flies to Britain tomorrow morning for his one-year master's. He and Wang Fang take a walk in
the park where they had their first date.

2. Which three memories come back to her on the metro?
3. How has her idea of love changed?
4. Why does she write "{这些|zhè xiē}{小|xiǎo}{事|shì}，{当时|dāng shí}{没|méi}{觉得|jué de}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}"? What has she realised?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. She cried ({他|tā}{一|yì}{转身|zhuǎn shēn}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{哭|kū}{了|le}), although she had smiled and told him to go.
2. His nervousness on their first date; his bringing her meals every day when she was ill; his
   encouragement when her job hunt went badly.
3. She used to think love had to be romantic, with flowers and presents; now she thinks it means
   being there when the other person needs you.
4. At the time she took those small things for granted; looking back, she sees how much they meant:
   they showed his love, and now they move her. She doesn't say "I took him for granted" in so many
   words; the contrast between {当时|dāng shí} and {现在|xiàn zài} tells you.

"**Saturday 15 September, sunny.** This morning I went to the airport to see Li Ming off. We hardly
talked on the way. At the airport he checked in and was about to go through security. He gave me a
hug and said, 'A year goes quickly.' I smiled and said, 'Mm, off you go.' But the moment he turned
round, I cried. On the metro back I thought of many things from these three years: on our first date
he was so nervous he couldn't speak; when I was ill he brought me food every day; when my job hunt
wasn't going well, he was the one who kept encouraging me. At the time I didn't think much of these
little things; thinking of them now, they move me deeply. Friends often envy us and say we're very
close. I used to think love had to be romantic, with flowers and presents. Now I understand that love
is being there when the other person needs you. In the evening, alone at home, I felt bored and just
couldn't get into a book. At eleven my phone rang: a message from Li Ming: 'I've arrived. Don't
worry.' Looking at those few words, my heart was suddenly calm. I told myself: don't be sad, and don't
worry. We're both working for the future. In a year's time, we'll never have to be apart again."
</details>

## Write it

**A sentence about a picture.** The picture: a girl holding an envelope with a university's name on
it, jumping in the air; her parents behind her are clapping and laughing. Write one sentence with {激动|jī dòng}
or {兴奋|xīng fèn}.

**A short text.** Write 80–120 characters about a moment that moved you, or something you regret. Say
what happened, how you felt, and how you feel about it now. Use {使|shǐ} or {让|ràng}, and one of {再也|zài yě}{不|bù}, {怎么|zěn me}{也|yě} or {受不了|shòu bu liǎo}.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {收到|shōu dào}{大学|dà xué}{的|de}{通知书|tōng zhī shū}，{她|tā}{兴奋|xīng fèn}{得|de}{跳|tiào}{了|le}{起来|qǐ lái}，{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{也|yě}{高兴|gāo xìng}{得|de}{笑|xiào}{了|le}。 — When she got the university's acceptance
  letter, she jumped for joy, and her parents laughed with delight too. ({通知书|tōng zhī shū}: a letter of admission)
- {去年|qù nián}{冬天|dōng tiān}，{我|wǒ}{一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén}{在|zài}{外地|wài dì}{工作|gōng zuò}，{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{心情|xīn qíng}{很|hěn}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}。{那|nà}{天|tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{不|bú}{太|tài}{熟悉|shú xī}{的|de}{同事|tóng shì}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{送|sòng}{来|lái}{了|le}{药|yào}{和|hé}{一|yì}{碗|wǎn}{热|rè}{汤|tāng}。{她|tā}{只|zhǐ}{说|shuō}{了|le}{一|yí}{句|jù}：“{快|kuài}{吃|chī}{吧|ba}，{好好|hǎo hǎo}{休息|xiū xi}。”{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{小|xiǎo}{事|shì}{使|shǐ}{我|wǒ}{非常|fēi cháng}{感动|gǎn dòng}，{直到|zhí dào}{现在|xiàn zài}，{我|wǒ}{怎么|zěn me}{也|yě}{忘不了|wàng bu liǎo}{那|nà}{碗|wǎn}{汤|tāng}。{从|cóng}{那|nà}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{看|kàn}{到|dào}{需要|xū yào}{帮助|bāng zhù}{的|de}{人|rén}，{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{去|qù}{帮|bāng}{一下|yí xià}。 — Last winter I was working away from home on my own, fell ill and was
  very low. That evening a colleague I hardly knew brought me medicine and a bowl of hot soup. She only
  said, "Eat it while it's hot and get some rest." This small kindness moved me deeply: to this day,
  I can't forget that bowl of soup. Since then, whenever I see someone who needs help, I go and help.
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Feelings
{这个|zhè ge}{消息|xiāo xi}{使|shǐ}{大家|dà jiā}{非常|fēi cháng}{激动|jī dòng}。
= The news made everyone very excited.
{天气|tiān qì}{太|tài}{热|rè}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo}{了|le}！
= It's too hot: I can't stand it!
{那|nà}{家|jiā}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}{我|wǒ}{再也|zài yě}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。
= I'm never going to that restaurant again.
{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu}{睡不着|shuì bu zháo}。
= I just couldn't get to sleep last night.
{你|nǐ}{还|hái}{说|shuō}{呢|ne}！{你|nǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{也|yě}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}。
= Look who's talking! You were late yesterday too.
{祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{周末|zhōu mò}{愉快|yú kuài}！
= Have a nice weekend!
```

## Pronunciation

- {受不了|shòu bu liǎo} shòu bu liǎo: {了|liǎo} is liǎo (to manage), not le; {不|bu} is light. {受得了|shòu de liǎo} shòu de liǎo.
- {兴奋|xīng fèn} xīng fèn: {兴|xīng} is xīng here, first tone; in {高兴|gāo xìng} gāo xìng it's fourth tone.
- {后悔|hòu huǐ} hòu huǐ, {可惜|kě xī} kě xī, {羡慕|xiàn mù} xiàn mù, {愉快|yú kuài} yú kuài: watch *ui*, *xi*, *xian* and *yu*.
- {幸福|xìng fú} xìng fú and {兴奋|xīng fèn} xīng fèn: similar syllables, different tones and meanings.
- {啊|ā} ā at the start of a sentence: a high, level "ah!". The particle at the end ({好|hǎo}{啊|a} hǎo a) is light.
- {嗯|èn} èn: a short falling "mm"; with the mouth closed, many speakers say it as ǹg.

## Common mistakes

- {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{使|shǐ}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} in a chat is correct but sounds like writing; say {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}.
- ~~{使|shǐ}{我|wǒ}{看看|kàn kan}~~ for "let me see": {使|shǐ} can't mean "let". Say {让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{看看|kàn kan}.
- {我|wǒ}{再也|zài yě}{没|méi}{去|qù}{了|le} is heard in casual speech, but the standard forms are {我|wǒ}{再也|zài yě}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo} (I never went again) and
  {我|wǒ}{再也|zài yě}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le} (I'm never going again).
- {受不了|shòu bu liǎo} with {了|le} at the end means it has just become unbearable: {我|wǒ}{受不了|shòu bu liǎo}{了|le}！ is right, with two {了|le} (liǎo
  in the complement, le at the end).
- ~~{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感人|gǎn rén}~~ for "I'm moved": {感人|gǎn rén} describes the story. Say {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{感动|gǎn dòng}; {这个|zhè ge}{故事|gù shi}{很|hěn}{感人|gǎn rén}.
- {我|wǒ}{失去|shī qù}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{钥匙|yào shi} for losing your keys sounds odd: for an object, say {我|wǒ}{的|de}{钥匙|yào shi}{丢|diū}{了|le}. {失去|shī qù} is for losing
  something abstract or for ever ({失去|shī qù}{机会|jī huì}, {失去|shī qù}{朋友|péng you}).

## Key points

- {激动|jī dòng} (strong emotion), {兴奋|xīng fèn} (thrilled), {感动|gǎn dòng} (moved) / {感人|gǎn rén} (moving); {伤心|shāng xīn} (heartbroken), {失望|shī wàng} (disappointed),
  {后悔|hòu huǐ} (regret your act), {可惜|kě xī} (a pity); {烦|fán}, {烦恼|fán nǎo}, {讨厌|tǎo yàn}, {无聊|wú liáo}, {羡慕|xiàn mù}, {得意|dé yì}; {幸福|xìng fú} (deep happiness), {愉快|yú kuài} (pleasant).
- {感情|gǎn qíng} (feelings between people), {感受|gǎn shòu} (your experience), {感觉|gǎn jué} (a sensation); {爱情|ài qíng}, {爱心|ài xīn}, {心情|xīn qíng}, {内心|nèi xīn}, {气|qì}.
- {使|shǐ} + person + feeling: written {让|ràng}; it can't mean "let" or "ask to".
- {受不了|shòu bu liǎo} / {受得了|shòu de liǎo} (shòu bu liǎo / shòu de liǎo): can't stand / can stand.
- {再也|zài yě}{不|bù} + verb (+ {了|le}): never again from now; {再也|zài yě}{没|méi} + verb (+ {过|guo}): never again since then.
- {怎么|zěn me}{都|dōu} / {怎么|zěn me}{也|yě} + {不|bù} / {没|méi} (+ potential complement): however hard you try.
- {还|hái} X {呢|ne}: "and you call yourself X!"; {还|hái}{说|shuō}{呢|ne}: "look who's talking".
- {感|gǎn} makes "a sense of": {安全感|ān quán gǎn}, {幸福感|xìng fú gǎn}, {责任感|zé rèn gǎn}. {啊|ā} ā: oh! {嗯|èn} èn: mm, yes.
- New characters: {悔|huǐ} {恼|nǎo} {惜|xī} {浪|làng} {漫|màn} {嗯|èn} {幸|xìng} {福|fú} {羡|xiàn} {慕|mù} {厌|yàn} {奋|fèn} {愉|yú} {永|yǒng}; ✎ {永|yǒng}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: News, the internet and videos: 对于, 与, 而
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

During Wang Fang's summer internship at the news website, her first article goes online. This
lesson gives you the words of the media, old and new: the internet ({互联网|hù lián wǎng}), web pages and addresses
({网页|wǎng yè}, {网址|wǎng zhǐ}), videos ({视频|shì pín}), text messages ({短信|duǎn xìn}), radio ({广播|guǎng bō}) and TV series ({电视剧|diàn shì jù}), and the verbs for
sending, forwarding and replying. It also adds three small words that every news report uses:

- {对于|duì yú} (as for, regarding), and how it differs from {对|duì};
- {与|yǔ}, the written "and, with", beside {和|hé} and {跟|gēn};
- {而|ér}, the written "and, while, but", which you met in lesson 05.

At the end you can read a short news report in written style, talk about how you get your news, and
retell a short passage you hear.

## {对于|duì yú} and {对|duì}: as for, towards

### {对于|duì yú}: as for, regarding

{对于|duì yú} + a topic introduces what the sentence is about: "as for…, regarding…, when it comes to…". It's
formal; you'll meet it in news, reports and essays, and in careful speech:

{对于|duì yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}，{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。 — On this question, people's views differ. ({看法|kàn fǎ}: a view, lesson 25)

{对于|duì yú}{学生|xué sheng}{来说|lái shuō}，{最|zuì}{重要|zhòng yào}{的|de}{是|shì}{学习|xué xí}。 — For students, the most important thing is studying.

{学校|xué xiào}{对于|duì yú}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{非常|fēi cháng}{重视|zhòng shì}。 — The school takes this matter very seriously. ({重视|zhòng shì}: lesson 12)

{对于|duì yú}…{来说|lái shuō} is "for…, from the point of view of…", a common frame.

### {对|duì}: wider, and more spoken

{对|duì} can do everything {对于|duì yú} does: {对|duì}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}，{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng} is just as correct, and more spoken. But {对|duì} has
jobs that {对于|duì yú} doesn't:

- {对|duì} + person + attitude, "towards someone": {他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 (He's good to me.) {老师|lǎo shī}{对|duì}{学生|xué sheng}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn}。 Not ~~
  {他|tā}{对于|duì yú}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}~~.
- {对|duì} after an adverb or a modal verb: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{对|duì}{这个|zhè ge}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}。 (We're all interested in this.) {你|nǐ}{应该|yīng gāi}{对|duì}{他|tā}{说|shuō}
  “{谢谢|xiè xie}”。 Not ~~{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{对于|duì yú}{这个|zhè ge}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}~~: {对于|duì yú} doesn't come after {都|dōu}, {也|yě}, {很|hěn}, {会|huì}, {应该|yīng gāi} and the like.

| | {对于|duì yú} | {对|duì} |
|---|---|---|
| introducing a topic | {对于|duì yú}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}… | {对|duì}{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}… |
| a person and an attitude | ✗ | {他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} |
| after an adverb or a modal verb | ✗ | {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{对|duì}…{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù} |
| style | formal, written | any style |

When in doubt, {对|duì} is never wrong where {对于|duì yú} is right; the reverse doesn't hold.

## {与|yǔ}: and, with (written)

{与|yǔ} yǔ is the written partner of {和|hé} and {跟|gēn}. It joins two nouns ("A and B") or marks the person or thing
you do something with:

| Spoken | Written | |
|---|---|---|
| {我|wǒ}{和|hé}{他|tā} | {我|wǒ}{与|yǔ}{他|tā} | he and I |
| {跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{见面|jiàn miàn} | {与|yǔ}{朋友|péng you}{见面|jiàn miàn} | to meet friends |
| {跟|gēn}…{有关|yǒu guān} | {与|yǔ}…{有关|yǒu guān} | to be connected with… |
| {跟|gēn}…{相比|xiāng bǐ} | {与|yǔ}…{相比|xiāng bǐ} | compared with… (lesson 09) |
| {跟|gēn}…{不同|bù tóng} | {与|yǔ}…{不同|bù tóng} | different from… |

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{活动|huó dòng}{与|yǔ}{环保|huán bǎo}{有关|yǒu guān}。 — This event is about environmental protection. ({环保|huán bǎo}: lesson 28)

{与|yǔ}{去年|qù nián}{相比|xiāng bǐ}，{今年|jīn nián}{的|de}{网购|wǎng gòu}{人数|rén shù}{增加|zēng jiā}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 — Compared with last year, many more people shop online this year. ({增加|zēng jiā}: to increase, lesson 28)

Titles love {与|yǔ}: the Chinese title of *The Old Man and the Sea* is 《{老人|Lǎo rén}{与|yǔ}{海|Hǎi}》. In a news headline or a
book title, {与|yǔ} is the usual "and"; in conversation it sounds stiff, so say {和|hé} or {跟|gēn}.

## {而|ér}: and, while, but (written)

{而|ér} ér joins two parts of a sentence in writing (lesson 05). Two uses matter here:

- adding, between two adjectives: {简单|jiǎn dān}{而|ér}{有效|yǒu xiào} (simple and effective), {美丽|měi lì}{而|ér}{安静|ān jìng} (beautiful and quiet);
- contrasting, between two clauses, like "while, whereas": {南方|nán fāng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{暖和|nuǎn huo}，{而|ér}{北方|běi fāng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。 (Winters
  in the south are mild, while in the north they're cold. {暖和|nuǎn huo}: lesson 26)

{而|ér} often comes with {却|què} (lesson 14) for a sharper contrast: {别人|bié ren}{都|dōu}{走|zǒu}{了|le}，{而|ér}{他|tā}{却|què}{还|hái}{在|zài}{工作|gōng zuò}。 (Everyone else had left,
but he was still working.)

You know {而|ér} from {而且|ér qiě} (moreover), from {不|bú}{是|shì}…{而|ér}{是|shì} (not… but…, lesson 05) and from {然而|rán ér} (however, lesson 14).
On its own it belongs to writing; in speech say {但是|dàn shì}, {可是|kě shì} or just put the two clauses side by side.

## The media

### The internet: {互联网|hù lián wǎng} and the words built on {网|wǎng}

{互联网|hù lián wǎng} (the internet) is the full word; in speech people mostly say {网|wǎng} or {网上|wǎng shàng} (on the internet, online):
{上网|shàng wǎng} (to go online), {在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng} (online). Many words start with {网|wǎng}:

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {网页|wǎng yè} | a web page | {这个|zhè ge}{网页|wǎng yè}{打不开|dǎ bu kāi}。 (This page won't open.) |
| {网址|wǎng zhǐ} | a web address | {你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{网址|wǎng zhǐ}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{吧|ba}。 |
| {网友|wǎng yǒu} | an internet user; an online friend | {很|hěn}{多|duō}{网友|wǎng yǒu}{在|zài}{下面|xià miàn}{留言|liú yán}。 (Lots of people left comments below it. {留言|liú yán}: to leave a comment) |
| {网购|wǎng gòu} | to shop online; online shopping | {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}，{一般|yì bān}{都|dōu}{网购|wǎng gòu}。 |

{线上|xiàn shàng} (online) and {线下|xiàn xià} (offline, in person) are newer words for the two sides of a service or an event:
{线上|xiàn shàng}{课程|kè chéng} (an online course: {课程|kè chéng}, lesson 01), {线下|xiàn xià}{活动|huó dòng} (an in-person event), {线上|xiàn shàng}{线下|xiàn xià}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{报名|bào míng} (you can sign up
online or in person).

### News and information: {消息|xiāo xi}, {信息|xìn xī}, {获取|huò qǔ}

- {消息|xiāo xi} xiāo xi is "news" about something, or a message from someone: {好|hǎo}{消息|xiāo xi} (good news), {我|wǒ}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{发|fā}{了|le}{一|yì}{条|tiáo}{消息|xiāo xi}
  (I sent you a message; {条|tiáo}, the measure word for messages and news items). Light second syllable.
- {信息|xìn xī} xìn xī is "information", the general word: {获取|huò qǔ}{信息|xìn xī} (to obtain information), {信息|xìn xī}{时代|shí dài} (the information
  age; {时代|shí dài}, an age). In everyday speech, a {信息|xìn xī} can also be a text message.
- {获取|huò qǔ} (to obtain, to acquire) is written, used for information and knowledge: {现在|xiàn zài}{人们|rén men}{主要|zhǔ yào}{从|cóng}{网上|wǎng shàng}{获取|huò qǔ}{新闻|xīn wén}。
  (Nowadays people mainly get their news online.) In speech, say {得到|dé dào} or {找|zhǎo}{到|dào}.

### Sending, forwarding, replying

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {发送|fā sòng} | to send (a message, a file) | {请|qǐng}{在|zài}{下午|xià wǔ}{五|wǔ}{点|diǎn}{前|qián}{发送|fā sòng}。 |
| {发出|fā chū} | to send out, to give out (a notice, a sound) | {学校|xué xiào}{发出|fā chū}{通知|tōng zhī}，{明天|míng tiān}{放假|fàng jià}。 |
| {转发|zhuǎn fā} | to forward, to share | {他|tā}{把|bǎ}{这|zhè}{篇|piān}{文章|wén zhāng}{转发|zhuǎn fā}{给|gěi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{朋友|péng you}。 |
| {回复|huí fù} | to reply; a reply | {收到|shōu dào}{邮件|yóu jiàn}{以后|yǐ hòu}{请|qǐng}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{回复|huí fù}。 ({尽快|jǐn kuài}: as soon as possible) |

  (15 strokes).
- {际|jì}: 阝 (a mound, on the left) + {示|shì} (lesson 14's {表示|biǎo shì}). Traditional 際 is 阝 + {祭|jì} (13 strokes).
- {频|pín}: {步|bù} (a step, lesson 07) + {页|yè} (a page; originally "head"). Traditional 頻 is {步|bù} + {頁|yè}.

2. Old people and children ({其中|qí zhōng}{老年|lǎo nián}{人|rén}{与|yǔ}{儿童|ér tóng}{最|zuì}{多|duō}).
3. To show who the service helps most: people who can't easily get to the library. The resident's
   words ({以前|yǐ qián}…{很|hěn}{不|bù}{方便|fāng biàn}，{而|ér}{现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{就|jiù}{能|néng}{借|jiè}{到|dào}{书|shū}{了|le}) give a real example of the main fact. The article
   doesn't say "this helps the elderly" in its own voice; it lets a resident say it.
4. Work with nearby schools to hold an in-person reading group every month, and put videos of the
   events online ({将|jiāng}{与|yǔ}{附近|fù jìn}{的|de}{学校|xué xiào}{合作|hé zuò}……{并|bìng}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{播放|bō fàng}{活动|huó dòng}{的|de}{视频|shì pín}).

"**Community library launches online lending service.** Our website (Wang Fang, intern): To make
borrowing easier for residents, the Xincheng community library has launched an online lending
service this month. Residents just choose the books they want on the library's web page or on their
phones, and staff will deliver them to their door within two days. According to the person in charge
of the library, in the first week after the service began more than three hundred residents borrowed
books online, most of them old people and children. Library staff told this reporter that many young people
are too busy at work to go to the library, and the online service makes it easy for them to borrow
books too. A young person who works at a company nearby said: 'I used to go to the library less than
once a year; now I borrow two or three books online every month.' Residents have welcomed the service. A resident
in their seventies said: 'My legs are bad, and it used to be very hard to get to the library, but now I
can borrow books at home.' Internet users have also left comments under the library's video: 'We hope
there will be online reading events too.' The library says that as its next step it will work with
nearby schools to hold an in-person reading group every month, and will put videos of the events
online, so that more people can discover the pleasure of reading."
</details>

{据|jù} (according to: the {据|jù} of HSK 3's {根据|gēn jù}) and {将|jiāng} (will, lesson 05) are typical of news reports; {并|bìng} (and
also) is lesson 14's. A spoken version would say {图书馆|tú shū guǎn}{说|shuō}，{他们|tā men}{以后|yǐ hòu}{会|huì}{跟|gēn}{附近|fù jìn}{的|de}{学校|xué xiào}{一起|yì qǐ}…

## Speaking: retell what you hear

In the speaking test, as reported from the sample papers, you hear a short passage twice and retell
it in your own words, in about forty seconds. Listen to this passage (play it, without reading), then
retell it: who, what, why, and what changed.

```speak
# Grandpa and the radio
{现在|xiàn zài}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}{视频|shì pín}、{看|kàn}{新闻|xīn wén}，{很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{听|tīng}{广播|guǎng bō}{了|le}。{不过|bú guò}，{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{还是|hái shi}{会|huì}{收听|shōu tīng}{广播|guǎng bō}。{他|tā}{说|shuō}，{听|tīng}{广播|guǎng bō}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{可以|kě yǐ}{一边|yì biān}{做饭|zuò fàn}{一边|yì biān}{了解|liǎo jiě}{国际|guó jì}{国内|guó nèi}{的|de}{消息|xiāo xi}，{眼睛|yǎn jing}{也|yě}{不|bú}{累|lèi}。{最近|zuì jìn}，{他|tā}{还|hái}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{下载|xià zǎi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{广播|guǎng bō}{软件|ruǎn jiàn}，{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{收听|shōu tīng}{节目|jié mù}。{他|tā}{说|shuō}：“{这样|zhè yàng}{又|yòu}{方便|fāng biàn}{又|yòu}{有意思|yǒu yì si}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{成|chéng}{了|le}{网友|wǎng yǒu}{了|le}！”
= These days lots of people watch videos and read the news on their phones every day, and hardly anyone listens to the radio any more. But my grandpa still listens to the radio every morning. He says that while he listens he can cook and catch up on the news from home and abroad at the same time, and his eyes don't get tired. Recently he even downloaded a radio app to his phone and listens to programmes online. He says: "This way it's handy and fun: I've become an internet user too!"
```

{下载|xià zǎi} (to download; xià zài is also heard) and {软件|ruǎn jiàn} (an app, software) are HSK 5 words.

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

{现在|xiàn zài}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{看|kàn}{视频|shì pín}{和|hé}{新闻|xīn wén}，{不|bú}{太|tài}{听|tīng}{广播|guǎng bō}{了|le}。{可是|kě shì}{说话|shuō huà}{人|rén}{的|de}{爷爷|yé ye}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{都|dōu}{听|tīng}{广播|guǎng bō}，{因为|yīn wèi}{他|tā}{可以|kě yǐ}{一边|yì biān}{做饭|zuò fàn}{一边|yì biān}{听|tīng}{新闻|xīn wén}，{眼睛|yǎn jing}{不|bú}{累|lèi}。{最近|zuì jìn}{他|tā}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{听|tīng}{广播|guǎng bō}，{他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}，{还|hái}{说|shuō}{自己|zì jǐ}{也|yě}{成|chéng}{了|le}{网友|wǎng yǒu}。 — Many people now watch videos and news on their phones and don't listen to the radio much. But the
speaker's grandfather listens every morning, because he can cook while he hears the news, and it
doesn't tire his eyes. Recently he's been listening online on his phone; he finds it handy, and says
he's become an internet user too.
</details>

Keep the order of the passage, use your own words ({不|bú}{太|tài}{听|tīng} for {很|hěn}{少|shǎo}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{听|tīng}), and keep the ending, which is
the point.

## Write it

**A sentence about a picture.** The picture: a young woman on a sofa, holding up her phone and
filming a cat playing with a ball of wool. Write one sentence with {视频|shì pín}.

**A short text.** Write 80–120 characters on how you get your news: which media you use ({网上|wǎng shàng}, {电视|diàn shì},
{广播|guǎng bō}, {视频|shì pín}…), what you like and dislike about them, and whether you forward things. Use {对于|duì yú} or {对|duì}…{来说|lái shuō} once.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

- {她|tā}{正在|zhèng zài}{给|gěi}{她|tā}{的|de}{猫|māo}{拍|pāi}{视频|shì pín}，{准备|zhǔn bèi}{发|fā}{到|dào}{网上|wǎng shàng}。 — She's filming her cat, ready to put the video online.
- {我|wǒ}{主要|zhǔ yào}{从|cóng}{网上|wǎng shàng}{获取|huò qǔ}{新闻|xīn wén}，{一般|yì bān}{是|shì}{在|zài}{手机|shǒu jī}{上|shàng}{看|kàn}。{网上|wǎng shàng}{的|de}{消息|xiāo xi}{又|yòu}{多|duō}{又|yòu}{快|kuài}，{可是|kě shì}{有的|yǒu de}{不|bù}{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}。{所以|suǒ yǐ}，{看|kàn}{到|dào}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{转发|zhuǎn fā}{的|de}{消息|xiāo xi}，{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{先|xiān}{查|chá}{一下|yí xià}。{对于|duì yú}{我|wǒ}{来说|lái shuō}，{最|zuì}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{方法|fāng fǎ}{是|shì}{多|duō}{看|kàn}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{网站|wǎng zhàn}，{再|zài}{自己|zì jǐ}{判断|pàn duàn}。{晚上|wǎn shang}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{会|huì}{看|kàn}{一会儿|yí huìr}{电视|diàn shì}{新闻|xīn wén}。 — I get my news mainly online, usually on my phone. There's a lot of it and it's fast, but some of
  it isn't true. So when I see something lots of people are forwarding, I check it first. For me, the
  best way is to look at several websites and then judge for myself. When I have time in the evening, I
  also watch the TV news for a while. ({判断|pàn duàn}: to judge, lesson 25)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# The media
{对于|duì yú}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}，{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{清楚|qīng chu}。
= As for that, I'm not too sure.
{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{网址|wǎng zhǐ}{发|fā}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{吧|ba}。
= Send me the web address.
{地铁|dì tiě}{里|lǐ}{手机|shǒu jī}{没有|méi yǒu}{信号|xìn hào}。
= There's no phone signal on the underground.
{这|zhè}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}{最近|zuì jìn}{很|hěn}{流行|liú xíng}。
= This TV series is very popular at the moment.
{收到|shōu dào}{邮件|yóu jiàn}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{请|qǐng}{尽快|jǐn kuài}{回复|huí fù}。
= Please reply as soon as you get the email.
{我|wǒ}{拍|pāi}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{视频|shì pín}，{马上|mǎ shàng}{转发|zhuǎn fā}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}。
= I've made a video: I'll forward it to you right away.
```

## Pronunciation

- {视频|shì pín} shì pín, {信息|xìn xī} xìn xī, {信号|xìn hào} xìn hào: *sh* against *x*, and *in* in {频|pín}, {信|xìn}.
- {消息|xiāo xi} xiāo xi has a light {息|xī}; in {信息|xìn xī} xìn xī it keeps its first tone.
- {与|yǔ} yǔ (and) is third tone. In {参与|cān yù} (to take part, HSK 5) it's yù; in a classical text it can be yú
  (lesson 25h2). Today's {与|yǔ} is yǔ.
- {广播|guǎng bō} guǎng bō, {播放|bō fàng} bō fàng: {播|bō} is first tone, bō.
- {转发|zhuǎn fā} zhuǎn fā: zhuǎn is third tone here (to turn, to pass on); {转|zhuàn} is also read zhuàn (to spin).
- {互联网|hù lián wǎng} hù lián wǎng: fourth, second, third.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{他|tā}{对于|duì yú}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}~~: an attitude towards a person takes {对|duì}: {他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}.
- ~~{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{对于|duì yú}{这个|zhè ge}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}~~: {对于|duì yú} doesn't come after an adverb such as {都|dōu}; say {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{对|duì}{这个|zhè ge}{很|hěn}{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}.
- {我|wǒ}{与|yǔ}{他|tā}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you} in conversation isn't wrong, but it sounds like writing: {我|wǒ}{和|hé}{他|tā}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}{朋友|péng you}.
- {我|wǒ}{获取|huò qǔ}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{短信|duǎn xìn} sounds wrong for "I got your text": {获取|huò qǔ} is for information and knowledge in writing; a
  message you get is {收到|shōu dào}: {我|wǒ}{收到|shōu dào}{了|le}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{短信|duǎn xìn}.
- {观看|guān kàn} for an ordinary "watch" sounds formal: {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{部|bù}{电影|diàn yǐng}, not {观看|guān kàn}.
- The audience of a radio show is {听众|tīng zhòng}; of a film or a match, {观众|guān zhòng}.

## Key points

- {对于|duì yú} + topic: as for, regarding (formal); {对于|duì yú}…{来说|lái shuō}: for… {对|duì} does all of this and more: {对|duì} + person
  ({他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}), and after adverbs and modal verbs ({都|dōu}{对|duì}…{感兴趣|gǎn xìng qù}).
- {与|yǔ} = written {和|hé} / {跟|gēn}: {与|yǔ}…{有关|yǒu guān}, {与|yǔ}…{相比|xiāng bǐ}, {与|yǔ}…{不同|bù tóng}, titles (《{老人|Lǎo rén}{与|yǔ}{海|Hǎi}》).
- {而|ér} (written): adds ({简单|jiǎn dān}{而|ér}{有效|yǒu xiào}) or contrasts ({南方|nán fāng}…，{而|ér}{北方|běi fāng}…), often with {却|què}.
- The internet: {互联网|hù lián wǎng}, {网页|wǎng yè}, {网址|wǎng zhǐ}, {网友|wǎng yǒu}, {网购|wǎng gòu}, {线上|xiàn shàng} / {线下|xiàn xià}; {消息|xiāo xi} (news, a message), {信息|xìn xī} (information), {获取|huò qǔ}.
- Sending: {发送|fā sòng}, {发出|fā chū}, {转发|zhuǎn fā}, {回复|huí fù}, {短信|duǎn xìn}; {信号|xìn hào}, {打通|dǎ tōng} / {打不通|dǎ bu tōng}.
- Media: {图片|tú piàn}, {视频|shì pín}, {播放|bō fàng}, {广播|guǎng bō}, {收听|shōu tīng}, {听众|tīng zhòng}, {观看|guān kàn}, {电视剧|diàn shì jù} ({一|yí}{部|bù}{电视剧|diàn shì jù}), {流行|liú xíng}, {记者|jì zhě}, {国际|guó jì}, {推出|tuī chū}.
- New characters: {播|bō} {剧|jù} {际|jì} {频|pín} {众|zhòng} {线|xiàn} {与|yǔ}; ✎ {际|jì} {众|zhòng} {线|xiàn} {与|yǔ}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Giving opinions: 不管 / 无论…都, 一方面…另一方面, 拿…来说
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Giving short opinions is one of the things the level-4 standard expects: saying what you think, why,
and what the other side might say. This lesson brings together the grammar for it:

- the **[[unconditional sentence]]** {不管|bù guǎn} / {无论|wú lùn} / {不论|bú lùn}…{都|dōu} / {也|yě}: whatever, however, no matter;
- **[[一方面…另一方面]]**, to set out two sides of one question;
- the fixed formats {拿|ná}…{来说|lái shuō} (take… for example), {在|zài}…{方面|fāng miàn} (in terms of…) and {就是说|jiù shì shuō} (that is to say), and two
  more for strong decisions, {说|shuō}{什么|shén me}{也|yě}{得|děi} and X {就|jiù}{是|shì}{了|le};
- the written question words {是否|shì fǒu} (whether or not) and {能否|néng fǒu} (whether one can).

You'll also learn the words of opinion and judgement: {看法|kàn fǎ}, {想法|xiǎng fǎ}, {说法|shuō fǎ} and {主意|zhǔ yi}; {肯定|kěn dìng}, {确实|què shí}, {也许|yě xǔ} and {估计|gū jì};
{好处|hǎo chù} and {坏处|huài chu}, {多数|duō shù} and {少数|shǎo shù}. At the end you can take part in a discussion, read a short argued text, and
answer the kind of opinion question the speaking test asks.

## {不管|bù guǎn} / {无论|wú lùn} / {不论|bú lùn}…{都|dōu}: no matter…

An **[[unconditional sentence]]** says that the result holds whatever the condition is. The first clause
starts with {不管|bù guǎn}, {无论|wú lùn} or {不论|bú lùn} and contains an open choice; the second has {都|dōu} or {也|yě} before its verb:

{不管|bù guǎn}{天气|tiān qì}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}，{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}。 — Whatever the weather, he goes running every day.

{无论|wú lùn}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}，{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}。 — Wherever you go, I'll go with you.

{不论|bú lùn}{多|duō}{忙|máng}，{她|tā}{也|yě}{会|huì}{给|gěi}{父母|fù mǔ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。 — However busy she is, she always rings her parents.

{不管|bù guǎn} is the spoken one; {无论|wú lùn} and {不论|bú lùn} are more formal. All three work the same way.

### The open choice

The {不管|bù guǎn} clause must leave the condition open. It needs one of these:

| Open element | Example |
|---|---|
| a question word ({谁|shéi}, {什么|shén me}, {哪儿|nǎr}, {怎么|zěn me}, {怎么样|zěn me yàng}, {多|duō}) | {不管|bù guǎn}{谁|shéi}{来|lái}，{都|dōu}{要|yào}{先|xiān}{登记|dēng jì}。 (Whoever comes must sign in first. {登记|dēng jì}: to register) |
| {多|duō} + adjective (however…) | {无论|wú lùn}{多|duō}{难|nán}，{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{试试|shì shi}。 (However hard it is, I'll give it a try.) |
| A {还是|hái shi} B | {不管|bù guǎn}{下雨|xià yǔ}{还是|hái shi}{下|xià}{雪|xuě}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{进行|jìn xíng}。 (Rain or snow, the match will go ahead.) |
| A {不|bù} A | {不管|bù guǎn}{你|nǐ}{同意|tóng yì}{不|bu}{同意|tóng yì}，{我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{要|yào}{去|qù}。 (Whether you agree or not, I'm going.) |

A plain statement can't follow {不管|bù guǎn}: ~~{不管|bù guǎn}{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{他|tā}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}~~ is wrong, because {天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng} leaves nothing
open. Say {不管|bù guǎn}{天气|tiān qì}{多|duō}{冷|lěng} (however cold) or use {虽然|suī rán} (although): {虽然|suī rán}{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{他|tā}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}{了|le}.

### {都|dōu} and {也|yě}

The second clause needs {都|dōu} (more common) or {也|yě} after its subject and before the verb: {我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}, {她|tā}{也|yě}{会|huì}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}.
Leaving it out is the commonest mistake with these sentences.

{不管|bù guǎn} alone is also a verb, "not to care about, not to bother with": {别人|bié ren}{怎么|zěn me}{说|shuō}，{我|wǒ}{不管|bù guǎn}。 (I don't care what other
people say.)

## {一方面|yì fāng miàn}…{另一方面|lìng yì fāng miàn}: on the one hand… on the other

**[[一方面…另一方面]]** sets out two sides of one question, or two reasons for one thing. The second clause
often has {也|yě} or {还|hái}:

{上|shàng}{网课|wǎng kè}{一方面|yì fāng miàn}{很|hěn}{方便|fāng biàn}，{另一方面|lìng yì fāng miàn}{也|yě}{容易|róng yì}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{分心|fēn xīn}。 — Online classes are convenient on the one hand, but on the other they make it easy to get distracted. ({分心|fēn xīn}: to be distracted)

{他|tā}{来|lái}{北京|Běi jīng}{工作|gōng zuò}，{一方面|yì fāng miàn}{是|shì}{为了|wèi le}{赚|zhuàn}{钱|qián}，{另一方面|lìng yì fāng miàn}{也|yě}{想|xiǎng}{多|duō}{了解|liǎo jiě}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — He came to work in Beijing partly to earn money and partly because he wants to get to know China better.

The two sides can be against each other (the first example) or pull the same way (the second). English
"on the one hand… on the other hand" only does the first, so use "partly… and partly…" or "for one
thing… for another…" for the second.

{方面|fāng miàn} alone is an "aspect, side, respect": {在|zài}{这|zhè}{方面|fāng miàn} (in this respect), {各|gè}{方面|fāng miàn} (in every respect).

## Three fixed formats for opinions

### {拿|ná}…{来说|lái shuō}: take… for example

{拿|ná} + an example + {来说|lái shuō} introduces a case that supports what you've just said:

{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{网购|wǎng gòu}。{拿|ná}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{来说|lái shuō}，{她|tā}{觉得|jué de}{在|zài}{商店|shāng diàn}{里|lǐ}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{更|gèng}{放心|fàng xīn}。 — Lots of people don't like shopping online. Take my mum: she feels safer buying things in a shop.

{拿|ná}{北京|Běi jīng}{来说|lái shuō}，{地铁|dì tiě}{越|yuè}{来|lái}{越|yuè}{方便|fāng biàn}{了|le}。 — Take Beijing: the metro is getting more and more convenient.

It's close to {比如|bǐ rú} (for example, HSK 3), but {拿|ná}…{来说|lái shuō} takes one case and talks about it at some length.

### {在|zài}…{方面|fāng miàn}: in terms of…, when it comes to…

{在|zài} + an area + {方面|fāng miàn} limits what you're saying to one area:

{在|zài}{学习|xué xí}{方面|fāng miàn}，{他|tā}{从来|cóng lái}{不|bú}{让|ràng}{父母|fù mǔ}{担心|dān xīn}。 — When it comes to studying, he never gives his parents cause to worry.

{这|zhè}{家|jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{在|zài}{服务|fú wù}{方面|fāng miàn}{做|zuò}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — This company does very well on service.

### {就是说|jiù shì shuō}: that is to say

{就是说|jiù shì shuō} (often {也就是说|yě jiù shì shuō} or {这就是说|zhè jiù shì shuō}) explains what the previous sentence means, in other words:

{他|tā}{说|shuō}{他|tā}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{也就是说|yě jiù shì shuō}，{他|tā}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{来|lái}{了|le}。 — He says he's busy: in other words, he isn't coming today.

The {就是|jiù shì} here is {就|jiù} + {是|shì}, "is precisely"; it's not the {就是|jiù shì} "even if" of lesson 26.

### Two more: {说|shuō}{什么|shén me}{也|yě}{得|děi} and X {就|jiù}{是|shì}{了|le}

Two fixed formats for firm decisions round off the set (the reference sheet *Fixed formats* has them
all):

- {说|shuō}{什么|shén me}{也|yě}{得|děi} + verb: "whatever happens, (I) must…": {这|zhè}{次|cì}{比赛|bǐ sài}，{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{什么|shén me}{也|yě}{得|děi}{参加|cān jiā}。 (I'm taking part in this
  competition, whatever it takes.) {得|děi} is děi, "must".
- X + {就|jiù}{是|shì}{了|le} at the end: "just X, that's all; don't worry": {你|nǐ}{放心|fàng xīn}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{一定|yí dìng}{按时|àn shí}{到|dào}。 (Just don't worry: I'll be
  there on time.) {不|bú}{会|huì}{就|jiù}{问|wèn}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{了|le}。 (If you don't know, just ask.)

## {是否|shì fǒu} and {能否|néng fǒu}: whether (written)

{是否|shì fǒu} is the written {是|shì}{不|bu}{是|shì}, and {能否|néng fǒu} the written {能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}. They put a yes-or-no question inside a sentence:

{他|tā}{是否|shì fǒu}{同意|tóng yì}，{现在|xiàn zài}{还|hái}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}。 — Whether he agrees isn't known yet.

{能否|néng fǒu}{成功|chéng gōng}，{关键|guān jiàn}{在于|zài yú}{大家|dà jiā}{是否|shì fǒu}{努力|nǔ lì}。 — Whether it succeeds depends above all on whether everyone works hard. ({在于|zài yú}: to lie in)

{请问|qǐng wèn}，{这里|zhè lǐ}{是否|shì fǒu}{可以|kě yǐ}{停车|tíng chē}？ — Excuse me, may one park here? (a notice or a formal question)

Three things to watch:

- {是否|shì fǒu} and {能否|néng fǒu} already ask the question, so no {吗|ma}: ~~{这里|zhè lǐ}{是否|shì fǒu}{可以|kě yǐ}{停车|tíng chē}{吗|ma}~~ is wrong.
- {是否|shì fǒu} goes before the verb or adjective it questions, often a whole verb phrase: {是否|shì fǒu}{参加|cān jiā}, {是否|shì fǒu}{满意|mǎn yì}. {能否|néng fǒu} is
  {能|néng} + {否|fǒu} (not), so it covers {能|néng} only.
- In speech, say {是|shì}{不|bu}{是|shì} and {能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}: {他|tā}{同|tóng}{不|bu}{同意|tóng yì}，{我|wǒ}{还|hái}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}.

## Words for opinions

### Views and ideas: {看法|kàn fǎ}, {想法|xiǎng fǎ}, {说法|shuō fǎ}, {主意|zhǔ yi}

| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {看法|kàn fǎ} | a view, an opinion (on a question) | {你|nǐ}{对|duì}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{看法|kàn fǎ}？ (What's your view on this?) |
| {想法|xiǎng fǎ} | an idea, what you think; a plan | {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{想法|xiǎng fǎ}：{我们|wǒ men}{周末|zhōu mò}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}{吧|ba}。 |
| {说法|shuō fǎ} | a way of putting it; a claim, a version | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{说法|shuō fǎ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{准确|zhǔn què}。 (That way of putting it isn't quite accurate.) |
| {主意|zhǔ yi} | an idea for what to do, a plan | {好|hǎo}{主意|zhǔ yi}！ / {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{主意|zhǔ yi}{了|le}。 (I don't know what to do.) |

{看法|kàn fǎ} is your opinion about an issue ({对|duì}…{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}). {想法|xiǎng fǎ} is broader: what's in your head, including plans. {主意|zhǔ yi}
is a practical idea, a way out ({出主意|chū zhǔ yi}, to suggest what to do); its {意|yì} is light, zhǔ yi. {意见|yì jiàn} (lesson 14) is
an opinion offered to someone, often a criticism.

### Certain or not: {肯定|kěn dìng}, {确实|què shí}, {也许|yě xǔ}, {估计|gū jì}, {怀疑|huái yí}, {判断|pàn duàn}

| Word | How sure | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {肯定|kěn dìng} | certainly, definitely; to confirm | {他|tā}{肯定|kěn dìng}{知道|zhī dào}。 / {老师|lǎo shī}{肯定|kěn dìng}{了|le}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{想法|xiǎng fǎ}。 (The teacher approved our idea.) |
| {确实|què shí} | indeed, really (confirms what was said) | {这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{确实|què shí}{很|hěn}{复杂|fù zá}。 (This question really is complicated.) |
| {估计|gū jì} | to reckon, to estimate | {我|wǒ}{估计|gū jì}{他|tā}{不|bú}{会|huì}{来|lái}{了|le}。 / {估计|gū jì}{要|yào}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。 |
| {也许|yě xǔ} | perhaps, maybe | {也许|yě xǔ}{他|tā}{忘|wàng}{了|le}。 |
| {怀疑|huái yí} | to doubt; to suspect | {我|wǒ}{怀疑|huái yí}{他|tā}{说|shuō}{的|de}{不|bú}{是|shì}{真|zhēn}{的|de}。 (I suspect what he said isn't true.) |
| {判断|pàn duàn} | to judge; a judgement | {你|nǐ}{的|de}{判断|pàn duàn}{是|shì}{对|duì}{的|de}。 |

{怀疑|huái yí} + a clause is "to suspect that…": {我|wǒ}{怀疑|huái yí}{他|tā}{病|bìng}{了|le} means you think he probably is ill. To doubt something,
say {怀疑|huái yí} + noun: {我|wǒ}{怀疑|huái yí}{这个|zhè ge}{说法|shuō fǎ} (I doubt that claim).

### Real and true: {实际|shí jì}, {实际上|shí jì shàng}, {真正|zhēn zhèng}, {完全|wán quán}

- {实际|shí jì} (reality; practical, realistic): {这个|zhè ge}{计划|jì huà}{不|bú}{太|tài}{实际|shí jì}。 (This plan isn't very realistic.) {实际情况|shí jì qíng kuàng} (the
  actual situation).
- {实际上|shí jì shàng} (in fact, actually) corrects an impression: {他|tā}{看起来|kàn qǐ lai}{很|hěn}{冷静|lěng jìng}，{实际上|shí jì shàng}{非常|fēi cháng}{紧张|jǐn zhāng}。 (He looks calm, but
  actually he's very nervous.)
- {真正|zhēn zhèng} (real, genuine) goes before a noun or a verb: {真正|zhēn zhèng}{的|de}{朋友|péng you} (a true friend), {我|wǒ}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{明白|míng bai}{了|le} (I really
  understood).
- {完全|wán quán} (completely): {我|wǒ}{完全|wán quán}{同意|tóng yì}。 {完全|wán quán}{不|bù}{一样|yí yàng}。

### Same, different, opposite: {相同|xiāng tóng}, {同样|tóng yàng}, {相反|xiāng fǎn}, {区别|qū bié}

- {相同|xiāng tóng} (identical, the same) is formal and goes before a noun or after {是|shì}…{的|de}: {相同|xiāng tóng}{的|de}{问题|wèn tí}; {我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}{是|shì}{相同|xiāng tóng}{的|de}。
  In speech, {一样|yí yàng}.
- {同样|tóng yàng} (likewise, the same; equally): {同样|tóng yàng}{的|de}{错误|cuò wù} (the same mistake), {学生|xué sheng}{要|yào}{尊重|zūn zhòng}{老师|lǎo shī}，{同样|tóng yàng}，{老师|lǎo shī}{也|yě}{要|yào}{尊重|zūn zhòng}{学生|xué sheng}。
- {相反|xiāng fǎn} (opposite; on the contrary): {他|tā}{不但|bú dàn}{没|méi}{生气|shēng qì}，{相反|xiāng fǎn}，{还|hái}{表扬|biǎo yáng}{了|le}{我|wǒ}。 (Far from being angry, he praised me.)
- {区别|qū bié} (a difference; to tell apart): {这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{词|cí}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{区别|qū bié}？ {你|nǐ}{能|néng}{区别|qū bié}{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{字|zì}{吗|ma}？

### Society, law and the way things are done

{社会|shè huì} (society): {社会|shè huì}{问题|wèn tí} (a social problem), {走向|zǒu xiàng}{社会|shè huì} (to go out into the world, after school). {法律|fǎ lǜ} (law):
{遵守|zūn shǒu}{法律|fǎ lǜ} (to obey the law; {遵守|zūn shǒu}, HSK 5). {法|fǎ} alone is "a method, a way" ({方法|fāng fǎ}, {办法|bàn fǎ}, {看法|kàn fǎ}, {说法|shuō fǎ} all have it) and, in
writing, "law". {方式|fāng shì} is "a way, a manner": {生活方式|shēng huó fāng shì} (way of life), {用|yòng}{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{方式|fāng shì} (in this way). {调查|diào chá} is "to
investigate; a survey": {做|zuò}{调查|diào chá}. {从中|cóng zhōng} (from it, out of it) is written: {从中|cóng zhōng}{学|xué}{到|dào}{很|hěn}{多|duō} (to learn a lot from it).

### Parts and sounds

- {键|jiàn}: 钅 (metal) + {建|jiàn} jiàn (to build, lesson 14's {建议|jiàn yì}): the sound exactly. A key on a keyboard is {键|jiàn} ({键盘|jiàn pán},
  a keyboard), and {关键|guān jiàn}, the crucial point, has it too. Traditional 鍵 is {金|jīn} + {建|jiàn}.
- {估|gū}: 亻 + {古|gǔ} gǔ, the sound part you met in lesson 21 ({姑|gū} gū).
- {判|pàn}: {半|bàn} bàn (half) + 刂 (knife). A memory aid: a knife cutting something in half, to decide between the
  two. {半|bàn} gives a close sound (bàn for pàn).
- {怀|huái}: 忄 + {不|bù}. Traditional 懷 is very different: 忄 + {褱|huái}, 19 strokes. So "忄 + {不|bù}" is true of simplified
  {怀|huái} only.
- {肯|kěn}: {止|zhǐ} (stop) on top of ⺼ (flesh, the {月|yuè} of body words).
- {社|shè}: 礻 (the altar radical, from {示|shì}) + {土|tǔ} (earth). The same 礻 is in {礼|lǐ} and {福|fú} (lesson 23).
- {断|duàn}: {米|mǐ} inside an open frame on the left, {斤|jīn} (an axe) on the right. Traditional 斷 has four small 幺
  (threads) on the left instead: 18 strokes. {断|duàn} is also in {不断|bú duàn} (continuously), lesson 27.
- {疑|yí}: fourteen strokes in four parts: 匕 and {矢|shǐ} on the left, then the right side with 疋 at its foot.
  Look-alike: {凝|níng} (to freeze, HSK 6) adds 冫.

- **{社|shè}**: 礻 ({点|diǎn}, {横撇|héng piě}, {竖|shù}, {点|diǎn}), then {土|tǔ} ({横|héng}, {竖|shù}, {横|héng}).

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. That students' main task is to study and a job harms their studies; and that a job has many
   advantages.
2. Pocket money every month, and much better skills with people: he used to blush with strangers, and
   now he can deal calmly with any customer.
3. Most working students work under ten hours a week and their marks don't suffer; a few work over
   twenty hours, fall asleep in class and fail exams.
4. Neither simply for nor against: students can work if they judge that they can manage both, and
   the hours must be reasonable. The real point, in the last sentence, is that what matters is whether

"**Should university students take part-time jobs?** Should university students work part-time?
People's views on this question differ a great deal. Some think students' main task is to study and
that a job will affect their studies; others think a job has many advantages. On the one hand, a job
really does teach students things they can't learn from books. Take my classmate Xiao Zhang: he works
at a café, and not only does he earn some pocket money every month, he has also made great progress
in dealing with people. He used to blush when he met people he didn't know; now, whatever kind of
customer he meets, he can solve the problem calmly. On the other hand, a job has its disadvantages.
Last year our college did a survey and found that most working students work fewer than ten hours a
week, and their results haven't suffered; but a few work more than twenty hours a week, and as a
result they often sleep in class and fail their exams. So my view is: students can take part-time
jobs, but first they should judge whether they can do both things well at once. That is to say, the
hours must be reasonable and mustn't affect their studies. In fact, whether or not you have a job,
what really matters is whether you can learn something from it."
