## Pronunciation

- {好处|hǎo chù} hǎo chù and {坏处|huài chu} huài chu: the word list gives {坏处|huài chu} a light second syllable; {好处|hǎo chù} is heard both
  with a full fourth tone and light (hǎo chu).
- {主意|zhǔ yi} zhǔ yi: light {意|yì}. In {意见|yì jiàn} yì jiàn and {注意|zhù yì} zhù yì it's yì.
- {不论|bú lùn} bú lùn ({不|bù} before a fourth tone), {不管|bù guǎn} bù guǎn (before a third). {无论|wú lùn} wú lùn.
- {怀疑|huái yí} huái yí: two rising tones. {估计|gū jì} gū jì, {肯定|kěn dìng} kěn dìng, {确实|què shí} què shí.
- {是否|shì fǒu} shì fǒu and {能否|néng fǒu} néng fǒu: {否|fǒu} is fǒu, third tone (as in {否则|fǒu zé}, lesson 11).
- {社会|shè huì} shè huì: *sh*, *e*; {多数|duō shù} duō shù and {少数|shǎo shù} shǎo shù: {数|shù} is shù, the noun.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{不管|bù guǎn}{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{他|tā}{都|dōu}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}~~: the {不管|bù guǎn} clause needs an open choice: {不管|bù guǎn}{天气|tiān qì}{多|duō}{冷|lěng} or {不管|bù guǎn}{天气|tiān qì}{冷|lěng}{不|bu}{冷|lěng}.
- ~~{无论|wú lùn}{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}，{我|wǒ}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}~~ without {都|dōu}: the second clause needs {都|dōu} or {也|yě}: {我|wǒ}{都|dōu}{跟|gēn}{你|nǐ}{一起|yì qǐ}{去|qù}.
- ~~{这里|zhè lǐ}{是否|shì fǒu}{可以|kě yǐ}{停车|tíng chē}{吗|ma}？~~: {是否|shì fǒu} already asks; drop {吗|ma}.
- {我|wǒ}{怀疑|huái yí}{他|tā}{病|bìng}{了|le} means you think he's ill, not that you doubt it. To doubt a claim: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{相信|xiāng xìn} or {我|wǒ}{怀疑|huái yí}{这个|zhè ge}{说法|shuō fǎ}.
- {好|hǎo}{主意|zhǔ yi} is a good idea for what to do; {好|hǎo}{看法|kàn fǎ} isn't said. Say {你|nǐ}{的|de}{看法|kàn fǎ}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{道理|dào li} (your view makes sense; {道理|dào li}: sense,
  reason).
- {一方面|yì fāng miàn}…{一方面|yì fāng miàn} also exists, but today {另一方面|lìng yì fāng miàn} is the usual second half: {一方面|yì fāng miàn}…，{另一方面|lìng yì fāng miàn}…

## Key points

- Unconditional: {不管|bù guǎn} / {无论|wú lùn} / {不论|bú lùn} + open choice (question word, {多|duō} + adjective, A {还是|hái shi} B, A {不|bù} A), then {都|dōu} / {也|yě}:
  {不管|bù guǎn}{多|duō}{忙|máng}，{她|tā}{都|dōu}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}. A plain statement takes {虽然|suī rán}, not {不管|bù guǎn}.
- {一方面|yì fāng miàn}…，{另一方面|lìng yì fāng miàn} ({也|yě} / {还|hái})…: two sides, or two reasons.
- {拿|ná}…{来说|lái shuō} (take… for example), {在|zài}…{方面|fāng miàn} (in terms of…), ({也|yě}){就是说|jiù shì shuō} (in other words); {说|shuō}{什么|shén me}{也|yě}{得|děi} + verb
  (whatever happens, must), X {就|jiù}{是|shì}{了|le} (just X).
- {是否|shì fǒu} = written {是|shì}{不|bu}{是|shì}, {能否|néng fǒu} = written {能|néng}{不|bu}{能|néng}; no {吗|ma} after them.
- {看法|kàn fǎ} (a view), {想法|xiǎng fǎ} (an idea), {说法|shuō fǎ} (a claim, a way of putting it), {主意|zhǔ yi} (a plan, zhǔ yi).
- {肯定|kěn dìng}, {确实|què shí}, {估计|gū jì}, {也许|yě xǔ}, {怀疑|huái yí} (+ clause: to suspect), {判断|pàn duàn}; {实际|shí jì} / {实际上|shí jì shàng}, {真正|zhēn zhèng}, {完全|wán quán}.
- {相同|xiāng tóng} (formal), {同样|tóng yàng}, {相反|xiāng fǎn}, {区别|qū bié}; {好处|hǎo chù} / {坏处|huài chu}, {关键|guān jiàn}, {多数|duō shù} / {少数|shǎo shù}, {普遍|pǔ biàn}, {复杂|fù zá}; {社会|shè huì}, {法律|fǎ lǜ}, {方式|fāng shì}, {调查|diào chá}, {从中|cóng zhōng}.
- New characters: {键|jiàn} {估|gū} {怀|huái} {疑|yí} {肯|kěn} {社|shè} {判|pàn} {断|duàn}; ✎ {社|shè} {断|duàn}.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Mencius's mother moves house: 孟母三迁
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

{孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān}, "Mencius's mother moved three times", is one of the best-known family stories in Chinese. It's
told to children, quoted by parents choosing where to live, and used as a set phrase about how much
surroundings shape a child. This lesson tells the story in modern Chinese (our own retelling, not a
translation of the old text), says where it comes from, and looks at how people use the phrase today.

## Who Mencius was

{孟子|Mèng zǐ} (Mencius, in pinyin Mèng zǐ) was a thinker of the Warring States period. His traditional dates are
about 372–289 BCE, but they aren't certain. He followed the teaching of Confucius ({孔子|Kǒng zǐ}, HSK 3), and in the
Confucian tradition he is ranked second only to Confucius himself; the book of his sayings and
conversations, 《{孟子|Mèng zǐ}》, became one of the classics every educated person read. "Mencius" is the Latin form
of {孟子|Mèng zǐ}, as "Confucius" is of {孔夫子|Kǒng fū zǐ}. {子|zǐ} after a surname is an old title of respect, "Master": {孟子|Mèng zǐ} is
"Master Meng".

## Where the story comes from

The story is told in the 《{列女传|Liè nǚ zhuàn}》 (*Biographies of Exemplary Women*), a collection of short lives of women
from early Chinese history, put together in the Han dynasty. It's traditionally attributed to the
scholar {刘向|Liú Xiàng} (Liu Xiang, 77–6 BCE). The 《{列女传|Liè nǚ zhuàn}》 was written down nearly three centuries after Mencius,
and nobody can say whether the family really moved three times: read it as a story about Mencius,
not as a record. In it, his mother is a model of a wise parent, and this is one of several stories
about how she brought him up.

## The story

> **{孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān}**
>
> {孟子|Mèng zǐ}{小时候|xiǎo shí hou}，{跟|gēn}{母亲|mǔ qīn}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{一起|yì qǐ}。{最|zuì}{早|zǎo}，{他们|tā men}{家|jiā}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{墓地|mù dì}{旁边|páng biān}。{孟子|Mèng zǐ}{常常|cháng cháng}{跟|gēn}{邻居|lín jū}{家|jiā}{的|de}{孩子|hái zi}{一起|yì qǐ}，{学|xué}{大人|dà ren}{在|zài}{墓地|mù dì}{里|lǐ}{做|zuò}{的|de}{事|shì}，{玩|wán}{埋人|mái rén}{的|de}{游戏|yóu xì}。{母亲|mǔ qīn}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{了|le}，{心|xīn}{想|xiǎng}：“{这个|zhè ge}{地方|dì fang}{不|bú}{适合|shì hé}{孩子|hái zi}{住|zhù}。”{于是|yú shì}，{她|tā}{带|dài}{着|zhe}{孟子|Mèng zǐ}{搬|bān}{了|le}{家|jiā}。
>
> {第|dì}{二|èr}{次|cì}，{他们|tā men}{搬|bān}{到|dào}{了|le}{市场|shì chǎng}{旁边|páng biān}。{市场|shì chǎng}{里|lǐ}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{热闹|rè nao}，{孟子|Mèng zǐ}{又|yòu}{学|xué}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{做买卖|zuò mǎi mai}{的|de}{人|rén}，{大声|dà shēng}{地|de}{叫卖|jiào mài}{东西|dōng xi}。{母亲|mǔ qīn}{想|xiǎng}：“{这里|zhè lǐ}{也|yě}{不|bú}{适合|shì hé}{孩子|hái zi}{住|zhù}。”{他们|tā men}{又|yòu}{搬家|bān jiā}{了|le}。
>
> {第|dì}{三|sān}{次|cì}，{他们|tā men}{搬|bān}{到|dào}{了|le}{学校|xué xiào}{旁边|páng biān}。{学校|xué xiào}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}{和|hé}{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{礼貌|lǐ mào}，{见面|jiàn miàn}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{互相|hù xiāng}{行礼|xíng lǐ}，{说话|shuō huà}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{客气|kè qi}。{孟子|Mèng zǐ}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{也|yě}{学|xué}{着|zhe}{他们|tā men}{的|de}{样子|yàng zi}，{玩|wán}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{祭祀|jì sì}{和|hé}{行礼|xíng lǐ}{的|de}{游戏|yóu xì}。{母亲|mǔ qīn}{高兴|gāo xìng}{地|de}{说|shuō}：“{这|zhè}{才|cái}{是|shì}{孩子|hái zi}{应该|yīng gāi}{住|zhù}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}！”{他们|tā men}{就|jiù}{在|zài}{那里|nà lǐ}{住|zhù}{了|le}{下来|xià lái}。
>
> {孟子|Mèng zǐ}{的|de}{母亲|mǔ qīn}{明白|míng bai}，{孩子|hái zi}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{学|xué}{身边|shēn biān}{的|de}{人|rén}{做|zuò}{的|de}{事|shì}。{所以|suǒ yǐ}{她|tā}{觉得|jué de}，{给|gěi}{孩子|hái zi}{找|zhǎo}{一|yí}{个|gè}{好|hǎo}{的|de}{环境|huán jìng}，{比|bǐ}{什么|shén me}{都|dōu}{重要|zhòng yào}。{后来|hòu lái}，{孟子|Mèng zǐ}{努力|nǔ lì}{学习|xué xí}，{成为|chéng wéi}{了|le}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{伟大|wěi dà}{的|de}{思想家|sī xiǎng jiā}。
>
> “{孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān}”{这个|zhè ge}{说法|shuō fǎ}，{一直|yì zhí}{流传|liú chuán}{到|dào}{今天|jīn tiān}。{人们|rén men}{用|yòng}{它|tā}{来|lái}{说明|shuō míng}，{生活|shēng huó}{的|de}{环境|huán jìng}{对|duì}{孩子|hái zi}{的|de}{影响|yǐng xiǎng}{很|hěn}{大|dà}；{也|yě}{用|yòng}{它|tā}{来|lái}{表扬|biǎo yáng}{那些|nà xiē}{为|wèi}{孩子|hái zi}{的|de}{教育|jiào yù}{付出|fù chū}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{的|de}{父母|fù mǔ}。{今天|jīn tiān}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{父母|fù mǔ}{为了|wèi le}{让|ràng}{孩子|hái zi}{上|shàng}{好|hǎo}{学校|xué xiào}，{愿意|yuàn yì}{搬|bān}{到|dào}{学校|xué xiào}{附近|fù jìn}{住|zhù}。{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{说|shuō}，{这|zhè}{就|jiù}{是|shì}{现代|xiàn dài}{的|de}“{孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān}”。

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {迁|qiān} | to move (house), written; in speech {搬家|bān jiā} |
| {墓地|mù dì} | a graveyard ({墓|mù}, a tomb) |
| {邻居|lín jū} | a neighbour (HSK 3) |
| {埋人|mái rén} | to bury someone ({埋|mái}, to bury) |
| {于是|yú shì} | so, thereupon (written, lesson 28) |
| {做买卖|zuò mǎi mai} | to trade, to do business ({买卖|mǎi mai}, buying and selling) |
| {叫卖|jiào mài} | to cry one's wares, call out what you're selling |
| {行礼|xíng lǐ} | to bow, to salute (a formal greeting) |
| {祭祀|jì sì} | a ceremony to honour ancestors or gods |
| {住|zhù}{了|le}{下来|xià lái} | to settle down there ({下来|xià lái}: staying for good) |
| {伟大|wěi dà} | great (of people and achievements) |
| {思想家|sī xiǎng jiā} | a thinker ({思想|sī xiǎng}, thought + {家|jiā}) |
| {流传|liú chuán} | to be handed down, to spread |
| {环境|huán jìng} | surroundings, environment |
| {付出|fù chū} | to give, to put in (effort, time, money) |
| {现代|xiàn dài} | modern (HSK 5) |

<details>
<summary>Our translation</summary>

"**Mencius's mother moves three times.** As a child, Mencius lived with his mother. At first their
home was beside a graveyard. Mencius often played with the neighbours' children, copying what the
grown-ups did in the graveyard and playing at burying people. When his mother saw this, she thought:
'This is no place for a child to live.' So she took Mencius and moved. The second time, they moved
next to a market. The market was busy every day, and now Mencius copied the traders, calling out his
wares at the top of his voice. His mother thought: 'This is no place for a child either.' They moved
again. The third time, they moved next to a school. The teachers and students there were very
courteous: they bowed to each other when they met and spoke politely. When Mencius saw this, he
copied them, playing at ceremonies and bows. His mother said happily: 'This is the place a child
should live!' And there they settled. Mencius's mother understood that children love to copy the people around
them, so she felt that finding good surroundings for her child mattered more than anything. Later Mencius studied hard and became a great thinker. The
phrase 'Mencius's mother moved three times' has come down to us today. People use it to say that the
place where children grow up has a great influence on them, and to praise parents who give a great
deal for their children's education. Today many parents are willing to move near a school so that
their child can go to a good one. Some people say this is the modern 'Mencius's mother moved three
times'."
</details>

## The grammar in the story

The retelling uses grammar you know from this course:

- {学|xué}{起|qǐ}{了|le}…, {玩|wán}{起|qǐ}{了|le}…: {起|qǐ} (+ {了|le}) after a verb marks the start of a new activity: "began copying, took to
  playing".
- {于是|yú shì} (so, then) joins a decision to its cause, in a narrative: {母亲|mǔ qīn}{看|kàn}{到|dào}{了|le}……{于是|yú shì}，{她|tā}{带|dài}{着|zhe}{孟子|Mèng zǐ}{搬|bān}{了|le}{家|jiā}。
- {成为|chéng wéi}{了|le}{一|yí}{位|wèi}{伟大|wěi dà}{的|de}{思想家|sī xiǎng jiā}: {成为|chéng wéi} (to become, lesson 05) with the formal measure word {位|wèi}.
- {用|yòng}{它|tā}{来|lái}{说明|shuō míng}…: {用|yòng} + something + {来|lái} + verb, "use it to…": the {来|lái} shows the purpose.
- {这|zhè}{才|cái}{是|shì}…: {才|cái}{是|shì} stresses "this, at last, is the right one".

## {孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān} today

{孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān} is a four-character set phrase like those of lesson 22, but one with a story behind it, a
{成语|chéng yǔ} (an idiom; HSK 5 teaches more). You use it in two ways:

- to say that surroundings matter for children: {孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān}{的|de}{故事|gù shi}{告诉|gào su}{我们|wǒ men}，{环境|huán jìng}{对|duì}{孩子|hái zi}{的|de}{成长|chéng zhǎng}{很|hěn}{重要|zhòng yào}。 ({成长|chéng zhǎng}: growing up)
- to describe parents who move, or go to great lengths, for their child's schooling:
  {为了|wèi le}{孩子|hái zi}{上学|shàng xué}，{他们|tā men}{家|jiā}{搬|bān}{了|le}{三|sān}{次|cì}，{真|zhēn}{是|shì}{孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān}{啊|a}。

Some people use it with a smile or a sigh, about the cost of homes near famous schools; others with
admiration. As with all set phrases, the tone comes from the situation.

## Key points

- {孟子|Mèng zǐ} (Mencius, about 372–289 BCE, traditional dates): a Confucian thinker, second only to Confucius in
  the tradition; {子|zǐ} is "Master".
- The story is in the 《{列女传|Liè nǚ zhuàn}》, a Han-dynasty collection traditionally attributed to {刘向|Liú Xiàng}; it's a story,
  not a record.
- Graveyard → market → school: each time the boy copied his surroundings, and his mother moved until
  he copied people worth copying.
- Today {孟母三迁|Mèng mǔ sān qiān} is a set phrase about how surroundings shape children, and about parents who move for
  their children's education.

lessons.title: Zhuangzi's butterfly: 庄周梦蝶
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Two thousand years ago a man dreamt he was a butterfly, woke up, and wasn't sure any more which of
the two he was. The passage that tells it is one of the most famous in Chinese, and only about sixty
characters long. This lesson gives the classical text with pinyin, explains its words, retells it in
modern Chinese and in English (our own translation), and sets out what readers have taken from it.
You don't need to learn the classical words; enjoy the sound, and notice how much of today's Chinese
is already in it ({梦|mèng}, {不知|bù zhī}, {必有|bì yǒu}).

## Zhuangzi and his book

{庄子|Zhuāng zǐ} (Zhuangzi, "Master Zhuang") is the name of a thinker, {庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu} (Zhuang Zhou), and of the book that carries
his name. He lived in the fourth century BCE (his dates are uncertain: sources give about 369–286 or
369–298 BCE). The book 《{庄子|Zhuāng zǐ}》 grew over time, and the first seven chapters (the "inner chapters") are generally
thought to be Zhuangzi's own; the rest has other hands in it. It's one of the founding texts of Daoism ({道家|Dào jiā}), full of stories,
jokes and strange characters, and it questions what we think we know.

The butterfly story ends the second chapter, 《{齐物论|Qí wù lùn}》 (*Qí wù lùn*, often translated "On the Equality of
Things" or "Discussion on Making All Things Equal").

## The passage

The text, checked character by character against two transcriptions (named in the course notes), with
its pinyin:

> {昔者|xī zhě}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}{梦为|mèng wéi}{胡蝶|hú dié}，{栩栩然|xǔ xǔ rán}{胡蝶|hú dié}{也|yě}，{自喻适志与|zì yù shì zhì yú}！{不知周也|bù zhī Zhōu yě}。
>
> {俄然觉|é rán jué}，{则蘧蘧然周也|zé qú qú rán Zhōu yě}。
>
> {不知周之梦为胡蝶与|bù zhī Zhōu zhī mèng wéi hú dié yú}，{胡蝶之梦为周与|hú dié zhī mèng wéi Zhōu yú}？
>
> {周与胡蝶|Zhōu yǔ hú dié}，{则必有分矣|zé bì yǒu fēn yǐ}。{此之谓物化|cǐ zhī wèi wù huà}。

### Words

| Classical | Here | Modern Chinese |
|---|---|---|
| {昔者|xī zhě} | once, long ago | {以前|yǐ qián} |
| {梦为|mèng wéi} | to dream of being ({为|wéi} wéi: to be, become; lesson 12's {为|wéi} wéi) | {梦见|mèng jiàn}{自己|zì jǐ}{变成|biàn chéng} |
| {胡蝶|hú dié} | a butterfly (today written {蝴蝶|hú dié}, with {虫|chóng} "insect" added) | {蝴蝶|hú dié} |
| {栩栩然|xǔ xǔ rán} | lively, fluttering ({然|rán}: -ly, "in such a way") | {快乐|kuài lè}{地|de}{飞来飞去|fēi lái fēi qù} |
| {也|yě} | (ends a statement: "it was…") | {是|shì} |
| {自喻适志|zì yù shì zhì} | delighted with itself, doing as it pleased ({喻|yù} here: pleased; {适志|shì zhì}: suited to its wishes) | {自己|zì jǐ}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{愉快|yú kuài}、{很|hěn}{自在|zì zai} |
| {与|yú} | (ends an exclamation or a question, read yú; also written {欤|yú}) | {啊|a}, {吗|ma} |
| {不知周也|bù zhī Zhōu yě} | it didn't know it was Zhou | {不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{自己|zì jǐ}{是|shì}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu} |
| {俄然|é rán} | suddenly | {忽然|hū rán} |
| {觉|jué} | to wake up (jué, as in {觉得|jué de}) | {醒|xǐng} |
| {则|zé} | then, and there | {就|jiù} |
| {蘧蘧然|qú qú rán} | solidly, unmistakably; or "with a start": readers differ | {明明白白|míng míng bái bái}{地|de}, {吃惊|chī jīng}{地|de} |
| {之|zhī} | (lesson 21's {之|zhī}: here between the subject and its verb, making "that Zhou dreamt…") | {的|de} |
| {必有分矣|bì yǒu fēn yǐ} | there must be a distinction ({分|fēn} fēn; {矣|yǐ}: a final particle) | {一定|yí dìng}{有|yǒu}{区别|qū bié} |
| {此之谓|cǐ zhī wèi} | this is what is called | {这|zhè}{就|jiù}{叫作|jiào zuò} |
| {物化|wù huà} | the transformation of things: one thing becoming another | {万物|wàn wù}{的|de}{变化|biàn huà} |

The same character {与|yǔ} appears in the passage with two readings: yú at the end of a clause (an
exclamation or a question, like {欤|yú} or {吗|ma}), and yǔ in {周与胡蝶|Zhōu yǔ hú dié} (Zhou and the butterfly), the "and" of lesson 24.
Some transcriptions write yǔ for both.

## In modern Chinese

{以前|yǐ qián}，{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}{做|zuò}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{梦|mèng}，{梦见|mèng jiàn}{自己|zì jǐ}{变成|biàn chéng}{了|le}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{蝴蝶|hú dié}，{一|yì}{只|zhī}{快乐|kuài lè}{地|de}{飞来飞去|fēi lái fēi qù}{的|de}{蝴蝶|hú dié}。{他|tā}{觉得|jué de}{非常|fēi cháng}{愉快|yú kuài}，{完全|wán quán}{忘|wàng}{了|le}{自己|zì jǐ}{是|shì}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}。{忽然|hū rán}，{他|tā}{醒|xǐng}{了|le}，{发现|fā xiàn}{自己|zì jǐ}{明明白白|míng míng bái bái}{还是|hái shi}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}。{这|zhè}{时候|shí hou}{他|tā}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}：{是|shì}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}{在|zài}{梦|mèng}{里|lǐ}{变成|biàn chéng}{了|le}{蝴蝶|hú dié}{呢|ne}，{还是|hái shi}{蝴蝶|hú dié}{在|zài}{梦|mèng}{里|lǐ}{变成|biàn chéng}{了|le}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}？{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}{和|hé}{蝴蝶|hú dié}，{一定|yí dìng}{是|shì}{有|yǒu}{区别|qū bié}{的|de}。{这|zhè}{就|jiù}{叫作|jiào zuò}“{物化|wù huà}”。

{蝴蝶|hú dié} (a butterfly), {明明白白|míng míng bái bái} (clearly, unmistakably), {自在|zì zai} (at ease), {万物|wàn wù} (all things).

## Our translation

> Once Zhuang Zhou dreamt he was a butterfly, a butterfly fluttering here and there, happy with itself
> and doing as it pleased. It didn't know it was Zhou. Suddenly he woke up, and there he was, solidly
> Zhou. He didn't know whether he was Zhou who had dreamt he was a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming
> it was Zhou. Between Zhou and a butterfly there must surely be a difference. This is what is called
> the transformation of things.

## What readers have taken from it

The passage is short, and readers have argued about it for two thousand years. Three readings come up
again and again; they are interpretations, and none is the only right one:

- **Doubt about what is real.** While dreaming, the dreamer is sure the dream is real. So how can
  anyone be sure, awake, that this isn't another dream? Read this way, the story questions how far we
  can trust our own experience.
- **Change without fixed borders.** The last words, {物化|wù huà}, point to change: things turn into one another,
  as a man becomes a butterfly in a dream. Read this way, the line "there must be a difference" isn't a
  conclusion but the start of a puzzle: the difference is real, yet Zhou and the butterfly pass into
  each other, and the borders we draw between things are less fixed than they seem. This fits the
  chapter's title, *making all things equal*.
- **Freedom and ease.** The butterfly is happy and does as it pleases because it isn't worrying about
  who it is. Some readers see in it Zhuangzi's ideal of living freely and lightly, without clinging to
  a fixed idea of oneself.

As a set phrase, {庄周梦蝶|Zhuāng Zhōu mèng dié} (or {庄生梦蝶|Zhuāng shēng mèng dié}) is used for the feeling that life is like a dream, or that we can't be
sure what is real: {有时候|yǒu shí hou}{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{自己|zì jǐ}{像|xiàng}{庄周梦蝶|Zhuāng Zhōu mèng dié}，{分不清|fēn bu qīng}{是|shì}{梦|mèng}{还是|hái shi}{真|zhēn}{的|de}。 (Sometimes I feel like Zhuangzi and his
butterfly: I can't tell whether it's a dream or real. {分不清|fēn bu qīng}: can't tell apart.)

## Key points

- {庄子|Zhuāng zǐ} (Zhuang Zhou, 4th century BCE, dates uncertain): a Daoist thinker; the book 《{庄子|Zhuāng zǐ}》 is named after
  him. The butterfly passage ends its second chapter, 《{齐物论|Qí wù lùn}》.
- The passage: {昔者|xī zhě}{庄周|Zhuāng Zhōu}{梦为|mèng wéi}{胡蝶|hú dié}……{此之谓物化|cǐ zhī wèi wù huà}。 {胡蝶|hú dié} is the old spelling of {蝴蝶|hú dié}; {觉|jué} jué is "to
  wake"; {与|yú} is yú at the end of a clause and yǔ ("and") in {周与胡蝶|Zhōu yǔ hú dié}.
- Modern words already in it: {梦|mèng}, {不知|bù zhī}, {必有|bì yǒu} ({一定|yí dìng}{有|yǒu}), {之|zhī} ({的|de}), {此|cǐ} ({这|zhè}, lesson 01).
- Readings: doubt about what is real; the transformation of things ({物化|wù huà}); freedom and ease. All are
  interpretations.
- {庄周梦蝶|Zhuāng Zhōu mèng dié} today: life feels like a dream; you can't tell dream from reality.

lessons.title: Climate and the earth: 即使…也, 稍微, 低于
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Module 6 turns from people to the world around them: the weather and the climate in this lesson,
animals, plants and science in lesson 27, the environment in lesson 28 and the arts in lesson 29,
before the exam lessons. You already talk about today's weather with HSK 2 and HSK 3 words ({晴|qíng}, {阴|yīn},
{下雨|xià yǔ}, {刮风|guā fēng}, {冷|lěng}, {热|rè}, {凉快|liáng kuai}). Now you'll describe a climate, read a temperature in a forecast, and
say what stays true whatever the weather does. This lesson teaches:

- {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}…: even if…, still…; and its spoken twin {就是|jiù shì}…{也|yě}…;
- {稍微|shāo wēi} / {稍|shāo}: slightly, a little ({稍微|shāo wēi}{暖和|nuǎn huo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}, {请|qǐng}{稍|shāo}{等|děng});
- {低于|dī yú} / {高于|gāo yú}: lower than / higher than, the written way to compare numbers;
- temperatures: {摄氏度|shè shì dù}, {零下|líng xià}, {气温|qì wēn}, {温度|wēn dù}, {高温|gāo wēn}, {低温|dī wēn}, {降温|jiàng wēn};
- the climate and the earth: {气候|qì hòu}, {寒冷|hán lěng}, {暖和|nuǎn huo}, {很|hěn}{干|gān} (dry), {阳光|yáng guāng}, {云|yún}, {地球|dì qiú}, {海洋|hǎi yáng}, {大自然|dà zì rán};
- parts of a country: {东部|dōng bù}, {西部|xī bù}, {南部|nán bù}, {北部|běi bù}; {农村|nóng cūn} and {村|cūn}.

At the end you can compare the climate of two places, follow a written weather report and give
advice that holds "even if".

## {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}…: even if

{即使|jí shǐ} starts a clause that imagines a situation, often an extreme one; {也|yě} in the second clause says
the result holds all the same. English says "even if" or "even though (it may)":

{即使|jí shǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{要|yào}{去|qù}。 — Even if it rains tomorrow, we're still going.

{即使|jí shǐ}{气温|qì wēn}{降|jiàng}{到|dào}{零下|líng xià}{十|shí}{度|dù}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{去|qù}{跑步|pǎo bù}。 — Even if the temperature drops to minus ten, he
still goes running every morning.

{即使|jí shǐ}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{同意|tóng yì}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{想|xiǎng}{试一试|shì yi shì}。 — Even if you don't agree, I want to give it a try.

{即使|jí shǐ}{是|shì}{夏天|xià tiān}，{山|shān}{上|shàng}{的|de}{晚上|wǎn shang}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。 — Even in summer, nights in the mountains are cold.

The last example puts a noun after {即使|jí shǐ}{是|shì}: "even (when it's) summer". {也|yě} is an adverb, so it goes
after the subject of the second clause and before its verb or adjective, as in every pair you know
(lesson 25's {不管|bù guǎn}…{都|dōu} works the same way). {即使|jí shǐ} can come first or after the subject:

{他|tā}{即使|jí shǐ}{很|hěn}{累|lèi}，{也|yě}{会|huì}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{做|zuò}{完|wán}。 — Even when he's very tired, he finishes his homework.

The result is often negative: {即使|jí shǐ}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{不|bù}{买|mǎi}。 (Even if it's cheap, I'm not buying it.)

### {即使|jí shǐ} or {虽然|suī rán}?

Both pairs are translated "although / even though", but they don't do the same job. {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì}
(HSK 3) talks about a *fact*; {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} about a *supposition*, something that may or may not be
true, or that you push to the limit to make a point. This is a **[[hypothetical concession]]**: you
grant a possibility and say it changes nothing.

| Pair | The first clause is… | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì} | a fact | {虽然|suī rán}{今天|jīn tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{但是|dàn shì}{我们|wǒ men}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{了|le}。 It was raining today, but we still went. |
| {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} | a supposition | {即使|jí shǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{去|qù}。 Even if it rains tomorrow, we'll go. |
| {如果|rú guǒ}…{就|jiù} | a supposition with a result | {如果|rú guǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。 If it rains tomorrow, we won't go. |
| {不管|bù guǎn}…{都|dōu} | any case at all | {不管|bù guǎn}{下|xià}{不|bu}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{去|qù}。 Rain or no rain, we're going. |

So "even if it rains tomorrow" can't take {虽然|suī rán}: tomorrow's rain isn't a fact yet. And {即使|jí shǐ} never
pairs with {就|jiù}: the whole point is that the result doesn't depend on the condition.

## {就是|jiù shì}…{也|yě}…: the spoken "even if"

In everyday speech, {就是|jiù shì} often does the work of {即使|jí shǐ}. The pattern and the {也|yě} are the same:

{就是|jiù shì}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{去|qù}。 — Even if it rains, I'm going.

{就是|jiù shì}{再|zài}{忙|máng}，{你|nǐ}{也|yě}{得|děi}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{啊|a}！ — However busy you are, you've still got to eat!

{就是|jiù shì} with {再|zài} + adjective ("even if it's more… still") is especially common. {即使|jí shǐ} sounds more careful
and is the one for writing; {就是|jiù shì} belongs to conversation.

{就是|jiù shì} has other jobs you know, so look at what follows it. Before a clause with {也|yě} later, it's
"even if". Before a noun it's "is exactly, is precisely": {这|zhè}{就是|jiù shì}{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}{的|de}{那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū}。 (This is exactly the
book I meant.) And in conversation, after a good point, {就是|jiù shì} + a clause adds a small drawback: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}
{外套|wài tào}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}，{就是|jiù shì}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{贵|guì}。 (This coat looks good; it's just a bit expensive.) Lesson 25's {就是说|jiù shì shuō}
("that is to say") is a fourth.

## {稍微|shāo wēi} and {稍|shāo}: slightly

{稍微|shāo wēi} makes a change or a difference small. On its own it sounds unfinished, so it almost always
has a small amount word after the adjective or verb:

- {稍微|shāo wēi} + adjective + {一点儿|yì diǎnr} / {一些|yì xiē}: {今天|jīn tiān}{稍微|shāo wēi}{暖和|nuǎn huo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 (It's slightly warmer today.)
- {稍微|shāo wēi} + verb + {一下|yí xià} / {一点儿|yì diǎnr}: {请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}{稍微|shāo wēi}{等|děng}{一下|yí xià}。 (Please wait a moment.) {菜|cài}{里|lǐ}{稍微|shāo wēi}{放|fàng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{盐|yán}。 (Put a
  little salt in the dish.)
- {稍微|shāo wēi} + {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} + adjective, for something slightly unwelcome: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{毛衣|máo yī}{稍微|shāo wēi}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{大|dà}。 (This sweater
  is a tiny bit big.)

In a comparison with {比|bǐ}, {稍微|shāo wēi} goes before the adjective: {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{稍微|shāo wēi}{冷|lěng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。 (Today is a little
colder than yesterday.)

{稍|shāo} is the one-syllable, written form. You'll meet it in notices, forecasts and polite set phrases:
{请|qǐng}{稍|shāo}{等|děng} (one moment, please: on the phone or at a counter), {气温|qì wēn}{稍|shāo}{有|yǒu}{下降|xià jiàng} (temperatures fall slightly,
in a forecast). In your own speech, say {稍微|shāo wēi}.

| | Use it for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {稍微|shāo wēi}…{一点儿|yì diǎnr} | a small difference (neutral) | {稍微|shāo wēi}{快|kuài}{一点儿|yì diǎnr} a little faster |
| {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} + adjective | something a bit too much, unwelcome | {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng} a bit cold |
| adjective + {一点儿|yì diǎnr} | comparing, or asking for a change | {快|kuài}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}！ Faster! |

## {低于|dī yú} and {高于|gāo yú}: the written comparison

{于|yú} is a small written word you've met inside {由于|yóu yú} (lesson 17), {对于|duì yú} (lesson 24) and {便于|biàn yú} (lesson 13).
After an adjective it means "than": A {低于|dī yú} B is A {比|bǐ} B {低|dī}, A {高于|gāo yú} B is A {比|bǐ} B {高|gāo}. They belong to
forecasts, reports and notices, where numbers are compared:

{今天|jīn tiān}{夜里|yè lǐ}{的|de}{最|zuì}{低|dī}{气温|qì wēn}{将|jiāng}{低于|dī yú}{零|líng}{度|dù}。 — Tonight's lowest temperature will be below zero.

{今年|jīn nián}{夏天|xià tiān}{的|de}{气温|qì wēn}{高于|gāo yú}{往年|wǎng nián}。 — The temperatures this summer have been higher than in other years.
（{往年|wǎng nián}: in former years, written.）

In conversation you'd say {今天|jīn tiān}{夜里|yè lǐ}{比|bǐ}{零|líng}{度|dù}{还|hái}{冷|lěng} or {今天|jīn tiān}{夜里|yè lǐ}{会|huì}{到|dào}{零下|líng xià}. The negative {不|bù}{低于|dī yú} means "no
lower than", that is, "at least": {室内|shì nèi}{温度|wēn dù}{不|bù}{低于|dī yú}{十八|shí bā}{摄氏度|shè shì dù} (the indoor temperature is at least 18 °C;
{室内|shì nèi}: indoors, written).

## Temperatures: {摄氏度|shè shì dù}, {零下|líng xià} and three kinds of {温|wēn}

China, like most of the world, gives temperatures in degrees Celsius. In writing, 25℃ is read
{二十五|èr shí wǔ}{摄氏度|shè shì dù}; in speech people just say {二十五|èr shí wǔ}{度|dù}. Below zero is {零下|líng xià}:

{北京|Běi jīng}{冬天|dōng tiān}{最|zuì}{冷|lěng}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{气温|qì wēn}{会|huì}{降|jiàng}{到|dào}{零下|líng xià}{十|shí}{几|jǐ}{度|dù}。 — At its coldest, Beijing's winter temperature drops to
minus ten-something.

{明天|míng tiān}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}{气温|qì wēn}{十二|shí'èr}{度|dù}，{最|zuì}{低|dī}{气温|qì wēn}{零下|líng xià}{三|sān}{度|dù}。 — Tomorrow's high is 12 degrees, the low minus 3.

There are three {温|wēn} words to keep apart:

| Word | What it measures | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {气温|qì wēn} | the temperature of the air outside | {今天|jīn tiān}{气温|qì wēn}{很|hěn}{低|dī}。 |
| {温度|wēn dù} | the temperature of anything (a room, water, the air) | {这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{的|de}{温度|wēn dù}{太|tài}{高|gāo}{了|le}。 |
| {体温|tǐ wēn} | body temperature (lesson 06) | {护士|hù shi}{给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{量|liáng}{了|le}{体温|tǐ wēn}。 |

{高温|gāo wēn} and {低温|dī wēn} are "high / low temperatures" as nouns, in forecasts and on labels: {高温|gāo wēn}{天气|tiān qì} (a heat
wave), {三十五|sān shí wǔ}{度|dù}{以上|yǐ shàng}{的|de}{高温|gāo wēn} (heat over 35 degrees). {降温|jiàng wēn} is "to cool down", of the weather or
of a person in the heat: {明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{降温|jiàng wēn}{了|le} (it's going to turn colder tomorrow). {降|jiàng} jiàng on its own is
"to fall, to come down", in writing: {气温|qì wēn}{降|jiàng}{到|dào}{零|líng}{度|dù} (the temperature falls to zero); you know it from
{降价|jiàng jià} (lesson 09) and {下降|xià jiàng} (lesson 15).

## Describing a climate

{气候|qì hòu} is the climate, the weather a place has year after year; {天气|tiān qì} is the weather of one day.

- {寒冷|hán lěng} (cold, frigid) is the written word for a hard cold: {寒冷|hán lěng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}. In speech, {冷|lěng} or {很|hěn}{冷|lěng}.
- {暖和|nuǎn huo} nuǎn huo, the neutral second syllable, is pleasantly warm, the opposite of {凉快|liáng kuai} (pleasantly
  cool): {屋|wū}{里|lǐ}{很|hěn}{暖和|nuǎn huo} (it's nice and warm indoors).
- {北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{干|gān} (Beijing winters are very dry): {={干|gān}=}, first tone, is "dry", a different
  word from HSK 3's {干|gàn} (to do): same character, different tone. Traditional characters write
  them apart, {={乾|gān}=} for "dry" and {={幹|gàn}=} for "to do".
- {阳光|yáng guāng} is sunshine, {光|guāng} light in general: {灯光|dēng guāng} (lamplight), {月光|yuè guāng} (moonlight). {光|guāng} also has an adverb
  use, "only, just" ({光说不做|guāng shuō bú zuò} all talk and no action): the {光|guāng} of lesson 04's {不光|bù guāng}.
- {云|yún} is a cloud. {天|tiān}{上|shàng}{一|yí}{片|piàn}{云|yún}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu} (there isn't a cloud in the sky) uses {片|piàn}, lesson 27's measure
  word for something flat and spread out.
- Verbs of weather and nature: {风|fēng}{吹|chuī} (the wind blows), {吹|chuī} also "to blow" with your mouth
  ({吹一吹|chuī yi chuī}: blow on it, as on hot soup); {落|luò} luò (to fall, to set: {太阳|tài yang}{落|luò}{山|shān}{了|le}, the sun has gone down; {叶子|yè zi}{落|luò}{了|le}, the leaves have
  fallen); {流|liú} (to flow: {河|hé}{水|shuǐ}{向|xiàng}{东|dōng}{流|liú}, the river flows east).
- {深|shēn} is deep ({深水|shēn shuǐ}, deep water) and dark for a colour ({深|shēn}{蓝色|lán sè}, dark blue); {厚|hòu} is thick ({厚|hòu}{衣服|yī fu}, warm
  clothes; {厚厚|hòu hòu}{的|de}{雪|xuě}, deep snow: the doubled adjective is lively).

## The earth and its regions

{地球|dì qiú} is the earth as a planet, {大自然|dà zì rán} nature (the great outdoors and the natural world), {海洋|hǎi yáng} the
oceans (written; {海|hǎi} is the everyday "sea"), {星星|xīng xing} xīng xing the stars you see at night. {火|huǒ} is fire,
the {火|huǒ} of {火车|huǒ chē} (HSK 1).

For a part of a country or a region, add {部|bù} (part) to a direction: {东部|dōng bù}, {西部|xī bù}, {南部|nán bù}, {北部|běi bù}. Compare
them with HSK 3's {北方|běi fāng} and {南方|nán fāng}:

- {北方|běi fāng} / {南方|nán fāng}: the North / the South of China, as broad areas with their own food and ways
  ({北方|běi fāng}{人|rén}{爱|ài}{吃|chī}{面条|miàn tiáo}).
- {北部|běi bù} / {南部|nán bù} etc.: the northern / southern part of any named area: {中国|Zhōng guó}{西部|xī bù} (western China), {英国|Yīng guó}{北部|běi bù}
  (the north of Britain; {英国|Yīng guó}: Britain), {城市|chéng shì}{的|de}{东部|dōng bù} (the east of the city).

this week. Please take note. Monday and Tuesday: sunny, not much wind. Daytime highs around 12 °C,
slightly lower than last week; night-time lows of 2 °C. Lots of sunshine: a good time to go out for
a walk. Clouds will build up on Tuesday evening. Wednesday: overcast, with strong winds in the
afternoon. As the cold air arrives, temperatures will fall by eight to ten degrees, and the
night-time low will be below zero. In the strong wind please take care, and it's best not to park
under big trees.
Thursday to Sunday: sunny but cold, with daytime highs of only two or three degrees and night-time
lows of around minus seven. Also, there will be little rain or snow this week and the air will be
rather dry, so drink plenty of water and take care with fire. From next Monday the cold air will
slowly move away and temperatures will be slightly higher, but daytime highs will still be below
ten degrees. A reminder: when it turns cold, put on more clothes in good
time, and older people and children had better go out as little as possible in the mornings and
evenings. Drivers, please take care: even if it's sunny in the daytime, bridges and roads may freeze
at night, so be sure to drive slowly."

1. {即使|jí shǐ}{气温|qì wēn}{降|jiàng}{到|dào}{零下|líng xià}{十五|shí wǔ}{度|dù}，{他|tā}{也|yě}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{去|qù}{公园|gōng yuán}{跑步|pǎo bù}。 — Even when the temperature drops to minus
   fifteen, he goes running in the park every morning.
2. {农村|nóng cūn}{的|de}{晚上|wǎn shang}{没有|méi yǒu}{什么|shén me}{灯光|dēng guāng}，{孩子|hái zi}{们|men}{能|néng}{看见|kàn jiàn}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{星星|xīng xing}。 — There's little light at night in the
   countryside, so the children can see lots of stars.
3. {天气|tiān qì}{降温|jiàng wēn}{了|le}，{她|tā}{把|bǎ}{厚|hòu}{衣服|yī fu}{拿|ná}{出来|chū lái}{了|le}。 — It's turned colder, so she's taken out her warm clothes.
</details>

Then answer aloud, in three or four sentences: {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{什么样|shén me yàng}{的|de}{气候|qì hòu}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？ (What kind of climate
do you like, and why?)

<details>
<summary>A model answer</summary>

{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{四季|sì jì}{都|dōu}{有|yǒu}{的|de}{气候|qì hòu}。{春天|chūn tiān}{暖和|nuǎn huo}，{秋天|qiū tiān}{凉快|liáng kuai}，{冬天|dōng tiān}{虽然|suī rán}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{但是|dàn shì}{能|néng}{看见|kàn jiàn}{雪|xuě}。{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{太|tài}{热|rè}{的|de}{地方|dì fang}，
{因为|yīn wèi}{夏天|xià tiān}{三十五|sān shí wǔ}{度|dù}{以上|yǐ shàng}{的|de}{高温|gāo wēn}{让|ràng}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{难受|nán shòu}。 — I like a climate with all four seasons. Spring is warm
and autumn is cool, and in winter, though it's very cold, you get to see snow. I don't much like
very hot places, because heat over thirty-five degrees in summer makes me feel awful. ({四季|sì jì}: the
four seasons.)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Weather and climate
{即使|jí shǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{要|yào}{去|qù}。
= Even if it rains tomorrow, we're still going.
{就是|jiù shì}{再|zài}{忙|máng}，{你|nǐ}{也|yě}{得|děi}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{啊|a}！
= However busy you are, you've still got to eat!
{今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{稍微|shāo wēi}{暖和|nuǎn huo}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。
= Today is a little warmer than yesterday.
{请|qǐng}{稍|shāo}{等|děng}。
= One moment, please.
{明天|míng tiān}{最|zuì}{高|gāo}{气温|qì wēn}{十二|shí'èr}{度|dù}，{最|zuì}{低|dī}{气温|qì wēn}{零下|líng xià}{三|sān}{度|dù}。
= Tomorrow's high is twelve degrees, and the low minus three.
{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{冬天|dōng tiān}{又|yòu}{冷|lěng}{又|yòu}{干|gān}。
= Beijing's winters are cold and dry.
```

## Pronunciation

- {即使|jí shǐ} jí shǐ: a rising tone, then a dipping one. Don't read {即|jí} as jì, the sound of {既|jì} ({既然|jì rán}).
- {稍微|shāo wēi} shāo wēi: two first tones. {微|wēi} is wēi in the mainland standard (you may hear wéi from
  speakers in Taiwan).
- {暖和|nuǎn huo} nuǎn huo: the second syllable is neutral, and {和|hé} is huo here, not hé. Keep the *u* of nuǎn.
- {摄氏度|shè shì dù} shè shì dù: three falling tones; shè and shì share the *sh*.
- {={干|gān}=} (dry) is first tone, {干|gàn} (to do) fourth: {天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{干|gān}，{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{干|gàn}{什么|shén me}？
- {云|yún} yún and {运|yùn} yùn ({运动|yùn dòng}) differ only in tone.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{即使|jí shǐ}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{去|qù}~~: {即使|jí shǐ} pairs with {也|yě}, not {就|jiù}: {即使|jí shǐ}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{去|qù}。 ({就|jiù} goes with {如果|rú guǒ}, {只要|zhǐ yào}, {既然|jì rán}.)
- ~~{虽然|suī rán}{明天|míng tiān}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{去|qù}~~: tomorrow's rain is a supposition, not a fact, so it takes {即使|jí shǐ}: {即使|jí shǐ}{明天|míng tiān}
  {下雨|xià yǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{去|qù}。 {虽然|suī rán} is for what is already true.
- {稍微|shāo wēi} with a bare adjective ({今天|jīn tiān}{稍微|shāo wēi}{冷|lěng}) sounds unfinished: add {一点儿|yì diǎnr} or {一些|yì xiē}, {今天|jīn tiān}{稍微|shāo wēi}{冷|lěng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。
- ~~{今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}~~: in a {比|bǐ} sentence, no {很|hěn} (HSK 3); use {稍微|shāo wēi}…{一点儿|yì diǎnr} or {一点儿|yì diǎnr} for a small difference:
  {今天|jīn tiān}{比|bǐ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{稍微|shāo wēi}{冷|lěng}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。
- {低于|dī yú} and {高于|gāo yú} in a chat sound like reading the news aloud: they're fine in a report, but with a
  friend say {比|bǐ}…{低|dī} / {比|bǐ}…{高|gāo}.
- {气候|qì hòu} is the climate, not today's weather: {今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, not {今天|jīn tiān}{气候|qì hòu}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (said of a single day it
  sounds odd).

## Key points

- {即使|jí shǐ} + supposition, (subject) {也|yě} + result: even if. Spoken: {就是|jiù shì}…{也|yě} ({就是|jiù shì}{再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}…). For a fact use
  {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì}.
- {稍微|shāo wēi} + adjective + {一点儿|yì diǎnr} / {一些|yì xiē}, {稍微|shāo wēi} + verb + {一下|yí xià}; written {稍|shāo} ({请|qǐng}{稍|shāo}{等|děng}, {稍|shāo}{低|dī}).
- A {低于|dī yú} / {高于|gāo yú} B: written "lower / higher than"; {不|bù}{低于|dī yú}: at least.
- {气温|qì wēn} (air), {温度|wēn dù} (anything), {体温|tǐ wēn} (the body); {摄氏度|shè shì dù}, {零下|líng xià}, {高温|gāo wēn}, {低温|dī wēn}, {降温|jiàng wēn}.
- {气候|qì hòu} (climate) vs {天气|tiān qì} (weather); {很|hěn}{干|gān} (dry), {寒冷|hán lěng}, {暖和|nuǎn huo}, {阳光|yáng guāng}, {云|yún}.
- {北方|běi fāng} / {南方|nán fāng} (the North, the South) vs {东部|dōng bù} / {西部|xī bù} / {南部|nán bù} / {北部|běi bù} (part of a named area); {农村|nóng cūn}, {村|cūn}.
- New characters: {吹|chuī} {村|cūn} {洋|yáng} {厚|hòu} {即|jí} {农|nóng} {暖|nuǎn} {深|shēn} {稍|shāo} {微|wēi} {摄|shè} {氏|shì} {云|yún} (✎ {吹|chuī} {村|cūn} {农|nóng} {深|shēn} {云|yún}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Animals, plants and science: 棵, 幅, 片, 有着, 用来
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 26 described the weather and the earth. This lesson looks at what lives on it, plants and
animals, and at the language of science, the words you need for the expository texts of the exam:
an article that explains what something is, how it works and why it matters. It teaches:

- three measure words of nature and pictures: {棵|kē} ({一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù}), {幅|fú} ({一|yì}{幅|fú}{画|huà}), {片|piàn} ({一|yí}{片|piàn}{叶子|yè zi}, {一|yí}{片|piàn}{蓝天|lán tiān});
- {有着|yǒu zhe}, the written "have" of descriptions ({有着|yǒu zhe}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ});
- {用来|yòng lái} and {用于|yòng yú}: "is used to / for" ({叶子|yè zi}{可以|kě yǐ}{用来|yòng lái}{做|zuò}{茶|chá});
- {分为|fēn wéi}: "is divided into" ({植物|zhí wù}{分为|fēn wéi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng});
- {种|zhòng} zhòng (to plant) beside {种|zhǒng} zhǒng (kind), and {活|huó}, {死|sǐ}, {生命|shēng mìng};
- science words: {科学|kē xué}, {科技|kē jì}, {技术|jì shù}, {研究|yán jiū}, {过程|guò chéng}, {作用|zuò yòng}, {产生|chǎn shēng}, {引起|yǐn qǐ}, {不断|bú duàn}, {大量|dà liàng}, {大大|dà dà}, {多样|duō yàng}, {部分|bù fen}.

At the end you can read a short article about an animal, say what something is used for, and
describe how a plant grows.

## Measure words: {棵|kē}, {幅|fú}, {片|piàn}

You know the general {个|gè} and the measure words for animals ({只|zhī}, {条|tiáo}, {头|tóu}) from HSK 1–3. Three more belong
to nature and art:

| Measure word | For | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| {棵|kē} kē | trees and other plants | {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù}, {两|liǎng}{棵|kē}{花|huā}, {院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}{棵|kē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{树|shù} |
| {幅|fú} fú | pictures, paintings, maps | {一|yì}{幅|fú}{画|huà}, {墙|qiáng}{上|shàng}{挂|guà}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{幅|fú}{地图|dì tú} |
| {片|piàn} piàn | thin flat pieces; a stretch of land, water or sky | {一|yí}{片|piàn}{叶子|yè zi}, {两|liǎng}{片|piàn}{面包|miàn bāo}, {一|yí}{片|piàn}{草地|cǎo dì}, {一|yí}{片|piàn}{蓝天|lán tiān} |

- {棵|kē} is the measure word for anything that grows from the ground with a stem: trees, flowers,
  vegetables in the field ({一|yì}{棵|kē}{白菜|bái cài}, a cabbage). Its radical is {木|mù}, the tree.
- {幅|fú} is for something you look at on a surface: a painting, a drawing, a map. In conversation
  many people say {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{画|huà} too, as for a photo ({一|yì}{张|zhāng}{照片|zhào piàn}); {幅|fú} is the standard word for a painting, and the
  one you'd read in an exhibition or a book.
- {片|piàn} has two jobs. For a thin flat piece: {一|yí}{片|piàn}{叶子|yè zi} (a leaf), {一|yí}{片|piàn}{面包|miàn bāo} (a slice of bread), {吃|chī}{两|liǎng}{片|piàn}{药|yào}
  (take two tablets). For a wide stretch, seen as one surface: {一|yí}{片|piàn}{草地|cǎo dì} (a stretch of grass), {一|yí}{片|piàn}{蓝天|lán tiān}
  (a stretch of blue sky), {天|tiān}{上|shàng}{一|yí}{片|piàn}{云|yún}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu} (lesson 26). The second use often goes with {大|dà}:
  {一|yí}{大|dà}{片|piàn}{树林|shù lín} (a big stretch of woods; {树林|shù lín}: woods, lesson 28).

{片|piàn} is in {照片|zhào piàn} and {图片|tú piàn} (lesson 24) as well: a picture is a flat piece.

## {有着|yǒu zhe}: the written "have"

{有着|yǒu zhe} is {有|yǒu} with the {着|zhe} of a lasting state. You'll find it in descriptions and expository writing,
before an *abstract object with a modifier*: a long history, an important role, a close link,
special features:

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{植物|zhí wù}{有着|yǒu zhe}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ}。 — This plant has a long history.

{老虎|lǎo hǔ}{有着|yǒu zhe}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{力气|lì qi}。 — Tigers are very strong. (literally "have great strength")

{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{有着|yǒu zhe}{密切|mì qiè}{的|de}{关系|guān xi}。 — These two things are closely related. ({密切|mì qiè}: close, written)

In everyday speech, plain {有|yǒu} does the same job: {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{植物|zhí wù}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ}. {有着|yǒu zhe} never takes {了|le} or {过|guo}, has
no negative (for "doesn't have", say {没有|méi yǒu}), and isn't used for ordinary things you own: ~~{我|wǒ}{有着|yǒu zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}
{哥哥|gē ge}~~ is wrong; say {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}. Think of {有着|yǒu zhe} as "is marked by", "possesses (a quality)".

## {用来|yòng lái} and {用于|yòng yú}: what something is used for

{用来|yòng lái} + verb says what a thing is used to do. It's common in speech and writing:

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{叶子|yè zi}{可以|kě yǐ}{用来|yòng lái}{做|zuò}{茶|chá}。 — These leaves can be used to make tea.

{这|zhè}{把|bǎ}{刀|dāo}{是|shì}{用来|yòng lái}{切|qiē}{菜|cài}{的|de}。 — This knife is for cutting vegetables. ({切|qiē}: to cut, HSK 5)

The pattern {是|shì}{用来|yòng lái}…{的|de} is the usual way to explain what a thing is for. The fuller form is {用|yòng} X {来|lái} + verb,
"use X to…": {我们|wǒ men}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}{来|lái}{拍照|pāi zhào} (we use our phones to take pictures).

{用于|yòng yú} + noun (or verb phrase) is the written form, "is used in / for", the language of labels,
manuals and articles:

{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{技术|jì shù}{已经|yǐ jīng}{用于|yòng yú}{生活|shēng huó}{中|zhōng}{的|de}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{方面|fāng miàn}。 — This technology is already used in many areas of daily
life.

{这|zhè}{笔|bǐ}{钱|qián}{将|jiāng}{用于|yòng yú}{保护|bǎo hù}{动物|dòng wù}。 — The money will be used to protect animals. ({保护|bǎo hù}: to protect, lesson 28;
{笔|bǐ}: measure word for sums of money)

| | Followed by | Register | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {用来|yòng lái} | a verb | speech and writing | {用来|yòng lái}{做|zuò}{茶|chá} |
| {用于|yòng yú} | a noun or verb phrase | written | {用于|yòng yú}{研究|yán jiū} |

## {分为|fēn wéi}: is divided into

A {分为|fēn wéi} B ({和|hé} C) says what parts something is divided into: {一|yì}{年|nián}{分为|fēn wéi}{四|sì}{个|gè}{季节|jì jié} (the year is divided into
four seasons). {为|wéi} here is wéi, the {为|wéi} of {成为|chéng wéi} and {作为|zuò wéi} (lesson 12), and the phrase is written; in speech
people say {分成|fēn chéng}:

{植物|zhí wù}{可以|kě yǐ}{分为|fēn wéi}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng}。 — Plants can be divided into many kinds.

{这|zhè}{次|cì}{比赛|bǐ sài}{分为|fēn wéi}{两|liǎng}{部分|bù fen}：{笔试|bǐ shì}{和|hé}{口试|kǒu shì}。 — This contest has two parts: a written test and an oral one.
({口试|kǒu shì}: an oral exam.)

Two more words for parts: {部分|bù fen} bù fen (a part, a section; the second syllable is neutral) and its
compounds {大部分|dà bù fen} (most) and {一部分|yí bù fen} (some, a part): {大部分|dà bù fen}{学生|xué sheng}{都|dōu}{同意|tóng yì} (most of the students agree).

## Plants: {种|zhòng} zhòng, {土|tǔ}, {叶子|yè zi}

The same character {种|zhǒng} is two words:

- {种|zhǒng} zhǒng (third tone, HSK 3): a kind, a sort: {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{树|shù}, {很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng}{花|huā};
- {种|zhòng} zhòng (fourth tone, this lesson): to plant, to grow: {种|zhòng}{树|shù} (to plant trees), {种|zhòng}{菜|cài} (to grow
  vegetables).

{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{在|zài}{院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{种|zhòng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng}{花|huā}。 — My grandpa has planted lots of kinds of flowers in the yard. (zhòng
… zhǒng)

Read the word around it: before a noun with a number or {这|zhè} / {那|nà}, it's the measure word zhǒng ({这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}, {三|sān}{种|zhǒng});
as a verb with an object to plant, it's zhòng. {土|tǔ} is soil, earth ({土|tǔ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, the soil is good); {叶子|yè zi} yè zi is a
leaf ({树叶|shù yè}: leaves of a tree).

## Life: {生命|shēng mìng}, {活|huó} and {死|sǐ}

- {生命|shēng mìng} is life in the biological sense, what living things have: {每|měi}{个|gè}{生命|shēng mìng}{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{重要|zhòng yào} (every life matters).
  Daily life, the way you live, is HSK 3's {生活|shēng huó}.
- {活|huó} is "to live, to be alive": {这|zhè}{棵|kē}{树|shù}{已经|yǐ jīng}{活|huó}{了|le}{三百|sān bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{了|le} (this tree has lived for over three hundred
  years); {活|huó}{着|zhe} (alive). As an adjective it's "living, lively": {活|huó}{的|de}{鱼|yú} (a live fish). You know it from
  {生活|shēng huó} and {活动|huó dòng}.
- {死|sǐ} is "to die" and "dead": {那|nà}{棵|kē}{树|shù}{死|sǐ}{了|le} (that tree has died). Lesson 06's {累|lèi}{死|sǐ}{了|le}, {疼|téng}{死|sǐ}{了|le} use it as a
  degree complement, "to death": an exaggeration, not a death.
- {少见|shǎo jiàn} is "rare, seldom seen": {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{鸟|niǎo}{很|hěn}{少见|shǎo jiàn}; {全球|quán qiú} "the whole world, global": {全球|quán qiú}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng}{熊|xióng} (there are
  many kinds of bear in the world); {自然|zì rán} is nature ({大自然|dà zì rán}, lesson 26) and "natural": {你|nǐ}{说|shuō}{得|de}{很|hěn}{自然|zì rán} (you
  sound very natural).

## The language of science

{科学|kē xué} is science, and {科学家|kē xué jiā} a scientist; {科技|kē jì} is "science and technology" together, the word of news and
policy talk ({科技|kē jì}{发展|fā zhǎn}, developments in science and technology); {技术|jì shù} is technology and also a skill, a
technique: {他|tā}{开车|kāi chē}{的|de}{技术|jì shù}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (he's a skilled driver). {研究|yán jiū} is "to research" and "research" ({研究生|yán jiū shēng}, lesson
05, is a research student).

Science writing has favourite verb–object pairs. Learn them as pairs:

| Pair | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {起|qǐ}{作用|zuò yòng} / {有|yǒu}{作用|zuò yòng} | to have an effect, play a role | {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{药|yào}{对|duì}{感冒|gǎn mào}{很|hěn}{有|yǒu}{作用|zuò yòng}。 This medicine works well on colds. |
| {产生|chǎn shēng} + abstract noun | to produce, give rise to | {产生|chǎn shēng}{兴趣|xìng qù} (become interested), {产生|chǎn shēng}{影响|yǐng xiǎng} (have an influence) |

| {在|zài}…{的|de}{过程|guò chéng}{中|zhōng} | in the process of | {在|zài}{学习|xué xí}{的|de}{过程|guò chéng}{中|zhōng}，{我|wǒ}{认识|rèn shi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{朋友|péng you}。 |

{产生|chǎn shēng} and {引起|yǐn qǐ} both translate "cause, produce". {产生|chǎn shēng} is for something that comes into being (interest, an
influence, a feeling, a new thing); {引起|yǐn qǐ} is for a reaction or a problem that one thing sets off in
another: {他|tā}{的|de}{话|huà}{引起|yǐn qǐ}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{注意|zhù yì} (what he said caught everyone's attention).

Four words of amount and change:

- {不断|bú duàn} bú duàn: continuously, again and again ({不断|bú duàn}{提高|tí gāo}, keep improving; {不断|bú duàn}{学习|xué xí}, keep
  learning);
- {大量|dà liàng} dà liàng: a large amount of ({大量|dà liàng}{的|de}{水|shuǐ}, {大量|dà liàng}{研究|yán jiū}), mostly before a noun;
- {大大|dà dà} dà dà: greatly, before a verb ({科技|kē jì}{大大|dà dà}{改变|gǎi biàn}{了|le}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó});
- {多样|duō yàng} duō yàng: varied, diverse ({植物|zhí wù}{多样|duō yàng}, a variety of plants); the set phrase {多种多样|duō zhǒng duō yàng} is "of every
  kind".

{粗|cū} and {细|xì} are thick and thin for long round things: {粗|cū}{的|de}{树|shù} (a thick tree trunk), {细|xì}{的|de}{线|xiàn} (a fine
thread; {线|xiàn}, lesson 24's line). {厚|hòu} (lesson 26) is for flat things: a thick book, a thick coat.

- **产**: the first five strokes are those of {立|lì} (a dot, a horizontal, a dot, a short

1. A child is planting a small tree in a garden; an older man pours water on it. Word: {棵|kē}.
2. A painting of mountains and a river hangs on a classroom wall. Word: {幅|fú}.
3. A girl is cutting a lemon with a small knife on a kitchen table. Word: {用来|yòng lái}.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {爷爷|yé ye}{和|hé}{孩子|hái zi}{在|zài}{院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{种|zhòng}{了|le}{一|yì}{棵|kē}{小|xiǎo}{树|shù}。 — Grandpa and the child have planted a little tree in the yard.
2. {教室|jiào shì}{的|de}{墙|qiáng}{上|shàng}{挂|guà}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{幅|fú}{画|huà}，{画|huà}{的|de}{是|shì}{山|shān}{和|hé}{河|hé}。 — On the classroom wall hangs a painting of mountains and a
   river. ({墙|qiáng}: wall, HSK 5)
3. {这|zhè}{把|bǎ}{小|xiǎo}{刀|dāo}{是|shì}{用来|yòng lái}{切|qiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}{的|de}。 — This little knife is for cutting fruit.
</details>

## Speaking: retell it

The speaking test, as reported, asks you to retell a short passage you have heard. Listen to the
passage below twice with the words hidden, then retell it in your own words in about forty seconds,
keeping the order: what, where, why.

```speak
# Retell: a tree in the school yard
{我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{操场|cāo chǎng}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{棵|kē}{很|hěn}{老|lǎo}{的|de}{树|shù}，{听说|tīng shuō}{已经|yǐ jīng}{活|huó}{了|le}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{了|le}。{夏天|xià tiān}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{它|tā}{的|de}{叶子|yè zi}{又|yòu}{多|duō}{又|yòu}{绿|lǜ}，{学生|xué sheng}{们|men}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{树|shù}{下|xià}{看|kàn}{书|shū}、{聊天|liáo tiān}。{去年|qù nián}，{这|zhè}{棵|kē}{树|shù}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{很|hěn}{多|duō}{叶子|yè zi}{都|dōu}{落|luò}{了|le}。{学校|xué xiào}{请|qǐng}{来|lái}{了|le}{研究|yán jiū}{植物|zhí wù}{的|de}{专家|zhuān jiā}，{他们|tā men}{给|gěi}{树|shù}{换|huàn}{了|le}{新|xīn}{土|tǔ}，{还|hái}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{给|gěi}{它|tā}{浇水|jiāo shuǐ}。{今年|jīn nián}{春天|chūn tiān}，{树|shù}{上|shàng}{又|yòu}{长出|zhǎng chū}{了|le}{新|xīn}{叶子|yè zi}，{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{特别|tè bié}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
= Next to our school's sports ground there's a very old tree; they say it's over two hundred years old. In summer its leaves are thick and green, and the students love to read and chat under it. Last year the tree fell ill and lost lots of leaves. The school brought in plant experts, who gave it new soil and watered it every day. This spring new leaves grew again, and everyone was really happy.
```

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

{学校|xué xiào}{操场|cāo chǎng}{旁边|páng biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{棵|kē}{两百|liǎng bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{的|de}{老|lǎo}{树|shù}，{夏天|xià tiān}{学生|xué sheng}{们|men}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{在|zài}{树|shù}{下|xià}{看|kàn}{书|shū}。{去年|qù nián}{树|shù}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}，{叶子|yè zi}{落|luò}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。{专家|zhuān jiā}{给|gěi}{它|tā}{换|huàn}{了|le}{土|tǔ}，{每|měi}{天|tiān}{浇水|jiāo shuǐ}。{今年|jīn nián}{春天|chūn tiān}，{树|shù}{又|yòu}{长出|zhǎng chū}{了|le}{新|xīn}{叶子|yè zi}。 — There's a tree over two hundred
years old next to the school sports ground, and in summer the students like to read under it. Last
year it fell ill and lost many leaves. Experts gave it new soil and watered it every day. This
spring it grew new leaves again. ({专家|zhuān jiā}: expert, HSK 5; {浇水|jiāo shuǐ}: to water, HSK 5; {长出|zhǎng chū}: to grow, put
out.)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# Plants, animals and science
{院子|yuàn zi}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}{棵|kē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{树|shù}。
= There are three apple trees in the yard.
{墙|qiáng}{上|shàng}{挂|guà}{着|zhe}{一|yì}{幅|fú}{画|huà}。
= There's a painting on the wall.
{这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{叶子|yè zi}{可以|kě yǐ}{用来|yòng lái}{做|zuò}{茶|chá}。
= These leaves can be used to make tea.
{我|wǒ}{爷爷|yé ye}{种|zhòng}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng}{花|huā}。
= My grandpa has planted many kinds of flowers.
{这|zhè}{棵|kē}{树|shù}{已经|yǐ jīng}{活|huó}{了|le}{三百|sān bǎi}{多|duō}{年|nián}{了|le}。
= This tree is over three hundred years old.
{科技|kē jì}{大大|dà dà}{改变|gǎi biàn}{了|le}{我们|wǒ men}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó}。
= Science and technology have greatly changed our lives.
```

## Pronunciation

- {种|zhòng} zhòng (to plant) and {种|zhǒng} zhǒng (kind): read {种|zhòng}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{种|zhǒng}{花|huā} as zhòng hěn duō zhǒng huā.
- {棵|kē} kē is first tone; {课|kè} kè (lesson) and {颗|kē} kē (HSK 5) are its neighbours.
- {部分|bù fen} bù fen: neutral second syllable in this word, though {分|fēn} is fēn elsewhere.
- {研究|yán jiū} yán jiū: rising, then high level. Some speakers say yán jiù; the standard is jiū.
- {产生|chǎn shēng} chǎn shēng and {过程|guò chéng} guò chéng: *ch* in both, aspirated (a strong puff of air).
- {熊|xióng} xióng (bear) rhymes with {雄|xióng} and {胸|xiōng}: the final is *-iong*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{一|yí}{个|gè}{树|shù}~~ is a typical learner's mistake: trees take {棵|kē}, {一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù}. ~~{一|yì}{张|zhāng}{树|shù}~~ is
  wrong too.
- {一|yì}{张|zhāng}{画|huà} is heard in conversation, but for a painting {一|yì}{幅|fú}{画|huà} is the standard measure word; use {幅|fú} in
  writing.
- ~~{我|wǒ}{有着|yǒu zhe}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}~~: {有着|yǒu zhe} is for abstract qualities in writing ({有着|yǒu zhe}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ}). For people and things you
  have, use {有|yǒu}.
- {这|zhè}{把|bǎ}{刀|dāo}{用于|yòng yú}{切|qiē}{菜|cài} sounds like a manual, not speech; in conversation say {这|zhè}{把|bǎ}{刀|dāo}{是|shì}{用来|yòng lái}{切|qiē}{菜|cài}{的|de}.
- ~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{产生|chǎn shēng}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{注意|zhù yì}~~: attention is "caused" with {引起|yǐn qǐ}: {引起|yǐn qǐ}{了|le}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{注意|zhù yì}. {产生|chǎn shēng} goes with {兴趣|xìng qù},
  {影响|yǐng xiǎng}, {感情|gǎn qíng} and new things.
- {种|zhǒng} zhǒng / zhòng: {种|zhòng}{树|shù} (zhòng) is to plant trees, {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{树|shù} (zhǒng) this kind of tree.
- ~~{粗|cū}{的|de}{书|shū}~~: a thick book is {厚|hòu}; {粗|cū} is for long round things ({粗|cū}{的|de}{树|shù}, {粗|cū}{的|de}{线|xiàn}).

## Key points

- {棵|kē} for plants ({一|yì}{棵|kē}{树|shù}), {幅|fú} for pictures ({一|yì}{幅|fú}{画|huà}), {片|piàn} for thin pieces and wide stretches ({一|yí}{片|piàn}{叶子|yè zi},
  {一|yí}{片|piàn}{蓝天|lán tiān}).
- {有着|yǒu zhe} + abstract object (written): {有着|yǒu zhe}{很|hěn}{长|cháng}{的|de}{历史|lì shǐ}. Never with {了|le}, {过|guo} or {没|méi}.
- {用来|yòng lái} + verb ({是|shì}{用来|yòng lái}…{的|de}: what it's for); written {用于|yòng yú} + noun; {分为|fēn wéi} (written) / {分成|fēn chéng} (spoken).
- {种|zhòng} zhòng (to plant) vs {种|zhǒng} zhǒng (kind); {活|huó}, {死|sǐ}, {生命|shēng mìng} (biological life) vs {生活|shēng huó} (daily life).
- Science pairs: {起|qǐ}{作用|zuò yòng}, {产生|chǎn shēng}{兴趣|xìng qù} / {影响|yǐng xiǎng}, {引起|yǐn qǐ}{注意|zhù yì}, {在|zài}…{的|de}{过程|guò chéng}{中|zhōng}; {不断|bú duàn}, {大量|dà liàng}, {大大|dà dà}, {多样|duō yàng}; {粗|cū} / {细|xì} vs {厚|hòu}.
- New characters: {产|chǎn} {幅|fú} {技|jì} {术|shù} {虎|hǔ} {棵|kē} {命|mìng} {土|tǔ} {死|sǐ} {植|zhí} (✎ {产|chǎn} {技|jì} {术|shù} {虎|hǔ} {土|tǔ}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Protecting the environment: 为了…而…, 于是, 不…也…
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lessons 26 and 27 described the climate, plants and animals. This lesson is about looking after
them: rubbish, plastic, saving water and energy, clean air. It's also the lesson of notices and
signs, the short written texts you meet on every street and in every building in China, and the
exam's reading part is full of them. You'll learn:

- {为了|wèi le}…{而|ér}…: the written way to state a purpose ({为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}{而|ér}{少|shǎo}{开车|kāi chē});
- {于是|yú shì}: "so, and then", for what happened next in a story;
- **[[compressed sentences]]**: two clauses with no connector, held together by {不|bù}…{也|yě}, {再|zài}…{也|yě} or {一|yī}…{就|jiù}
  ({你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{知道|zhī dào});
- the words of the environment: {环保|huán bǎo}, {保护|bǎo hù}, {污染|wū rǎn}, {垃圾|lā jī}, {塑料|sù liào}, {节约|jié yuē}, {浪费|làng fèi}, {减少|jiǎn shǎo}, {增加|zēng jiā}, {空气|kōng qì}, {森林|sēn lín};
- the language of signs: {禁止|jìn zhǐ}{吸烟|xī yān}, {节约|jié yuē}{用|yòng}{水|shuǐ}, {危险|wēi xiǎn}, {请|qǐng}{远离|yuǎn lí}.

At the end you can read a notice about sorting rubbish, understand the signs around you, and
explain why you do something.

## {为了|wèi le}…{而|ér}…: purpose, in writing

You know {为了|wèi le} (HSK 3) for a purpose: {为了|wèi le}{学|xué}{好|hǎo}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}，{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{看|kàn}{中国|Zhōng guó}{电影|diàn yǐng}. In writing, the purpose and the
action are often linked with {而|ér} (lesson 05's written "and, but"): {为了|wèi le} + purpose + {而|ér} + action, a
**[[written purpose clause]]**.

{为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}{而|ér}{少|shǎo}{开车|kāi chē}。 — To protect the environment, drive less.

{他|tā}{为了|wèi le}{照顾|zhào gù}{生病|shēng bìng}{的|de}{妈妈|mā ma}{而|ér}{放弃|fàng qì}{了|le}{国外|guó wài}{的|de}{工作|gōng zuò}。 — He gave up a job abroad to look after his sick mother.

{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}{为了|wèi le}{减少|jiǎn shǎo}{污染|wū rǎn}{而|ér}{选择|xuǎn zé}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{上班|shàng bān}。 — Many people choose to take the metro to work to reduce
pollution.

The subject can go at the start or after {为了|wèi le} … {而|ér}: {他|tā}{为了|wèi le}…{而|ér}… or {为了|wèi le}…，{他|tā}…. {而|ér} itself has no
meaning you can translate: it marks the step from the purpose to the action, as "and so" might in
formal English. The pattern is a little formal; in conversation you'd usually drop {而|ér} ({为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}，
{我|wǒ}{少|shǎo}{开车|kāi chē}) or put the purpose at the end with {是|shì}{为了|wèi le} (HSK 3).

A shorter cousin is {为|wèi}…{而|ér}…, with a noun after {为|wèi}: {为|wèi}{健康|jiàn kāng}{而|ér}{运动|yùn dòng} (exercise for your health), {为|wèi}{理想|lǐ xiǎng}{而|ér}{努力|nǔ lì}
(work towards an ideal). Both are favourite patterns in speeches, slogans and essays.

## {于是|yú shì}: and so, and then

{于是|yú shì} joins two events in a story: the first happens, and *as a result of it* the
second follows.

{天|tiān}{下|xià}{起|qǐ}{了|le}{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}，{于是|yú shì}{我们|wǒ men}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{了|le}。 — It started to pour, so we went home.

{他|tā}{听说|tīng shuō}{塑料袋|sù liào dài}{对|duì}{环境|huán jìng}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{于是|yú shì}{每|měi}{次|cì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{都|dōu}{自己|zì jǐ}{带|dài}{袋子|dài zi}。 — He heard that plastic bags are bad for
the environment, so he now takes his own bag every time he shops.

{于是|yú shì} starts the second clause, before its subject ({于是|yú shì}{我们|wǒ men}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{了|le}), or follows it ({我们|wǒ men}{于是|yú shì}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{了|le}). It
belongs to *narration*: things that happened, or happen regularly. Compare it with {所以|suǒ yǐ} and {因此|yīn cǐ}:

| Word | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| {所以|suǒ yǐ} (HSK 2) | cause and result, any time, also for advice | {明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}。 |
| {因此|yīn cǐ} (lesson 17) | cause and result, written | {由于|yóu yú}{下|xià}{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{因此|yīn cǐ}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。 |
| {于是|yú shì} | what happened next, because of the first event | {下|xià}{大|dà}{雨|yǔ}{了|le}，{于是|yú shì}{比赛|bǐ sài}{推迟|tuī chí}{了|le}。 |

So {于是|yú shì} can't introduce advice or a plan about the future: ~~{明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{于是|yú shì}{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}~~ is wrong (use
{所以|suǒ yǐ}). And it doesn't explain a general cause: "Water boils at a hundred degrees, so…" is {所以|suǒ yǐ} or
{因此|yīn cǐ}, not {于是|yú shì}.

## Compressed sentences: {不|bù}…{也|yě}…, {再|zài}…{也|yě}…, {一|yī}…{就|jiù}…

A **[[compressed sentence]]** packs a complex sentence into one breath: no {如果|rú guǒ}, {即使|jí shǐ} or {因为|yīn wèi} at the start,
just two short clauses and an adverb that shows how they're related. They're very common in speech.

**{不|bù}…{也|yě}…: even if not…, still…** The first clause is negative, and {也|yě} says the result holds anyway:

{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{知道|zhī dào}。 — Even if you don't tell me, I know. (= {即使|jí shǐ}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{知道|zhī dào}。)

{他|tā}{不|bù}{来|lái}{我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{去|qù}。 — We'll go even if he doesn't come.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{事|shì}{不|bú}{做|zuò}{也|yě}{可以|kě yǐ}。 — It's fine not to do this. (Even if you don't do it, it's OK.)

**{再|zài}…{也|yě}…: however… still…** You met {就是|jiù shì}{再|zài}…{也|yě} in lesson 26; without {就是|jiù shì} it's a compressed sentence:

{再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 — However busy you are, you have to eat.

{这个|zhè ge}{问题|wèn tí}{再|zài}{难|nán}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{要|yào}{想|xiǎng}{办法|bàn fǎ}。 — However hard this problem is, I'll find a way.

**{一|yī}…{就|jiù}…: as soon as… (then)** HSK 3's {一|yī}…{就|jiù} is a compressed sentence too: {他|tā}{一|yí}{到|dào}{家|jiā}{就|jiù}{睡|shuì}{了|le} (he went to bed
as soon as he got home); {我|wǒ}{一|yí}{看|kàn}{就|jiù}{明白|míng bai}{了|le} (I understood the moment I looked).

A fourth kind uses {不|bù}…{不|bù}…, "if not…, then not…": {你|nǐ}{不|bù}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{走|zǒu} (I won't leave until you come). The set
phrase {不见不散|bú jiàn bú sàn} (literally "if we don't meet, we don't part": see you there, I'll wait for you) is
one of them.

| Pattern | Meaning | Full form | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| {不|bù}…{也|yě}… | even if not…, still… | {即使|jí shǐ}{不|bù}…{也|yě}… | {你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{知道|zhī dào}。 |
| {再|zài}…{也|yě}… | however…, still… | {就是|jiù shì}{再|zài}…{也|yě}… | {再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 |
| {一|yī}…{就|jiù}… | as soon as… | …{以后|yǐ hòu}{马上|mǎ shàng}… | {他|tā}{一|yí}{到|dào}{家|jiā}{就|jiù}{睡|shuì}{了|le}。 |
| {不|bù}…{不|bù}… | if not…, then not… | {如果|rú guǒ}{不|bù}…{就|jiù}{不|bù}… | {你|nǐ}{不|bù}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{走|zǒu}。 |

## Words of the environment

{环保|huán bǎo} is short for {环境保护|huán jìng bǎo hù} (environmental protection), and it works as an adjective too: {环保袋|huán bǎo dài} (a
reusable bag), {这|zhè}{种|zhǒng}{方法|fāng fǎ}{很|hěn}{环保|huán bǎo} (this is a very green way of doing it). {保护|bǎo hù} is "to protect":
{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}, {保护|bǎo hù}{动物|dòng wù}, {保护|bǎo hù}{眼睛|yǎn jing}.

{污染|wū rǎn} wū rǎn is both "pollution" and "to pollute": {空气|kōng qì}{污染|wū rǎn} (air pollution), {水|shuǐ}{被|bèi}{污染|wū rǎn}{了|le} (the water has
been polluted). {空气|kōng qì} kōng qì is the air we breathe; {烟|yān} yān is smoke and also a cigarette ({吸烟|xī yān} / {抽烟|chōu yān}:
to smoke); {吸|xī} xī is "to breathe in, to draw in" ({吸|xī}{一|yì}{口|kǒu}{气|qì}, take a breath; {吸烟|xī yān}).

{垃圾|lā jī} lā jī is rubbish ({扔|rēng}{垃圾|lā jī}, to throw rubbish away; {垃圾桶|lā jī tǒng}, a bin), and {扔|rēng} rēng is to throw, to throw
away: {别|bié}{把|bǎ}{瓶子|píng zi}{扔|rēng}{在|zài}{地上|dì shang} (don't throw bottles on the ground). {桶|tǒng} is a bucket or a bin; {袋子|dài zi} a bag ({塑料袋|sù liào dài}, a
plastic bag); {盒子|hé zi} a box ({饭盒|fàn hé}, a lunch box); {塑料|sù liào} sù liào plastic.

Four verbs of more and less, and how to use them:

| Verb | Meaning | Typical objects |
|---|---|---|

Signs use a clipped written style: no subject, no {了|le}, verbs with two-character objects. Learn them

### Stroke order

- **止**: the short vertical in the middle first, then the short horizontal to its right, the
  long vertical on the left, and the long horizontal at the bottom last.
- **扔**: 扌 (three strokes), then 乃: one stroke that turns three times and ends in a hook
  ({横折折折钩|héng zhé zhé zhé gōu}), and a left-falling stroke through it.
- **染**: 氵, then {九|jiǔ} (the left-falling stroke first, then the turning hook), then {木|mù}.
- **危**: the left-falling stroke and the short {横撇|héng piě} at the top, then the long horizontal, the
  long left-falling stroke, and 㔾 inside: {横折钩|héng zhé gōu}, then {竖弯钩|shù wān gōu} last.
- **增**: {土|tǔ} (its last stroke is a rising one, {提|tí}), then 曾: the two short strokes on top (a dot
  and a left-falling stroke), the middle box with the strokes inside it, and {日|rì} at the bottom.
