> {垃圾|lā jī}{分类|fēn lèi}{开始|kāi shǐ}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{可能|kě néng}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{麻烦|má fan}，{可是|kě shì}{只要|zhǐ yào}{每|měi}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{做|zuò}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}，{就|jiù}{能|néng}{起到|qǐ dào}{很|hěn}{大|dà}{的|de}{作用|zuò yòng}。{如果|rú guǒ}{有|yǒu}{问题|wèn tí}，{可以|kě yǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{问|wèn}{小区|xiǎo qū}{服务|fú wù}{中心|zhōng xīn}：0000 1234。{谢谢|xiè xie}{大家|dà jiā}{的|de}{支持|zhī chí}！
>
> {新城|Xīn chéng}{小区|xiǎo qū}{服务|fú wù}{中心|zhōng xīn}　{十|shí}{月|yuè}{二十|èr shí}{日|rì}

{剩饭|shèng fàn} is leftover food, {菜叶|cài yè} vegetable leaves, {果皮|guǒ pí} fruit peel; {服务|fú wù}{中心|zhōng xīn} a service centre ({服务|fú wù}, HSK 2's
{服务员|fú wù yuán}); {大|dà}{件|jiàn}{垃圾|lā jī} bulky rubbish ({件|jiàn}, the measure word for items); {家具|jiā jù} is lesson 10's furniture.

1. When does the new rule start, and what is it for?
2. Which bin does a used battery go in? And an old shirt?
3. A resident puts a bag of rubbish outside the building door at ten at night. Which rule have
   they broken?
4. What does the writer mean by {节约|jié yuē}{是|shì}{最好|zuì hǎo}{的|de}{环保|huán bǎo}?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. On the first of next month ({从|cóng}{下|xià}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{一|yī}{日|rì}{起|qǐ}); to protect the environment and reduce pollution
   ({为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}、{减少|jiǎn shǎo}{污染|wū rǎn}).
2. The battery goes in the red bin ({有害|yǒu hài}{垃圾|lā jī}); the shirt in the blue one ({旧|jiù}{衣服|yī fu}…{可回收|kě huí shōu}{垃圾|lā jī}).
3. The time rule: rubbish goes out only from seven to nine in the morning and six to eight in the
   evening ({其他|qí tā}{时间|shí jiān}{请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào}{把|bǎ}{垃圾|lā jī}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{楼|lóu}{门口|mén kǒu}).
4. That using less in the first place (fewer plastic bags, taking your own) does more for the
   environment than anything else; the best rubbish is the rubbish you never make. The notice
   doesn't say this outright: it's what the sentence implies after "use fewer plastic bags".

"**Xincheng compound: notice on sorting rubbish.** To all residents: To protect the environment and
reduce pollution, this compound will start sorting rubbish from the first of next month. The rules
are as follows. 1. Four bins of different colours will be placed at the door of each building. The
blue bin is for recyclable rubbish such as paper, plastic bottles and old clothes; the green bin for
kitchen waste such as leftover food, vegetable leaves and fruit peel; the red bin for harmful waste
such as batteries and out-of-date medicine; the black bin for all other rubbish. 2. Rubbish may be
put out from 7 to 9 every morning and from 6 to 8 every evening; at other times please don't leave
rubbish at the building door. 3. Please put your rubbish in a bag before throwing it away. Leaving
rubbish in the stairwells is prohibited. 4. Please use fewer plastic bags when you shop, and ideally
bring your own bag: saving is the best way to protect the environment. 5. Large items such as old
furniture and old televisions must not be left beside the bins: please phone the compound service
centre first, and we will arrange for someone to collect them. Sorting rubbish may be a bit
of a bother at first, but if everyone does a little, it can make a big difference. If you have any
questions, please phone the compound service centre: 0000 1234. Thank you all for your support!
Xincheng Compound Service Centre, 20 October."
</details>

## Write it

Write one sentence for each picture, using the word given.

1. A man waits at a bus stop; behind him, a sign shows a cigarette with a red line through it.
   Word: {禁止|jìn zhǐ}.
2. A woman turns off the tap while she brushes her teeth. Word: {节约|jié yuē}.
3. A young man has left his car at home and is cycling to work past a traffic jam. Word: {为了|wèi le}.

<details>
<summary>Model answers</summary>

1. {车站|chē zhàn}{禁止|jìn zhǐ}{吸烟|xī yān}，{他|tā}{只好|zhǐ hǎo}{把|bǎ}{烟|yān}{放|fàng}{回去|huí qù}{了|le}。 — Smoking isn't allowed at the bus stop, so he's had to put
   his cigarette away.
2. {为了|wèi le}{节约|jié yuē}{用|yòng}{水|shuǐ}，{她|tā}{刷牙|shuā yá}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{把|bǎ}{水|shuǐ}{关|guān}{了|le}。 — To save water, she turns the tap off while she brushes
   her teeth. ({刷牙|shuā yá}: to brush your teeth, HSK 5)
3. {为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}，{他|tā}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{骑|qí}{自行车|zì xíng chē}{上班|shàng bān}，{不|bù}{开车|kāi chē}{了|le}。 — To protect the environment, he cycles to work
   every day instead of driving.
</details>

## Speaking: a story from three pictures

The speaking test, as reported, asks you to tell a story from three numbered pictures after a few
minutes' preparation. Here are three, described in words:

1. In a park, a man finishes a bottle of water and throws it on the grass.
2. A little girl picks the bottle up and carries it to a bin with a recycling sign.
3. The man looks embarrassed, then picks up another piece of rubbish and puts it in the bin too.

Tell the story aloud in about a minute: say who, where, what happened and how it ended. Link the
steps with {先|xiān}, {然后|rán hòu}, {于是|yú shì}, {最后|zuì hòu}.

<details>
<summary>A model story</summary>

{一|yí}{个|gè}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{男人|nán rén}{在|zài}{公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{喝|hē}{完|wán}{一|yì}{瓶|píng}{水|shuǐ}，{就|jiù}{把|bǎ}{瓶子|píng zi}{扔|rēng}{在|zài}{了|le}{草地|cǎo dì}{上|shàng}。{旁边|páng biān}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小女孩|xiǎo nǚ hái}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}，{她|tā}{把|bǎ}{瓶子|píng zi}{捡|jiǎn}{起来|qǐ lái}，
{扔|rēng}{进|jìn}{了|le}{可回收|kě huí shōu}{垃圾桶|lā jī tǒng}{里|lǐ}。{男人|nán rén}{看见|kàn jiàn}{了|le}，{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{不好意思|bù hǎo yì si}，{于是|yú shì}{他|tā}{也|yě}{把|bǎ}{地上|dì shang}{的|de}{另|lìng}{一|yí}{个|gè}{垃圾|lā jī}{捡|jiǎn}{起来|qǐ lái}，{扔|rēng}{进|jìn}{了|le}{垃圾桶|lā jī tǒng}。
{最后|zuì hòu}，{他|tā}{对|duì}{小女孩|xiǎo nǚ hái}{说|shuō}：“{谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{以后|yǐ hòu}{不|bú}{会|huì}{乱扔|luàn rēng}{垃圾|lā jī}{了|le}。”

One Sunday, a man in a park finished a bottle of water and threw the bottle on the grass. A little
girl nearby saw it: she picked the bottle up and put it in the recycling bin. When the man saw that,
he felt very embarrassed, so he picked up another piece of rubbish from the ground too and put it
in the bin. In the end he said to the girl, "Thank you. I won't drop litter again." ({捡|jiǎn}: to pick
up, HSK 5; {小女孩|xiǎo nǚ hái}: little girl.)
</details>

## Say it

```speak
# The environment
{为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}，{我们|wǒ men}{少|shǎo}{开车|kāi chē}{吧|ba}。
= Let's drive less, to protect the environment.
{他|tā}{听说|tīng shuō}{塑料袋|sù liào dài}{对|duì}{环境|huán jìng}{不|bù}{好|hǎo}，{于是|yú shì}{每|měi}{次|cì}{都|dōu}{自己|zì jǐ}{带|dài}{袋子|dài zi}。
= He heard plastic bags were bad for the environment, so now he always brings his own bag.
{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{知道|zhī dào}。
= I know, even if you don't tell me.
{再|zài}{忙|máng}{也|yě}{要|yào}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。
= However busy you are, you have to eat.
{这儿|zhèr}{禁止|jìn zhǐ}{吸烟|xī yān}。
= Smoking isn't allowed here.
{别|bié}{浪费|làng fèi}{水|shuǐ}，{节约|jié yuē}{用|yòng}{水|shuǐ}。
= Don't waste water: save it.
```

## Pronunciation

- {垃圾|lā jī} lā jī: two first tones. In Taiwan you may hear lè sè; the mainland standard is lā jī.
- {污染|wū rǎn} wū rǎn: the *r* of rǎn is like the *s* in "pleasure"; keep it soft.
- {塑料|sù liào} sù liào: *s*, not *sh*. The top of {塑|sù}, 朔 shuò, once gave the sound but no longer matches.
- {扔|rēng} rēng: first tone, and the final is *-eng*, as in {冷|lěng} lěng.
- {增长|zēng zhǎng} zēng zhǎng: {长|zhǎng} is zhǎng (to grow) here, not cháng (long).
- {于是|yú shì} yú shì: yú with a rising tone, like {鱼|yú} (fish).

## Common mistakes

- ~~{明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{于是|yú shì}{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}~~: {于是|yú shì} tells what happened next in a story; for advice use {所以|suǒ yǐ}:
  {明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{下雨|xià yǔ}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{你|nǐ}{带|dài}{把|bǎ}{伞|sǎn}{吧|ba}。
- ~~{为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}{而|ér}~~ at the end of a sentence: the action comes after {而|ér} ({为了|wèi le}{保护|bǎo hù}{环境|huán jìng}{而|ér}{少|shǎo}{开车|kāi chē}), never
  before {为了|wèi le} in this pattern.
- ~~{增长|zēng zhǎng}{人数|rén shù}~~: say {增加|zēng jiā}{人数|rén shù}; {增长|zēng zhǎng} is for totals that grow over time ({经济|jīng jì}{增长|zēng zhǎng}) and rarely takes
  an object, and in speech {增加|zēng jiā} covers most uses.
- ~~{浪费|làng fèi}{钱|qián}{很|hěn}{多|duō}~~: {浪费|làng fèi} takes its object straight after it: {浪费|làng fèi}{了|le}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{钱|qián}。
- {禁止|jìn zhǐ} belongs to signs and rules ({禁止|jìn zhǐ}{吸烟|xī yān}); said to a friend it sounds like a rule book. To tell a
  person, say {别|bié}{抽烟|chōu yān} or {这儿|zhèr}{不|bù}{能|néng}{抽烟|chōu yān}.
- ~~{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}，{我|wǒ}{就|jiù}{知道|zhī dào}~~ for "even if you don't say, I know": the compressed sentence takes {也|yě}: {你|nǐ}{不|bù}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}
  {也|yě}{知道|zhī dào}。

## Key points

- {为了|wèi le} + purpose + {而|ér} + action (written); {为|wèi} + noun + {而|ér} + verb ({为|wèi}{健康|jiàn kāng}{而|ér}{运动|yùn dòng}).
- {于是|yú shì}: and so, then (what happened next in a story); {所以|suǒ yǐ} for any cause and result, including advice.
- Compressed sentences: {不|bù}…{也|yě} (even if not), {再|zài}…{也|yě} (however), {一|yī}…{就|jiù} (as soon as), {不|bù}…{不|bù} (if not…
  then not).
- {环保|huán bǎo}, {保护|bǎo hù}, {污染|wū rǎn}, {垃圾|lā jī}, {塑料|sù liào}, {节约|jié yuē} / {浪费|làng fèi}, {增加|zēng jiā} / {减少|jiǎn shǎo} / {增长|zēng zhǎng}, {起到|qǐ dào}…{作用|zuò yòng}, {禁止|jìn zhǐ}, {远离|yuǎn lí}.
- Signs: {禁止|jìn zhǐ}{吸烟|xī yān}, {禁止|jìn zhǐ}{停车|tíng chē}, {节约|jié yuē}{用|yòng}{水|shuǐ}, {危险|wēi xiǎn}！{请|qǐng}{远离|yuǎn lí}, {请勿|qǐng wù}{乱扔|luàn rēng}{垃圾|lā jī}.
- New characters: {袋|dài} {盒|hé} {垃|lā} {圾|jī} {禁|jìn} {止|zhǐ} {森|sēn} {林|lín} {扔|rēng} {塑|sù} {桶|tǒng} {烟|yān} {污|wū} {染|rǎn} {危|wēi} {险|xiǎn} {增|zēng} (✎ {止|zhǐ} {扔|rēng} {增|zēng}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Concerts, plays and the arts: writing and speaking
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This is the last lesson with new words. It has two halves. The first is about the arts: concerts,
plays and opera, and the words for performing, playing an instrument and being in the audience.
The second brings together the writing and speaking you have practised through the course and
prepares you for the exam's productive tasks, as they are reported from the sample papers:

- performance words: {演出|yǎn chū}, {演|yǎn}, {演员|yǎn yuán}, {演唱|yǎn chàng}, {歌手|gē shǒu}, {歌声|gē shēng}, {观众|guān zhòng}, {剧院|jù yuàn}, {话剧|huà jù}, {京剧|jīng jù}, {艺术|yì shù}, {精彩|jīng cǎi};
- playing instruments: {弹|tán} tán ({钢琴|gāng qín}, {琴|qín}), and the other verbs of music: {拉|lā}, {吹|chuī}, {打|dǎ};
- **[[discourse markers]]**: {首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…{最后|zuì hòu}…, {总之|zǒng zhī}, and {总结|zǒng jié} (to sum up), the words that give a text its
  shape;
- the writing tasks: a sentence with a given word about a picture, and a text of at least 80
  characters ({作文|zuò wén}), with a plan and a checklist;
- the speaking tasks: retelling a passage, telling a story from three pictures, answering
  questions.

At the end you can talk about a show you have seen, write a short, well-organised text about it,
and know what each exam task asks of you.

## Performing: {演出|yǎn chū}, {演|yǎn}, {演员|yǎn yuán}, {表演|biǎo yǎn}

{演出|yǎn chū} is a performance, a show, and also "to perform, to put on (a show)": {今天|jīn tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{有|yǒu}{演出|yǎn chū} (there's a
show tonight); {他们|tā men}{在|zài}{剧院|jù yuàn}{演出|yǎn chū} (they're performing at the theatre). It's the general word for concerts,
plays, opera and dance.

{演|yǎn} on its own is "to act, to play (a part)" and "to put on, to show (a play or film)": {他|tā}{在|zài}{电影|diàn yǐng}{里|lǐ}{演|yǎn}{一|yí}{个|gè}
{医生|yī shēng} (he plays a doctor in the film); {这个|zhè ge}{话剧|huà jù}{演|yǎn}{了|le}{三|sān}{个|gè}{月|yuè} (the play ran for three months). The person who
acts or performs is a {演员|yǎn yuán}, and HSK 3's {表演|biǎo yǎn} is "to perform, a performance" with the focus on showing
a skill: {表演|biǎo yǎn}{节目|jié mù} (to put on an act), {他|tā}{的|de}{表演|biǎo yǎn}{很|hěn}{精彩|jīng cǎi}.

For singing on stage, the word is {演唱|yǎn chàng} (to sing, in performance): {演唱会|yǎn chàng huì} is a concert by a singer or a
band, {音乐会|yīn yuè huì} a concert of music in general. A {歌手|gē shǒu} is a singer (by profession), and {歌声|gē shēng} is the sound of
singing: {我|wǒ}{听|tīng}{到|dào}{了|le}{美丽|měi lì}{的|de}{歌声|gē shēng} (I heard beautiful singing).

The places and kinds of show: {剧院|jù yuàn} (a theatre), {话剧|huà jù} (a play, spoken drama: the {话|huà} of {说话|shuō huà}), {京剧|jīng jù} (Peking
opera, the opera of {北京|Běi jīng}, which HSK 3's honors lesson described). {艺术|yì shù} is art in general ({艺术家|yì shù jiā}, an
artist; {美术史|měi shù shǐ}, art history).

The audience is {观众|guān zhòng}, the people who watch: {观众|guān zhòng}{都|dōu}{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le} (the audience all stood up). Lesson 24's {听众|tīng zhòng}
is the audience of a radio programme or a talk, the people who listen.

{精彩|jīng cǎi} is the word for a show, a match or a talk that is brilliant, exciting, full of good moments:
{演出|yǎn chū}{非常|fēi cháng}{精彩|jīng cǎi} (the performance was wonderful); {精彩|jīng cǎi}{的|de}{比赛|bǐ sài} (a thrilling match). It isn't used of
people or food: a brilliant person is {优秀|yōu xiù} (lesson 12), and food is {好吃|hǎo chī}.

## Playing an instrument: {弹|tán}, {拉|lā}, {吹|chuī}, {打|dǎ}

English "play" covers every instrument; Chinese chooses the verb by what your hands do:

| Verb | How it's played | Instruments |
|---|---|---|
| {弹|tán} tán | plucked or pressed with the fingers | {弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín} (piano), {弹|tán}{琴|qín}, {弹|tán}{吉他|jí tā} (guitar) |
| {拉|lā} lā | bowed: the hand pulls | {拉|lā}{小提琴|xiǎo tí qín} (violin), {拉|lā}{二胡|èr hú} (erhu) |
| {吹|chuī} chuī | blown | {吹|chuī}{笛子|dí zi} (flute) |
| {打|dǎ} dǎ | struck | {打|dǎ}{鼓|gǔ} (drums) |

{琴|qín} is the general word for many stringed and keyboard instruments; {钢琴|gāng qín} (steel + {琴|qín}) is the piano.
{弹|tán}{琴|qín} can mean playing the piano or playing a stringed instrument in general. ~~{玩|wán}{钢琴|gāng qín}~~ is a common
learner mistake: {玩|wán} is playing a game; music is {弹|tán}, {拉|lā}, {吹|chuī} or {打|dǎ}.

{弹|tán} has a second reading, dàn (a bullet, a bomb: {子弹|zǐ dàn}, HSK 6); for music it's always tán.

## Discourse markers: {首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {最后|zuì hòu}, {总之|zǒng zhī}

A **[[discourse marker]]** is a word that shows how the parts of a text fit together: which point comes
first, what's added, what's the conclusion. They matter in the exam: the reading part asks you to
put sentences back into a passage, and the connectors are the clues; and in writing and speaking,
they make your own text easy to follow.

{首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…{最后|zuì hòu}… lists points in order: "first…, second…, finally…":

{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{这个|zhè ge}{演出|yǎn chū}。{首先|shǒu xiān}，{演员|yǎn yuán}{演|yǎn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}；{其次|qí cì}，{音乐|yīn yuè}{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}；{最后|zuì hòu}，{票|piào}{也|yě}{不|bú}{贵|guì}。 — I liked the show. First,
the acting was good; second, the music was lovely; and finally, the tickets weren't expensive.

- {首先|shǒu xiān} is "first of all", the first step or the most important point: {首先|shǒu xiān}，{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{感谢|gǎn xiè}{大家|dà jiā} (first of all, I
  want to thank everyone).
- {其次|qí cì} is "next, secondly": it introduces a second point, often a less important one. In speech,
  {第|dì}{二|èr} or {还|hái}{有|yǒu} do the same job.
- After two points, {最后|zuì hòu} (finally) or {另外|lìng wài} / {此外|cǐ wài} (lesson 01: besides) add the last one.

To close a text, {总之|zǒng zhī} (in short, all in all: HSK 5) sums it up; {总的来说|zǒng de lái shuō} (on the whole) is a softer,
spoken version. {总结|zǒng jié} is the verb "to sum up" and the noun "a summary": {我们|wǒ men}{来|lái}{总结|zǒng jié}{一下|yí xià} (let's sum up);
{写|xiě}{一|yí}{个|gè}{总结|zǒng jié} (to write a summary).

| {首先|shǒu xiān} | first point or step | {第|dì}{一|yī} |
| {其次|qí cì} | second point | {第|dì}{二|èr}, {还|hái}{有|yǒu} |
| {然后|rán hòu} | the next step in time | {然后|rán hòu}, {接着|jiē zhe} |

| {另外|lìng wài}, {此外|cǐ wài} | an extra point | {还|hái}{有|yǒu} |

- **{京|jīng}**: you have read it since HSK 1 in {北京|Běi jīng}, but it's taught as a character only now. 亠 on top,
  {口|kǒu}, then {小|xiǎo} at the bottom.
- **A sound series: {青|qīng} qīng.** {精|jīng} jīng is {米|mǐ} + {青|qīng}, and {青|qīng} gives the sound in a whole family you know:
  {请|qǐng} qǐng, {情|qíng} qíng, {晴|qíng} qíng, {清|qīng} qīng, {睛|jīng} jīng ({眼睛|yǎn jing}). The tone and sometimes the first sound move, but
  the *-ing* stays.
- **Another: 采 cǎi.** {彩|cǎi} cǎi is 采 + 彡 (three strokes for "colour, pattern"); {菜|cài} cài (HSK 1) is
  艹 over 采: the same sound, another tone.
- **钅 for metal**: {钢|gāng} (steel) and {钱|qián}, {铁|tiě} ({地铁|dì tiě}), {钟|zhōng} ({分钟|fēn zhōng}), {镜|jìng} ({眼镜|yǎn jìng}, lesson 06). Traditional writes

- **{琴|qín}** has two {王|wáng} on top and {今|jīn} at the bottom.
- **{弹|tán}**: 弓 (a bow) + {单|dān}; the bowstring is a good memory aid for plucking strings, but treat it
  as a memory aid, not the character's history.
- **{艺|yì}**: 艹 over 乙, only four strokes in simplified; traditional 藝 has 19.

### Stroke order

- **京**: the dot, the long horizontal, then {口|kǒu}, and {小|xiǎo} last: its vertical hook first, then the
  left and the right strokes.
- **彩**: 采 first (爫, four short strokes, then {木|mù}), and 彡 last, its three
  left-falling strokes from top to bottom.
- **弹**: 弓 (three strokes: {横折|héng zhé}, {横|héng}, {竖折折钩|shù zhé zhé gōu}), then the two short strokes on top of {单|dān}, and {单|dān}.
- **艺**: 艹 (three strokes), then 乙: one stroke, the horizontal that turns down and ends in a
  hook.

"**A memorable performance.** Last month I went to the theatre with my classmates from the
art-history course to see Peking opera. The show started at half past seven, and the theatre was
full: old people, and lots of young people too. It was my first time, and it left a deep impression on me.
First, the actors' costumes were beautiful, with many bright colours. Professor Luo told us that you
can tell a character's personality from the colours painted on the actor's face: red characters tend
to be brave, while white ones are often villains. Second, the actors' movements were brilliant. They can not only sing but also
perform many very difficult movements. Every time an actor finished one, the audience cheered loudly,
and I joined in. Finally, the music of Peking opera was unlike any music I'd heard before. At first I
thought it was a bit noisy, but after listening for a while I gradually came to like it. All in all,
seeing Peking opera this time has made me very interested in Chinese art. Back home I even found a
few clips of Peking opera online, and I watch them whenever I have time. I'm planning to take my mum
and dad to see it when they come to Beijing next spring."

The colours are Anna's simplified report of what she was told; the meanings of face-paint colours
in Chinese opera are many and vary by role and play (red is often linked with loyalty and courage,
white with a crafty, scheming character).

## The writing part, as reported

Reports on the HSK 4 sample paper describe a writing part of six items in about 25 minutes:
five sentences, each built on a word you are given and about a picture, and one short text of at
least 80 characters. Check the format on the official site before the exam: what follows is our
practice for those tasks, not the exam's own questions.

### Task 1: a sentence with a given word

Each item shows a picture and a word; you write one sentence that uses the word and fits the
picture. A good sentence:

1. uses the word in its normal pattern (a measure word with a number, a verb with its object, a
   connector with its pair);
2. says something about the picture, not just the word ({他|tā}{在|zài}{弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín} is better than {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{钢琴|gāng qín});
3. adds one detail: who, where, when, how ({他|tā}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín});
4. is one you're sure is correct: a short right sentence beats a long wrong one.

Practice: write one sentence for each.

1. A young woman sings on a stage; the audience holds up their phones. Word: {演唱|yǎn chàng}.
2. A boy sits at a piano with his teacher beside him. Word: {弹|tán}.
3. A full theatre; everyone in the audience is clapping. Word: {观众|guān zhòng}.
4. Two people come out of a theatre, smiling and talking. Word: {精彩|jīng cǎi}.
5. A man stands in front of a list on a whiteboard, pointing to the first item. Word: {首先|shǒu xiān}.

| Part | What it does | Useful words |
|---|---|---|
| Opening (one or two sentences) | what, when, where, who | {上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}, {有|yǒu}{一|yí}{次|cì}, {我|wǒ}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}… |
| Middle (two or three points, or the story's steps) | the content | {首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {然后|rán hòu}, {最后|zuì hòu}; {不但|bú dàn}…{而且|ér qiě} |
| Close (one sentence) | how you felt, what you learned, your opinion | {总之|zǒng zhī}, {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}, {让|ràng}{我|wǒ}… |

Eighty characters is about six or seven short sentences.

Practice: write 80–120 characters on {你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{过|guo}{的|de}{一|yí}{次|cì}{演出|yǎn chū}{或者|huò zhě}{比赛|bǐ sài} (a performance or match you have seen).

<details>
<summary>A model text (about 110 characters)</summary>

{去年|qù nián}{夏天|xià tiān}，{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{朋友|péng you}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}{篮球|lán qiú}{比赛|bǐ sài}。{首先|shǒu xiān}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{非常|fēi cháng}{精彩|jīng cǎi}，{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{队|duì}{都|dōu}{打|dǎ}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}，{最后|zuì hòu}{一|yì}{分钟|fēn zhōng}{才|cái}{分出|fēn chū}{输赢|shū yíng}。
{其次|qí cì}，{观众|guān zhòng}{特别|tè bié}{热情|rè qíng}，{大家|dà jiā}{一直|yì zhí}{在|zài}{给|gěi}{自己|zì jǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{队|duì}{加油|jiā yóu}。{最后|zuì hòu}，{比赛|bǐ sài}{结束|jié shù}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{我们|wǒ men}{还|hái}{在|zài}{门口|mén kǒu}{见|jiàn}{到|dào}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{有名|yǒu míng}{的|de}{球员|qiú yuán}。
{总之|zǒng zhī}，{那|nà}{是|shì}{一|yí}{个|gè}{难忘|nán wàng}{的|de}{晚上|wǎn shang}。

Last summer my friend and I saw a basketball match in Beijing. First, the match was thrilling: both
teams played very well, and it was decided only in the last minute. Second, the crowd was really
enthusiastic, cheering their teams all the time. Finally, after the match, we even met a famous
player at the entrance. All in all, it was an unforgettable evening. ({分出|fēn chū}{输赢|shū yíng}: to decide who wins;
{热情|rè qíng}: warm, enthusiastic; {球员|qiú yuán}: a player.)
</details>

### A checklist for your {作文|zuò wén}

- **Length**: at least 80 characters; count roughly as you go.
- **Shape**: an opening, a middle, a close; a marker at the start of each point ({首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {最后|zuì hòu},
  {总之|zǒng zhī}).
- **Grammar you're sure of**: {了|le} for completed actions, a measure word with every number, the
  right {的|de} / {地|de} / {得|de} ({美丽|měi lì}{的|de}{歌声|gē shēng}, {认真|rèn zhēn}{地|de}{练习|liàn xí}, {弹|tán}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}), time and place before the verb.
- **Connectors in pairs**: {不但|bú dàn}…{而且|ér qiě}, {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì}, {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}, {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ}.
- **Characters**: write the ones you know; if you're stuck, rephrase with a word you can write
  rather than leave a gap.
- **Punctuation**: Chinese marks: 。，、？！ and “ ”; a full stop is a small circle, not a dot.
- **Read it once** at the end and correct anything you can.

## The speaking part, as reported

One detailed report on the speaking sample paper describes three parts; two reports give about 20
minutes in all, including about 10 minutes' preparation. In the 2026 pilot rounds, candidates for
levels 3–6 registered for the speaking test together with the written exam; one report says that in
Japan the two can still be registered separately. Check the rules where you will take the exam.

| Part | Task, as reported | What helps |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | listen to two short passages and retell each (reported as about 40 seconds each; one report says each passage is heard once) | keep the order; keep the key words; it doesn't have to be word for word |
| 2 | tell a story from three numbered photos (3 minutes' preparation, 2 minutes to speak) | say who and where first; link the pictures with {先|xiān}, {然后|rán hòu}, {于是|yú shì}, {最后|zuì hòu} |
| 3 | answer two questions (about 3½ minutes' preparation, 2 minutes to speak) | answer, give a reason, give an example, conclude |

### Part 1: retell

Listen to the passage twice with the words hidden, then retell it in your own words.

```speak
# Retell: the school concert
{上|shàng}{个|gè}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}，{我们|wǒ men}{学校|xué xiào}{举办|jǔ bàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}{音乐会|yīn yuè huì}。{来|lái}{演出|yǎn chū}{的|de}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{有的|yǒu de}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}，{有的|yǒu de}{弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小组|xiǎo zǔ}{演|yǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{很|hěn}{短|duǎn}{的|de}{话剧|huà jù}。{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yī}{年级|nián jí}{女生|nǚ shēng}{的|de}{演唱|yǎn chàng}，{她|tā}{的|de}{歌声|gē shēng}{非常|fēi cháng}{好听|hǎo tīng}，{观众|guān zhòng}{听|tīng}{完|wán}{以后|yǐ hòu}{都|dōu}{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。{音乐会|yīn yuè huì}{结束|jié shù}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{校长|xiào zhǎng}{说|shuō}，{明年|míng nián}{还|hái}{要|yào}{再|zài}{办|bàn}{一|yí}{次|cì}。
= Last Friday our school held a concert. The performers were all students: some sang, some played the piano, and one group put on a very short play. My favourite was a first-year girl's singing: her voice was lovely, and when she finished the audience all stood up. After the concert the head teacher said they'd hold another one next year.
```

<details>
<summary>A model retelling</summary>

{上|shàng}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}{学校|xué xiào}{办|bàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}{音乐会|yīn yuè huì}，{学生|xué sheng}{们|men}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}、{弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín}，{还|hái}{演|yǎn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{话剧|huà jù}。{一|yí}{个|gè}{一|yī}{年级|nián jí}{女生|nǚ shēng}{唱|chàng}{得|de}{特别|tè bié}{好|hǎo}，{观众|guān zhòng}{都|dōu}{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。{校长|xiào zhǎng}{说|shuō}{明年|míng nián}{还|hái}{要|yào}{再|zài}{办|bàn}。 — Last Friday the school held a concert: students sang,
played the piano and put on a little play. A first-year girl sang especially well, and the audience
all stood up. The head teacher said they'd hold another next year. ({校长|xiào zhǎng}: head teacher; {办|bàn}: to hold,
organise.)
</details>

### Part 2: three pictures

1. A girl practises the violin at home; her younger brother covers his ears.
2. Weeks later, the girl plays on a school stage; the brother sits in the front row.
3. The brother claps hardest of all and gives her flowers.

<details>
<summary>A model story</summary>

{姐姐|jiě jie}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{练习|liàn xí}{拉|lā}{小提琴|xiǎo tí qín}，{可是|kě shì}{开始|kāi shǐ}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{拉|lā}{得|de}{不|bú}{太|tài}{好听|hǎo tīng}，{弟弟|dì di}{常常|cháng cháng}{把|bǎ}{耳朵|ěr duo}{捂|wǔ}{上|shàng}。{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{学校|xué xiào}{举办|jǔ bàn}{了|le}{一|yì}{场|chǎng}{演出|yǎn chū}，
{姐姐|jiě jie}{上台|shàng tái}{表演|biǎo yǎn}，{弟弟|dì di}{坐|zuò}{在|zài}{第|dì}{一|yī}{排|pái}。{姐姐|jiě jie}{拉|lā}{得|de}{非常|fēi cháng}{精彩|jīng cǎi}，{演出|yǎn chū}{结束|jié shù}{以后|yǐ hòu}，{弟弟|dì di}{鼓掌|gǔ zhǎng}{鼓|gǔ}{得|de}{最|zuì}{用力|yòng lì}，{还|hái}{送|sòng}{给|gěi}{姐姐|jiě jie}{一|yí}{束|shù}{花|huā}。

— Every day the girl practised the violin at home, but at first it didn't sound very good, and her
little brother often covered his ears. A few weeks later the school put on a show: she performed on
stage, and her brother sat in the front row. She played brilliantly, and when the show was over her
brother clapped hardest of all and gave her a bunch of flowers. ({捂|wǔ}: to cover; {排|pái}: row, lesson 04;
{鼓掌|gǔ zhǎng}: to clap; {用力|yòng lì}: hard, with force; {一|yí}{束|shù}{花|huā}: a bunch of flowers.)
</details>

### Part 3: answering questions

Answer each question aloud in four or five sentences: give your answer, a reason, an example and a
conclusion. Then compare.

```speak
# Questions to answer
{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{演出|yǎn chū}{吗|ma}？{为什么|wèi shén me}？——{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{看|kàn}{演出|yǎn chū}，{尤其|yóu qí}{是|shì}{话剧|huà jù}。{首先|shǒu xiān}，{在|zài}{剧院|jù yuàn}{里|lǐ}{看|kàn}{演员|yǎn yuán}{演|yǎn}，{比|bǐ}{在|zài}{网上|wǎng shàng}{看|kàn}{视频|shì pín}{有意思|yǒu yì si}{多|duō}{了|le}。{其次|qí cì}，{看|kàn}{完|wán}{以后|yǐ hòu}{可以|kě yǐ}{跟|gēn}{朋友|péng you}{讨论|tǎo lùn}。{比如|bǐ rú}{上|shàng}{个|gè}{月|yuè}{我|wǒ}{看|kàn}{了|le}{一|yí}{个|gè}{关于|guān yú}{老人|lǎo rén}{生活|shēng huó}{的|de}{话剧|huà jù}，{看|kàn}{完|wán}{以后|yǐ hòu}{我们|wǒ men}{聊|liáo}{了|le}{很|hěn}{久|jiǔ}。{总之|zǒng zhī}，{看|kàn}{演出|yǎn chū}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{最|zuì}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{的|de}{周末|zhōu mò}{活动|huó dòng}。
= Do you like going to shows? Why? — I love shows, especially plays. First, watching actors on stage is much more interesting than watching videos online. Second, afterwards you can talk it over with friends. Last month, for example, I saw a play about old people's lives, and we talked about it for ages afterwards. All in all, going to a show is my favourite weekend activity.
{学习|xué xí}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{乐器|yuè qì}{有|yǒu}{什么|shén me}{好处|hǎo chù}？——{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{学习|xué xí}{乐器|yuè qì}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{好处|hǎo chù}。{首先|shǒu xiān}，{可以|kě yǐ}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{放松|fàng sōng}，{工作|gōng zuò}{累|lèi}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{弹|tán}{一会儿|yí huìr}{琴|qín}，{心情|xīn qíng}{就|jiù}{好|hǎo}{多|duō}{了|le}。{其次|qí cì}，{学|xué}{乐器|yuè qì}{需要|xū yào}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{练习|liàn xí}，{可以|kě yǐ}{让|ràng}{人|rén}{变|biàn}{得|de}{更|gèng}{有|yǒu}{耐心|nài xīn}。{所以|suǒ yǐ}，{如果|rú guǒ}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}，{我|wǒ}{建议|jiàn yì}{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{学|xué}{一|yì}{种|zhǒng}{乐器|yuè qì}。
= What are the benefits of learning an instrument? — I think learning an instrument has many benefits. First, it helps you relax: when you're tired from work, playing for a while makes you feel much better. Second, learning an instrument takes practice every day, which makes you more patient. So if you have the time, I'd suggest everyone learn one.
```

{乐器|yuè qì} yuè qì is a musical instrument (HSK 6).

## Say it

```speak
# At the theatre
{今天|jīn tiān}{的|de}{演出|yǎn chū}{非常|fēi cháng}{精彩|jīng cǎi}。
= Today's performance was wonderful.
{她|tā}{弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín}{弹|tán}{得|de}{特别|tè bié}{好|hǎo}。
= She plays the piano really well.
{观众|guān zhòng}{都|dōu}{站|zhàn}{起来|qǐ lái}{了|le}。
= The whole audience stood up.
{首先|shǒu xiān}，{演员|yǎn yuán}{演|yǎn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}；{其次|qí cì}，{音乐|yīn yuè}{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}。
= First, the acting was good; second, the music was lovely.
{总之|zǒng zhī}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{一|yí}{次|cì}{难忘|nán wàng}{的|de}{演出|yǎn chū}。
= All in all, it was a performance to remember.
```

## Pronunciation

- {弹|tán} tán (to play strings) has a rising tone; in {子弹|zǐ dàn} (bullet) it's dàn.
- {钢琴|gāng qín} gāng qín: first, then second tone; {琴|qín} has *q* (like *ch* in "cheese") and *-in*.
- {京剧|jīng jù} jīng jù and {精彩|jīng cǎi} jīng cǎi: {京|jīng} and {精|jīng} are both jīng.
- {演员|yǎn yuán} yǎn yuán and {演唱|yǎn chàng} yǎn chàng: {演|yǎn} is third tone; before a second or fourth tone it stays low.
- {观众|guān zhòng} guān zhòng: {众|zhòng} is zhòng, the {众|zhòng} of {听众|tīng zhòng}.
- {首先|shǒu xiān} shǒu xiān and {其次|qí cì} qí cì: the *c* of cì is a strong *ts*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~{玩|wán}{钢琴|gāng qín}~~ / ~~{打|dǎ}{钢琴|gāng qín}~~: the piano is {弹|tán}: {弹|tán}{钢琴|gāng qín}. {玩|wán} is for games; {打|dǎ} is for drums and ball games.
- ~~{他|tā}{很|hěn}{精彩|jīng cǎi}~~ of a person: {精彩|jīng cǎi} is for a show, a match, a talk. Say {他|tā}{演|yǎn}{得|de}{很|hěn}{精彩|jīng cǎi} or {他|tā}{很|hěn}{优秀|yōu xiù}.
- {观众|guān zhòng} for a radio audience: listeners are {听众|tīng zhòng} (lesson 24); {观众|guān zhòng} watch.
- {首先|shǒu xiān} with nothing after it: a list that opens with {首先|shǒu xiān} needs at least a {其次|qí cì} or a {然后|rán hòu} later.
- ~~{首先|shǒu xiān}{我|wǒ}{洗|xǐ}{了|le}{手|shǒu}，{其次|qí cì}{我|wǒ}{做|zuò}{了|le}{饭|fàn}~~: steps in time take {然后|rán hòu}; {其次|qí cì} is for points in an argument.
- In the writing task, ~~{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{演出|yǎn chū}~~ for a picture of a singer on stage says nothing about the picture.
  Write what you see: {她|tā}{在|zài}{台上|tái shàng}{演唱|yǎn chàng}.

## Key points

- {演出|yǎn chū} (a show; to perform), {演|yǎn} (to act, to put on), {演员|yǎn yuán}, {演唱|yǎn chàng} (to sing on stage), {歌手|gē shǒu}, {歌声|gē shēng}, {观众|guān zhòng},
  {剧院|jù yuàn}, {话剧|huà jù}, {京剧|jīng jù}, {艺术|yì shù}, {精彩|jīng cǎi} (of shows, not people).
- Instruments: {弹|tán} (piano, strings), {拉|lā} (bowed), {吹|chuī} (wind), {打|dǎ} (drums).
- Discourse markers: {首先|shǒu xiān}…{其次|qí cì}…{最后|zuì hòu} (points), {首先|shǒu xiān}…{然后|rán hòu} (steps), {另外|lìng wài} / {此外|cǐ wài} (extra), {总之|zǒng zhī} (in short);
  {总结|zǒng jié} (to sum up).
- Writing, as reported: five sentences with given words about pictures; a text of at least 80
  characters with an opening, points and a close.
- Speaking, as reported: retell two passages; a three-picture story; two questions (answer,
  reason, example, conclusion).
- New characters: {钢|gāng} {琴|qín} {京|jīng} {精|jīng} {彩|cǎi} {弹|tán} {艺|yì} (✎ {京|jīng}).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: The HSK 4 exam
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

You now know the 2,000 words and 1,096 characters that the new HSK 4 covers, and the grammar of the
level: the extended {把|bǎ} sentence and the {叫|jiào} / {让|ràng} passive, {不如|bù rú} and {跟|gēn}…{相比|xiāng bǐ}, double negatives, rhetorical
{难道|nán dào}, the written words {由|yóu}, {将|jiāng}, {与|yǔ}, {此|cǐ} and {之|zhī}, and the connector pairs from {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù} to {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě}. This last
lesson is about the exam itself: how it is built, the kinds of task, how to use your time, a short
practice set written for this course, and a page for the 150 characters to write by hand. It adds
no new words.

Everything here about the exam's format comes from reports on the official sample papers, which we
couldn't open ourselves. Formats can change: before you register, check the official HSK website
of Chinese Testing International (chinesetest.cn) and do an official sample paper.

## The new HSK 4

The **[[HSK]]** ({汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}{考试|kǎo shì}, the Chinese Proficiency Test) in its new version, often called HSK 3.0, has
nine levels; its syllabus was published in November 2025 and has been in force since July 2026.
Level 4 is the first of the three intermediate levels: 1,000 new words (2,000 in all), 441 new
characters (1,096 in all) and 400 characters to write by hand. The first official sitting of the
new exam was announced for 13 December 2026, after two pilot rounds; dates change, so check them on the
official site.

| Part | Questions | Time | Tasks, as reported |
|---|---|---|---|
| Listening | 32 (in two parts, 14 and 18) | about 20 minutes | listen and choose one of four answers: short dialogues, longer dialogues and short talks |
| Reading | 32 (10 + 15 + 7) | 30 minutes | a word for each gap from six choices (one is extra); short passages with questions; putting sentences back into a passage |
| Writing | 6 (5 + 1) | 25 minutes | five sentences, each with a given word, about a picture; a short text of at least 80 characters |
| **Written exam** | **70** | **about 85 minutes** in all, with time for your details and for the answer sheet | |
| Speaking test | 5 (2 + 1 + 2) | about 20 minutes, with about 10 minutes' preparation | retelling two short passages; a story from three numbered photos; answering two questions |

The question counts and times agree across the two detailed reports we found; the breakdown of the
speaking test comes from one of them. In the 2026 pilot rounds, candidates for levels 3–6 registered
for the **[[speaking test]]** together with the written exam, and two guides say the same of the new
exam; one report says that in Japan the two can still be registered and scored separately. Check the
rules where you will take it. The exam can be on paper or on a computer, depending on the test
centre.

### Listening

As reported, you hear short dialogues, longer dialogues and short talks (announcements, messages,
short accounts) and choose one of four answers. The 2021 standard's description of level 4 speaks of informal talk of
up to about 400 characters at 180–200 characters a minute, a normal speed. Questions ask
where, when and why, what someone will do, and above all what someone **means** or **feels**: a
rhetorical question ({难道|nán dào}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{吗|ma}？ = you must know), a polite refusal ({我|wǒ}{本来|běn lái}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{可是|kě shì}…), a point
that comes after {不过|bú guò} or {其实|qí shí}.

### Reading

The three reported parts:

1. **A word for each gap.** A passage or a set of sentences with gaps, and six words to choose from,
   one of them extra. Each word is used once.
2. **Short passages with questions**: notices, emails, adverts, short articles and stories, with four
   choices. Some questions ask what a word or sentence means in context, or what the writer implies.
3. **Putting sentences back.** A passage has gaps, and you choose which sentence goes in each. The
   connectors and the pronouns are the clues (see Strategies).

### Writing

Lesson 29 practised both reported tasks: five sentences, each built on a given word and about a
picture, and a text of at least 80 characters. On paper you write by hand; on a computer, check how
answers are entered when you register, and practise both handwriting and typing with pinyin.

### Speaking

Lesson 29 practised the three reported parts: retelling a short passage you hear (two of them;
the time is reported as about 40 seconds each, and one report says each passage is heard once), telling a story from three numbered photos (3 minutes' preparation, 2 to
speak), and answering two questions (about 3½ minutes' preparation, 2 to speak).

## Scoring

The old HSK 4 gave up to 100 points each for listening, reading and writing, and was passed with 180
of 300. For the new exam, no score scale or pass mark had been published in the sources we found:
don't assume the old figures still apply.

## Strategies

### Before the exam

- **Do an official sample paper**, first without a timer, then with one.
- **Review every word.** Your vocabulary reviews hold all 2,000 words of HSK 1–4. In the last
  weeks, bring every word to at least Advanced, and spend most time on the ones you keep missing.
- **Read with pinyin off**, in the reviews and in the lessons: the exam has none.
- **Listen every day**: the dialogues and speaking passages of modules 4–6, first with the words
  hidden.
- **Write by hand**: ten minutes a day on the page of 150 characters at the end of this lesson, and
  the 250 earlier ones in the character reference.
- **Speak for a minute a day** on a topic of the course (study, work, travel, health, family, the
  environment, the arts): opening, two points, a conclusion.

### During the exam

1. **Read the choices before the audio.** They tell you what to listen for: times, places, people,
   or an opinion.
2. **Listen for the turn.** What comes after {可是|kě shì}, {不过|bú guò}, {其实|qí shí}, {却|què} and {然而|rán'ér} is usually the answer; a
   rhetorical {难道|nán dào}…{吗|ma} or {不|bú}{是|shì}…{吗|ma} means the opposite of its form.
3. **Skim, then scan.** **[[Skimming]]**: read the title, the first and the last sentence to know what a
   text is about. **[[Scanning]]**: read the question, then look for the one fact it asks for.
4. **For a gap, decide the part of speech first.** After {很|hěn} or {非常|fēi cháng} comes an adjective; between a number
   and a noun, a measure word; before a verb, an adverb or a modal. Then check pairs: {即使|jí shǐ} → {也|yě}, {不但|bú dàn} /
   {不仅|bù jǐn} → {而且|ér qiě} / {还|hái}, {尽管|jǐn guǎn} → {但是|dàn shì} / {却|què}, {既然|jì rán} → {就|jiù}, {不管|bù guǎn} / {无论|wú lùn} → {都|dōu}, {只有|zhǐ yǒu} → {才|cái}.
5. **To put a sentence back, follow the links** (**[[sentence insertion]]**):
   - {首先|shǒu xiān}, {其次|qí cì}, {最后|zuì hòu} and {第|dì}{一|yī}, {第|dì}{二|èr} keep their order;
   - {于是|yú shì}, {因此|yīn cǐ}, {所以|suǒ yǐ} need a cause just before them; {但是|dàn shì}, {可是|kě shì}, {却|què} need something to contrast with;
   - {他|tā}, {她|tā}, {这|zhè}, {那|nà} and {这样|zhè yàng} point back to something already named;
   - {也|yě} and {还|hái} add to something of the same kind just mentioned.
6. **Answer every question.** Cross out what you know is wrong, then choose.
7. **Check your sentences** in the writing part: time and place before the verb, a measure word with
   every number, {了|le} and {过|guo} for the past, {的|de} / {地|de} / {得|de}, the pairs complete.

> {我|wǒ}{的|de}{老家|lǎo jiā}{在|zài}{北方|běi fāng}{的|de}{一|yí}{个|gè}{小|xiǎo}{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}。{那儿|nàr}{冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，(1) ___ {是|shì}{一|yī}{月|yuè}，{夜里|yè lǐ}{常常|cháng cháng}{到|dào}{零下|líng xià}{二十|èr shí}{度|dù}。(2) ___ {天气|tiān qì}{这么|zhè me}{冷|lěng}，{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{老人|lǎo rén}{每|měi}{天|tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{还是|hái shi}{去|qù}{河|hé}{边|biān}{散步|sàn bù}。{这|zhè}{几|jǐ}{年|nián}，{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{路|lù} (3) ___ {变|biàn}{好|hǎo}，{去|qù}{城|chéng}{里|lǐ}{也|yě}{方便|fāng biàn}{了|le}，(4) ___ {很|hěn}{多|duō}{年轻|nián qīng}{人|rén}{回|huí}{村|cūn}{里|lǐ}{开|kāi}{了|le}{饭馆|fàn guǎn}。{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{打算|dǎ suàn}{明年|míng nián}{回去|huí qù}，{让|ràng}{父母|fù mǔ}{的|de}{生活|shēng huó} (5) ___ {方便|fāng biàn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}。

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

(1) {尤其|yóu qí}: especially January. (2) {尽管|jǐn guǎn}: although it's so cold (a fact), with {还是|hái shi} in the second clause.
(3) {不断|bú duàn}: the roads keep getting better. (4) {于是|yú shì}: so, what happened next. (5) {稍微|shāo wēi}: a little more
convenient, with {一点儿|yì diǎnr} after the adjective. The extra word is {而|ér}: none of the gaps needs a written
"and, but".

## Can you do this?

- Describe an illness to a doctor: where it hurts, since when, how badly (lesson 06).
- Write a short job advertisement and answer questions about it (lesson 11).
- Follow a written notice (a rule, a delay, a change of plan) and say what to do (lessons 13, 17,
  28).
- Tell a story with its cause, process and result, from pictures or from memory (lessons 20, 28,
  29).
- Give an opinion with reasons and examples, and sum up (lessons 25, 29).
- Write 80–120 characters on a familiar topic, with an opening, two points and a conclusion (lesson
  29).
- Retell a short passage you've heard, keeping its order (lessons 27, 29).

If one of these is shaky, go back to its lesson and redo its questions before the exam.

## Common mistakes in the exam

- Taking a rhetorical question at face value: {难道|nán dào}{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{吗|ma}？ means "surely you know".
- Mixing the pairs: {即使|jí shǐ}…{也|yě} (not {就|jiù}), {尽管|jǐn guǎn}…{但是|dàn shì} / {还是|hái shi}, {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}, {不管|bù guǎn}…{都|dōu}, {只有|zhǐ yǒu}…{才|cái}.
- Missing the turn: in {我|wǒ}{本来|běn lái}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}，{可是|kě shì}…, the answer is what follows {可是|kě shì}.
- Using {于是|yú shì} for advice or a plan: {于是|yú shì} tells what happened next.
- In writing, a sentence that doesn't describe the picture, or that leaves out the given word.
- In writing, English word order: ~~{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{明年|míng nián}~~ → {我|wǒ}{明年|míng nián}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}.
- Leaving a gap empty: a guess may be right; an empty answer never is.

## Key points

- New HSK 4, as reported: listening 32, reading 32, writing 6 (70 questions, about 85 minutes), and
  a speaking test of 5 tasks in about 20 minutes, registered with the written exam. Check the
  official site for changes.
- Pass mark not published for the new exam (the old HSK 4: 180 of 300).
- Before: a sample paper, every word to Advanced, pinyin off, daily listening, handwriting, a minute
  of speaking a day.
- During: choices before the audio, listen for the turn, skim then scan, decide the part of speech
  for a gap, follow the connectors to put sentences back, answer everything, check your sentences.

That's the end of the course. {祝|zhù}{你|nǐ}{考试|kǎo shì}{顺利|shùn lì}！ (Good luck in the exam!)

lessons.title: Chinese instruments: guqin, guzheng, pipa, erhu
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 29 taught the verbs of music: {弹|tán} for what you pluck or press, {拉|lā} for what you bow, {吹|chuī} for what
you blow. This honors lesson puts them to work on four instruments you'll hear in any concert of
Chinese music, and then reads a concert programme ({节目单|jié mù dān}) in Chinese. It adds no words to your
reviews; the new instrument names are glossed where they appear.

## Four instruments

### {古琴|gǔ qín}: the scholar's zither

The {古琴|gǔ qín} (guqin; {古|gǔ}, ancient, HSK 5) is a long, narrow wooden zither with **seven strings**,
played lying flat on a table. The right hand plucks ({弹|tán}) and the left hand presses the strings or
just touches them lightly to make soft, ringing overtones. Its sound is quiet and low, made for a
small room rather than a hall.

UNESCO describes the instrument as more than 3,000 years old and its music as an art practised by
noblemen and scholars in intimate settings. In 2003 UNESCO proclaimed "guqin and its music" a
Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity, and in 2008 it was inscribed on the
Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. One of its best-known pieces is
《{流水|Liú shuǐ}》 (Flowing Water), which tradition links with the musician {伯牙|Bó Yá}.

### {古筝|gǔ zhēng}: the zither with bridges

The {古筝|gǔ zhēng} (guzheng) is also a zither played flat, but larger and brighter. The most common
kind has **21 strings**, and each string rests on a small **movable bridge**: moving the bridges
changes the tuning. Players usually wear small picks on their fingers and pluck with both hands. A
popular piece is 《{渔舟唱晚|Yú zhōu chàng wǎn}》 (Fishing Boats Singing at Dusk), in the arrangement of
{娄树华|Lóu Shù huá}.

The guqin has no bridges at all, which is the easiest way to tell the two apart.

### {琵琶|pí pa}: the pear-shaped lute

The {琵琶|pí pa} (pipa) has a pear-shaped wooden body and **four strings**. It's held upright, or almost
upright, on the lap, and plucked with the fingers of the right hand, very fast when the music calls
for it. It has been played in China for almost two thousand years. Its most famous solo,
《{十面埋伏|Shí miàn mái fú}》 (Ambush from Ten Sides), tells of a battle of the Chu–Han war (about
2,200 years ago): you hear horses, drums and fighting in the strings.

### {二胡|èr hú}: the two-stringed fiddle

The {二胡|èr hú} (erhu; {二|èr}, two) has **two strings** and is played with a bow ({拉|lā}{二胡|èr hú}). Its small
sound box, usually covered with snakeskin, rests on the player's knee, and the instrument stands
upright. Unusually, the hair of the bow passes **between** the two strings, so bow and instrument
never come apart. The erhu's voice is often compared to a human voice singing; one of its best-known
pieces is 《{二泉映月|Èr quán yìng yuè}》 (Moon Reflected on Second Spring), by the blind musician
{华彦钧|Huá Yàn jūn}, known as {阿炳|Ā Bǐng}, and recorded in 1950.

| Instrument | Strings | How it's played | Verb |
|---|---|---|---|
| {古琴|gǔ qín} guqin | 7 | flat on a table, plucked, no bridges | {弹|tán} |
| {古筝|gǔ zhēng} guzheng | usually 21 | flat, plucked with picks, movable bridges | {弹|tán} |
| {琵琶|pí pa} pipa | 4 | held upright, plucked | {弹|tán} |
| {二胡|èr hú} erhu | 2 | upright on the knee, bowed | {拉|lā} |

## Words for a concert

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {乐器|yuè qì} | musical instrument (HSK 6) |
| {乐曲|yuè qǔ} / {曲子|qǔ zi} | a piece of music |
| {独奏|dú zòu} | solo (to play alone) |
| {合奏|hé zòu} | ensemble (to play together) |
| {节目单|jié mù dān} | a programme (of a concert): {节目|jié mù} + {单|dān} (a list) |
| {弦|xián} | a string (of an instrument) |

{乐|yuè} in these words is yuè, "music", as in {音乐|yīn yuè}; the same character is lè in {快乐|kuài lè} (happy).

1. Which instrument is played lying on a table, and how many strings does it have?
2. What do the "{小桥|xiǎo qiáo}" of the guzheng do? (Use what you read in the lesson.)

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. The guqin ({弹|tán}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{放|fàng}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}), with seven strings ({有|yǒu}{七|qī}{根|gēn}{弦|xián}).

   programme invites them to sing along.

"**Concert of Chinese instruments: programme.** Time: Friday 30 November, 7.30 p.m. Place: the school
concert hall. **1. Guqin solo, Flowing Water.** The guqin is one of China's oldest instruments. It has
seven strings and is played lying on a table. Its sound isn't loud: it's very quiet, suited to
listening in a small room. This piece calls to mind water flowing in the mountains: please listen
quietly. **2. Guzheng solo, Fishing Boats Singing at Dusk.** The guzheng is bigger than the guqin; the
usual kind has twenty-one strings, each with a movable 'little bridge' under it. This piece is about
fishermen singing as they go home at sunset. **3. Pipa solo, Ambush from Ten Sides.** The pipa has
four strings, and the player holds it to play. This piece tells of a great battle over two thousand
years ago; the player plays very fast, and you can almost hear the horses. **4. Erhu solo, Moon
Reflected on Second Spring.** The erhu has only two strings and is played with a bow. Its sound is
very like a human singing voice and can express many feelings. This piece was written by a
musician who could not see, and people who hear it are often moved. **5. Ensemble, Jasmine Flower.**
To end, all the performers play together this song that many Chinese people can sing. You're welcome
to sing along! Please don't take photos during the performance, and please turn off your phones.
Thank you!"
</details>

## Key points

- {古琴|gǔ qín}: seven strings, flat on a table, plucked, no bridges; UNESCO's Masterpiece list in 2003, the
  Representative List in 2008.
- {古筝|gǔ zhēng}: usually 21 strings on movable bridges, plucked with picks.
- {琵琶|pí pa}: four strings, pear-shaped, held upright, plucked; 《{十面埋伏|Shí miàn mái fú}》.
- {二胡|èr hú}: two strings, bowed, the bow hair between the strings; 《{二泉映月|Èr quán yìng yuè}》.
- {弹|tán} for the first three, {拉|lā} for the erhu; {独奏|dú zòu} (solo), {合奏|hé zòu} (ensemble), {节目单|jié mù dān} (programme).

lessons.title: More from the Analects: three sayings
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 3's honors lesson on Confucius read three of his best-known sayings ({学|xué}{而|ér}{时|shí}{习|xí}{之|zhī}, {三|sān}{人|rén}{行|xíng} and {温|wēn}{故|gù}{而|ér}{知|zhī}{新|xīn}).
This one reads three more, each a single line of classical Chinese that people in China still
quote: on learning and thinking, on how to treat others, and on knowing what you know. For each you
get the text with pinyin, notes on the words, a paraphrase in modern Chinese and our own
translation, then a word on how readers have understood it. This is the history of ideas: what the
text says and how it has been read, not advice for your life.

The lesson adds no words to your reviews. Classical words are glossed where they appear.

## The Analects

《{论语|Lún yǔ}》, the Analects, is a collection of sayings and short conversations of {孔子|Kǒng zǐ}
(Confucius, traditionally dated 551–479 BCE) and some of his disciples. It was put together by his
followers after his death; scholars think it grew over a long time, and its twenty books are not a
single treatise but many short entries. For two thousand years it was one of the texts every
educated person learned, and many of its lines became set phrases.

Each entry usually begins {子曰|Zǐ yuē}: "the Master said". {曰|yuē} is the classical "to say"
(modern {说|shuō}); {子|zǐ}, "master", is the respectful way the book refers to Confucius.

## {学|xué}{而|ér}{不|bù}{思|sī}{则|zé}{罔|wǎng}，{思|sī}{而|ér}{不|bù}{学|xué}{则|zé}{殆|dài}

> {子曰|Zǐ yuē}：{学|xué}{而|ér}{不|bù}{思|sī}{则|zé}{罔|wǎng}，{思|sī}{而|ér}{不|bù}{学|xué}{则|zé}{殆|dài}。

From the second book of the Analects ({为政|Wéi zhèng}, 2.15).

| Word | Meaning here | Modern Chinese |
|---|---|---|
| {学|xué} | to learn, study (from teachers, books) | {学习|xué xí} |
| {而|ér} | and yet, but (lesson 05) | {但是|dàn shì} / {却|què} |
| {思|sī} | to think, reflect | {思考|sī kǎo} (HSK 5) |
| {则|zé} | then, in that case: the {则|zé} of {否则|fǒu zé} (lesson 11) | {就|jiù} |
| {罔|wǎng} | confused, at a loss | {不|bù}{明白|míng bai} |
| {殆|dài} | in danger, at risk | {危险|wēi xiǎn} |

**In modern Chinese:** {只|zhǐ}{学习|xué xí}，{不|bù}{思考|sī kǎo}，{就|jiù}{会|huì}{越|yuè}{学|xué}{越|yuè}{不|bù}{明白|míng bai}；{只|zhǐ}{思考|sī kǎo}，{不|bù}{学习|xué xí}，{就|jiù}{容易|róng yì}{出|chū}{问题|wèn tí}，{很|hěn}{危险|wēi xiǎn}。

**Our translation:** "Learning without thinking leaves you lost; thinking without learning puts you
in danger."

The two halves mirror each other, and the line is often quoted as a balance: study what others know,
and think it through yourself. Readers have differed on the last word: dictionaries give {殆|dài} here as
"in danger, uneasy", and some explain it as standing for {怠|dài}, "idle": thinking that never turns
into work. Either way, the saying asks for both halves together.

## {己|jǐ}{所|suǒ}{不|bú}{欲|yù}，{勿|wù}{施|shī}{于|yú}{人|rén}

> {子贡|Zǐ gòng}{问|wèn}{曰|yuē}：「{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{言|yán}{而|ér}{可以|kě yǐ}{终身|zhōng shēn}{行|xíng}{之|zhī}{者|zhě}{乎|hū}？」{子|zǐ}{曰|yuē}：「{其|qí}{恕|shù}{乎|hū}！{己|jǐ}{所|suǒ}{不|bú}{欲|yù}，{勿|wù}{施|shī}{于|yú}{人|rén}。」

From the fifteenth book ({卫灵公|Wèi Líng gōng}, 15.24). The disciple {子贡|Zǐ gòng} asks: "Is there one word that you
can live by all your life?" The Master answers: "Surely it's {恕|shù}, reciprocity! What you do not
want for yourself, do not do to others."

| Word | Meaning here | Modern Chinese |
|---|---|---|
| {己|jǐ} | oneself (the {己|jǐ} of {自己|zì jǐ}) | {自己|zì jǐ} |
| {所|suǒ} + verb | what (one…): {所|suǒ}{欲|yù}, what one wants | …{的|de}({东西|dōng xi}) |
| {欲|yù} | to want, wish for | {想要|xiǎng yào} |
| {勿|wù} | do not (the {勿|wù} of signs, lesson 28) | {不要|bú yào} |
| {施|shī} | to do (something) to, impose on | {对|duì}…{做|zuò}, {给|gěi} |
| {于|yú} | to, on (written, as in {用于|yòng yú}, {对于|duì yú}) | {对|duì}, {给|gěi} |
| {恕|shù} | putting yourself in another's place; reciprocity | {理解|lǐ jiě}{别人|bié ren} |

**In modern Chinese:** {自己|zì jǐ}{不|bú}{愿意|yuàn yì}{别人|bié ren}{对|duì}{自己|zì jǐ}{做|zuò}{的|de}{事|shì}，{也|yě}{不要|bú yào}{对|duì}{别人|bié ren}{做|zuò}。

**Our translation:** "What you would not want for yourself, do not do to others."

Many readers have compared this line with the "Golden Rule" found in other traditions ("Do to
others as you would have them do to you"); others point out that Confucius puts it as a negative,
what not to do, and some call it the "Silver Rule" for that reason. In the Analects it is tied to
{恕|shù}, the habit of judging how you treat others by how you would feel in their place.

## {知|zhī}{之|zhī}{为|wéi}{知|zhī}{之|zhī}，{不|bù}{知|zhī}{为|wéi}{不|bù}{知|zhī}，{是|shì}{知|zhì}{也|yě}

> {子曰|Zǐ yuē}：……{知|zhī}{之|zhī}{为|wéi}{知|zhī}{之|zhī}，{不|bù}{知|zhī}{为|wéi}{不|bù}{知|zhī}，{是|shì}{知|zhì}{也|yě}。

From the second book ({为政|Wéi zhèng}, 2.17), where the Master is speaking to his disciple {子路|Zǐ lù} (we quote
the saying itself, without his opening words).

| Word | Meaning here | Modern Chinese |
|---|---|---|
| {知|zhī} zhī | to know | {知道|zhī dào} |
| {之|zhī} | it (lesson 21's {之|zhī}, here as an object) | {它|tā} |
| {为|wéi} wéi | to treat as, take to be (lesson 12's {为|wéi} wéi) | {当|dāng}{作|zuò}, {就是|jiù shì} |
| {是|shì} | this (classical: not "to be") | {这|zhè} |
| {知|zhì} zhì | wisdom (written {智|zhì} in later texts) | {智慧|zhì huì}, {聪明|cōng ming} |
| {也|yě} | a full stop for a statement (not "also") | — |

The last {知|zhì} is read zhì in most modern editions: it stands for {智|zhì}, wisdom. {是|shì} here is the classical
"this", the use you know from {于是|yú shì} (lesson 28: "upon this").

**In modern Chinese:** {知道|zhī dào}{就是|jiù shì}{知道|zhī dào}，{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{就是|jiù shì}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}，{这|zhè}{才|cái}{是|shì}{真正|zhēn zhèng}{的|de}{聪明|cōng ming}。

**Our translation:** "To take what you know as known, and what you don't know as not known: that is
wisdom."

The line is often quoted against pretending to know, in a classroom or a meeting: being honest about
the limits of what you know is itself a kind of wisdom. Some readers also hear in it an
encouragement to find out what you don't yet know.

## Say them

```speak
# Three sayings
{学|xué}{而|ér}{不|bù}{思|sī}{则|zé}{罔|wǎng}，{思|sī}{而|ér}{不|bù}{学|xué}{则|zé}{殆|dài}。
= Learning without thinking leaves you lost; thinking without learning puts you in danger.
{己|jǐ}{所|suǒ}{不|bú}{欲|yù}，{勿|wù}{施|shī}{于|yú}{人|rén}。
= What you would not want for yourself, do not do to others.
{知|zhī}{之|zhī}{为|wéi}{知|zhī}{之|zhī}，{不|bù}{知|zhī}{为|wéi}{不|bù}{知|zhī}，{是|shì}{知|zhì}{也|yě}。
= To take what you know as known, and what you don't know as not known: that is wisdom.
```

A voice may read the last {知|zhì} as zhī; the standard reading is zhì.

## Reading them again

Each saying is built like a set phrase: short clauses, parallel shapes, no {的|de} and few function words.
Look at the shapes:

- {学|xué}{而|ér}{不|bù}{思|sī} / {思|sī}{而|ér}{不|bù}{学|xué}: the same four characters, with {学|xué} and {思|sī} swapped.
- {知|zhī}{之|zhī}{为|wéi}{知|zhī}{之|zhī} / {不|bù}{知|zhī}{为|wéi}{不|bù}{知|zhī}: "X {为|wéi} X" twice, the second with {不|bù}.
- {己|jǐ}{所|suǒ}{不|bú}{欲|yù} / {勿|wù}{施|shī}{于|yú}{人|rén}: four and four, "oneself" against "others" ({人|rén}).

That parallelism is what makes them easy to remember, and why they turn up in essays, speeches and
school walls. When you meet a four-character phrase in a modern text (lesson 22's {有|yǒu}{说|shuō}{有|yǒu}{笑|xiào}, HSK 5's
{成语|chéng yǔ}), you'll often find the same balance.

## Key points

- 《{论语|Lún yǔ}》, the Analects: sayings and conversations of Confucius (traditionally 551–479 BCE) and his
  disciples, put together after his death; entries begin {子曰|Zǐ yuē}.
- {学|xué}{而|ér}{不|bù}{思|sī}{则|zé}{罔|wǎng}，{思|sī}{而|ér}{不|bù}{学|xué}{则|zé}{殆|dài} (2.15): learning and thinking need each other.
- {己|jǐ}{所|suǒ}{不|bú}{欲|yù}，{勿|wù}{施|shī}{于|yú}{人|rén} (15.24): don't do to others what you wouldn't want; tied to {恕|shù} (reciprocity).
- {知|zhī}{之|zhī}{为|wéi}{知|zhī}{之|zhī}，{不|bù}{知|zhī}{为|wéi}{不|bù}{知|zhī}，{是|shì}{知|zhì}{也|yě} (2.17): admit what you don't know; the last {知|zhì} is zhì.
- Classical words: {而|ér} (and yet), {则|zé} (then), {己|jǐ} (oneself), {所|suǒ} (what), {欲|yù} (want), {勿|wù} (do not), {施|shī} (do to),
  {于|yú} (to), {之|zhī} (it), {为|wéi} wéi (take as), {是|shì} (this), {也|yě} (a full stop).

questions.stem: Choose the pair: ___ {你|nǐ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{决定|jué dìng}{了|le}， ___ {别|bié}{担心|dān xīn}{了|le}。 (Since you've made up your mind, stop worrying.)
questions.explanation: The first clause is a fact both speakers accept (you have decided), and the second draws a conclusion from it (so don't worry): that is {既然|jì rán}…{就|jiù}. {因为|yīn wèi}…{所以|suǒ yǐ} states a cause and its result, {如果|rú guǒ}…{就|jiù} imagines (if you decide…), and {虽然|suī rán}…{但是|dàn shì} is "although… but".

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct? (Since it's raining, let's not go.)
choices: {既然|jì rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{别|bié}{去|qù}{了|le}。
{既然|jì rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{就|jiù}{我们|wǒ men}{别|bié}{去|qù}{了|le}。
{既然|jì rán}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}，{所以|suǒ yǐ}{我们|wǒ men}{别|bié}{去|qù}{了|le}。
{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}{既然|jì rán}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{别|bié}{去|qù}{了|le}。
questions.explanation: {既然|jì rán} pairs with {就|jiù} (or {那|nà}, {还|hái}), not with {所以|suǒ yǐ}. {就|jiù} is an adverb, so it follows the subject of the second clause: {我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{别|bié}{去|qù}{了|le}. {既然|jì rán} itself starts its clause (or follows the subject: {你|nǐ}{既然|jì rán}{知道|zhī dào}{了|le}…), never after the verb.

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{本来|běn lái}{想|xiǎng}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{去|qù}，{后来|hòu lái}{买|mǎi}{到|dào}{了|le}{机票|jī piào}。" tell you?
choices: The speaker always travels by train.
The speaker went by train, as planned.
The speaker couldn't get a plane ticket.
The speaker had meant to go by train, but went by plane.
questions.explanation: {本来|běn lái} is "originally, at first", before something changed, and {后来|hòu lái} (later) tells you what changed: a plane ticket was bought. So the first plan, the train, was dropped.

questions.stem: Choose the words: {我|wǒ} ___ {上海|Shàng hǎi}，{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{那儿|nàr}{冬天|dōng tiān}{冷|lěng}{不|bu}{冷|lěng}。 (I've never been to Shanghai, so I don't know whether it's cold there in winter.)
questions.explanation: "Never (once, up to now)" is an experience: {从来|cóng lái}{没|méi} + verb + {过|guo}, here {从来|cóng lái}{没|méi}{去|qù}{过|guo}. {从来|cóng lái}{不|bú}{去|qù} is "never go" as a habit or a choice, which doesn't fit "I don't know what it's like". {从来|cóng lái} is seldom used without a negative, and {本来|běn lái}{没|méi}{去|qù} would be "originally didn't go".

questions.stem: A speaker opens a meeting: "___ {老师|lǎo shī}、 ___ {同学|tóng xué}，{大家|dà jiā}{好|hǎo}！" Which word fills both gaps?
questions.explanation: {各位|gè wèi} is the polite way to address a group: {各位|gè wèi}{老师|lǎo shī}、{各位|gè wèi}{同学|tóng xué} (teachers, students). {各种|gè zhǒng} is "all kinds of" ({各种|gè zhǒng}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}), {各个|gè gè} "each and every" ({各个|gè gè}{学院|xué yuàn}), and {任何|rèn hé} "any" ({任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}): none of them addresses people.

questions.stem: How do you say "Anyone can take part."?
choices: {任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。
{任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。
{任何|rèn hé}{个|gè}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。
{人|rén}{任何|rèn hé}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}。
questions.explanation: {任何|rèn hé} + noun before the verb needs {都|dōu} (or {也|yě}): {任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā}. {任何|rèn hé} takes the noun directly, without {个|gè}, and goes before it. {任何|rèn hé}{人|rén}{都|dōu}{不|bù}{可以|kě yǐ}{参加|cān jiā} says the opposite: no one may take part.

questions.stem: A college notice: "{本|běn}{学期|xué qī}{的|de}{课程表|kè chéng biǎo}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{学院|xué yuàn}{网站|wǎng zhàn}{上|shàng}，{请|qǐng}{大家|dà jiā}{认真|rèn zhēn}{查看|chá kàn}。 ___ ，{学院|xué yuàn}{还|hái}{为|wèi}{四年级|sì nián jí}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{准备|zhǔn bèi}{了|le}{一|yì}{门|mén}{写作|xiě zuò}{课|kè}。" ({查看|chá kàn}: to look over; {写作|xiě zuò}: writing) Which word fits a written notice best?
questions.explanation: The gap starts a new point ("in addition"), and the text is a formal notice, so the written word {此外|cǐ wài} fits. {还|hái}{有|yǒu} means much the same but is the spoken choice. {那么|nà me} (so, then) and {所以|suǒ yǐ} (therefore) would make the course a result of checking the timetable.

questions.stem: A notice says "{此次|cǐ cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{在|zài}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}。" How would you say {此次|cǐ cì} to a friend?
questions.explanation: {此|cǐ} is the written "this", so {此次|cǐ cì} is the written {这|zhè}{次|cì} (this time, on this occasion): {这|zhè}{次|cì}{考试|kǎo shì}{在|zài}{三|sān}{楼|lóu}. {那|nà}{次|cì} is "that time", {此外|cǐ wài} "besides", and {这里|zhè lǐ} "here".

questions.stem: You meet your Chinese teacher in the corridor. What do you say?
questions.explanation: {老师|lǎo shī} is how you address a teacher. {教师|jiào shī} is the formal word for the job ({一|yì}{名|míng}{中学|zhōng xué}{教师|jiào shī}, on forms and in the news) and is never used to address anyone. {教授|jiào shòu} is for a professor, with the surname ({罗|Luó}{教授|jiào shòu}{好|hǎo}), and {师生|shī shēng} means "teachers and students".

questions.stem: Choose the verb: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng} ___ {学校|xué xiào}{的|de}{足球|zú qiú}{队|duì}，{当|dāng}{一|yì}{名|míng}{队员|duì yuán}。 (I'd like to join the university football team and be a member.) ({队|duì}: team; {队员|duì yuán}: team member)
questions.explanation: To become a member of a team or an organisation is {加入|jiā rù}. ({参加|cān jiā}{足球|zú qiú}{队|duì} is heard in speech too, but {参加|cān jiā} is above all for events: {参加|cān jiā}{比赛|bǐ sài}, {参加|cān jiā}{考试|kǎo shì}.) {熟悉|shú xī} is to know well, {入学|rù xué} to start school, and {适应|shì yìng} to adapt.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {专业|zhuān yè} zhuān yè (major, subject): a high level tone, then a falling one, 1+4.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {本科|běn kē} běn kē (undergraduate study): a dipping tone, then a high level one, 3+1.

questions.stem: Write the missing character (in characters, or pinyin with tone marks): {我们|wǒ men}{中午|zhōng wǔ}{在|zài}{食|shí} ___ {吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。 (We have lunch in the canteen.)
questions.explanation: {食堂|shí táng} shí táng (canteen). {={堂|táng}=} is ⺌ and {冖|mì} over {口|kǒu}, with {土|tǔ} at the bottom: the same top as {常|cháng} cháng, which gives a close sound.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? ___ {业|yè} (major, subject of study)
questions.explanation: {专业|zhuān yè} zhuān yè. {={专|zhuān}=} has only four strokes: two horizontals, one stroke that goes down, turns and sweeps left, and a dot. {传|chuán} (亻 + {专|zhuān}, chuán) and {转|zhuǎn} ({车|chē} + {专|zhuān}, zhuǎn) are built on it, and {车|chē} chē is a car.

questions.stem: Listen to two friends. What does the second one suggest?

audio.text:
明天的课不上了，老师病了。
既然明天不上课，我们就去爬山吧。

choices: going hiking, since there's no class
studying at home, because it will rain
questions.explanation: The first speaker says tomorrow's class is off because the teacher is ill. The second takes that as an accepted fact and draws a conclusion: {既然|jì rán}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bú}{上课|shàng kè}，{我们|wǒ men}{就|jiù}{去|qù}{爬|pá}{山|shān}{吧|ba} (since there's no class tomorrow, let's go hiking).

questions.stem: Listen to the start of an announcement. Who is it for?

audio.text: 各位同学，大家好！欢迎此次春季入学的新同学加入我们学院。

choices: the students, especially the new ones starting this spring

questions.stem: How do you say "I've already handed in my homework."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}。
{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{交|jiāo}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{了|le}。
{我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{把|bǎ}{交|jiāo}{作业|zuò yè}{了|le}。
questions.explanation: Subject + {已经|yǐ jīng} + {把|bǎ} + object + verb + {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{已经|yǐ jīng}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{交|jiāo}{了|le}. {已经|yǐ jīng} goes before {把|bǎ}, and the verb needs something after it (here {了|le}), so {我|wǒ}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{已经|yǐ jīng}{交|jiāo} is wrong twice. {把|bǎ} always comes before its object, and the verb follows the object.

questions.stem: Which {把|bǎ} sentence is complete?
choices: {你|nǐ}{读|dú}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{一下|yí xià}。
{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{一下|yí xià}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{读|dú}。
{你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{读|dú}{一下|yí xià}。
questions.explanation: The verb of a {把|bǎ} sentence can't stand alone at the end: {一下|yí xià} after it makes a polite request, {你|nǐ}{把|bǎ}{这个|zhè ge}{句子|jù zi}{读|dú}{一下|yí xià} (read this sentence, please). {一下|yí xià} follows the verb, never the {把|bǎ} phrase.

questions.stem: How do you say "I didn't bring my homework."?
questions.explanation: The negative goes before {把|bǎ}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{带|dài}{来|lái}. Modal verbs ({应该|yīng gāi}, {能|néng}) and time adverbs ({已经|yǐ jīng}) go there too. Putting {没|méi} between the object and the verb ({把|bǎ}{作业|zuò yè}{没|méi}{带|dài}{来|lái}) is the commonest {把|bǎ} mistake.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I read the text through three times."
questions.explanation: The number of times is a verb measure word, so it follows the verb (and {了|le}): {把|bǎ}{课文|kè wén}{读|dú}{了|le}{三|sān}{遍|biàn}. {遍|biàn} counts going through something from beginning to end.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {这|zhè}{篇|piān}{作文|zuò wén}{写|xiě}{得|de}{太|tài}{差|chà}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng} ___ {写|xiě}{一|yì}{篇|piān}。 (This essay is too poor: I want to write a new one from scratch.) ({作文|zuò wén}: essay; {篇|piān}: its measure word)
questions.explanation: The first try is being replaced, from the beginning: {重新|chóng xīn}{写|xiě} (rewrite). {又|yòu} is for a repetition that has already happened ({他|tā}{又|yòu}{迟到|chí dào}{了|le}), so it doesn't fit a plan. {还|hái} (still) and {才|cái} (only then) don't mean "again" here.

questions.stem: How is 重 read in 重写 (to rewrite)?
questions.explanation: {重|chóng} (again) before a one-syllable verb: {重写|chóng xiě}, {重做|chóng zuò}, {重来|chóng lái}, as in {重新|chóng xīn}. In {重要|zhòng yào} and {重点|zhòng diǎn} the same character is zhòng (heavy, important).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The teacher doesn't allow us to use our phones in class."?

{老师|lǎo shī}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{不|bù}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}。
{老师|lǎo shī}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{我们|wǒ men}{在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}。
{我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{老师|lǎo shī}{在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}。
questions.explanation: {允许|yǔn xǔ} + person + what they may do, as with {让|ràng}: {老师|lǎo shī}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{我们|wǒ men}{用|yòng}{手机|shǒu jī}, with {在|zài}{课堂|kè táng}{上|shàng} before the verb it describes. The negative {不|bù} goes before {允许|yǔn xǔ}. {我们|wǒ men}{不|bù}{允许|yǔn xǔ}{老师|lǎo shī}… says the opposite: we don't allow the teacher.

questions.stem: Choose the measure word: {办公室|bàn gōng shì}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng} ___ {打印机|dǎ yìn jī}。

questions.stem: "{明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{学|xué}{第|dì}{九|jiǔ}{课|kè}，{今天|jīn tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{先|xiān}{预习|yù xí}{一下|yí xià}。" What is the speaker going to do tonight?
questions.explanation: {预习|yù xí} is preparing a lesson before it is taught: lesson 9 is tomorrow, so tonight is a first look. Going over a lesson afterwards is {复习|fù xí}, and studying on your own in a set study period is {自习|zì xí}.

questions.stem: Choose the word for the gap: "{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}{改|gǎi}{作业|zuò yè}{很|hěn}{认真|rèn zhēn}。{她|tā}{不|bù}{只|zhǐ}{写|xiě}{分数|fēn shù}，{还|hái}{会|huì}{把|bǎ}{每|měi}{个|gè} ___ {都|dōu}{画|huà}{出来|chū lái}，{让|ràng}{学生|xué sheng}{自己|zì jǐ}{改|gǎi}。" ({画|huà}: to mark, draw)
questions.explanation: She marks every mistake for the students to correct themselves: {把|bǎ}{每|měi}{个|gè}{错误|cuò wù}{都|dōu}{画|huà}{出来|chū lái}. {错误|cuò wù} is the noun "mistake". {正确|zhèng què} (correct), {合格|hé gé} (up to standard) and {严格|yán gé} (strict) are adjectives and don't fit {每|měi}{个|gè} ___.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {打|dǎ} ___ (to print)
questions.explanation: {打印|dǎ yìn} dǎ yìn. {={印|yìn} has a left part of three strokes and 卩 on the right. {即|jí} ({即使|jí shǐ}, lesson 26) and {却|què} (but, lesson 14) end in 卩 too, but their left sides differ; {节|jié} jié ({节日|jié rì}) has 艹 on top.=}

questions.stem: Listen to two friends. What does the first one want to do?

audio.text:
你的打印机能用吗？我想打印一下考试时间表。
能用，可是有点儿慢。

questions.stem: Listen to a teacher before an exam. What must the students do first?

audio.text: 考试马上开始了，请大家先把手机关了，再把书放进包里。

questions.stem: Listen. What should the listener do?

({整个|zhěng gè}: whole, lesson 15.) {重写|chóng xiě}: here {重|chóng} is chóng, not zhòng.

questions.stem: Listen. What will happen in Friday's class?

audio.text: 星期五的课改成自习，大家可以在教室复习，也可以预习下一课。

choices: There will be an oral exam.
The class is cancelled and the room is closed.
The teacher will hand back the marks.
It becomes a study period for revising or preparing.
questions.explanation: {改成|gǎi chéng}{自习|zì xí}: it becomes a study period. Students can revise ({复习|fù xí}) or prepare the next lesson ({预习|yù xí}) in the classroom, so the room is open.

choices: Passing the written exam alone is enough.
A candidate who arrives at 9.10 can still take the exam.
The exam is on Wednesday afternoon.
